body:
**What happens**

Building a Mac app (`--platform mac-app`) with the kidwithsword upstream at commit `94d1895` (installed by NX2Apple on 2026-11-25) gets through every step, then fails at the final **Mac app** step:

```
[9/9] Mac app · starting …
    · launcher and host (clones of the game files)
✗ Mac app (16s)
swiftc failed (1): .../upstreams/kidwithsword/dm/ios/Sources/LauncherHome.swift:357:48: error: cannot find 'MicTesterView' in scope
357 |             .sheet(isPresented: $testingMic) { MicTesterView(m: m) }
[RED] pack_app.py exit code 1
```

For Ocarina of Time (0400486024DEC000), that's about 1.5 hours of build work lost at the last step.

**Cause**

`LauncherHome.swift` now uses the new mic tester (`MicTesterView`, defined in `dm/ios/Sources/MicTester.swift`). The Mac launcher shares `LauncherHome.swift`, but `dm/mac/pack_app.py` (lines 94–95) doesn't compile `MicTester.swift`. Adding it to that list won't work either, because `MicTester.swift` uses `AVAudioSession`, which is iOS-only.

**Fix that worked for me**

In `dm/ios/Sources/LauncherHome.swift`, wrap the "Test Microphone" section (around line 333) and the `.sheet(isPresented: $testingMic)` modifier (line 357) in `#if os(iOS)` … `#endif`. After that change, the Mac launcher type-checks, and the rebuild (which reused the work folder) finished in about 5 minutes and produced a working app.

The problem is in cheemu21/kid-with-sword-remake, which has issues turned off, so I'm reporting it here. Pinning NX2Apple to the previous upstream commit, or applying this patch, would avoid it until the fork is fixed.

**Environment**

- MacBook Pro, Apple M1 Max, macOS 27.2 (26B123)
- NX2Apple 1.5.1-rc3
- Upstream: kidwithsword `94d1895`
title: Mac app build fails at the last step: cannot find 'MicTesterView' in scope (kidwithsword 94d1895)

body:
### Idea

Two switches in Settings > Controls, in a new "Game window" card, for every Mac game. Both are off by default.

- **Keep window on top**: passes `DM_WINDOW_TOP=1`. The engine already reads it and keeps the window at the floating level.
- **Controllers in the background**: passes `DM_PAD_BACKGROUND=1`. The controllers keep playing while another app is in front, and the keyboard and mouse are released as now. The engine side is https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/3368.

Use case: play with a controller with a guide, a chat or a video next to the game, without the game window losing the controller or going behind other windows.

### Plan

`GameStart` adds the two variables for Play and console mode, read from the launcher's defaults. The texts are added in all ten languages. Mac launcher only.

### Done when

Each switch passes its variable on the next start, and nothing is passed while it is off.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

A working branch has `GameWindowOptions` (NXCore), `GameWindowCard` (NXLauncher), a unit test, and the settings navigation and gallery coverage entries. A PR follows once this has the go.

</details>
title: Mac launcher: global Game window settings (keep window on top, controllers in the background)

body:
### Idea
Add `tools/build-ios-shell`, one script that goes from a game dump and `prod.keys` to the shared iPhone/iPad shell app.

Today the route in `frontend-ios/README.md` ("A shell built from the scripts alone") is three manual steps. Two are easy to get wrong:
- Skipping `romfs_image.py --append-msl` leaves the app showing "Update game data".
- `build_shell.sh` takes the `.framework` path, not its folder, and needs a Python with fonttools.

### Plan
One script runs: framework build, shaders on the image (append, or replace on a rerun), `build_shell.sh`, then either an unsigned IPA or a signed build with `--team`, and with `--device` the install and the game image copy (`devicectl`). Keys are read, never copied or printed. It adds no engine files.

### Done when
- Unsigned and signed builds work from a clean work folder.
- A test in `tools/tests` covers argument handling.
- The docs link to it.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

I have a working script. I ran the unsigned and the signed build (no install) on one game with Xcode 27.2. The install and copy steps reuse commands that worked by hand. I have not run it on other games or on an iPhone.

Where the shaders step belongs (this script, or `build_ipa_from_nsp.py --shell-framework` upstream) is open. I would send an upstream issue to seedds/nxnative if you prefer.

</details>
title: Idea: one command from a game dump to the iOS shell app (tools/build-ios-shell)

### This is

A problem

### What happens, or what you would like

## 问题描述

在 NX2Apple 1.5.1 里用 **Kid with Sword（KWS）特调引擎**构建《塞尔达传说：时之笛》(Switch 2, 0400486024DEC000) 的 iPhone 版时，构建界面只提供「单个游戏，全部打包」模式，**找不到任何把游戏数据外置的选项**（相当于 `--romfs separate` / `DM_COPY_ROMFS=NO`）。

结果产出的 IPA 有 **31.1 GB**，内部构成：

| 条目 | 解压大小 |
|---|---|
| Payload/DmIOS.app/romfs.img | 24.44 GiB |
| Payload/DmIOS.app/msl | 4.72 GiB |
| Payload/DmIOS.app/pso | 4.39 GiB |
| 程序与其余文件 | ~0.15 GiB |

单个 24.4 GB 的文件远超 iOS 侧载工具能处理的体积（AltServer 约 2 GiB 单文件限制；此前一个 4.9 GB 的 IPA 也报过 PackageExtractionFailed），AltStore / Sideloadly / LiveContainer 都无法安装。

## 期望行为

KWS 引擎自己的文档就是用外置 romfs 构建的：

```
python3 scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py ~/Games/OcarinaOfTime --romfs separate --env-file env.txt
```

`dm/ios/tools/build_ipa.sh` 也支持 `DM_COPY_ROMFS=NO`，注释明确说明是为「大游戏的完整包会超出 iOS 解压上限」设计的：游戏文件不进 IPA，App 从 `Documents/romfs.img` 读取，用 `scripts/push_romfs.sh` 推送。KWS 的 README 安装步骤也是让用户单独把游戏文件拷到手机。

也就是说引擎支持，但启动器在选用 KWS 时没有暴露这个选项，强制全打包，导致产出的 IPA 根本没法用它自己文档推荐的工具签名安装。

## 复现步骤

1. NX2Apple 1.5.1，引擎切换到 Kid with Sword
2. 选择时之笛 (Switch 2)，目标 iPhone / iPad
3. IPA 选项里只有「单个游戏，全部打包」，没有外置/分离 romfs 的选项
4. 构建得到 0400486024DEC000.ipa，31.1 GB，内含 24.4 GB 的 romfs.img

## 环境

- NX2Apple 1.5.1（引擎固定点 3f37dd3d…）
- KWS 上游版本 94d1895（2026-11-25 安装）
- macOS 27.3 / Apple M6 (Mac18,5) / 24 GB / Xcode 27.2
- iPhone 18 Pro Max / iOS 27

## 建议

在选用 KWS 引擎构建时，把 `--romfs separate` / `DM_COPY_ROMFS=NO` 暴露成一个选项（或直接对 KWS 默认启用，因为它的 README 就是这么构建的）。否则 KWS 的 iPhone 出包路径产出的是一个无法签名的 IPA。

如果需要，我可以帮忙测试启用该选项后的构建。

body:
### 使用场景

我用 NX2Apple 的 MacNativeGames 引擎构建了《塞尔达传说 旷野之息》1.9.0。现在可以通过下面的命令给现有 App 加载金手指，运行时日志也确认补丁已加载：

```sh
open --env "TOTK_PCHTXT=/absolute/path/to/BotW-1.9.0.pchtxt" \
  "/absolute/path/to/Breath of the Wild.app"
```

希望能在游戏库的「管理 → 金手指」里选择一个 `.pchtxt`，记住选择，以后直接点「开始游戏」就能生效。第一版做到**启动前选择、下次启动生效**，就能省去单独维护启动器的麻烦。[MacNativeGames 启动时补丁文档](https://github.com/ly05010419/MacNativeGames/blob/main/docs/mods.md#code-patches-at-launch-totk_pchtxt-mac)

### 实现思路

1. **按实际启动的构建选择配置。** 同一游戏可能同时有 nxnative 和 MacNativeGames 两个构建。可以从已有的 `launchWithMacEngine(_:upstream:)` 和 `manageItems(_:)` 入手，让金手指面板跟随玩家选中的构建。首个支持对象可以是已验证的《旷野之息》1.9.0。[多引擎启动与管理菜单](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/blob/main/frontend/Sources/NX2Apple/LauncherView%2BMultiBuild.swift)
2. **导入时核对 Build ID。** 例如这版《旷野之息》的 App 内有 `Contents/Resources/totk/extracted/botw190/exefs/main.build-id`，可与 `.pchtxt` 的 `@nsobid-` 比较。上游启动时使用完整的 **40 位十六进制 ID**。匹配后，按引擎、Title ID 和 Build ID 保存补丁选择及启用状态；不匹配时显示双方的 ID，方便玩家换文件。[上游补丁读取逻辑](https://github.com/ly05010419/MacNativeGames/blob/main/games/totk/runtime/pchtxt.h)
3. **启动时传入补丁路径。** 在默认「开始游戏」和显式「使用 MacNativeGames 启动」共用的启动路径上，将补丁绝对路径作为 `TOTK_PCHTXT` 传给本次游戏进程。关闭金手指后，下一次照常启动。补丁保存在 App 包外，切换时无需重建游戏。

**验收场景：** 导入匹配的补丁后，两种启动入口都能加载它；关闭后再次启动，游戏恢复原效果；同一游戏切换到 nxnative 构建时使用各自的配置。用含空格和中文的路径测试一次，也能覆盖常见的游戏库目录。
title: 支持从 NX2Apple 游戏库为 MacNativeGames 构建启用 `.pchtxt` 金手指（macOS）

### Engine pin `9922456…` (chain `df1800562702`) miscompiles 32 native mesh shaders on M1/M2 — foliage GPU hangs and a flat-coloured flower artifact in Ocarina of Time

**What happens.** The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (`0400486024DEC000`, v131072), built as a Mac app with **NX2Apple 1.5.0** (bundled engine pin `99224562186a8fdb7e97afb872319a21941ec317`, upstream 2026-11-20, shader chain `df1800562702`), on an **Apple M1 Max** (32-core GPU, `applegpu_g13s` pipeline archive), 32 GB, macOS 26.7.3: every session ends in a GPU fault within 45 s to 5 min.

```text
frame 1107  Caused GPU Hang Error (00000003:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorHang)   — recovered
frame 1178  Caused GPU Hang Error                                                   — recovered
frame 3905  Caused GPU Address Fault Error (0000000b:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorPageFault)
frame 3907  Ignored (for causing prior/excessive GPU errors) → GPU access revoked
            front end: the GPU no longer runs the game's work; telling the player and quitting
launcher:   the host exited with 70
```

macOS filed `firmware-detected lockup` (signature 577, `guilty_dm` 1) four times, then `BIF0 page fault` (signature 562, read, level 2, address `0xC104B29C00`, `guilty_dm` 2). Separately, some flower blossoms in Hyrule Castle Town render flat (measured RGB 82/207/239, or white) with a correct alpha silhouette and flicker; cutting them with the sword brings the textures back.

**Root cause, confirmed upstream.** This is [seedds/nxnative#3152](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/issues/3152): `mesh_subgroup_noinline` marks every helper with `simd_*` calls `noinline`, and Apple's Metal compiler miscompiles a `noinline` subgroup helper that calls another one, so the mesh shaders write outside their spilled stage ranges. Fixed upstream by [`6dc27632`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/6dc276325e169e0fefd00c21bda3bd7d4164df28) ("chain/mesh: pass subgroup inputs by value", PR #3169), which moves the chain to `648a020c093b`.

**Where this pin sits.** `99224562186a8fdb…` is **85 commits behind** `6dc27632`. The experimental engine manifest (`releases/download/engine-experimental/latest.json`, built 2026-11-22T11:50Z) still pins the same `99224562186a8fdb…`, so no channel currently carries the fix.

**Evidence.**
- My report with both app logs and the seven `gpuEvent` reports: [seedds/nxnative#3225](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/issues/3225)
- A third-party M1 Max report on the same pin/chain that patched exactly the 32 affected mesh shaders and eliminated the hangs, with the full key list: [seedds/nxnative#3164 (comment)](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/issues/3164#issuecomment-7085609910)

**Ask.** Lift the engine pin to `6dc27632` or newer (Stable and/or Experimental) so a rebuild picks the fix up. Its chain differs from `df1800562702`, so games would recompile their shaders on the next build — expected, and the launcher already announces that.

Until then, M1/M2 users hit GPU hangs in Ocarina of Time on launcher builds, and hand-patching the 32 libraries in a 5.3 GB `b-df1800562702.img` plus clearing the `applegpu_g13s` archive is the only local way out.
title: Engine pin 9922456 (chain df1800562702) miscompiles 32 mesh shaders on M1/M2 — Ocarina of Time GPU hangs; bump past 6dc27632

body:
### This is

A problem

### What happens, or what you would like

**Setup:** NX2Apple runs as a guest app inside LiveContainer (SideStore integrated, installed via iLoader), no JIT, free personal team with all app slots in use, so a separate install is not an option. The game framework was built on the Mac and copied to `Documents/Frameworks`.

**Steps**
1. Export the signing certificate from SideStore as .p12 and import it in NX2Apple (Settings → Import .p12 certificate).
2. Start the game. NX2Apple signs the framework on the device at launch.
3. Launch fails: "iOS refused the code signature of this game's framework…"

`log.txt`:

    [RED] boot: F_ADDFILESIGS_RETURN failed for …/Documents/Frameworks/DmGame04007EF01F8AE000.framework/DmGame04007EF01F8AE000: errno=1 (Operation not permitted)
    [RED] boot: …: iOS refused the code signature of this game's framework. Install the game again from NX2Apple.

**What I verified**
- The imported certificate is the same one LiveContainer signs its guests with (same serial, team and private key; compared SideStore's export with LiveContainer's "Export Cert").
- The failure is in `F_ADDFILESIGS_RETURN`, not `F_CHECK_LV`, so the team matches and iOS rejects the signature itself.
- **Workaround that works:** sign the same framework on the Mac with Apple's `codesign` and the same certificate (`codesign --force --sign "<identity>" --timestamp=none <framework>`), remove the certificate in NX2Apple (otherwise it re-signs at launch), copy the framework into `Documents/Frameworks`. The game then starts normally.

So the difference seems to be in the signature written by `MachOLocalSigner` (660c7d2 / 1007a6c) compared to `codesign`.

**Related (.p12 import, v1.5.0):** the password keyboard did not open (fixed by #1549, after v1.5.0). As a workaround I used a .p12 with an empty password and found:
- SideStore's export with an empty password has no MAC and an unencrypted key bag. iOS rejects it as "not a valid .p12".
- Re-encoded with Apple's `SecItemExport` and an empty password, iOS reports "wrong password".
- Only OpenSSL's encoding is accepted: `openssl pkcs12 -export -passout pass: -certpbe PBE-SHA1-3DES -keypbe PBE-SHA1-3DES -macalg sha1`.

Maybe worth handling or mentioning in the import hint.

### What you expected

The framework signed on the device with the imported .p12 loads, just like the same framework signed on the Mac with codesign and the same certificate.

### NX2Apple version

v1.5.0

### Computer and OS

MacBook Air M2, macOS 27.2.1 · iPhone Duo, iOS 27.2, NX2Apple inside LiveContainer without JIT

```markdown

```

title: Unable to build Tears of the Kingdom with MacNativeGames engine

body:
### Which step failed

Runtime rendering: black screen with missing shader-map entries.

### The message

## Environment

- **NX2Apple:** 1.5.0
- **Engine build:** `99224562186a8fdb7e97afb872319a21941ec317-ebcbf51f244f`
- **Host:** Mac mini, Apple M4 Pro
- **macOS:** 27.0 (Build 26A428)
- **Target:** iPhone / iPad
- **Xcode:** 27.2 (Build 27B52)
- **iOS SDK:** 27.2

## Summary

The application launches but displays a black screen while audio and controller input remain active. Runtime logs report shaders missing from the shader map.

This report focuses on the rendering failure.

## Prerequisite: local workaround for #1576

Testing initially stopped at the survey failure documented in #1576: an absent `ExeFS/sdk` module caused an unhandled `FileNotFoundError`.

A local change allowed survey to complete and testing to proceed. That change has not been established as a general solution. The rendering failure below was observed using that modified build; any relationship between the workaround and the rendering failure remains unconfirmed.

## Observed behavior

- The application launches, but the display remains black.
- Audio is active.
- Controller input is detected.
- Performance diagnostics report approximately 30 FPS.
- Build diagnostics report 112 shaders.
- Runtime logs report requested shaders absent from the shader map.

The reported frame rate does not confirm that graphics are being rendered correctly.

## Relevant runtime errors

Shader identifiers have been replaced with placeholders:

```text
[dm] [nvn-mtl] [RED] shader <SHADER_ID_1> is not in the shader map
[dm] [nvn-mtl] [RED] shader <SHADER_ID_2> is not in the shader map
```

## Expected behavior

The application should render the expected graphics. If required shaders are unavailable or unsupported, it should provide an actionable diagnostic.

## Current status

The missing shader-map entries were observed alongside the black screen. Their exact cause, and whether they fully explain the rendering failure, have not been independently confirmed.

Later testing reported completion of build and deployment stages. This alone does not establish that rendering was fixed.

## Requested assistance

- Investigate the missing shader-map entries and their relationship to the black screen.
- Identify the minimal sanitized diagnostics needed to distinguish a shader-processing problem from a mapping or loading problem.
- Determine whether the local survey workaround could affect the runtime result.
- Advise whether this rendering report belongs in another repository.

### Copy diagnostics

## Privacy and attachment confirmation

body:
Version: NX2Apple 1.5.0 (macOS)

## What happened
Super Mario Odyssey, freshly built with MacNativeGames (MNG), appears in the library with the yellow "未构建" ("Not built") chip instead of being detected as built, and it never gets the "MNG 构建" chip. The App itself is installed at /Applications/Super Mario Odyssey.app, launches fine, plays fine, and its save works — it is a genuine, current MNG build.

This is more than a cosmetic label: because it is flagged "Not built", the library offers "Build..." instead of "Play", so a working Odyssey cannot be launched from NX2Apple's game library.

## Expected
A MacNativeGames-built Odyssey should be detected as built (Play button), and should carry the "MNG 构建" chip like the other MNG titles on the same machine.

## Root cause found
The app maps installed Apps to library entries via a hardcoded bundle-ID allowlist embedded in the NSPortBuilder binary (URLForApplicationWithBundleIdentifier). The list contains:

org.macnativegames.totk, botw, bananza, dkb, oot, dread, mk8d, mkw,
pokopia, pkp, ori, ss, ssbu, wonder, jamboree, la, alc, aoc, by3,
unicorn, worldend, tomodachi, mvdk, gallery, ...

but it is missing `org.macnativegames.odyssey`. Since the Odyssey App's bundle ID is not in the list, NX2Apple can't associate the installed App with the Odyssey library entry, so it reports "Not built" and skips the MNG chip.

## Evidence
- Odyssey's actual bundle ID is `org.macnativegames.odyssey` (from Info.plist); it is a real, latest MNG build (express update, signature verified, opens and plays).
- Odyssey's title ID `0100000000010000` IS present in NX2Apple's own game catalog (artwork + library entry) — the game is known, only the installed App is not linked to it.
- On the same machine, every other installed MNG game in the allowlist — totk, botw, bananza, oot, dread, mk8d — correctly shows "MNG 构建" and a Play button; Odyssey alone shows "Not built".
- The binary allowlist includes those IDs but not odyssey.

## Suggested fix
Add `org.macnativegames.odyssey` (and a `-native` variant if applicable) to the bundle-ID allowlist used for both build detection and the library MNG chip.

Note the related string `upstream.mngOnlyFiveTitles` ("Available only for 5 supported titles") suggests the list is intentionally narrow; if Odyssey is deliberately excluded, please clarify — but as a maintained MNG title users can build and play, it should at least be detected as built.
title: Super Mario Odyssey (org.macnativegames.odyssey) shown as "未构建 / Not built" and missing the "MNG 构建" chip

### This is An idea ### What happens, or what you would like **Today**, the Library tells you things with notices drawn in the slot under the top bar (`noticeSlot` in `recentPage`). They're drawn as an overlay on the hero, so they take space from the page you're looking at: - In a wide, short window (1440 × 722 pt, current `main` at `c8de838d`), the skipped-files notice and the engine-update notice cover the game's badges and most of its title. At 900 × 680 they push the hero down instead. This is case (a) of #1462, still present after #1458. - Each notice has to be dismissed by hand, and once it's gone there's no record of it. Today, on main at 1440 × 722: the two notices cover the game's badges and most of its title.

**Idea: a notification center in the top bar.** 1. Search moves into the segmented control, next to Library and Builds. 2. Its place goes to a bell, with a badge counting the **active** notices. 3. The bell opens a popover with a segmented control: **Active** (the default) and **Resolved**, each with its count. 4. Nothing needs to be dismissed. A notice stays in Active while its cause is there, and moves to Resolved, with a check, when it's fixed (for example, after the app is signed again). 5. Resolved has a **Clear** button. Active doesn't, because those notices still need something from you.

Proposed top bar: search moves into the segmented control; a bell counts the active notices.

Popover, Active (the default): notices that still need something from you, each with its action.
Popover, Resolved: fixed notices stay as history and can be cleared.
Design file, with both popover states, the rules below and the captures behind them: [Figma, notification center](https://www.figma.com/design/bL559p5RwNXAFP0iWJ9rI9?node-id=15-163) (view only). It's built only from the existing tokens and pieces: `LauncherSegmented` for the tabs, `DSRowButtonStyle` for each notice's action, `DSTextButtonStyle` for Clear, and the `DSTone` symbols and colors for each notice. The icons are the SF Symbols the launcher already uses (`magnifyingglass`, `bell`, `gearshape.fill`). **Rules it would need** - **Errors that block playing stay on the page too.** `engine.failure`, or an expired signature, also keeps showing where it is today, not only in the popover. A badge or a popover is fine for things that aren't urgent, but shouldn't be the only place for something you need to know. - **Notices about the selected game** (`hero.refresh`, `hero.signature`) lose their context in a global list. They could keep a `DSChip` on the hero that opens their entry. - **The badge counts only Active** and clears as notices resolve. **Alternatives I looked at** - *Keep the slot and push the hero down* (move `noticeSlot` into the `VStack`). This fixes the overlap, but at 1440 × 722 two notices take close to a third of the window, and every new notice costs more. - *Transient toasts.* They don't cover anything for long, but they disappear and leave no history, which is the opposite of what a skipped-files warning needs. - *Keep it as it is.* The overlap in short windows stays. **Open questions** - How long Resolved keeps its history, and whether it survives a relaunch. - Controller navigation for the popover (`padScope`). - New strings: "Notifications", "Active", "Resolved", "Clear". - Whether Clear asks for confirmation. I'd say no, since it only removes history. I'm a product designer and happy to take this further (states, every notice type, all ten languages) if the direction makes sense to you. ### What you expected The game's details are never covered, notices don't need dismissing, and there's a history of what happened and what's already fixed. ### NX2Apple version v1.5.0 (launcher source at `main` `c8de838d`) ### Computer and OS MacBook Pro M4 Pro, macOS 27.2 ### No keys, no game files - [x] Nothing attached here contains keys, game files or data extracted from a game.
title: Mac launcher: a notification center in the top bar instead of notices over the Library

This Mac.

Existing Mac app and legacy build folder, reused through --from-seed.

### Computer and OS
MacBook Pro, M1 Max, 64 GB RAM, macOS 27.2.1 (26B131).

### Cause and proposed fix
Measured from the source image index.
- Retained Metal sources and metadata total 38.786 GiB.
- Shader packages add 4.300 GiB.
- Subtotal before ExeFS and other data is 43.086 GiB.

In dm/tools/build_seed.py, SEED_MAX_BYTES is 32 << 30.
_pack_metal_sources_one also retains all source payloads through read_bytes().

```python
source_path = lib / name
quota.charge(1, source_path.stat().st_size, name)
files_map[name] = source_path
```
The existing shader_lib.write streams these paths, including image entries.

### Validation
15 existing test_build_seed*.py tests passed.
Synthetic folder and image tests verified streaming, content preservation and quota rejection.
Full game rebuilding and runtime validation after the patch remain unverified.

title: The Legend of Zelda Breath of the Wild [01007EF00011E000] missing font when building via MacNativeGames engine

body:
The nxkit work folder and the Fast Refresh build seeds always sit on the internal disk. One game can take 16 GB or more there. The shell cache can already move to another folder, these two cannot.

### Idea

Settings, Tools gets two more rows under the shell cache row: the nxkit work folder and the build seeds. Each works like the shell cache row: Open, Move, and Use default when moved.

### Plan

- Reuse the shell cache move (rename on one drive, copy and verify on another, the old folder goes only after the check).
- The nxkit work folder moves into `NX2Apple-nxkit` inside the picked folder.
- The build seeds and `refresh-builds` move together into `NX2Apple-build-seeds`.
- Engine processes get `DM_SEED_CACHE_DIR` when the seeds are not in the default place. A `DM_SEED_CACHE_DIR` set by the player still wins.
- If the drive is not connected, a build stops early with a clear note. Nothing is written to the internal disk instead.

### Done when

- Both caches can move to an external drive and back from Settings.
- Nothing changes for a player who never moves them.
title: Launcher: move the nxkit work folder and the build seeds to another drive

When an iOS build fails only at sending the app to the iPhone, the failure card's **Retry** builds the whole game again instead of sending the app again. The app was already built and signed; only the transfer failed. Retry should resend it, as **Install built games** does.

### This is

A problem

### What happens, or what you would like

1. Build a game for iOS with the iPhone connected (here Balatro).
2. Every step passes, then sending the app to the iPhone fails (a transfer or pairing error).
3. Press **Retry** on the failure card.
4. The build starts again from the first step: extract, check files, rewrite, shaders, game framework, pack, shared app, signing. Cached steps go faster, but packing and signing run again, and the game data is packed again.

### What you expected

Retry after a transfer or pairing failure sends the app that was just built, without building anything. A real rebuild stays on **Build game**.

### NX2Apple version

1.5.0-local (`tools/try-local` from main at f82be32d)

### Computer and OS

MacBook Air M2 (Mac14,2), macOS 27.2

### Copy diagnostics

Not attached: the cause is in the code (below).

### No keys, no game files

- [x] Nothing attached here contains keys, game files or data extracted from a game.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- `frontend/Sources/NXModel/BuildStore+Failure.swift`, `fixBuildFailure`: `case .deviceTransfer, .devicePairing: runBuild()`. `BuildFailureCard` labels that action **Retry** (`fail.retry`).
- The launcher already has an install-only path: `installBuiltGames()` / `installBuiltShell(framework:titleID:name:)` (Builds page, **Install built games (n)**). Retry for these two kinds could call that for the game just built.
- Also: the text of the transfer error is shown on the card only. After Retry replaces it, it is in no log file, so it cannot be looked up later.
- Not checked: which of the two kinds the failure here was. The card was replaced by the new build before it was read.
</details>
title: iOS build: Retry after a failed transfer to the iPhone rebuilds the whole game instead of sending it again

Up next above the Build queue, both listing Balatro: Overall progress at 95% with GL shader capture just started: Show all steps, the same three steps: ### What you expected - The overall bar knows every step of the build from the start, gives each step a share by its usual length, and fills by the current step's progress inside its share. Better still, the bar shows the steps as segments. - Show all steps lists every step of the build, the ones to come as pending. - No Up next section: the Build queue is enough. ### NX2Apple version 1.5.0-local (`tools/try-local` from main at f82be32d) ### Computer and OS MacBook Air M2 (Mac14,2), macOS 27.2 ### Copy diagnostics Not attached: the screenshots show it. ### No keys, no game files - [x] Nothing attached here contains keys, game files or data extracted from a game.
Details - `BuildProgress.overallFraction` (`NXCore/BuildProgress.swift`) divides the done steps by `total = max(totalStages, highest step id seen)`. Without a `[k/n]` total from the script, the total is only the steps seen so far, so two done steps out of two seen give the 95% cap. Each step also counts the same, whatever its length. - `build.stages` grows as the script prints steps. The card and the steps sheet (#1457) both read it, so neither can list steps that have not started. - `BuildUpNextSection` (`BuildProcessCard.swift`) shows the queue's waiting games, the same entries as the Build queue section. - Not checked: an iOS build, and a build whose script prints `[k/n]`.

### Which step failed

The key check, before the build

### The message

### Summary
> **Note:** `0400486024DEC000` (*The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time*, `v131072`) already recompiles and builds cleanly on the current **stable release (`v1.4.0`)**. This enhancement request is strictly meant as feedback for **upcoming/future releases** to prevent regressions and make the Windows build experience smoother out of the box.

While testing `0400486024DEC000` on Windows via `nspb_qt.win.driver`, a few pipeline bottlenecks and edge cases stood out in newer pre-release builds—specifically around `shader_map.tsv` validation timing, single-threaded small-file I/O during `shader_split.py`, and engine/profile sync before tagging a release.

### 1. Pre-Flight Profile & `shader_map.tsv` Validation (Fail Fast)
* **Current behavior (in pre-release builds):** When an upcoming engine pin updates `shader_split.py` without re-splitting older game profiles (`0400486024DEC000`), the build unpacks 24.4 GB (`[1/5]`), verifies files (`[2/6]`), rewrites binaries (`[3/7]`), and runs 16+ minutes of shader splitting (`[4/7]`) before failing with `the split shader tables differ from game profile 0400486024DEC000's`.
* **Proposed optimization:**
  * Add a CI check / `splitter_hash` metadata field on game profiles so future releases automatically verify that profile `.tsv` tables match the pinned `shader_split.py` revision before publishing.
  * When `shader_map.tsv` row counts match within tolerance and only `BAHS` offsets shifted due to a splitter update, consider supporting an opt-in `--allow-resplit-tables` fallback (or an early pre-flight warning) rather than failing ~25 minutes into the build.

### 2. Parallelize `shader_split.py` & Reduce Windows NTFS Overhead
* **Current behavior:** Splitting `186,583` individual shader files into `shader\pkg.partial\` takes ~17 minutes (~184 files/sec) on Windows due to single-threaded Python execution, per-file NTFS handle creation overhead, and Windows Defender real-time scanning on `Downloads\..._build`.
* **Proposed optimization:**
  * Parallelize `BAHS` parsing / `zstd` decompression across CPU cores using `multiprocessing.Pool` (or `concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor`).
  * Stage split shaders in memory or a single packed container/archive during splitting rather than creating 180k+ loose files on NTFS.
  * Default the Windows work directory to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\NS Port Builder\work` (and/or surface a one-click Windows Defender folder exclusion hint in the Windows launcher).

### 3. Granular Stage Checkpointing (`[3/7]` & `[4/7]`)
* **Current behavior:** `extract/` is preserved on failure, which saves unpack time on retries, but `[3/7] rewrite` (~8 min) and `[4/7] shader split` (~17 min) re-run from scratch if a downstream step fails or a profile setting is tweaked.
* **Proposed optimization:** Persist stage completion markers/hashes for `rewrite` and `shader_split` in the work directory so unchanged inputs can skip straight to shader compilation/packaging.

---
*Tested on Windows x64 (`nspb_qt.win.driver`) with `0400486024DEC000` (`v131072`). Works without issues on stable `v1.4.0`; filed to help keep future releases smooth.*

In Chinese, a title mixes two weights of Chinese characters. Characters that Japanese also uses are heavy, the Simplified-only ones are a step lighter. The launcher font (Manrope) has no Chinese characters, so the system picks a fallback per character. On a Mac whose first language is Japanese, that fallback is a Japanese font, and characters it lacks fall back again to a Chinese font with another weight. ### This is A problem ### What happens, or what you would like Console mode, launcher language Simplified Chinese, Mac languages Japanese, English, Simplified Chinese (in that order). The large title on the home screen reads 塞尔达传说 智慧的再现: - heavy: 塞 智 慧 的 再 (in the Japanese font) - lighter: 尔 达 传 说 现 (Simplified only, in a Chinese font) ### What you expected Every character of a title has the same weight. Suggestion: give Manrope a cascade list for CJK that follows the launcher's language, not the Mac's (`kCTFontCascadeListAttribute` in `Typography.ctFont`): PingFang SC for Simplified Chinese, PingFang TC or HK for Traditional, Hiragino Sans for Japanese, each at the weight asked for. ### NX2Apple version 1.5.0-local (`tools/try-local` from main at f82be32d) ### Computer and OS MacBook Air M2 (Mac14,2), macOS 27.2 ### Copy diagnostics Not attached: a font problem, the screenshot shows it. ### No keys, no game files - [x] Nothing attached here contains keys, game files or data extracted from a game.
Details - `frontend/Sources/NXLauncher/Typography.swift` builds every launcher font from the embedded Manrope with only a `wght` variation, and no cascade list. CoreText then falls back per character by the system's preferred languages. - `DS.Console.Font.largeTitle` is `manrope(34, .heavy)`. Smaller texts probably show it too, less visibly. - Seen in the console mode title. Not checked: the desktop launcher, Traditional Chinese, and a Mac whose first language is Chinese (likely fine there). - Related: #1513 (same screen, the card animation).

body:
Building several games at once gives no way to choose where the builds go. Each game is built beside its own game files. If that drive is full, the queue skips or fails every game, and the player has to open each game's build page to change "Save to".

### Idea

- The Build selected sheet shows where the builds will go and lets the player change it for the whole batch.
- When the free space check stops a queued game, the message offers to pick another folder instead of only skipping it.

### Why

- Library games keep `outputDirectory` = the folder of their package file (`Library.swift`, the library scan).
- `BuildSelectedSheet` queues that folder as it is. Only the single build page has "Save to" (`FilesCard`).
- A library on a full external drive makes every game in the batch fail, while the system drive has room.

### Done when

- A batch can be sent to one chosen folder from the Build selected sheet.
- A game skipped for space can be retried in another folder without opening its build page.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

Seen on 1.5.0-local (main at f82be32d). Three games from one library folder on an external APFS volume with 240 MB free: two were skipped by the free space check (needed 16.86 GB and 1.48 GB), one failed ("needs at least 6 GB"). The system drive had 54 GB free.

Code paths:
- `frontend/Sources/NX2Apple/Library.swift`: the scan sets `game.outputDirectory` to the package's folder.
- `frontend/Sources/NX2Apple/BuildSelectedSheet.swift`: the queue entry takes `game.outputDirectory`.
- `frontend/Sources/NXModel/BuildStore+Operation.swift`: a queued entry's `outputDirectory` replaces `outDir`.
- `frontend/Sources/NX2Apple/FilesCard.swift`: "Save to" exists on the single build page only.

Not checked: the Qt front end and the iPhone shell.
</details>
title: Build selected: choose where the builds go, and another folder when a drive is full

title: it cant pack the ipa

body:
### Which step failed

Packing (the Mac app step). The launcher marks the run failed with no stage line in red; the queue's recorded reason is `构建失败，见下方日志。最后一行：KeyError: 'v851968'`.

### The message

```
KeyError: 'v851968'
```

Raised from `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py`, `report_profile_status()`:

```python
disp = g.builds()[pkg_ver]['display'] if derived else ''
```

Line 3767 of the engine tree of pin `0b5fd602` (the same statement is in upstream main, in the same function). It fails before any build work, so the log's last line is a bare Python traceback.

### Root cause

Fast refresh (`--from-seed`) stages the **seed's own profile copy** as the game object `g`, and takes the version from the seed's metadata:

```python
pkg_ver = args.package or PACKAGE or seed.get('pkg_ver') or 'v0'
```

For this game the two disagree:

| Where | What it says |
| --- | --- |
| `build-seeds/0100CD801CE5E000/seed.json` | `"pkg_ver": "v851968"`, `"profile_kind": "derived"`, `romfs_identity … version=1.1.3 build=v851968` |
| `build-seeds/0100CD801CE5E000/profile/0100CD801CE5E000/game.tsv` | one `build` row: `v0  1.0  main=a00bbcca…` — no `v851968` |
| engine `dm/games/0100CD801CE5E000/game.tsv` (the registered profile) | one `build` row: `v851968  1.1.3  main=294d9209…` |

So the staged `g.builds()` is `{v0}` while `pkg_ver` is `v851968`, and the blind index raises.

A **full rebuild does not hit this**, because it uses the registered profile, which has the `v851968` row — that is why the only way through is 重新构建.

Likely origin (observed, not proven): the seed's profile copy came from the build work folder, whose `game.tsv` is kept across builds (documented behaviour), and that copy was written when the game was first built **base-only** (v0). Later builds with the update refreshed `seed.json` but not that copy.

### Why it matters

Every app/engine update asks for a refresh of every built game, so this game's 快速刷新 fails every single time and the seed cache never pays off for it.

### How to reproduce

1. Build the game from its base package alone (v0), so a seed with a derived v0 profile is persisted.
2. Add update 1.1.3 (`v851968`) and build again (this succeeds).
3. After an app or engine update, click 快速刷新 → `KeyError: 'v851968'`.

### Suggested fix

Smallest, at the crash site:

```python
disp = g.builds()[pkg_ver]['display'] if derived and pkg_ver in g.builds() else ''
```

with a readable message instead of the traceback when the staged profile describes another version, e.g. "the build seed's profile describes v0 but the seed is v851968: rebuild, or drop the seed's profile copy".

Better, so the refresh actually works: when the staged derived profile has no `build` row for `pkg_ver`, stage the registered profile instead (`_find_registered_profile_dir`) or copy the registered build row into the staged profile — the same kind of self-heal patch 0061 already does for `gfx_api`.

### Environment

- NX2Apple 1.5.0 (rc10), engine pin `0b5fd6020093407af8bb5ad166e78e00bd2b7242`, launcher engine dir `…/engine/0b5fd602…-9fca6938dbbe`
- MacBook Air M5 (Mac17,3), 24 GB, macOS 27.2.1, Xcode 27.2, Metal 32023.922
- Fork patches line: `ios-game-data-folder, ios-slim-ipa, mac-keymap, hades2-update-profile, fork-patches-stamp, … build-add-persistent-build-seeds-and-fast-refres, … build-seed-infer-and-self-heal-gl-and-vulkan-gfx, …` (56 entries, `dm/fork_patches.txt`)

### Game, title ID and versions

Balatro, `0100CD801CE5E000`, base 1.0 (`v0`), update 1.1.3 (`v851968`). Built for **This Mac**. Game files: **NSZ** (base + update), no DLC.

### The launcher's record of the failed run

```json
{"fastRefresh": true, "target": "mac-app", "status": "failed",
 "inputs": {"base": ["…/巴拉特罗/nsz本体/Balatro [0100CD801CE5E000][v0][APP].nsz"],
            "update": ["…/巴拉特罗/upd-v1.1.3/[UPD][v1.1.3][0100CD801CE5E800][v851968].nsz"],
            "dlc": []},
 "reason": "构建失败，见下方日志。最后一行：KeyError: 'v851968'"}
```

### Build log

Not available: the launcher keeps no per-run log for a fast refresh, and the game's own `…_build/logs/` is from the last full rebuild. Say the word and I will re-run it with whatever logging you want and post the log.

### Seed audit on this machine (why only this game)

All 10 seeds under `~/Library/Application Support/nxnative/build-seeds`:

- 7 have no profile copy at all (registered profiles) → not affected
- `0400C76024710000`: derived, `pkg_ver=v0`, profile `v0` → consistent
- `0100CD801CE5E000`: derived, `pkg_ver=v851968`, profile `v0` → **mismatch, this report**

### Duplicate check

Searched both repositories for `KeyError`, `build seed`, `fast refresh`, `derived profile`. Closest: #1296 (the seed cache feature), #1396 / #1438 (seed validation and GL/VK inference), #1341, #1343 / #1335 (Windows profile manifest) — none covers a seed whose profile copy describes a different version than the seed itself.

body:
### Which step failed

Shader capture or shader split

### The message

[RED] arc/data.trpfs: the game's decoder in the Mac host failed on a 21009849 → 70786896 byte stream
[dm] [RED] DM_OODLE_SERVE: request 9895: emulated heap full (96 MB)
[dm] [RED] DM_OODLE_SERVE: request 9895 (21009849 -> 70786896 bytes) failed

The block is fine: it asks for 21 MB in and 70.8 MB out, and `Decoder` already holds 40 MB of
buffers (scratch 16 MB + in 8 MB + out 16 MB), so one request needs about 128 MB. The guest heap
is a fixed 96 MB (`arm64_emu.py`: `heap_size: int = 96 << 20`), so `Machine.malloc` raises
`EmuError('emulated heap full (96 MB)')` and the file is reported unreadable.

A one-file patch that grows the heap on demand (64 MB steps, 2 GB cap) is attached:
`nx2apple-oodle-heap-grow.patch`. `git apply` from the repo root; it touches only
`frontend-qt/nspb_qt/win/arm64_emu.py`.

[nx2apple-oodle-guest-fault-fix.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35113005/nx2apple-oodle-guest-fault-fix.patch)

body:
### Which step failed

Prepare Xcode, app build or IPA pack

### The message

I'm experiencing a consistent build failure when trying to build an iOS IPA using NX2Apple.

The build progresses normally through shader processing, framework generation, and app preparation, reaching approximately 85% (Stage 6 of 7). However, it fails during the final stages, specifically at `CopySwiftLibs`.

The error reported in the build log is:

```text
error: unexpected service error: The Xcode build system has crashed. Build again to continue.

** BUILD FAILED **
```

The NX2Apple interface reports this as a signing failure, but the actual failing build command is `CopySwiftLibs`, rather than an explicit `codesign` error.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open NX2Apple.
2. Select a game from the library.
3. Start building the game for iOS.
4. Allow the build process to complete shader processing and framework preparation.
5. The build fails at approximately 85%, during the `CopySwiftLibs` stage.

### Expected behavior

The build should complete successfully, generate the iOS IPA, and proceed with signing and packaging.

### Actual behavior

The build fails during `CopySwiftLibs`, with the following error:

```text
CopySwiftLibs .../DmShell.app

error: unexpected service error:
The Xcode build system has crashed.
Build again to continue.
```

The build log identifies the following failed commands:

- `CopySwiftLibs` (target: DmShell)
- Building project DmShell with scheme DmShell and configuration Release

All preceding build stages appear to complete successfully, including:

- NSP extraction
- File validation
- Shader splitting
- iOS shader compilation
- Game framework generation
- Game data packaging
- Shared app preparation

### Additional observations

During the failed build, macOS also displayed a system warning indicating that application memory was exhausted.

I'm not sure whether this is directly related to the Xcode build system crash, but it may be relevant.

The shader output and Xcode project build stages also consume a considerable amount of storage, although the build reaches the final stages before failing.

### Environment

| Component | Version / Details |
|---|---|
| NX2Apple | 1.4.0 |
| macOS | 27.2.1 (Build 26B131) |
| Mac | Apple M2 |
| Xcode | 27.2 (Build 27B52) |
| iOS SDK | 27.2 |
| Metal compiler | 32023.922 |
| Python | 3.13.18 |
| .NET SDK | 11.0.100 |
| Game | Pokémon Pokopia |
| Build target | iOS |

### Diagnostics

NX2Apple diagnostics report that all required dependencies are present:

- Xcode + iOS SDK: OK
- Metal Toolchain: OK
- xcodegen: OK
- zstd: OK
- spirv-cross: OK
- glslangValidator: OK
- Python and required packages: OK

The Metal compiler versions match the expected pinned version.

### Attachments

I'm attaching the following files to help investigate the issue:

- Full NX2Apple build log.
- NX2Apple diagnostics report.
- Screenshot showing the build failure at Stage 6 of 7.
- Screenshot showing the macOS memory warning.

Has anyone experienced a similar issue with `CopySwiftLibs` or the Xcode build system crashing during the final stages of an iOS build?

Could this be related to memory pressure, the Metal toolchain, or something specific to the current Xcode version?

Thanks!

Build ID for this game: Not known yet. Build the game first.

We have brought up Civilization VII on an iPhone Duo through NX2Apple v1.5.0-rc8, including handheld 1920×1080 output, direct touch mapping and a 1920×1344 full-screen experiment.

The engine findings and candidate patches are reported upstream:
https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/issues/3033

Game details:
- Title ID 0100C3601518C000, update v1638400 (profile version 1.5.0.1).
- main build ID 5d9401301ab2bb4917bafd939e5b3dd8.
- Engine ID 94a0944755da1a443f42651bf7ee49ab24ed5ee5-d599bd14eb6d.
- iPhone Duo, iOS 27.2; Xcode 27.2 on Apple silicon macOS 26.6.2.
- Shader chain b-19d183a2b462.

The handheld configuration dimensions are initialized separately from docked dimensions. Redirecting the handheld size load to the existing 1920×1080 literal, together with outgoing gesture coordinate conversion, restored the player's direct touch interaction at 1080p.

For the taller Duo output, the swapchain and crop could become 1920×1344 while the host still reported a 1920×1080 presentation shape. A narrowly enabled source-shape experiment corrected that report and the player confirmed full-screen gameplay. Independent X/Y gesture mapping and optional HUD adjustments followed.

These are local integration candidates, with inherited fork patches and diagnostics. Clean-engine reproduction, automated regression coverage, all UI states and long-duration stability remain pending. The upstream issue includes the patch text and validation limitations. No game assets, keys, signing material or private raw logs are attached.

Sharing this here so the NX2Apple maintainers can follow the upstream discussion and consider integration when reviewed.
title: Civilization VII on iPhone Duo: handheld 1080p and native full-screen bring-up (upstream #3033)

body:
### Which step failed

Something else: the MacNativeGames build stops before it even creates its work folder (`OcarinaOfTime_build` is never made, no `.app.ready` residue).

### The message

```
构建失败，见下方日志。最后一行：
ERROR: use the complete original update 131072 in the dump/NUP
```

### Game, title ID and versions

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2), `0400486024DEC000`, one `.nup` that already holds the base game and update `v131072`. There is no separate update package for this title on my disk, and MNG's install page says a `.nup` needs nothing else.

### Built for

This Mac

### Game files

A single `.nup` (`The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time [0400486024DEC000][v131072].nup`, 25.6 GB)

### What happens

1. I pick that `.nup` as the game. It lands in game-folder mode, and the launcher fills all three rows from the one file: 本体 = the `.nup`, 更新包 = the same `.nup`, DLC = empty (`library.json` -> `inputs.base/update/folder` all point at the same path). That is expected: the file *is* base + 131072.
2. With `buildUpstream = macnativegames`, the launcher runs `build_app.py <the .nup> --platform macos -o … --work … --update <the same .nup>`.
3. MNG refuses any `--update` for this title: `games/oot/build.py:760` -> `if args.update or args.dlc or args.mod: raise ValueError('use the complete original update 131072 in the dump/NUP')`. `build_oot` turns that ValueError into the `ERROR:` line above, and nothing else is attempted.

### Root cause (front end)

`frontend/Sources/NXCore/MacNativeGamesBuilder.swift`, `arguments(...)`, route `.unifiedBuildApp` (`0400486024DEC000` is in `unifiedTitleIDs`):

```swift
if !updatePath.isEmpty {
    args += ["--update", updatePath]
}
```

There is no exemption for an input that already contains its update. For every other title an update row means a separate NSP; for Switch 2 `.nup` (and for an exported dump folder with `updates/131072/`) the row is filled from the same input, and MNG rejects the flag. MNG's own troubleshooting table has a row for exactly this: "`use the complete original update 131072 in the dump/NUP`, `leave out --update, --dlc and --mod` -> give only the `.nup` or the dump folder, it already holds the update".

### Suggested fix

In `arguments(...)`, leave `--update` out when the game input is not a decrypted package that needs it, i.e. when `isUnencryptedInput` is true and the input is a `.nup`, or, more generally, when `updatePath == gameInput`. A cheap and safe guard:

```swift
let updateAddsNothing = isUnencryptedInput && (gameInput == updatePath)
…
if !updatePath.isEmpty && !updateAddsNothing { args += ["--update", updatePath] }
```

(The same guard applies to the `--dlc` loop only if a `.nup` ever fills the DLC row.)

### Why there is no in-app workaround

`frontend/Sources/NX2Apple/FilesCard.swift`, `optionalSections`: the 清除 button is drawn only when `build.gameFolderRowText(slot.id) == nil`. A `.nup` picked as the base makes `BuildStore+Inputs.swift` call `scan(folder:)` ("a .nup file is one game"), so every row is game-folder mode, all per-row buttons are hidden, and `clear(id)` in that state runs `leaveGameFolder()` — it would empty the whole game, not one row. A player therefore cannot drop just the update row and retry, which is why this stops an otherwise ready Mac build.

### Build log

The launcher kept no log file for this attempt (`~/Library/Application Support/NS Port Builder/logs/` does not exist on my Mac), and nothing was written to the game folder; the only output was the `ERROR:` line above, which the launcher already shows as the last line of the build log.

### Environment

- NX2Apple 1.5.0, engine pin `94a0944755da1a443f42651bf7ee49ab24ed5ee5-d599bd14eb6d`, `buildUpstream = macnativegames`
- MacNativeGames checkout 2026-11-17 (includes the #2070 lowering + retry fixes), work tree under `~/Library/Application Support/NX2Apple/upstreams/macnativegames`
- Apple M5, macOS 27.2.1 (26B131), Xcode 27.2 (27B52) with the Metal toolchain, python3.14 present, 293 GB free
- The same `.nup` builds and runs through the default nxnative engine, so the dump itself is fine

I checked both trackers before filing: no issue mentions this message, and `MacNativeGamesBuilder.arguments` on `main` still appends `--update` unconditionally. #1417 touches the same argument list (add-ons for per-game routes) but not this case.
title: MacNativeGames route adds --update for a .nup (Ocarina of Time), so the MNG script stops: "use the complete original update 131072 in the dump/NUP"

title: DLCs not installed

body:
### This is
A problem

### What happens, or what you would like
After a shared iOS game's build finishes, signing fails because the device has Developer Mode disabled.
The launcher shows the raw error without an installation recovery action.
For classified device errors, the failure card's retry calls `runBuild()` instead of retrying the completed installation.

### What you expected
Explain the device setting and retry signing, installation and pending data transfer using the existing built games.

### NX2Apple version
1.4.0. Retry routing is also present on main at `5e7791a3`.

### Computer and OS
Apple M5 Mac, macOS 27.2, Xcode 27.2 (27B52).

### Copy diagnostics
Not included. Reproduced with isolated process-runner fixtures and the supplied Xcode error.

### No keys, no game files
- [x] Nothing attached here contains keys, game files or data extracted from a game.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

The device error is `Developer Mode disabled ... enable Developer Mode in Settings → Privacy & Security.`

`BuildFailureClassifier.classifyInstall(.sign, ...)` returns no classification when the team is already listed.
`BuildStore.fixBuildFailure(.deviceTransfer/.devicePairing)` calls `runBuild()`.
The install already has built framework and archive paths.

A regression test fails on the existing routing for single-game, built-shell and batch installation recovery.
Related historical reports: #132 and #145. They are closed, and this report concerns the remaining failure-card recovery path.

</details>
title: Mac: retry failed iOS installations without restarting game builds

title: Super Mario Wonder Nintendo Switch 2 Edition builds without the DLC

body:
### Which step failed

Prepare Xcode, app build or IPA pack

### The message

### This is
A problem

### What happens, or what you would like

I cannot complete an iOS build of Pokopia and Donkey Kong using NX2Apple 1.4.0.

The build fails with:

`error: unexpected service error: The Xcode build system has crashed. Build again to continue.`

Xcode reports `CopySwiftLibs` as the failed build task.

During investigation, I found an unusually large `DMROMFS1` image inside one of the generated game frameworks. Its size is approximately 31.7 GB.

I would like to know whether this asset size is expected and whether it could be related to the Xcode build system crash.

### What you expected

The iOS build should complete successfully without crashing the Xcode build system.

### Game and title ID

- Game: Pokémon Violet
- Title ID: `0400A3A01EE4C000`
- Target: iOS

### NX2Apple version

1.4.0

### Computer and OS

- MacBook Air
- Apple M2
- 8 GB RAM
- macOS 27.2.1 (Build 26B131)
- Xcode 27.2 (Build 27B52)
- iOS SDK 27.2
- Metal compiler: Apple metal 32023.922.4

### Copy diagnostics

I will paste the complete output from NX2Apple Settings → Copy diagnostics here.

Relevant details:
- All dependencies reported as present.
- Xcode and iOS SDK detected.
- Metal Toolchain detected.
- Python 3.13.18.
- .NET SDK 11.0.100.

### Build log

The build log reports:

`CopySwiftLibs ... (in target 'DmShell' from project 'DmShell')`

The final error is:

`error: unexpected service error: The Xcode build system has crashed. Build again to continue.`

The preceding CodeSign commands for the game frameworks do not show an explicit signing failure.

A warning also appears:

`Metadata extraction skipped, no AppIntents.framework dependency found`

This warning does not appear to be directly related.

### Additional investigation

The following file was found:

`DmGame0400A3A01EE4C000.framework/msl/b-d24f05cf9d78.img`

- Exact size: 31,731,272,054 bytes.
- File signature: `DMROMFS1`.
- Present in both the source frameworks directory and the generated app's Frameworks directory.
- Both copies have exactly the same size, with different modification timestamps.

A second file with the same filename exists in another framework and is approximately 1.8 GB. Its header metadata differs.

A separate Xcode `SWBBuildService` report showed approximately 34.36 GB of writes over 286 seconds, with heavy activity involving `FileCopyTaskAction`, `pbxcp`, `copyTree`, and `copyRegular`. At the time, approximately 101 GB of free disk space was reported.

I cannot confirm that the large asset is the direct cause of the crash.

### Questions

1. Is a `DMROMFS1` image of approximately 31.7 GB expected?
2. Should this entire image be copied into the generated iOS app?
3. Could the size of this asset or the associated copy operations contribute to the Xcode build system crash?
4. Is there a recommended way to validate this asset or reduce the I/O load during packaging?

body:
Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit Remastered crackles in menus and races when the iPhone uses Nothing Ear earbuds. The built-in speaker sounds normal. The engine fix is proposed in [nxnative PR #2989](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/2989).

### Game and title ID

Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit Remastered, `010029B0118E8000`. Base `v0` with update 1.0.3 (`v196608`).

### Where it runs

iPhone shared IPA exported from NX2Apple 1.4.0 and imported into LiveContainer. Tested on an iPhone 18 Pro Max with iOS 27.0.1. The build used engine upstream `ccd834e0` and shader chain `d24f05cf9d78`.

### Reproduction

1. Start the game using the built-in speaker and listen in the menu or a race.
2. Quit the game, connect the Nothing Ear, and relaunch. Rapid clicks begin in the menu and continue during gameplay. They also continued with the earbuds' Low Lag mode enabled.

Expected behavior is continuous game audio on both routes.

### Runtime diagnostics

| Output | Host frames requested per callback | Underruns in the first 8,000 callbacks |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| iPhone speaker | 240 | 4 |
| Nothing Ear | 278–279 | 669 |

The Bluetooth route granted 5.80 ms at 44.1 kHz, so the callback asks for more frames from the host’s 48 kHz stream. The engine sometimes runs out of queued audio and pads the remaining samples with zeros. The upstream regression test reproduces this with the original code and passes with the proposed patch. Playback on iPhone with that upstream patch is still pending.

iOS 27.2 and macOS 27.0.1 (26A434).

Built an iOS game framework with the bundled engine's reference build script. Installed it into the existing NX2Apple shared app using `NSPortBuilder --install-shell`.

body:
### Idea

The MacNativeGames engine should build Xenoblade Chronicles 3 (`010074F013262000`) with its update and add-ons.

- MacNativeGames has a one-command build for XC3 since [ly05010419/MacNativeGames#2269](https://github.com/ly05010419/MacNativeGames/pull/2269) (merged): `games/xc3/build.py` takes the base game, the 2.2.1 update, the four add-ons and optional shared fonts.
- NX2Apple's MacNativeGames list (`MacNativeGamesBuilder.perGameTitleIDs`) does not have it, so the launcher says the game is not supported.
- `main` already passes add-ons per port (`PerGamePort.supportsDLC`), so only the port itself is missing. The first version of this issue asked to read `files.dlc` from `game.json`. `main` no longer reads `game.json`, so that plan is dropped.

This gives XC3 players a path that plays well inside NX2Apple, while #1117 stays open for nxnative.

### Plan

- `PerGamePort.xc3`: `--update`, `--dlc` once per add-on, the optional `--shared-fonts` (never asked for: the game has its own fonts).
- The bundle ID `org.macnativegames.xc3`, Supported games, and the Windows front end's MacNativeGames list.
- Tests for the add-on path edge cases.

PR: #1418.

### Done when

- An XC3 build through the MacNativeGames engine gets its update and add-ons.
- The other MacNativeGames games get the same arguments as before.
- Mac and Windows list the same MacNativeGames games.
title: MacNativeGames engine: build Xenoblade Chronicles 3 with its add-ons

body:
### Idea

Let the Mac launcher keep a game's build files (`<title ID>_build`) apart from the finished `.app`.

- Build files on an external drive, the app on the Mac.
- The game plays without the drive.
- The drive is needed only to build, update or rebuild.

Today the build folder always sits beside the app, so both must live on the same disk.

### Plan

- A "Build files" row under "Save to" on the Builds page. Empty keeps today's layout.
- The build, update and rebuild paths look in that folder first.
- With the drive unplugged, the launcher says to connect it instead of building into `/Volumes/<name>` on the Mac's disk.

### Done when

- A build with the setting puts `_build` on the chosen drive and the app in the output folder.
- Without the setting nothing changes.
- The Qt launcher is out of scope for now.
title: Launcher: keep build files on another drive than the app

body:
### Game and title ID

13 Sentinels: Aegis Rim (Asia), `01008D7016438000`

### Base game and update versions

Base 1.00 (v0), no update. `main` build `311947020f64f5742ce3c16162c4d87f`.

### Where it runs

Mac app (built for This Mac)

### Device, chip and RAM

Mac, Apple M2, 8 GB. External screen at 144 Hz.

### macOS or iOS / iPadOS version

macOS 27.2

### How it was installed

Built by the launcher into a library folder on an external disk. The disk runs at USB 2.0 speed (about 40 MB/s read).

### NX2Apple version

1.5.0 (release candidate 4)

### What happens, and when

The game crashes about 9 seconds after the start, before the logo shows: `SIGSEGV` at `main+0x309128`, the host exits with 139. It does not happen on every start.

**Cause.** At the end of a frame the game's main thread waits for its render thread only as long as the frame's time lasts (`main+0x30c194`), then goes on without it (a skipped frame). The render thread's first submission waits on the host for the pipeline archive and the prepare step. From this disk the 131 MB archive in `save/pso_archive` takes 2 to 7 s to open. The main thread runs on meanwhile and reads the next screens' files from the same disk, which makes the wait longer. The render thread's first draws then bind a texture entry of index -1 (`x0` = entries + `0xffffffff` × `0xe8`).

**Measured.** 21 starts in a window: all 13 with a wait (archive plus prepare) of 7 s or more crashed, none of the 8 below 6.5 s did. Language, fullscreen, the encode thread, shader prefetch, pipeline prebuild, `DM_PSO_PREPARE=0` and `DM_PREEMPT=1` do not change it.

**Fix.** Cutting the three branches that end the wait (`main+0x30c27c`, `+0x30c284`, `+0x30c2bc`) makes the main thread wait until the render thread is done. 9 of 9 starts ran with it. A pull request follows.

### What you expected

The game starts, as it does from an internal disk.

### Launch options changed from the defaults

Language Simplified Chinese, fullscreen on, encode thread on, A/B and X/Y swapped. The crash is the same with the defaults.

### Copy diagnostics

Not copied.

### Game profile lines from the build log

```

[dm] sdk: NintendoSDK nnSdk-11_4_3-Release (major 11)
```

### The game's log

body:
### This is

A problem

### What happens, or what you would like

Mac setup still requires .NET SDK 10, although the engine now ships native tools. The missing SDK blocks build readiness through the dependency check. Please align the Mac dependency gate and player requirements with the current engine.

### What you expected

Ordinary Mac game builds should not require an SDK used only to rebuild the engine's native tools.

### NX2Apple version

v1.4.0 stable, `NX2Apple-macOS-arm64.zip`; SHA-256 `0f95f7c95f57045fe416ea41dc3a2fe7fdd1ca1af8fbf93370295c5e1dcd3f0e`. Current `main`: `aa350afbbc6ec8c8fc4b2961e7cce58427daee6c`.

### Computer and OS

Apple M5 Pro, arm64, macOS 27.2.

### No keys, no game files

- [x] Nothing attached here contains keys, game files or data extracted from a game.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## Summary

The launcher requires an SDK that normal Mac builds no longer invoke. The README repeats this player requirement, and the Brewfile still attributes it to running the extractor and translator.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On a Mac without any .NET SDK, open the stable app's dependency setup.
2. Observe the required .NET SDK 10 row.
3. With other prerequisites and build inputs ready, the missing dependency prevents build readiness.
4. Installing the SDK makes the row pass, even though the engine uses its committed native tools.

The supplied first-launch observation showed `dotnet MISSING`; installation of SDK 10.0.404 made all eight dependency rows pass. The saved post-install dependency report confirms the passing row. The gate was verified from current source; it was not rerun without the installed SDK. No complete game build was run in this investigation.

## Expected behavior

The [stable release notes](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/releases/tag/v1.4.0) state: “The engine no longer needs .NET”. For ordinary Mac game builds, SDK absence should not prevent build readiness. Rebuilding the native tools from C# source remains a separate developer operation that requires the SDK.

## Actual behavior

- [DependencyCheck.swift, lines 83–86](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/blob/aa350afbbc6ec8c8fc4b2961e7cce58427daee6c/frontend/Sources/NXCore/DependencyCheck.swift#L83-L86) unconditionally appends the .NET dependency.
- `Toolchain.findDotnet()` accepts a candidate only when `--list-sdks` reports SDK 10 or newer.
- [DependencyStore.swift, line 94](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/blob/aa350afbbc6ec8c8fc4b2961e7cce58427daee6c/frontend/Sources/NXModel/DependencyStore.swift#L94) requires every dependency row to pass.
- [BuildStore.swift, line 441](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/blob/aa350afbbc6ec8c8fc4b2961e7cce58427daee6c/frontend/Sources/NXModel/BuildStore.swift#L441) requires `deps.allPresent` for `canBuild`.
- [README requirements](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/blob/aa350afbbc6ec8c8fc4b2961e7cce58427daee6c/README.md#L70-L72) still say the app installs SDK 10.
- [Brewfile](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/blob/aa350afbbc6ec8c8fc4b2961e7cce58427daee6c/Brewfile#L7) says the extractor and translator run on that SDK.

Both inspected engines use native `nx_extract` and `dmsh_xlate` binaries in `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py`. The launcher selects that script with `--platform mac-app` for Mac builds. The extractor lookup runs `nx_extract --source-sha`, validates its digest, and returns that executable. The shader preflight likewise runs the committed translator's `--source-sha`. Both `.csproj` files set `PublishAot=true`. The remaining `dotnet publish` command is in `dm/tools/native_tools.sh`, which rebuilds those binaries. Windows' managed-tool path is outside this report.

I unpacked the hash-verified stable archive and synced the current checkout's pinned engine and patch series. For each engine, I ran both native tools with an empty scratch HOME, `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin`, and a nonexistent `DOTNET_ROOT`. No `dotnet` was available on that PATH. All four commands exited zero, and each reported digest matched its accompanying C# sources:

| Engine | Extractor digest | Translator digest |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stable bundle | `eb660696a669ac76` | `fcb37fccd2f53012` |
| Current checkout | `eb660696a669ac76` | `c75f3cb403920cde` |

## Evidence

- Expected source: The stable release notes quoted above, and each engine's native-tool build path.
- Failure source: The unconditional dependency row, `allPresent`, and `canBuild` source chain linked above.
- Evidence provenance: static
- Local verification: static-proof
- Reproduction completeness: complete

Runtime reproduction of the SDK-free launcher gate was not run. The first-launch missing-row observation was supplied separately.

The valid trigger is absence of any .NET SDK with the repository, game inputs, and other prerequisites ready. SDK absence makes the unconditional row false, then `allPresent` false, and therefore `canBuild` false. The native-tool probes separately confirm these executable preflights run without an external .NET installation.

## Restoration check

With no .NET SDK installed and all actual Mac build prerequisites present, dependency readiness should pass. The same valid inputs should reach the engine's build entry point. Missing prerequisites that the engine actually uses should still block readiness. Player documentation should describe these requirements consistently.

## References

- https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/pull/1125 — Its merged engine bump explicitly lists the Mac .NET dependency check as unfinished follow-up.
- https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/pull/1142 — Its follow-up removes unused engine helpers and preserves Windows managed-tool support.

## Triage assessment

- Impact level: P2
- Assessment status: supported
- Impact basis: SDK-free Mac setup cannot reach build readiness until an unnecessary SDK is installed.
- Workaround status: available
- Workaround basis: The supplied run installed SDK 10 through the offered setup path, after which all eight rows passed.

</details>
title: fix(deps): Mac setup still requires .NET after the engine stopped needing it

body:
### This is

An idea

### What happens, or what you would like

### Idea
The touch controls sit at fixed places. On an 11-inch iPad the top row (ZL, L, L3 / ZR, R, R3) sits very high, and players have different hands and grips.

I'd like to add an editor in the game (gear › Controller layout › Adjust Gamepad Layout) to move and resize the controls in groups.

### Plan
- Six groups: each shoulder side, left stick, D-pad, A B X Y, the centre buttons.
- Drag to move, pinch or a slider to resize (50–150 %, never under 44 pt).
- Move both sides together, or each side on its own.
- Save for all games or for one game; one value, `DM_TOUCH_GROUPS`.
- No saved layout: the controls stay exactly as today.
- Engine part as patches in `patches/`, shell part in `frontend-ios`.

### Done when
- The editor works on iPad and iPhone, portrait and landscape.
- The shell keeps the layout for all games or per game.
- Tests for the layout rules; a self-test (`DM_PAD_LAYOUT_TEST`).

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Built and played on an 11-inch iPad. The editor's tests pass on Simulators of three iPhone sizes, an 11-inch and a 13-inch iPad Pro; not yet run on a real iPhone.
- With no layout saved, the pad is byte-identical to today's: checked over 3,528 screen and layout cases.
- Builds on the fork's touch-layout patch 0020 and menu-words patch 0040.
- A draft PR with the work is linked below as a sketch; it waits for the go.

</details>

### What you expected

_No response_

main (37393005)

### Idea

Unify the Mac desktop launcher and console mode around one clear visual language.
Keep game artwork, controls, progress and navigation consistent across Library, Builds, Settings and setup.
Preserve existing build, install, export, recovery and controller functions.

### Plan

- Desktop: responsive Library, rounded Builds table, guided build flow, grouped Mac/iOS queues, shared footer and clearer Settings/setup.
- Console: large artwork, consistent right-side sheets, visible context, keyboard/controller focus and glanceable build progress and notifications.
- Reuse shared controls, artwork status indicators and transitions. Preserve partial platform results and retry only failed work.

### Done when

- One draft PR presents Desktop Launcher and Console Mode separately, with matched before/after screenshot accordions.
- Existing functions and keyboard/controller navigation are retained, with regression coverage for changed behavior.
- Build, test, performance and bundle results are disclosed alongside simulation and hardware limits.
- Review uses the approved English screenshot library. No additional localized screenshots are requested for this pass.

<details>
<summary>Review evidence and scope</summary>

The review library contains 70 English before/after pairs using the same nine-title catalog.
Demo build states and device results are simulated. This does not claim gameplay or physical-device validation.
The change targets the Mac launcher and shared text catalogs. It does not change the engine or iOS shell source.
Release scheduling remains with the maintainers.

</details>

Draft PR: https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/pull/1392

body:
### This is A problem ### What happens, or what you would like

I'm experiencing a persistent code-signature error when attempting to launch games through NX2Apple 1.5.0 on my iPhone 15 Pro.

The games build successfully, their frameworks are signed and transferred to my iPhone, but neither game launches.

Both games produce the same error:

iOS refused the code signature of this game's framework. Install the game again from NX2Apple.

Repeatedly using Install built games does not resolve the issue.

Environment

Component | Version -- | -- NX2Apple | 1.5.0 (Stable) Engine commit | 0c078130f6db7d0d32c1dc28146feaf97713f008 macOS | 27.2.1 (26B131) Mac | MacBook Air, Apple M5 Xcode | 27.2 (27B52) iOS SDK | 27.2 iPhone | iPhone 15 Pro iOS | 27.2.1 Signing | Apple Development certificate Developer Mode | Enabled Certificate trust | Enabled Dependencies | All present and reporting ready

Games affected

  • Fire Emblem Engage

  • Final Fantasy Resonance

Both games exhibit the same framework-signature error.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Build an iOS game using NX2Apple 1.5.0.

  2. Select the connected iPhone and valid Apple Development signing team.

  3. Complete the build and installation process.

  4. Transfer the game files and framework to the device.

  5. Open NX2Apple on the iPhone and attempt to launch the game.

  6. Observe the code-signature rejection.

  7. Return to NX2Apple on macOS and select Install built games.

  8. Attempt to launch the game again.

The error persists after reinstalling.

Expected behaviour

The signed game framework should load successfully and launch the game on the iPhone.

Actual behaviour

The game fails to launch with the code-signature error.

No game log is produced because execution never begins.

Investigation performed

1. Verified the signing identity

Ran:

security find-identity -v -p codesigning

Result: one valid Apple Development signing identity was found.

2. Checked the cached framework

The cached framework is located at:

~/Library/Application Support/NX2Apple/shell/frameworks/DmGame0100606026F12000.framework

Running codesign --verify against this framework returned:

code object is not signed at all
In architecture: arm64

I understand that NX2Apple signs a temporary copy before transferring it, so the unsigned cache may be expected.

3. Independently tested framework signing

Copied the cached framework to a temporary directory, signed it using my valid Apple Development identity, and verified it.

Verification returned:

valid on disk
satisfies its Designated Requirement

This confirms that macOS can successfully sign and verify the framework, although it does not establish that the transferred framework is accepted by iOS.

4. Examined NX2Apple installation logs

The installation log shows the following operations completing without reported errors:

/usr/bin/xattr -cr .../DmGame0100606026F12000.framework

/usr/bin/codesign --force --sign "Apple Development: ..." --timestamp=none .../DmGame0100606026F12000.framework

/usr/bin/xcrun devicectl device copy to ... --destination Documents/Frameworks/.staging-0100606026F12000-5fd501bd/DmGame0100606026F12000.framework

/usr/bin/xcrun devicectl device copy to ... --destination Documents/Frameworks/.staging-0100606026F12000-5fd501bd/.ready

Both the framework directory and .ready marker appear in the device-copy logs.

The .ready file is reported as 71 bytes.

There are no explicit signing or transfer failures in the final 50 lines of the build log.

5. Examined iPhone Console logs

The following sandbox denials appeared around the time of the error:

Sandbox: DmShell(1192) deny(1) process-info-codesignature others [SpringBoard(37)]

Sandbox: DmShell(1192) deny(1) system-info vfs.disk-space

These may be unrelated, as neither directly identifies a failed validation of the game framework.

I have not yet identified an explicit dlopen, dyld or amfid error explaining the rejection.

Additional observations

  • The NX2Apple app itself launches correctly on the iPhone.

  • Both games build and transfer successfully.

  • The same failure occurs across two different games.

  • Repeatedly reinstalling built games makes no difference.

  • Developer Mode is enabled and the development certificate is trusted.

  • All dependencies report as ready.

  • The issue appears to occur before game execution.

Questions

  1. Is this a known issue with NX2Apple 1.5.0's iOS game-framework loading mechanism?

  2. Does iOS 27.2.1 introduce any compatibility issues with loading frameworks from Documents/Frameworks?

  3. Is the cached framework expected to remain unsigned, with signing performed only on the temporary installation copy?

  4. Is there a recommended way to verify that the framework retains a valid signature after being transferred to the iPhone?

  5. Are additional diagnostics available for the exact framework-loading failure?

I can provide the full NX2Apple diagnostics, build logs and iPhone Console capture if needed.

### What you expected _No response_ ### NX2Apple version 1.5.0 ### Computer and OS MacBook Air M5, OS 27.2.1 ### Copy diagnostics ```markdown ``` ### No keys, no game files - [x] Nothing attached here contains keys, game files or data extracted from a game.

body:
### Idea

The 3D touch layout drives the camera with a floating right stick. Hold your finger a little away from where it landed and the camera keeps turning. Short drags hardly move it, which is the opposite of a mobile swipe camera. On the left, a thumb that starts near the stick's centre makes the character wander.

I have this open upstream as seedds/nxnative#258. I'd like to carry it here as a patch until it merges.

### Plan

Four iOS rows in the Controls section. Defaults keep today's behaviour.

- `DM_TOUCH_SWIPE`, the camera follows finger speed instead of the floating stick
- `DM_TOUCH_SWIPE_GAIN`, swipe sensitivity from 25 to 400 %
- `DM_TOUCH_RIGHT_AREA`, where a camera touch can start
- `DM_TOUCH_LEFT_DEADZONE`, left-stick dead zone from 0 to 40 %

#258 also adds a floating left stick. I'm leaving that out because it's claimed in #1090.

### Done when

- The four rows work in the iOS shell on an iPhone, folded and unfolded on an iPhone Duo too.
- Nothing changes for players who leave them alone.
