### This is

A problem

### What happens, or what you would like

With the output folder on my external drive, every build stops before it starts:

> Not enough free space on /Volumes/T7/NX2Apple Games. The game files alone need at least 51.24 GB and Zero KB is free.

The drive (Samsung T7, formatted ExFAT) has well over 100 GB free according to Finder. The same drive built fine with 1.3.0, which didn't have this check.

**Cause:** `BuildSpace.available(at:)` in `frontend/Sources/NXCore/BuildSpace.swift` (the #966 space check) reads `volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsageKey`, and macOS answers 0 for that key on this drive. Only a nil answer skips the check, so `spaceProblem()` treats the 0 as real and blocks the build. `DriveCopy.volume(at:)` reads the same drive with `statfs` and gets the right number.

**Suggested fix:** fall back to `statfs` when the important-usage value is 0 or missing.

```diff
--- a/frontend/Sources/NXCore/BuildSpace.swift
+++ b/frontend/Sources/NXCore/BuildSpace.swift
@@ -36,7 +36,10 @@ package struct BuildSpace: Equatable, Sendable {
         let values = try? url.resourceValues(forKeys: [.volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsageKey])
-        return values?.volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsage
+        // macOS answers 0 (or nothing) for "important usage" on some external drives, such as exFAT ones.
+        // statfs reads those drives right (DriveCopy uses it for the same drives), so fall back to it.
+        if let important = values?.volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsage, important > 0 { return important }
+        return DriveCopy.volume(at: url.path, fm: fm)?.freeBytes
     }
```

Workaround until it's fixed: choose an output folder on the Mac's internal drive.


Built from v1.4.0-rc2 with this change, the build on the T7 starts normally.

### What you expected

The check reads the drive's real free space (over 100 GB) and the build starts.

body:
### Which step failed

Mac host (building the Mac player)

### The message

```
In file included from front_mac.m:22:
./input_preferences_mac.h:8:70: error: called object type 'NSString *' is not a function or function pointer
    8 |     return NSBundle.mainBundle.bundleIdentifier ?: [@"org.nxnative." DM_GAME_ID lowercaseString];
      |                                                     ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ ^
gen/010049900F546000/game_profile.h:13:20: note: expanded from macro 'DM_GAME_ID'
   13 | #define DM_GAME_ID (dm_game_cur()->id)
```

The same error comes from controllers_mac.m:13.

Cause. input_preferences_domain() builds the preferences domain by joining two string literals at compile time: @"org.nxnative." DM_GAME_ID. That only compiles when DM_GAME_ID is a literal, as game.py header_one writes it. For a multi-program title (a profile with programs), header_multi defines it as (dm_game_cur()->id), a runtime const char *, and the expression no longer compiles. Super Mario 3D All-Stars (010049900F546000) is the profile that does this, so every single-program game is unaffected.

The line comes from patches/0081-support-steam-controller-and-shared-mac-control.patch, which is adapted from [seedds/nxnative#221](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/issues/221). That pull request is still open and has the same line. It is unchanged on main as of 2026-11-10.

Fix. Box the ID at run time, as front_mac.m already does with @(DM_GAME_ID):

```
 static NSString *input_preferences_domain(void) {
-    return NSBundle.mainBundle.bundleIdentifier ?: [@"org.nxnative." DM_GAME_ID lowercaseString];
+    return NSBundle.mainBundle.bundleIdentifier ?: [[@"org.nxnative." stringByAppendingString:@(DM_GAME_ID)] lowercaseString];
 }
```
Tested.

- With the change applied to the installed engine, the full Super Mario 3D All-Stars build completes.
- front_mac.m and controllers_mac.m compile against the generated gen/010049900F546000/game_profile.h.
- A small test program, compiled with both forms of DM_GAME_ID, returns the same domain as before for a single-program game (org.nxnative.0100000000010000) and org.nxnative.010049900f546000 for the multi-program one.

body:
### Game and title ID

Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave (Switch 2) — `04007EF01F8AE000`

### Base and update versions

Base v0 + update **v131072** (the version the profile registers). Packed from the 27.49 GB `.ipa` produced by 1.2.3 first, then rebuilt from `patched_v131072` in Xcode.

### Where it runs

iPhone — a single-game app built straight from the generated `DmIOS.xcodeproj`, **not** the shared shell.

### Device

iPhone 18 Pro Max (`iPhone19,7`), iOS 27.2 (24B119), 12 GB.

### NX2Apple version

1.2.3, engine pin `88c7e03f51e3`, Xcode 27.2 on macOS 27.2 (Mac mini M4).

### What I did

`GAMES.md` says "No IPA built / Not tried" for this title, so these are the two gaps that stopped the generated project from installing and running:

1. **The bundle ID is globally taken.** The generated project has `PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER = org.nxnative.04007EF01F8AE000` in two places. Signing stops at "Failed to register the bundle identifier … unavailable". I changed both to a personal ID (`com.<me>.fefortunesweave`).

2. **The project requests no entitlements, but the game needs the jetsam budget.** There is no `CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS` in `Gen/dm.xcconfig` and no `.entitlements` file next to `Gen/`. I created `Gen/DmIOS.entitlements` with `com.apple.developer.kernel.increased-memory-limit` = `true` and added `CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS = $(SRCROOT)/Gen/DmIOS.entitlements` to `Gen/dm.xcconfig`. Xcode then re-registered the App ID and the new profile carried the entitlement (checked with `security cms -D` on the `.mobileprovision`).

3. Built `Release` for the device, installed with `xcrun devicectl device install app`, and trusted the developer certificate on the phone (`FBSOpenApplicationErrorDomain error 3` before that).

If the generator could do 1 and 2 itself (a unique bundle ID, and the entitlement the profile asks for), an iPhone build of this title would need no manual edits at all.

### Result

Runs, locked 60 fps. From `log.txt` in the Files app, after 40,500 frames (~11 minutes of play):

```text
[dm] [nvn] on-screen up to frame 40500: 300 frames, dropped 0 (discarded 0), p99 16.67 ms; footprint 2084 MiB; brightness 0.55; thermal 1
[dm] [nvn] timing up to frame 40500: frame time p50 16.65 / p95 17.19 / max 19.71 ms (300 frames); NVN submit+present p50 2.57 / max 5.55 ms; GPU p50 10.16 / max 17.55 ms
[dm] [nvn] power up to frame 40500: CPU energy 1.51 W, 25.2 mJ per frame (60.0 fps); CPU 64% (100 = one core), 82% of it on performance cores
[dm] [nvn-mtl] memory up to frame 40200: resident 2083 MB, GPU allocated 9156 MB, ...; headroom to the system memory limit 6108 MB
[dm] audren: render time mean 0.07 ms / max 0.64 ms (5 ms budget per frame); 0 underruns
```

- frame time p50 16.65 ms, p95 17.19 ms, max 19.71 ms — 0 dropped frames in the measured window
- resident 2,083 MB, GPU allocated 9,156 MB, **6,108 MB headroom** to the limit with the entitlement in effect
- CPU 1.51 W, 25.2 mJ per frame, 64% of a single core; thermal state 1 the whole run
- audio: 0 underruns, mean render 0.07 ms
- no error lines in the log

Memory is not the obstacle for this one on a 12 GB device — it idles around 2.1 GB resident with more than half the budget free.

### Suggestion

The "No IPA built" note for this title looks out of date now; it can probably be listed as playable on an iPhone, with the increased-memory-limit entitlement as the requirement. Happy to send more of the log or a screenshot if that helps.

### Game and title ID

Splatoon Raiders,  0400380020056000

### Base game and update versions

base 1.0.0, no updates

### Where it runs

Mac app (built for This Mac)

### Device, chip and RAM

Macbook Air M4, 16GB

### macOS or iOS / iPadOS version

MacOS 27.0.1

### How it was installed

I ran the app the launcher built.

### NX2Apple version

V.1.3.1 RC1

### What happens, and when

During particle-intensive scenes in Splatoon Raiders (specifically stages with heavy ink overlays / Steel Eel mechanics), the application encounters a host GPU queue error (`MTL4CommandQueueErrorDomain`) and terminates back to desktop.

### What you expected

The game should continuously process multi-entity particle passes (such as ink overlays during the Steel Eel stage) without triggering host GPU command queue timeouts (`MTL4CommandQueueErrorDomain`), dropping frames smoothly rather than terminating the application process back to desktop.

### Launch options changed from the defaults

Handheld mode (720p), Upscaling and Game's Upscaler were both with MetalFX, only Metal 4 Pipelines was turned in the settings.

body:
### Idea

Let a mod be built from the player's own game files. A fan translation such as [oot-hr](https://github.com/mbanusic/oot-hr) (Croatian, Ocarina of Time) can't ship the game's archives. It ships the text and a script, and each player builds the mod from their own RomFS. Today that means unpacking the RomFS by hand and copying the result into the mods folder.

Mods already load (#34, #57, #573). This only adds the build step.

### Plan

- A mod folder may hold `nx2apple-mod.json`: the RomFS paths the build reads (`needs`) and the command (`build`). The first item of `build` is a script in the mod folder. `{game}` and `{out}` are replaced by folders.
- Mods shows **Build** for such a mod. The launcher asks first, because this runs the mod's own code.
- The launcher copies `needs` out of the game's `romfs.img`, or the build folder's `RomFS.img`. It runs the script with its Python and writes `<mod>/romfs`. The mod then works like any other.
- Mac launcher first. The iPhone shell takes the built folder as it is.

### Done when

- A recipe mod is listed as needing a build, with a Build button, until its `romfs/` exists.
- Build makes `romfs/` from the game's files, and the log names the error when it fails.
- oot-hr builds this way and its text shows in the game.
title: Mods built from the player's own game files (a fan translation as a recipe)

body:
### Which step failed

Pipeline prebuild or Pipeline archive

### The message

The launcher does not display a specific error message before crashing. Instead, NSPortBuilder terminates unexpectedly during the Pipeline Archive stage.

The crash report identifies the following error:

Exception Type: EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGSEGV)
Exception Subtype: KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0x0000000000000000
Termination Reason: Namespace SIGNAL, Code 11

The relevant stack trace is:

Thread 4 Crashed:
0   ??? 0x0
1   NSPortBuilder
    static BuildProgress.psoArchiveProgress(workDir:batchSize:) + 1404
2   NSPortBuilder
    closure #1 in closure #1 in BuildStore.startPSOPoll(stageID:step:) + 52

The same crash occurs with both Breath of the Wild and Echoes of Wisdom.

body:
Mario Tennis Fever stays white at startup on an M5 Pro Mac after pipeline prewarm completes.
Both sampled runs show a queue-completion receipt wait while the NVN replay worker waits on its condition variable.
Please advise which queue, producer, and receipt instrumentation would distinguish the unresolved dependency.

<details>
<summary>Environment, reproduction, controlled tests, and redacted evidence</summary>

### Game and title ID

Mario Tennis Fever, `0400D4201C6EA000`.

### Base game and update versions

NUP input, selected update `v327680`. Runtime main build ID prefix: `104BCE6874603701`.
The base package version and NACP display version were not independently captured for this report.
The launch window's “Version 1.0” is app metadata, not evidence of the game's update version.

### Where it runs

Mac app (built for This Mac). This report concerns the standalone Mac app, not an iPhone run.

### Device, chip and RAM

Apple M5 Pro. Exact Mac model and installed RAM were not supplied.

### macOS or iOS / iPadOS version

Affected Mac: macOS 26.7.1 (`25G241`), confirmed by both process samples.
Build toolchain: Xcode 27.2, Apple Metal `32023.922` (`metalfe-32023.922.4`).
The build toolchain version is not the affected Mac's runtime OS version.

### How it was installed

Running the locally built native Mac app, named Mac26 locally, through its per-game launch window.
The build used the standard Python build path, not the experimental nxb builder.

### NX2Apple version

Frontend version not captured. The per-game window's “Version 1.0” does not establish the NX2Apple frontend version.
Prior build records identify engine `c78d7375bea9c862679ec294a6a69ff3e22e18d0` and patch stamp `66e8bc624c49`.
Both runtime logs identify shader chain `e9a97471681b`, but say `commit not recorded`.

**Local modification:** `MAC_METAL` in `dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_build.py` added `-mmacosx-version-min=26.0`.
The app and matching shader chain were rebuilt through the Python driver with that deployment target.
This addressed an earlier unsupported Metal language-version error, absent from both supplied runs.
This is a locally modified build report, not a demonstrated regression in an unmodified release.

### What happens, and when

1. Launch the same Mac26 app with Docked mode and the settings below.
2. Allow pipeline preparation to finish.
3. The game remains white before reaching a usable title screen, with no audible sound reported.
4. Sample the still-running Fever `dmhost` process while it remains white.

The failure reproduced in the baseline and Metal-4-off runs, each with a runtime log and process sample.
A later launch-options test also reportedly stayed white, but has no new runtime log or sample.
There is no evidence here of a crash or a proven GPU deadlock.

### What you expected

A rendered, responsive title screen and progression into the game.

### Launch options changed from the defaults

The complete defaults comparison was not captured. Effective settings and tested changes follow.

| Test | Metal 4 pipelines | Encode thread | Other relevant settings | Result and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline | `DM_PSO_MTL4=1` | `DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=0` | Docked, `DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=off`, `DM_PRESENT_SNAP=0`, HUD off | White; runtime log and process sample |
| Controlled pipeline-path A/B | `DM_PSO_MTL4=0`, enforced by per-title env file | `DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=0` | Same relevant settings as baseline | White; fresh runtime log and process sample |
| Later user test | Off, shown as env-file-fixed | On | Docked, MetalFX upscaling, frame buffering off, HUD off | User reports unchanged white screen; settings screenshot only |

The A/B log explicitly confirms the alternate pipeline path:

```text
[nvn-mtl] DM_PSO_MTL4=0: render pipelines are built through the MTLDevice (no bases, no pipeline archive)
```

The later screenshot confirms configured selections, not effective runtime values or the sampled wait state.
MetalFX also differs from the two logged runs, so this is not an isolated encoder-only comparison.
`DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD` controls deferred Metal encoding, not whether the NVN replay worker exists.

### Copy diagnostics

The launcher's Copy diagnostics output was not captured. Available build provenance and runtime evidence are recorded above.
No Python/.NET versions or dependency-check results are inferred.

### Game profile lines from the build log

The original build-log profile-summary lines were not supplied with these runtime captures.
Both runtime logs identify profile `0400D4201C6EA000` and main build prefix `104BCE6874603701`.
The pinned profile selects `v327680`.

### The game's log

Two complete logs were reviewed privately. Only curated, redacted evidence is included here, rather than raw logs or samples.

Both runs report:

```text
fork patches: none
build: commit not recorded, shader chain e9a97471681b, profile 0400D4201C6EA000
pipeline prewarm done: shaders 871 / render pipelines 466 / compute pipelines 8
```

The prewarm line above is condensed, not a byte-for-byte full log line.
Baseline pipeline preparation took 1.01 seconds; the Metal-4-off run took 0.51 seconds.
Neither complete log contains the earlier unsupported-language rejection.
Both report five manifest keys absent from the shader map; this alone does not identify a required missing shader.

Audio callbacks continue. The baseline reports 12,000 rendered audio frames, all silent.
Callbacks establish audio-service activity, not guest main-loop progress or audible sound.

The matching NRO loads and its init runs: hash prefix `1ec347bc9f4664b4`, size 24,764,416 bytes.
Four top-level RomFS entries match the documented nested CRA layout and do not establish missing assets.

Both logs warn that a virtual-pool mapping remains page-table-only because of host-page alignment.
That limitation is a lead, not a demonstrated cause of this hang.
The 64 GiB Mac alias reservation is expected virtual address space, not physical memory use or OOM evidence.

### Crash report

No crash. Two live process samples were checked programmatically, including all 36 call-graph threads in each.

| Capture | Guest main samples at receipt wait | NVN replay samples at condition wait | Physical footprint | Peak footprint |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline | 2,425 / 2,425 | 2,425 / 2,425 | 422.8M | 472.4M |
| Metal 4 off | 2,496 / 2,496 | 2,496 / 2,496 | 392.5M | 462.5M |

Symbolic stacks, with addresses and unrelated frames omitted:

```text
Guest main, both captures:
  nvn_queue_finish            nvn_queue.inc:250
  nvn_sync_wait               nvn_queue.inc:239
  _pthread_cond_wait
  __psynch_cvwait

NVN queue replay, both captures:
  nq_worker                  nvn_queue.inc:141
  _pthread_cond_wait
  __psynch_cvwait
```

No captured thread stack shows Metal pipeline compilation, an AGX driver wait, or `mtl_wait`.
This does not rule out earlier GPU work or establish a complete dependency cycle.

At the pinned source, line 239 waits for `nq_sync_encoded` before the physical `mtl_wait` at line 243.
For queue finish, this means waiting for logical tail-receipt publication, not yet a demonstrated physical GPU-completion wait.
Replay line 141 is the ordinary condition wait; mapped-event polling uses line 140.
Queue heads, sync snapshots, and producer receipts were not captured, so the missing dependency remains unknown.

Please advise on bounded instrumentation for queue heads, sync wait kinds, producer receipts, and publication/wakeup transitions.
The goal is to distinguish missing publication, an unresolved producer, and queue ordering without assuming a proven lock cycle.

Pinned source:
- [Queue worker and readiness checks](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/c78d7375bea9c862679ec294a6a69ff3e22e18d0/dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_queue.inc#L109-L167)
- [Queue finish and logical versus physical waits](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/c78d7375bea9c862679ec294a6a69ff3e22e18d0/dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_queue.inc#L230-L253)
- [Title profile and documented coverage](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/tree/c78d7375bea9c862679ec294a6a69ff3e22e18d0/dm/games/0400D4201C6EA000)

### Fork patches line

`fork patches: none` in both logs.
That runtime marker does not negate the disclosed local deployment-target modification or establish stock-release provenance.

### Screenshots and performance numbers

The later private screenshot shows only launch settings, not gameplay or a white game-rendering surface.
Its relevant selections are transcribed in the test table. No raw screenshot is uploaded here.
No meaningful gameplay FPS measurement is available; HUD was off.

### Related reports checked

No matching startup receipt-wait report was found in the title, title-ID, white-screen, or queue-finish searches.
- [NX2Apple #1039](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/pull/1039) covers offline NRO decoding, not this runtime wait.
- [nxnative #1246](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/issues/1246) concerns Adventure performance and textures after boot.
- [nxnative #1723](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/issues/1723) concerns an on-court GPU hang, not this sampled startup receipt wait.

### No keys, no game files

- [x] Nothing attached here contains keys, game files or data extracted from a game.

Only curated diagnostic text and public source links are included. No raw memory, register dumps, or process samples are uploaded.

</details>
title: Mario Tennis Fever (macOS): white startup screen, queue completion wait with idle replay worker

body:
### Idea

Play with phones as controllers, one player per phone. The engine side is proposed in seedds/nxnative (link below). Here the fork carries it as a patch, and the launcher gets a "Phone controllers" setting.

### Plan

- Carry the engine change as a patch (`Upstream-Status: forwarded` once the upstream PR is open). It adds `DM_NETPAD` and a Mac-only "Phone controllers" row in the settings list, off by default.
- Later, a separate PR for the launcher: the Mac's LAN address and a QR code for the companion web controller, and how many phones are connected.
- Open question: bundle the companion sender (Node) or document it as an optional separate tool. I would not bundle a Node runtime without your agreement.

### Done when

- A phone joins as its own player in a Mac game, and the controller prompt counts it.
- The setting is off by default and works from the settings window.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Design and protocol: see the upstream issue (to be linked in a comment).
- Loopback only (`127.0.0.1`), opt-in. Pads take players from `pad_slots.h`, so they work with a physical controller, `DM_KBD_PLAYER=own`, `DM_PAD_PRESS_TO_JOIN` and `DM_PAD_MERGE`.
- Tested: host unit tests, `dmhost` builds for two profiles. Not tested: a phone driving a real game, regress runs, rumble, motion, iOS.
- I am an outside contributor, so I will wait for a maintainer's yes and a milestone before opening a feature PR here.
</details>
title: Phone controllers: one player per phone

body:
Ocarina of Time reproducibly crashes during Navi's opening flight on Duo, before Link becomes controllable.
Disabling manifest prewarm and shader prefetch gets past startup, but on-demand shader loading still triggers a Metal argument-buffer assertion.
Please investigate the failing shader's compiled bindings. Related assertion: #666.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction, environment and redacted diagnostic evidence</summary>

### Game and title ID

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, `0400486024DEC000`.

### Base game and update versions

Full NUP containing the base game and update, targeting profile `0400486024DEC000`, update `v131072`.
The base display version was not recorded.

### Where it runs

iPhone or iPad (built for iPhone / iPad), NX2Apple shared iOS shell with a per-game framework.

### Device, chip and RAM

Duo, Apple A20 Pro. Physical RAM was not recorded.
The runtime identifies `Apple A20 Pro GPU`.

### macOS or iOS / iPadOS version

Runtime: Duo on iOS 27.2.
Build host: Mac with M5 Pro, macOS 26.7.1, Xcode 27.2 and Metal compiler 32023.922.
The runtime confirms host shader libraries compiled for `iphoneos` by Metal 32023.922.
A same-input build comparison against macOS 27 has not been performed. Build-host causation is unproven.

### How it was installed

NX2Apple shared shell with the built game framework and its matching game data.
The sideloading tool and version were not recorded.

### NX2Apple version

Installed shell reports `1.0`. The desktop frontend release version was not recorded.
Build context identifies upstream engine `c78d7375bea9c862679ec294a6a69ff3e22e18d0`, patch suffix `66e8bc624c49`.
The phone log records shader chain `89f44f9b6bb0`, but says the build commit was not recorded.

### What happens, and when

1. Launch this game in the shared shell with the options below.
2. Start the opening sequence and let the intro play.
3. Continue through the Great Deku Tree scene to Navi flying to find Link.
4. The app crashes at that scene, before controllable gameplay.

I reached the same scene and crashed twice after applying the startup workaround.
Only one post-workaround run has a supplied log. The second run confirms the scene reproduction, without a second trace.

The logged run ends with `SIGABRT` and `bufferIndex 0 does not identify an argument buffer`.
Its last timed frame is 18,498 at 743.23 seconds.

### What you expected

Navi's flight renders correctly, the opening finishes, and Link becomes controllable without an assertion.

### Launch options changed from the defaults

The per-game environment contains:

```text
DM_PSO_MANIFEST=off
DM_NVN_PREFETCH=0
```

Both values appear in the new boot log. Other relevant logged values:

```text
DM_PSO_MTL4=1
DM_PSO_PREBUILD=1
DM_FPS_TARGET=60
DM_FPS_HOLD=off
DM_DYNAMIC_RESOLUTION=0
DM_UPSCALER=metalfx
DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=metalfx
DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=1
```

The earlier startup-crash run used `DM_UPSCALER=game`. This was not a controlled two-switch comparison.

### Copy diagnostics

The full launcher Copy diagnostics output was not captured. Available identifiers are listed above.
The runtime records shader-input stamp `4bd48f723876` and 42,848 shader-map entries.
RomFS mounts successfully with 187,182 entries. The 12.5 GB guest address-space setup succeeds with a 9 GB application pool.

Build history includes manual Python `patch_nso.py` recovery for `main`, `subsdk0` and `sdk` after missing rewrite outputs.
This used the same pinned engine and profile. The report concerns the resulting device runtime crash.

### Game profile lines from the build log

The original build-log profile lines are unavailable in this report. The device runtime confirms the selected profile:

```text
[dm] build: commit not recorded, shader chain 89f44f9b6bb0, profile 0400486024DEC000
```

### The game's log

Curated excerpts from the supplied post-workaround runtime log follow.
Full raw logs remain private because they include container paths and memory dumps.
Omitted sections include all registers, raw memory, stack dumps and private identifiers.
The crash header below omits the raw stack-pointer address; symbolic backtrace offsets are retained.

Boot values, original lines 5, 19, 27 to 29:

```text
boot: DM_ENV_FILE_KEYS=DM_PSO_MANIFEST DM_NVN_PREFETCH
boot: DM_NVN_PREFETCH=0
boot: DM_PSO_MANIFEST=off
boot: DM_PSO_MTL4=1
boot: DM_PSO_PREBUILD=1
```

First concrete pipeline failure, original line 1209:

```text
[dm] [nvn-mtl] [RED] failed to create render pipeline (vertex 159dd3b0b888a665_b fragment ccfff02a2829b620_b): Compilation failed due to an interrupted connection: XPC_ERROR_CONNECTION_INTERRUPTED. This error occurred after multiple retries.
```

There are 159 `[RED]` lines containing `XPC_ERROR_CONNECTION_INTERRUPTED`, including ordinary and task/mesh pipeline failures.
Their relationship to the later assertion is unproven. The compiler service's reason for disconnecting is absent.

The last footprint sample is 2.20 GB, peak 2.29 GB. An earlier memory sample reports 5,986 MB memory-limit headroom.
These are sampled engine metrics, not final RSS measurements. The supplied runtime logs do not establish an out-of-memory termination.

First fatal assertion and crash header, original lines 1998 to 1999:

```text
-[_MTLFunction newArgumentEncoderWithBufferIndex:reflection:functionReflection:]:11352: failed assertion `bufferIndex 0 does not identify an argument buffer'
[dm] CRASH sig=6 addr=__pthread_kill+0x8 pc=__pthread_kill+0x8 lr=pthread_kill+0xe4
```

Symbolic fatal backtrace, original line 2012:

```text
[dm] bt: abort+0x94 err+0 <redacted>+0 MTLReportFailure+0x344 <redacted>+0xa4 shader_load+0x16e4 shader_get+0x80 prog_get+0x1cc mtl_prog_snapshot+0x1c nq_snapshot_object+0x1fc cap_rec_fields+0x56c nq_flatten+0x174 nq_flatten+0xd8 nq_flatten+0xd8 nvn_queue_submit+0xf4 dm_bigstack_ret+0 main+0x570358 main+0xdd26c0 main+0x3482ec8 sdk+0x1673d0 sdk+0x16eb58 dm_thread_enter+0x18
```

The earlier startup log hits the same assertion through `shader_load`, `warm_shader` and `warm_task`.
The post-workaround trace instead reaches `shader_load` through program snapshot and queue submission.
Neither fatal trace identifies the failing shader key, so identical assertion text does not establish identical shader identity.

### Crash report

No Apple `.ips` crash report or jetsam report was supplied. The evidence above is the runtime's fatal assertion and backtrace.

### Fork patches line

Exact fork-patches log line is not included. The build context's patch suffix is `66e8bc624c49`.

### Screenshots and performance numbers

No screenshot is attached. I observed about 60 fps at the intro/menu, then about 46 fps with Great Deku Tree visual artifacts.
These are observations from the device display, not a captured performance trace.

### Suggested investigation and related reports

- #666 reports this assertion for Persona 5 Royal in a prefetch path. This report supplies an Ocarina on-demand reproduction.
- #670 is closed and unmerged. Its prefetch workaround does not establish a fix for this on-demand failure.
- At the pinned upstream revision, `dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m:5650` creates the argument encoder when JSON-derived `rf.nb` is nonzero.
- `dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_refl.m:46` assigns route-B ABI buffer index 0.
- Please log the failing shader key, stage and selected entry immediately before encoder creation.
- Please compare the JSON binding expectation with the compiled function's reflection, including argument-buffer layout at index 0.
- Please also record function constants and specialization state. The current log cannot identify the fatal shader or prove its cause.

A fix needs validation through Navi's flight into correctly rendered, controllable Link. Title/menu success alone does not cover this failure.

### No keys, no game files

- [x] Nothing attached here contains keys, game files or data extracted from a game.

</details>
title: Ocarina of Time (iOS): reproducible argument-buffer assertion during opening Navi sequence

### Game and title ID

Xenoblade Chronicles 3 (010074F013262000), with its four DLC

### Base game and update versions

update 2.2.0 (v655360)

### Where it runs

Mac app (built for This Mac)

### Device, chip and RAM

Mac with Apple M2, 8 GB

### macOS or iOS / iPadOS version

macOS 27.2

### How it was installed

Run the app the launcher built (fullscreen, 1920x1080, a 144 Hz screen switched to 120 Hz)

### NX2Apple version

main 4ff8fee7 (local test build, 1.3.1-local), engine 81906931

### What happens, and when

In battle, and in real-time cutscenes, the picture flickers: in some frames the whole 3D scene (ground, characters, effects) is one flat colour, while the HUD on top (party gauges, damage numbers, tips) is drawn correctly. The colour differs between such frames: grey, black, dark blue, light blue or white.

30 screen captures in a row during the first battle: 6 had the flat scene, 24 were normal. Outside battle it is rarer (1 of 6 around a tip window).

The game runs at about 17 to 27 fps here (GPU 33 to 57 ms a frame).

### What you expected

Every frame shows the 3D scene.

### Launch options changed from the defaults

None for the reported runs. Diagnostic switches were added only for the investigation below.

### The game's log

```
fork patches: none
[nvn] WindowInitialize swap chain 2 textures (2 active), interval 1, first 1920x1080 format 0x25
[nvn-mtl] present snapshots off (game profile present_snap): the screen shows the game's own texture
[nvn-mtl] segmented submission: a segment is submitted between passes every 64 draws (DM_NVN_CUT, 0 = off)
[nvn-mtl] display link silent for 387 ms (active): dropping 1 queued frames not yet displayed, the game continues (stall #5; back to normal when the link returns)
[nvn-mtl] display link silent for 585 ms while active: the present thread takes drawables itself (rescue #4), the link is tried again in 24 s
[nvn-mtl] present pacing mode 1 → 0 (frame 5872)
```

No `[RED]` line matches the flicker.

### Investigation

I am investigating this now and will post what I find here.

- LNPANDY/NX2Apple#455 (bright and dark frames alternating, fixed by seedds/nxnative#1025) is a different problem: this build has that fix, and here the scene is gone, not darker.
- A pass dump of four frames (`DM_CTL` `passdump`) shows the same 277 passes in each frame. The swapchain alternates between two textures, and the 1280x720 scene texture is drawn into it the same way in every frame.
- Colour-target dumps of three frames show the swapchain and the scene texture correct.
- Next: tell whether the flat colour is already in the swapchain texture once the frame's GPU work is done, or whether the screen shows the texture before that work finished (the display link's stalls and pacing changes above). Then find the pass or the present path that causes it.

### No keys, no game files

- [x] Nothing attached here contains keys, game files or data extracted from a game.

body:
On the Builds page of a running build, the stage names were in two languages, and one was in English.

### What happened

Xenoblade Chronicles 3 (010074F013262000), Mac app, main 4ff8fee7. The launcher is set to Chinese now. Going by the names below, it was in Japanese when the build started and changed to Chinese while it ran. The list then read:

- `nx_extract のビルド`, `v655360 の抽出`, `書き換え`, `アドレス領域`, `シェーダーの分割`, `Mac シェーダー` (Japanese, the stages that started before the change)
- `Mac 主机程序`, `管线存档`, `Mac App` (Chinese, the stages that started after it)
- `check v655360 files` (English in every language)

### Expected

- All stage names follow the launcher's current language, also after a change during the build.
- The "check files" stage has a translated name.

### Cause

- `BuildStore.handleEvent` turns the script's English name into the current language once, when the stage starts (`Stage.localizedName(name, t)`), and stores only the result in `Stage.name`. A later language change does not reach it. The same happens in the older `--progress lines` form (`BuildProgress.parseStage`) and the install stages.
- The script names the stage `check <version> files` (`PROG.stage(f'check {ver} files', …)` in `build_ipa_from_nsp.py`). `localizedName` handles a version part for `extract`, `pack`, `unpack` and `… shader capture`, but not for `check … files`, and no language table has a `stage.check` key, so the name is shown as the script wrote it.

### Fix idea

- Keep the script's name in `Stage` (for example `rawName`) and localize when the row is drawn (`ProgressCard`, `ConsoleBuildsPage`, the activity bar), or localize the stored names again when the language changes.
- Add `stage.check` ("check %@ files") to all ten tables, with the `check <part> files` form in `localizedName`, and a test next to the other `localizedName` cases.
title: Builds page: stage names keep the language they started in, and "check files" is not translated

body:
The Builds page lists a build's stages as one line each: a name, a short detail and, for the running stage, its clock and bar. The player cannot see more of a stage, how long a finished stage took, or how long the whole build has left.

### Idea

- Each stage row can be expanded and collapsed:
  - **Collapsed** (as today): name, detail, the running stage's clock and bar.
  - **Expanded**: the stage's steps so far, the count with its unit (files, bytes, shaders), the time each finished step and the stage took, its summary, and the last lines of its log.
  - The running stage starts expanded, the others collapsed. A failed stage opens by itself on its error.
- Finished stages show how long they took (`3:42`), and stages the build reused say so.
- The stages to come are listed as waiting, so the player sees how many are left.
- An estimate of the whole build's remaining time, at the top of the Builds page and in the activity bar: "about 25 min left (estimate)".

### Why

- A build can run for an hour. Today the player sees only the current stage, and not whether the build is near its end.
- The details are already there but only in the log: the script's `step` events, the counts, each stage's `elapsed` and summary in `stage_end`, and `logs/*.log` in the build folder.
- A failure is easier to read and report when the stage shows its own last lines.

### Done when

- Every stage row on the Builds page can be expanded and collapsed, and shows its steps, times and log lines.
- Finished stages show their time; waiting stages are listed.
- The build shows a total remaining time when it can be estimated, and nothing (not a wrong number) when it cannot.
- Console mode's Builds page gets the same total, and expanding where it fits a controller.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Desktop rows: `ProgressCard` (`NXLauncher/ProgressCard.swift`) draws one `HStack` per stage. Console mode: `ConsoleBuildsPage.stageRow`.
- What the script sends (`--progress json`, `build_ipa_from_nsp.py`): `stage` with `k` and `n` (the stage count), `step`, `progress` (`done`, `total`, `unit`, `frac`, `eta`, `elapsed`), `stage_end` (`ok`, `summary`, `elapsed`).
- `BuildStore.handleEvent` keeps only the last step as `detail`, and writes a stage's `elapsed` into the log text only. `n` is read but no waiting stages are made from it.
- The current estimate is per stage only: `Stage.remaining(at:)`, with the checks of #934 (5 to 99 %, 30 s run, within a factor of five).
- Total estimate, an approach: remember each stage's time per game (and the size of its input) after a build. The total is the running stage's estimate plus the remembered times of the stages to come, with stages the build reuses (`fingerprint()`) left out. A game built for the first time has no total, or one from other games scaled by size, marked as rough.
- The library does not record build or stage times today (`library.json` has no such field), and the build folder keeps logs but no times.

</details>
title: Builds page: expandable stage details and an estimate of the total time left

body:
While a game builds, the library's Build game… button of every other unbuilt game is disabled. Its Rebuild pill is too. The player should be able to add the selected game to the build queue from there.

### Idea

- While a build runs, the hero of an unbuilt game shows **Add to build queue** in place of the disabled Build game….
- Rebuild (for a game built with older tools) adds to the queue during a build too.
- The game's status then says it is queued, and a second press does nothing.

### Why

- Today the only way to queue during a build is the Build page's "Build selected games…", away from the game the player is looking at.
- The queue was made for this: one game after another, without waiting at the Mac.

### Done when

- During a build, an unbuilt game's hero adds it to the queue in one press.
- A queued game shows as queued in the library.
- The queued game starts when the running build ends, whoever started it (needs #1107).

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- `LauncherView+HeroAction.heroPrimary`: the button is `.disabled(launching || (m.running && !game.isReady) || …)`. Its action, `primaryAction`, opens the build setup (`configureBuild`) for a game that is not ready.
- `heroRebuildButton` (`LauncherView+Library.swift`): enqueues only `if !m.running`, and is `.disabled(m.running || …)`.
- `BuildSelectedSheet.add()` enqueues during a build, so the queue itself allows it.
- #1107: games queued during a build that the queue did not start never start. This change would hit it often, so it should land after or with that fix.

</details>
title: Library: add the selected game to the build queue while another game builds

body:
The library already finds Switch packages in the games folders and lists them as not built. In console mode, such a game's page only offers "Open on the desktop". It could build the game, or queue it, from there.

### Idea

- On the page of a game that is not built, console mode offers:
  - **Build**, when nothing builds
  - **Add to build queue**
- "Open on the desktop" stays as a row for what console mode cannot do.

### Why

- From the couch, a game found on the drive can be built without going to the desktop.
- The scan already does the hard part: it finds `.nsp`, `.nsz`, `.xci`, `.xcz` and `.nup`, groups the base, update and DLC, and records the inputs.

### Done when

- Console mode can start a build of a scanned game or add it to the queue.
- It checks what the desktop checks first (keys saved, game files present) and says what is missing.
- The Builds page shows the build or the queued game.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Console mode: `ConsoleGamePage` shows `console.openOnDesktop` for a game that is not ready. The Builds page says builds start on the desktop (`console.builds.noneNote`).
- The queue already takes a library game as a snapshot (`QueueEntry(game:engineID:)`, `BuildQueueStore.enqueue`). Console mode could use the same.
- Seen here: a folder with three packages added in Settings > Library was scanned, and the three games showed with the filter on Owned.
- Open point: a scanned game's `outputDirectory` is its package's folder (`sourceGames(in:)`), so its Mac app is built beside the packages.
- Related: #1107 (queued games that never start).

</details>
title: Console mode: Build or Add to queue on the page of a game that is not built

body:
Every launch scans each games folder again and reads the packages' title IDs and names again. A `.nx2apple` folder in each games folder could keep what was read, so the next launch only reads new or changed files.

### Idea

- When the library scans a games folder, it writes a hidden `.nx2apple/` folder there.
- It keeps, per package (`.nsp`, `.nsz`, `.xci`, `.xcz`, `.nup`): the file's name, size and modification time, its title ID, the game's names and its icon or cover.
- On the next launch, or when the library opens, a file with the same name, size and time is taken from there without reading it.
- Only new or changed files are read. Settings > Rescan still reads everything.

### Why

- Today `Library.discover()` runs at every start. It walks each root, and a package whose name has no title ID is read through its NCA headers (#1012). Names without a profile are read by the engine's extractor, once per launch (`TitleNameLookup`).
- Large folders on an external drive make this slow, and the same work repeats each time.
- The cache travels with the drive: another Mac, or the launcher after a reinstall, sees the games at once.

### Done when

- A second launch with no changed files reads no package.
- A changed, added or removed file is noticed and only that file is read.
- A folder that cannot be written (read-only drive) still works, with today's scan.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Scan: `Library.discover()` from `LauncherView` on start, on a change of the saved keys, and Settings > Rescan. `sourceGames(in:)` walks four levels and reads title IDs with `PackageTitleID.Resolver`.
- Today's results live in `library.json` and `artwork/<title ID>.jpg` under `~/Library/Application Support/NS Port Builder`. They are per Mac, and the scan does not use them to skip files.
- Open points: a file format with a version number; never keys or game data in the cache, only IDs, names and the picture; the folder hidden, and ignored by the scan itself.

</details>
title: Library: keep each games folder's scan in a .nx2apple folder, so the next launch does not read every package again

body:
The launcher's notices are silent: a finished or failed build, a controller that connects or leaves. From the couch in console mode, or in another app, they are easy to miss. Short sounds would tell them apart without looking.

### Idea

- A short sound for each kind of notice:
  - build finished, build failed
  - controller connected, controller disconnected
  - maybe: the build queue done, a transfer to a device done
- Success and failure sound different, so the player knows without reading.
- One switch "Sounds for notices" in Settings and on console mode's General page, on by default.

### Why

- Today only the system notification of a build plays a sound, and only when Notification Center allows it. Console mode's banners (#1004) make no sound.
- Console mode is used from a distance, where a banner is easy to miss.

### Done when

- Each kind above plays its sound once, also while the launcher is in front.
- The switch turns all of them off.
- No sound plays while a game runs, and a build notice does not play twice (its own sound and the notification's).

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Build notices: `BuildNotifier.post` sets `content.sound = .default` (`BuildNotifications.swift`). #1100 shows the banner and its sound while the launcher is in front too.
- Console notices: `LiveConsoleDriver.showToast` through `ConsoleNoticeQueue` (`ConsoleNotices.swift`), for example `console.connected` and `console.disconnected` in `LiveConsoleDriver.swift`. None plays a sound.
- Sounds: macOS system sounds (`NSSound(named:)`, for example Glass and Basso) need no new files and no license. Own sounds would need to be original.
- A game started from console mode already hides the notices while it starts. The same rule can hold for sounds.

</details>
title: Launcher: sounds for notices (build finished or failed, controller connected or gone)

body:
After an engine update that changes only the Mac host (for example #952's Home menu, patch 0122), every built game must be rebuilt from its game files to get it. The launcher could refresh just the host in the built app.

### Idea

- A built Mac app holds two parts: the game (translated code `Resources/dm/*.patched.bin`, shaders `msl/`, `romfs.img`) and the host (`MacOS/dmhost`, `MacOS/nxnative`), which draws the in-game menus.
- When the new engine changes only the host, offer "Update in-game menus" for games built with older tools. It rebuilds `dmhost` for the game, replaces it in the app and signs it again. No game files and no keys are needed.
- When the game part changed too, keep "Build again" as now.

### Why

- A full rebuild needs the game files and keys, and the library may no longer point to them.
- The host is built from the engine and the game's profile, not from the game files. In a Balatro build here, the "Mac host" stage took 1 s.
- The build script already reuses the rewrite and shader stages when their inputs are unchanged, but only while the game files are there.

### Done when

- The launcher can tell a host-only engine change from one that changes the game part.
- A host-only refresh updates a built app without its game files, and the game starts with the new menu.
- "Built with different tools" goes away after the refresh.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- `dmhost` is built per game: `make -C dm/host GAME=<title ID> dmhost` (`build_mac_host` in `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py`). Two games' hosts differ even without their signatures (the title ID and tables are in it), so one shared binary is not enough.
- Stage reuse: `fingerprint()` keys each stage on its own tool files (`tool_files`), not on the engine commit. A change under `dm/host` leaves the rewrite and shader keys as they were.
- Open question for the engine: whether a host change can break the interface to the translated code. The refresh should run only when the engine marks the change as host-only, or when the stage keys match.
- Seen with main 4ff8fee7, Balatro (0100CD801CE5E000) built on 2026-11-08: its `dmhost` has none of patch 0122, so a short press of Home does nothing.

</details>
title: Built Mac games: update only the host (in-game menus) after an engine update, without the game files

body:
### This is

A problem

### What happens, or what you would like

Games added to the build queue while a build runs never start once that build ends. The queue is not paused, but it waits forever.

Steps:
1. Start a game's build with Build (not from the queue).
2. While it runs, add three games with "Select games".
3. The first build fails, or press Stop.
4. Nothing starts. The queue shows three waiting games and no Resume button.

Restarting the launcher brings the "queue from before the restart" prompt, which works around it.

### What you expected

When any build ends, the next queued game starts. After Stop, the queue pauses and offers Resume, as it does for a build the queue started.

### NX2Apple version

1.3.1-local, built from main 4ff8fee7 (after #1097) with `tools/try-local`

### Computer and OS

MacBook Air M2 (Mac14,2), 8 GB, macOS 27.2

### Copy diagnostics

Not attached. The queue file is enough here (below).

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- `build-queue.json` after step 4: `paused: false`, three entries `queued`, none `running`. The first game is not in the queue.
- `LauncherStores.init`, `queueWatch`: when `build.running` turns false, it calls `queue.buildEnded` only if `queue.running != nil`. A build the queue did not start leaves `queue.running` nil, so nothing calls `processNext()`.
- `BuildQueueStore.enqueue` calls `processNext()`, which returns while `busy()` is true. So games added during a build only start if something calls `processNext()` later.
- A build the queue started works: `buildEnded` runs `processNext()`, and Stop sets `paused` with Resume on the Build page.
- Console mode's Builds page lists the queue but shows no paused state and no Resume.

</details>

### No keys, no game files

- [x] Nothing attached here contains keys, game files or data extracted from a game.
title: Build queue: games queued during a build that the queue did not start never start

body:
Console mode has no click-to-select, and the home rows ignore the mouse wheel and dragging. Some pointer input should stay, also for a DualSense touchpad later.

### Idea

- A click or tap on a game tile selects it first: the focus ring moves to it. A second click on the selected tile opens it.
- The mouse wheel or a trackpad scroll moves between the home rows, as up and down on the pad do.
- Dragging up or down on the rows does the same.

### Why

- Today the first click opens the game page at once. With a touch screen or a trackpad you cannot look at a game first.
- Only the focused row and the start of the next one are drawn. A scroll or a drag cannot reach the other rows.
- A DualSense touchpad used as a pointer would need the same select-then-open rule.

### Done when

- One click selects, a second click on the same tile opens. A or X on a controller works as now.
- A scroll or a drag of one step moves one row up or down.
- Tests cover both.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- `ConsoleHomeView.tile`: the button's action is `driver.focus(id)` then `openGamePage` (or `resume` for a paused game) in one step. It was the same before #1097: the first click started the game.
- `ConsoleHomeView.rows`: the rows draw from the focused one down (`sections.dropFirst(focusedIndex)`), clipped to one row and the start of the next. The outer vertical `ScrollView` only scrolls in a short window. So a wheel or drag cannot change rows. The horizontal scroll inside a row works with a trackpad.
- Seen on main at 4ff8fee7 (after #1097), built with `tools/try-local`, macOS 27.2, Apple silicon.

</details>
title: Console mode: a click selects a tile first, and the mouse wheel moves between rows

body:
## Proposal

A unified **per-game Options + effective configuration + preparation/ready** flow for Mac game launch, using existing engine/frontend setting metadata wherever possible. This is a UX/integration proposal informed by a working local OoT prototype, not a request to expose every diagnostic switch or a claim these changes are already in released NX2Apple.

Related: #929 (OoT findings), #1092 (monitor selection), #1086 (controller mapping diagrams), #1089 (motion controls), and [the runtime findings](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/issues/1987). This should complement those proposals and the current settings screens, not duplicate their implementation.

## Player problem

Our M2 Max player repeatedly needed to ask which app/options were current, whether window size meant internal rendering resolution, whether a pause meant the GPU was too slow or a new pipeline was compiling, and whether changes would invalidate preparation. Button actions worked while sprinting failed because actual stick travel did not reach the advertised range. A single clear pre-play view helped make the local build understandable and usable.

The player is continuing to play and reports much smoother results. This is local `eed7c4295853` + changes / chain `8aca4f744799`, macOS 26.6.2, Xcode 27.2, OoT v131072, **not current-main or released-frontend validation**.

## Proposed sections

| Section | Settings to surface | Important distinction |
|---|---|---|
| Display | Window/fullscreen, logical window size, monitor, optional performance HUD | Display/window size is not the game's internal rendering resolution. Reuse #1092's stable display UUID and canonical `DM_SCREEN` behavior; our local numeric-ID prototype is not the preferred production implementation. |
| Graphics | 30 / experimental 60 target, supported docked/handheld mode, independent optional edge smoothing, explicit presets | Show exactly which values a preset changes. Handheld may lower quality; a target is not guaranteed achieved FPS. |
| Controller | Per-model mapping, live button/stick values, deadzone/response, guided range calibration | Show whether input is GameController or raw HID. Preserve full travel and distinguish L/R, ZL/ZR, Minus/Plus and stick clicks. Tie calibration to that device; complement #1086/#1089 rather than replace them. |
| Audio/loading | Game output volume; optional loading background/music, mute/volume | Original/user-supplied assets; no dependency on redistributing game artwork/music. Respect mute; stop loading music when play begins. |
| Preparation | Supported mapped-compute coverage, recorded render/native coverage, bounded workers, cache status | Never describe render bases, shader libraries or all mapped compute as “every pipeline is ready.” Unknown state combinations and texture streaming remain possible. |
| Advanced experiments | Only reviewed per-game/per-build options, reversible and visibly experimental | Our fog/local-shadow/blur prototype uses diagnostic omissions, **not** validated production quality controls. Do not enable these by default or copy them to unrelated games. |

Only show options supported by the packaged engine/game. Several behaviors above are local additions, so capability/version checks are essential. Avoid asking users to paste local-only `DM_*` values into a release that does not implement them.

## Proposed flow and settings summary

1. Open Options before preparation; show remembered choices plus **effective value and source** (default, preset, saved choice, game profile, explicit environment override). Existing environment precedence should remain visible and honored.
2. Apply commits atomically; Cancel changes nothing. A compact “Changes” summary shows old → new values and explains image-quality and preparation implications. Keep per-game settings separate from per-controller calibration.
3. **Prepare & Play** snapshots the effective settings and begins preparation. Show progress, cache reuse, engine commit, shader-chain/game-build identity and separate compute/render/native counts. Avoid blind “clear cache” advice.
4. At completion, present **Press A to continue**, with mouse/keyboard alternatives. Ignore A held before ready; do not leak confirmation into the game. A short cached startup should not flash or briefly play music unexpectedly.
5. Options changed at the ready screen trigger the required preparation again **before gameplay**. The prototype restarts the process to guarantee startup-only settings take effect; production can use its own coordinated restart mechanism. Active gameplay/save transactions must not be interrupted by editing launch choices.
6. Provide Restore defaults and a small **Copy effective settings** report with versions, selected/effective values and coverage. Exclude keys, game paths, saves and raw cache payloads by default.

## Prototype evidence and limits

The local AppKit prototype has six sections, remembered Apply/Cancel behavior, original loading artwork/quiet synthesized music, and a ready gate. UI checks cover persistence/Cancel isolation, preset environment handoff, calibration preservation and fresh-A/held-A logic; audio/HID and documentation checks pass. A synthetic host handoff verifies relative paths and isolated saves. This supports the flow, not a finished cross-device frontend implementation.

All 4,125 mapped compute pipelines are prepared locally. Latest observed coverage is 4,437 ordinary render states and 201 native states. Newly encountered native pipelines still took ~6–7 seconds in a completed play session, so counts and limitations need to be honest. Existing automatic state recording already makes future launches better; users should not need manual manifest merging after every session.

Experimental local effects reductions felt faster to the player, but we have no matched GPU benchmark for them. They can remove shared effects or leave incomplete shadows. Dust, SSAO and screen-space/volumetric compute were not disabled. These experiments are feedback for designing a capability-gated Advanced section, not production-ready quality presets.

There is no whole-game, locked-60-FPS or second-Mac clean-install claim. No game data, keys, compiled game shaders, GPU archives, personal saves or raw logs are attached. The companion installer remains private; this proposal shares the UX/technical lessons without publishing it. Prepared with Codex assistance and the player's ongoing feedback.

## Suggested acceptance checks

- Selected values, effective values and override source agree with the actual launched process.
- Unsupported options are absent/disabled with an explanation; canonical upstream setting metadata is reused.
- Preset diffs, Apply/Cancel and restore-default behavior are tested; calibration is not overwritten by a graphics preset.
- Changed startup settings cannot silently bypass required preparation.
- A held confirm button cannot skip loading or become an unintended in-game action.
- No game assets or private key/save data are needed for the UI tests or settings export.
title: Mac launch Options: effective-settings summary and preparation/ready flow — OoT prototype findings

### Idea

A setting in the Mac launcher for the display a game opens on. Today the game always opens on the launcher window's screen. With several screens, players cannot send a game to the TV or the monitor they want without moving the launcher first.

### Plan

- Settings → General: **Display**, with "Same as the launcher" (today's behavior, the default) and one row per connected screen, by name.
- Store the screen's UUID (`CGDisplayCreateUUIDFromDisplayID`), not its number: the number changes when a screen is plugged in again.
- At launch, resolve the UUID to today's number and pass it as `DM_SCREEN`. The engine already moves the window there before fullscreen.
- A missing screen falls back to the launcher's screen.
- Optional: a switch for "Change the refresh rate in fullscreen" (`DM_SCREEN_MATCH=0` when off), for setups like #1085.

### Done when

- A game opens and goes fullscreen on the chosen screen.
- Unplugging that screen falls back without an error.
- No engine change is needed.
title: Mac: choose the display a game opens on

body:
### Idea

The on-screen controls can be moved and resized (`DM_TOUCH_LAYOUT`, `DM_TOUCH_SIZE`, `DM_TOUCH_STICK`), but three things players ask for in other ports are missing:

- **Opacity.** The controls draw at a fixed opacity (`dm/ios/Sources/DmGamepad.m`), so they cover the picture in dark scenes or are hard to see in bright ones.
- **A floating left stick.** The stick sits where it was placed. A stick that appears where the thumb lands is easier on a large phone and on an iPad.
- **Holding ZL / ZR.** Games that want a trigger held for a long time (aiming, running) tire the finger. S2Arm locks ZL / ZR after a 2-second hold and unlocks them with a tap: [jhaizhou-ops/S2Arm#77](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/S2Arm/pull/77). Its on-screen controls were redone in [jhaizhou-ops/S2Arm#134](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/S2Arm/pull/134). We take the problems, not the code (Apache-2.0).

### Plan

- Opacity for all controls, then per control in the layout editor, saved with the layout.
- A **Floating** choice beside the stick's positions.
- Hold to lock for ZL and ZR, off by default, with a visible locked state.
- The drawing is in the engine's iOS front end, so each part goes to seedds/nxnative as a pull request and lands here as a patch, as usual.

### Done when

- The three options work in the iOS shell on an iPhone and an iPad, and the layout editor shows them.
- Players who change nothing see the controls as today.
title: Touch controls: opacity, a floating left stick, and hold to lock ZL / ZR

body:
### Idea

The engine has switches for motion: `DM_MOTION=0` turns live motion off, `DM_MOTION_AXES` and `DM_MOTION_ACC_SIGN` map the axes, `DM_MOTION_GAIN` sets the tilt correction, and `DM_MOTION_HID` reads a Pro Controller's IMU over HID (`dm/host/hle_hid.c`). None of them is in the launcher. A player whose pad turns the camera by itself, or whose gyro reads on the wrong axis, has to write `env.txt` by hand.

Reports here show the need: #971 (gyro stopped after v1.3.0) and #914 (no motion from an 8BitDo Ultimate 2). Upstream has the same request with a reproducible case, where looking up also turns the camera sideways: seedds/nxnative#1941.

### Plan

- A **Motion** section in a game's controller options, on the Mac and in the iOS shell: on / off, the axes as a small choice of the usual mappings (not free text), and the gain.
- Show where player 1's motion comes from: GameController, HID, or none. That answers most "no gyro" reports without a log.
- The values go to the game as the `DM_MOTION*` variables. Our own button mapping stays as it is; this only adds motion.
- If upstream adds motion rows to `dm/games/settings.tsv`, use those instead of our own rows.

### Done when

- Motion can be turned off and its axes changed without editing `env.txt`, on the Mac and on iOS.
- The source of motion is shown for a connected pad.
- Tests cover the variables written for each choice.
title: Motion settings in the launcher: on or off, axes, gain, and where motion comes from

body:
### Idea

A game has one save tree. Two people on one Mac or one iPad, or two playthroughs, share it. In-game slots help for progress, but shared files such as `option.sav` or `account.sav` still collide. Today the only way is to rename folders by hand while the game is closed.

The engine already reads the save folder from `DM_SAVE` (`dm/host/hle_fs.c`), so the launcher can point a game at another folder without an engine change. The same request is open upstream: seedds/nxnative#1748.

### Plan

- A **Save profile** row in a game's options (Mac launcher, iOS shell): pick a profile, add, rename, delete. The default profile is today's folder, so nothing moves for anyone who never opens the row.
- Each other profile is a folder beside the default one; Play sets `DM_SAVE` to it.
- Cloud saves (#957, #864) and save import / export (#411) work on the chosen profile, and say which one.
- Deleting a profile asks first and keeps a copy in the Trash, like the save-keeping game deletion.

### Not in this issue

- More than one user account inside the game (the engine has one fixed `Uid`). That is an engine change and belongs upstream.

### Done when

- Two profiles of one game keep separate saves on the Mac and on the iPad, and switching needs no file work.
- A player who never uses profiles sees no change in where saves are.
- Tests cover the folder for each profile, renaming, and the cloud-save folder per profile.
title: Save profiles: more than one save per game, by pointing DM_SAVE at a profile folder

body:
### Idea

A free Apple ID can register at most 10 App IDs in 7 days. Past that, signing fails with Apple's error 9120, and the launcher shows it like any other signing failure. Nothing says that the limit is the cause, that waiting a few days or using a paid team fixes it, or that rebuilding will not help. Every rebuild with a new bundle ID even brings the next failure closer.

S2Arm, which started from this launcher, gives this case its own error code and its own message on the Mac and on Windows: [jhaizhou-ops/S2Arm@6b14d3d7fb](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/S2Arm/commit/6b14d3d7fb) and [a0f2434b53](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/S2Arm/commit/a0f2434b53), released in [v0.2.1](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/S2Arm/releases/tag/v0.2.1). We take the problem, not their code (Apache-2.0).

### Plan

- Recognise 9120 (and Apple's wording around it) in the output of `xcodebuild` / the signing step, in `ShellInstall` and in the Qt launcher.
- A failure row of its own: the free Apple ID's limit of 10 App IDs in 7 days was reached; when the oldest one frees up, if it is known; a paid team has no such limit; rebuilding now does not help.
- The shared app uses one App ID for all games, so name it as the way to stay under the limit.

### Done when

- A signing log with 9120 gives that row on the Mac and on Windows, in every launcher language.
- Tests cover the classifier with a real 9120 log excerpt and with a log that only looks similar.
title: Install: say when a free Apple ID has used its 10 App IDs in 7 days (Apple error 9120)

body:
### Idea

The mapping screens draw one controller for every pad: `ConsolePadDiagram` in console mode on the Mac and `XboxControllerDiagram` on iPhone are both an Xbox-shaped outline. A PlayStation, Switch Pro or phone-clip controller (Backbone, Kishi, GameSir G8 and the like, with the phone in the middle) looks nothing like it, so the user has to translate "the button at this place" onto their own pad before they can change a mapping.

Instead, keep a list of mainstream controllers plus a few standard layouts, match the connected controller against it, and draw the diagram of that controller. Remapping then happens on a picture of the pad in your hands.

This is a long-term UI idea, not for a current milestone. It is written down here so it is not lost.

### Plan

1. **A controller list.** Each entry names a family and the layout to draw:
   - Mainstream pads: Xbox (incl. Elite paddles), DualShock 4, DualSense / DualSense Edge, Switch Pro, Joy-Con pair, common phone-clip pads.
   - Standard layouts as a fallback: Xbox-style, PlayStation-style, Nintendo-style (A/B swapped places), split phone-clip, generic.
   - Matching: vendor and product ID where the Mac sees them (IOKit HID), `GCController.productCategory` / `vendorName` and the `GCExtendedGamepad` subclass elsewhere. An unknown pad falls back to the standard layout its buttons fit, and the user can pick another one by hand.
2. **Per-controller 2D diagrams** in the existing style (outline, Switch names, rings for changed buttons, tap to open a row), so the current mapping flow keeps working with each shape.
3. **Extras a controller has:**
   - PlayStation: the light bar colour (`GCDeviceLight`) and the touchpad (`touchpadButton`, `touchpadPrimary` / `touchpadSecondary`) shown and mappable.
   - Back paddles (Xbox Elite, DualSense Edge, pads that expose them) drawn on a back view and mappable.
4. **Later, a 3D view.** Models made in Blender for the mainstream pads, as close to 1:1 as practical, exported to USDZ and shown with RealityKit / SceneKit:
   - The model follows the controller's gyro (`GCMotion`) and can also be turned freely by hand, so back paddles and triggers are easy to reach.
   - Gyro and stick settings get a live view on the model: stick deadzones (see #1025) as the shaded area round each stick, gyro movement as the model's rotation.
   - The models are drawn by us. No meshes or textures taken from manufacturers or other apps.

### Done when

- A connected controller from the list shows its own diagram in the mapping screen on Mac console mode and on iOS, and an unknown one shows the closest standard layout with a way to switch.
- A phone-clip controller shows the split layout, with the phone's place in the middle.
- PlayStation pads show the light bar and touchpad, and paddles can be mapped where the controller exposes them.
- (Later) the 3D view rotates with the gyro and by hand, and shows deadzones and gyro settings live.
title: Controller mapping: draw the connected controller (per-model diagrams, PlayStation light bar and touchpad, later a 3D model that follows the gyro)

Idea — Linux as a platform for the launcher and the engine

**This issue is written on DannyBaanks' behalf by Step 5, an AI assistant made by StepFun. He is answering through me and asked me to say so explicitly, so I will: he filed this issue through an AI pair programmer, and all of the work described below was done with AI assistance under his direction, on his own machine. Nothing here is hidden and he does not want it to be. He stands behind it fully — audit anything you want: the code, the patches, the measurements, the commit history. He is happy to fix whatever you find, and to redo any part of it in whatever shape you prefer.**

## What I would like, and the design note this form asks for

The launcher (`frontend-qt/`) is Python and Qt and is already cross-platform for Windows and macOS, so Linux is a small, honest change there. The engine (`seedds/nxnative` plus `patches/`) is where the work is, and the repository's own seams make it possible without rewriting the host:

1. **The launcher on Linux (M1).** Venv path, file-manager calls (`FileManager1`, then `xdg-open`), tool discovery, and the dependency panel renamed to the Linux tools (`zstd` required, `spirv-cross` and `glslangValidator` optional). Three platform-independent bugs were found and fixed on the way, all of which were bugs on macOS too: the children ran with the machine's locale (an English log pattern could not match a Spanish `strerror`), the ASCII temp folder created `C:\Windows\Temp` on Linux, and a deferred-check timer raced a test. Test suite: 438 tests green on Linux.

2. **The host's service layer on Linux (M2/M3).** One patch adds a stand-in layer under `dm/host/linux/` (the same shape as the repository's existing shims) that answers the Apple interfaces the host takes: Mach VM and threads over `/proc/self/mem`, `mmap` and `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`, GCD over threads, the Mach-O section lookup over the host's own ELF sections. What has no Linux equivalent is reported instead of pretended (`vm_remap` is a copy, another thread's registers are not readable, the instruction counters read zero). A second patch makes it two runtimes: `ARCH=aarch64` and `ARCH=x86_64` both build static ELFs, `run-linux --mode qemu` runs the ARM64 host under `qemu-aarch64-static`, `--mode native` runs the machine's own host with no emulator and no silent fallback to one. The x86_64 host loads, relocates and inspects the game's ARM64 modules and stops where their code would start with exit 86, because the engine has no instruction-set translation and none was added. `tools/engine.py check` applies all 71 patches cleanly.

3. **Already running past M3, kept out of the PR until the go:** the audio service (`nn::audio AudioOut`) over ALSA straight through the kernel interface, no alsa-lib, the ELF stays static; and the input layer over evdev, same reasoning (no SDL, no X11 dependency). Both are measured on a real machine, both have tests, and both keep the "report instead of pretend" rule of the stand-in layer.

## The alternatives considered, and why they were not chosen

- **Link alsa-lib / SDL2 / X11 dynamically instead.** It is what most projects do, and it would be less code. It breaks the port's one hard rule: a static ELF runs on any Linux of the same architecture with nothing installed. The kernel interfaces (ALSA ioctl, evdev) are small and stable, so the same behaviour is reachable with no dependency at all. Where a library is unavoidable (a window system), the fallback is a headless front end that already exists and is honest about what it does.
- **Wayland instead of KMS for the surface.** Wayland is the future but needs a compositor and a different surface path; KMS/DRM gives full-screen video with the same ioctl style and works on a Raspberry Pi as-is. The front-end seam (`dm/host/front.h`) keeps both open, so the choice is not locked in.
- **x86_64 with an ARM64-to-x86 JIT.** A project of its own, the size of the graphics port again. Not for a first version.
- **Port the graphics layer to Vulkan in the same PR.** It is the biggest and least certain piece (the Metal backend is ~15k lines and builds every pool as a zero-copy buffer, which a discrete GPU cannot honour). It belongs in its own issue and its own PR, behind the headless harness.

## What I expect to happen next, following CONTRIBUTING.md

- This issue decides the go and the milestone (this is the "Fixes, features and ideas" form, marked as an idea).
- PR #1073 stays open, unreviewed, until the go is here. It already contains M1, the two engine patches and the plan page; if the maintainers prefer, it can be split into a small Qt-only PR plus the engine parts going to `seedds/nxnative` first, exactly as the note in the PR says.
- The engine patches (0106/0107) go upstream to `seedds/nxnative` first, as "Helping with games" asks, and the repository's series picks them up from there.

**Computer and OS:** Ubuntu 24.04, x86_64, with a HDA NVidia card on HDMI and an eDP panel (KMS accessible); an ARM64 machine is not available, which is why the guest's own code has not been run yet — that limit is stated in the PR body and in the plan page, not glossed over.

**NX2Apple version:** the fork on `main` at `51ca125b` (engine at its pin, 71 patches).

Nothing attached contains keys, game files or data extracted from a game. No keys or game files are included in this issue.
title: Idea: Linux as a platform — the launcher and the engine

body:
### Idea

The Mac launcher has no single place that shows a game's save. Today it is spread over three places:

- **Manage › Saves…** copies a save between this Mac and an iPhone or iPad (#66).
- **Launch options › Cloud saves** sets one game's cloud saves folder (#499).
- Where the save lives on disk is decided without a word by the library marker: beside the app in `<folder>/save/<title ID>` when the app's folder holds `.nx2apple-library`, else in `~/Library/Application Support/nxnative/<title ID>/save`.

#1041 shows the cost. A player moved one game's app into a subfolder. Its save stayed in `~/Library` while another game saved beside its app, and finding out took `ls -la` in Terminal. Nothing in the launcher says where a save is, when it was last written, or whether it syncs.

### Plan

A **Saves** page in the Mac launcher with every built Mac game in one list:

- Each row has the game's name and artwork, the folder its save is in and what put it there (library folder, default location, an env.txt line), the date of the newest save file, and its size.
- Each row has a **cloud saves switch**, one click. On uses the cloud folder for every game (#864: iCloud Drive › nxnative Saves, or NX2Apple Saves when the iPhone app already shares it). Off turns them off as Launch options › Cloud saves does today (`GameCloudSaves`). The row shows the last session's sync from the log (`CloudSaveSync.state`), and a game with its own folder keeps it.
- At the top, **Cloud saves for every game** and its folder (#864), so a player can turn on iCloud for everything at once.
- Row actions: **Show in Finder**, **Saves…** (the existing Mac ↔ iPhone sheet) and **Backups** when there are any.
- A note on a row whose save is not where its app is, as in #1041, so a moved app is visible.

It reads what the launcher already reads (`SaveTransfer.macSave`, `CloudSaveSync.resolve`, `GameCloudSaves`) and writes only what Launch options already writes. No engine change, so games built before it work without a rebuild. Moving saves to another folder stays with #864. Console mode gets the page after its redesign (#901).

### Done when

- Every built Mac game is in the list with its real save folder, newest save date and cloud state.
- One click turns a game's cloud saves on or off, with the same result as Launch options › Cloud saves, and the switch for every game does the same for all of them.
- Tests cover the list's data and the switch. The PR has before and after screenshots in English and Chinese.

Related: #864, #957, #1041, #499, #411, #907.
title: Idea: a Saves page in the Mac launcher, every game's save at a glance with a cloud saves switch

body:
### Idea

With a paid team, `org.nxnative.shell` is registered to another team. A new iPhone / iPad install of the shared app tries that identifier first, fails to sign, and only then retries under `org.nxnative.shell.<team>` (#392, #839). Every new install with a paid team pays for one failing sign.

A new install (no `shell.json` yet) could start directly with `org.nxnative.shell.<team>` when a team is selected.

### Plan

- In `ShellInstaller.install`, when `shell.json` does not exist yet and a team is selected, start with `ShellLibrary.teamVariant(team:)` and not `org.nxnative.shell`.
- Keep the stored identifier as it is for existing installs: the app's Documents (game data, saves) belong to it.
- Decide what a free Apple ID gets. It may not be able to register a new identifier at all, so it may need to keep `org.nxnative.shell`.

This changes the default bundle ID for everyone who installs for the first time, so it needs a maintainer's go before a PR.

### Done when

- A first install with a paid team signs once, under `org.nxnative.shell.<team>`.
- An existing install keeps its stored identifier.
- Tests cover a first install, an existing install, and a team without a paid membership.
title: Shared app: start a new install with the team's bundle ID
