## What happens

When the Build tab target selector sits on `mac-app` with a game chosen in the form, running a standalone iOS action from the Library or Settings tab (`resignOnDevice`, `reinstallOnDevice`, `saveIPA`, `sendGameData`, `copyToDrive`, or `confirmShellMove`) sets `BuildStore.running = true` while `target` is `mac`. As a result:

1. `LauncherView.activityBar` and `BuildPage` read `m.target == BuildTarget.mac` and display `Mac build in progress` during an iPhone operation.
2. `BuildRecorder` and `LauncherView` treat `m.running` as a full game build, calling `library.rememberInputs(m)` and showing the `BUILDING` badge on the unrelated game sitting in the Build form.

## Expected behavior

Standalone iOS operations should report `runningTarget == BuildTarget.ios` while active without mutating the Build form's `target` picker or marking the Build form's game as `BUILDING`, and restore `runningTarget` to `target` once finished.
title: Standalone iOS re-sign or reinstall shows 'Mac build in progress' and marks the Build form's game as BUILDING when target sits on mac-app

body:
## What happens

When an iPhone game installed in the shared app (`DmShell.app`) is re-signed from the Library tab before its current 7-day free Apple ID provisioning profile has completely expired (for example with 5 or 6 days left), `xcodebuild -allowProvisioningUpdates` reuses the unexpired cached `.mobileprovision` in `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/UserData/Provisioning Profiles/` (or `~/Library/MobileDevice/Provisioning Profiles/`) instead of requesting a new 7-day profile from Apple. As a result, `DmShell.app/embedded.mobileprovision` keeps its old `ExpirationDate` and the hero countdown stays at the old day count.

## Expected behavior

Clicking Re-sign should temporarily stage the app's existing `embedded.mobileprovision`, `_CodeSignature`, and matching cached provisioning profiles for that bundle ID and team so `xcodebuild -allowProvisioningUpdates` requests and embeds a fresh 7-day profile, rolling back cleanly if `xcodebuild` fails.
title: Re-sign button on a free Apple ID reuses the cached provisioning profile instead of renewing for 7 days

body:
## Historical local test-order hang (requested from #555)
On 2026-11-03, the following pair hung both on the offline-import branch and a clean detached upstream checkout at 8e1a26fa. The library test/class passed alone.

### Reproduction used

git checkout 8e1a26fa
cd frontend
PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH" swift test --filter "LauncherControlWidthTests.testEveryRowControlOnTheRealPagesFitsInEveryLanguage|LibraryTests.testCompletedBuildAppearsAutomaticallyInCollection"

### Actual macOS sample excerpts preserved in diagnostic history
Pristine upstream process sampled with: sample 92812 1 -file /tmp/nx2apple-pristine-hang.sample.txt

	a) line 24: Dispatch Thread Soft Limit: 70 reached in 680 of 680 samples -- too many dispatch threads blocked in synchronous operations
	b) line 99: 680 LibraryTests.testCompletedBuildAppearsAutomaticallyInCollection() ... LibraryTests.swift:617
	c) line 104: 680 SystemProcessRunner.capture(_:) ... ProcessRunner.swift:132

A separate sample of the same test-order failure included repeated AppKit worker stacks:

    _dispatch_worker_thread2
    _dispatch_root_queue_drain
    _dispatch_client_callout
    _dispatch_call_block_and_release
    -[NSAnimation _runBlocking] + 416
    -[NSRunLoop(NSRunLoop) runMode:beforeDate:]
    __CFRunLoopRun
    mach_msg2_trap

The main stack reached process capture through Toolchain.dotnetRoot. This suggests synchronous work/animation workers are relevant, but is NOT an established root cause. Dedicated stderr-thread and window/spinner-teardown experiments did not resolve the full flow and were reverted. The diagnostic process was terminated after sampling; no hooks were bypassed.

### Evidence limits / current status
The full temporary sample file no longer exists; the excerpts above were recovered verbatim from recorded tool results, not a newly captured/full attachment. I cannot supply the missing complete original sample. Exact historical OS/Xcode versions were not retained in the recovered excerpts.

This is a historical report, **not a current-main regression claim**. On 2026-11-09, the #555 branch rebased onto e0ce357 and synchronized to its engine pin passed the full required local hook suite (923 Swift tests, 34 skipped, zero failures). Thus the old hang did not block that run. I am filing separately as requested so its history is not misattributed to the offline feature; happy for this to be closed as no longer reproducible if the current suite is sufficient.

Related discussion: https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/pull/555

body:
### Idea

Make Switch 2 controllers work in Mac games. seedds/nxnative added Bluetooth LE support for them on 2026-11-09 (a342d6401af8, rumble in 8c436e330adf). Both are ahead of the current pin, so a bump will bring that code here.

The bump will not connect it, though. Upstream calls it from `dm/host/front_mac.m`, and patch 0081 moves the controller code from there into `controllers_mac.m`, a file upstream does not have. I tried a bump to upstream main (9983d659e610) in a scratch clone: 13 patches conflict, among them 0074 and 0081 in `front_mac.m`, and the state upstream's code uses there (`g_slots`, `g_merge`) now lives in `controllers_mac.m`.

I connected it in `controllers_mac.m` on my Mac (about 40 lines, plus a small merge in `haptics_apple.m`) and played with it.

### Tested

- Apple M6, macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27.2
- The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, `0400486024DEC000`, v131072, on pin c78d7375 with upstream's two commits added
- Pro Controller 2: pairing with Sync, buttons and sticks, rumble. Upstream's rumble commit lists only Joy-Con 2 as checked, so this adds a Pro Controller 2 result.
- The connection timed out once during play. The controller came back without restarting the game.
- `t_switch2` passes (104 checks).
- Not tested: Joy-Con 2, motion in a game, press to join, iOS.

### Plan

1. Two `backport` patches for those upstream commits, without their `front_mac.m` changes.
2. One `fork-only` patch that connects it in `controllers_mac.m`, since that file comes with patch 0081. The next bump then drops the backports and keeps this patch.

If you would rather wait for the bump, only step 2 is needed, and I can send it on top of that bump instead.

It stays Mac only and off by default (the "Switch 2 controllers" setting, `DM_SW2`). `pad_switch2_apple.m` imports IOBluetooth, so it has to stay out of the iOS build. Upstream's iOS work is still open in seedds/nxnative#1900.

### Done when

- With the setting on, a Pro Controller 2 pairs, plays and rumbles in a Mac game.
- With it off, controllers behave as they do today.
- `python3 tools/engine.py check` and `t_switch2` pass, and the iOS build is unaffected.
title: Switch 2 controllers on the Mac: connect upstream's Bluetooth support in controllers_mac.m

body:
### Idea

Monster Train 2 and Overcooked! All You Can Eat have `present_interval display` and no `fps_target`: the host shows a frame at every display tick where the game asks for one every two, so they run at 60 fps. The launcher's Frame rate choice (30 / 60) is only shown for `fps_target` games, so these two have no 30 fps choice. The only way is `DM_PRESENT_INTERVAL=game` in an env file.

30 fps is the Switch's rate and uses less power: Overcooked on an M1 Pro takes about 0.15 W of CPU at 30 fps and 0.86 W at 60.

### Plan

- `settings.tsv`: a Frame rate row for `DM_PRESENT_INTERVAL` (30 fps = `game`, 60 fps = `display`, default `display`), shown when `DM_GAME_PRESENT_DISPLAY==1&DM_GAME_FPS_TARGET==0`. A game with both keys keeps its one `DM_FPS_TARGET` row.
- `settings.py`: a shown condition of several joined by `&` holds when all of them do.
- No launcher code changes: the launcher draws the row from the app's `launcher.json`, like every other choice.

### Done when

Overcooked and Monster Train 2 show Frame rate 30 / 60 in Launch options. Choosing 30 fps runs the game at its own interval (the log says `interval mode game`). Games with `fps_target` still show their one Frame rate row.
title: Frame rate choice (30 / 60 fps) for games shown at every display tick

### Game and title ID

0400486024DEC000

### Base game and update versions

update v131072, packed from a NUP

### Where it runs

Mac app (built for This Mac)

### Device, chip and RAM

MacBook Pro 14-inch, M3 Pro (14-core GPU), 18 GB

### macOS or iOS / iPadOS version

macOS 27.2 (26B123)

### How it was installed

I run the Mac app the launcher built

### NX2Apple version

1.3.0

### What happens, and when

The game uses far more memory than an 18 GB Mac can afford. Activity Monitor shows the game process at **10.24 GB**. System-wide: 16.29 GB of 18 GB used, 4.81 GB compressed, 877.9 MB swap, memory pressure in the yellow. CPU is mostly idle (77 % idle), so this is not CPU load.

It happens every run. Most of the growth comes in one step, between frame 900 and frame 1200 (the title screen into the first loaded area). After that it stays flat until I quit:

The game runs and saves fine; the rest of the Mac slows down while it runs.

I expected a better memory management and efficiency

body:
### Idea

To play on an iPhone away from home, the game's data has to be in the shared app before you leave. The data is already on the computer: `romfs.img` sits in the game's archive folder, and since #790 the Mac and the iPhone builds share it. Nothing has to be extracted or built again to send it. What is missing is a way to send it that does not get in the way:

- **Mac.** Step 3 sends the data with `devicectl`, over the cable or Wi-Fi. While it runs the launcher is busy and cannot build. It sends only the game just built (#994). A large file stalls (#899, fixed in #1027 by sending it in parts) and the progress can look stuck (#967).
- **Windows.** There is no way into the device. The data goes to a drive or a folder and then into the Files app by hand, or into the IPA, which sideloaders refuse at 7 GB (#947).

The launcher pushes the data, the phone does nothing. The app does not have to be open, and the trust is the pairing the device already has with the computer. No network code in the app, no pairing of its own.

### Plan

**1. A send queue that runs in the background**
- A send no longer blocks the launcher: a build can run at the same time. The Builds page shows the queue with each game's progress.
- The queue holds one or more games of the shared app, for one device. Each game's data folder is found as in #994.
- The size and the connection are shown once, when a game is added. After that there is no question.
- When the device goes away (cable out, locked, out of Wi-Fi), the item waits. When the device is back it resumes from the parts already on the device, with the identity check of #1027 (`partsReceipt`).
- Wi-Fi through `devicectl` stays. With both a cable and Wi-Fi, the cable is used.

**2. AFC over the cable as the second way**
- `house_arrest` (`VendContainer`) on the shared app's bundle ID, then AFC writes to `Documents/games/<title ID>/`.
- The same part names as #1027 (`romfs.img.nxpart.NNNN.NNNN`), so the app's `DataParts` joins them with no change. The sizes on the device are read back to resume.
- Used when `devicectl` refuses the copy (#578), when its listing does not show the app, or when CoreDevice does not see the device.
- `house_arrest` needs an app signed with `get-task-allow`. When it is refused, the Finder or Files way stays.

**3. Windows through AFC**
- Apple Devices (or iTunes) brings Apple Mobile Device Service and usbmuxd. Step 3 of the Qt launcher gets "To the device" next to "To a drive or folder".
- The same checks as on the Mac: the `romfs.id` identity, and the free space from the shell's log.
- The library has to be chosen before code. pymobiledevice3 is GPL-3.0 and cannot ship in the MIT zip. Options: the libimobiledevice tools (LGPL-2.1) as separate programs, or a small AFC client of our own (usbmux, lockdown, `house_arrest`, AFC).

### To check first
- AFC to a USB-C iPad from a Mac: usbmuxd does not see it over NCM. Does a CoreDevice tunnel work without root?
- Whether `devicectl` copies to a locked device over Wi-Fi. Over the cable it needs the device unlocked.
- `house_arrest` on a shared app installed by AltStore, SideStore or Sideloadly, not only one signed by the launcher.

### Not in this issue
- Wi-Fi on Windows, and the phone fetching the data itself (step 2 of #233). Later, if people ask for it.
- The game's iOS build. The device needs it in the shared app first: the data alone does not make a game built only for the Mac playable. Saves go through iCloud saves (#957).

### Done when
- A Mac sends the data of several games in the background while a build runs, resumes after the cable is pulled or the device locks, and the app joins the parts at its next start.
- When `devicectl` refuses the copy, AFC over the cable delivers the same files.
- The Windows launcher sends a game's data into the shared app over the cable.
- Tests cover the queue's states (waiting, resumed, done), the AFC writer against a fake, and the Windows send against a fake device.

### Depends on
- #1027 (the data in parts, resumed by part)
- #994 (every game's data without a build)
title: Send game data in the background: devicectl in parts on a Mac, AFC over the cable as the second way and on Windows

body:
### Background

In #1026 I reported controller problems in the iOS shell of 1.3.0: the focus ring's shape, the gear and the game language that cannot be reached, Settings rows that flicker, and the button mapping page. I then tried to fix them on top of the current views, on an iPad mini (A17 Pro, iPadOS 27.2). What I learned:

- Much of the flicker and the stray presses come from iPadOS itself. It also turns the controller into UIKit input, moves a focus of its own and presses the control it is on as A comes up (the "echo" that `InputGate` guards against). A `GCEventInteraction` on the window (`handledEventTypes = .gamepad`, `receivesEventsInView = false`) hands the controller to the Game Controller framework only. This seems worth having whatever the UI ends up being.
- The ring's shape and the gear can be fixed locally. But a native `Form` draws only the rows in view, so the shell's own focus cannot see the rows further down, and each native control (menus, segmented pickers, toolbar items) needs a workaround of its own. After a few rounds it still did not feel solid.

### Idea

The console mode in #901 is SwiftUI built around a `ConsoleDriver` protocol, with its own focus and controller navigation that I have tested with real controllers on the Mac. To see whether it could also serve iOS, I built a local prototype: the console mode's views compiled for iOS without changes, small shims for the Mac-only parts (filling the screen, dragging with the mouse, the row's scroll view) and the existing `MockConsoleDriver`. With a controller on the iPad it works well.

A real version would need: the console views in a package both apps can build, an iOS driver on `ShellHostModel` (games, Play, options, cloud saves, button mapping, controllers), and touch and iPhone layouts. Nothing of this is pushed. I know neither #816 nor #901 has a milestone yet, so this is a question about direction, not a plan to build.

### Questions

1. @v0lumehi No rush: I saw in #901 that you will come back to the UI later. When you do, could #901 get a review? This builds on it, and I am holding further console mode changes until it has been looked at.
2. I know you like the native design that iOS has now. Would you rather keep it? That is fine with me. If so, tell me and I will help with controller support and bugs there instead, starting with the `GCEventInteraction` fix from #1026.

Thanks for your time.
title: iOS: could the console mode from #901 also serve as the iOS shell's controller UI?

body:
### This is

A problem

### What happens, or what you would like

On iPad, the controller list of the iOS shell (`main`, `GamepadAdapter`) shows a GameSir G7 Pro at **100 %**. It looked made up, so I read what each OS hands over for the same controller. The app does not invent the number, but the three systems disagree with each other. Battery numbers from a controller cannot be taken at face value.

**Controller:** GameSir G7 Pro in its Xbox mode. In that mode it reports itself as an Xbox Wireless Controller: Bluetooth name `Xbox Bluetooth Gamepad`, VID/PID `045E:02FD` (the Xbox One S controller), firmware `9.0.3` as macOS lists it, GameController `productCategory` `Xbox One`. The only hint that it is not a Microsoft pad is its Bluetooth address: `D6:20:40:F6:9A:2A`, one off from the same pad in its own mode (`GameSir-G7 Pro`, `3537:1022`, `D6:20:40:F6:9A:2B`). Its battery was full (just taken off its charging dock). Connected over Bluetooth on every system, no cable.

| System | API | Reading | Shown |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| iPadOS 27.2 | GameController `GCDeviceBattery` | `batteryLevel` 1.0, `batteryState` `.full` (2), 15 reads over 75 s | iOS shell: 100 % |
| macOS 27.2 | GameController `GCDeviceBattery` | `batteryLevel` 0.0, `batteryState` `.unknown` (-1), every read for 60 s | console mode: outline only |
| Windows 10 22H2 | XInput `XInputGetBatteryInformation` | type `BATTERY_TYPE_DISCONNECTED`, level `EMPTY` (nothing usable) | Qt launcher shows no battery |
| Windows 10 22H2 | Windows.Gaming.Input `RawGameController.TryGetBatteryReport()` | `Discharging`, 100 of 1000 mWh (10 %), 5 reads | |
| Windows 10 22H2 | PnP Bluetooth battery property | empty | |

So for one full controller: 100 % on iPad (right by luck, or a fixed value: not known yet), unknown on Mac, 10 % on Windows (wrong). The iPad reading also says `.full`, which normally means "on power and charged", while the pad was on Bluetooth with no cable.

How it was read: on iPad, a `ShellDemo` build of `main` with one `NSLog` in `GamepadAdapter.publish()` (raw `batteryLevel` and `batteryState`) and the 30 s poll set to 5 s. On the Mac, a small `swift` script polling `GCController.controllers()`. On Windows, PowerShell calling `xinput1_4.dll` and `Windows.Gaming.Input`.

**For anyone designing a battery display** (the Mac console mode, the iOS shell, a future Windows one):

1. **The number comes from the controller's own report, read by the OS.** The same pad gives different readings on each OS. The app cannot check it, so show what the OS says, nothing more precise than it, and never fill a gap with a guess (no "100 % when unknown").
2. **Third-party pads that pose as Xbox or DualShock controllers cannot be told apart by name or category.** This one carries Microsoft's VID/PID and name. GameController on iOS exposes no VID/PID at all, so a per-model exception is not possible there.
3. **`.unknown` with level 0 means "no reading".** Show no number. Both the Mac (`ConsolePadSnapshot.batteryReading`) and iOS (`GamepadAdapter.publish()`) already do this.
4. **`.full` does not prove a cable.** Here it came over Bluetooth. The Mac maps `.full` to a full battery with the charging bolt (`batteryReading`, `case .full: return (1, true)`), which would draw a bolt on this pad. iOS maps `.full` to 100 % without the bolt. Before the two are unified, decide which is wanted. Copying the Mac rule to iOS would add a wrong bolt here.
5. **Battery changes are not announced on iOS by a notification, but `batteryLevel` and `batteryState` are key-value observable.** The Mac observes them, and iOS polls every 30 s.
6. **A DualShock 4 over Bluetooth (and pads that copy it) sends its battery only after the host has sent it an output report.** The Mac primes every controller with its player (`primeOutputs`). The iOS adapter does not, so a DS4 on iOS may stay at "No battery level". This is not tested on a device.
7. **Windows: XInput and Windows.Gaming.Input disagree for the same pad.** XInput had nothing, Windows.Gaming.Input had a wrong 10 %. If the Qt launcher ever shows a battery, test both.

Not verified yet: whether a genuine Xbox Wireless Controller, a DualShock 4/DualSense and a Switch Pro Controller read the same on iPadOS, macOS and Windows. A follow-up for whoever has one: the same three reads with the controller full, then again when it is lower. Also open: whether this GameSir keeps reporting 1.0 on iPad once its battery runs down. If it does, the iPad's 100 % is a fixed value too.

### What you expected

A level that matches the controller, or no number when the OS has no trustworthy one. Nothing in the app needs to change for this report. It records what the systems hand over, so that the next battery design accounts for it.

### NX2Apple version

`main` at 9821bf2c (iOS shell built from source as `ShellDemo`). Mac console mode from `main` at the same commit.

### Computer and OS

iPad mini (A17 Pro), iPadOS 27.2 (24B119). MacBook Air M2 (Mac14,2), macOS 27.2 (26B123). Windows 10 22H2 (19045).

### Copy diagnostics

Not applicable: no game was involved, and the readings are in the table above.

### No keys, no game files

- [x] Nothing attached here contains keys, game files or data extracted from a game.

### This is

A problem

### What happens, or what you would like

`ArtworkPanelTests.testHeroBottomEdgeFadesCleanlyWithoutBrightSeam`, added in c1eeed00 (#1001), fails on every run on this Mac with an unchanged `frontend/` at `main` 9821bf2c:

```
cd frontend && swift test --filter ArtworkPanelTests/testHeroBottomEdgeFadesCleanlyWithoutBrightSeam
Tests/NX2AppleTests/ArtworkPanelTests.swift:181: error: -[NX2AppleTests.ArtworkPanelTests testHeroBottomEdgeFadesCleanlyWithoutBrightSeam] : XCTAssertLessThanOrEqual failed: ("21") is greater than ("20") - Bright 1px seam leaked at hero bottom edge y=799: peak=21
```

It's one pixel row (`y=799`), one shade over the limit (21 against 20). The other rows the loop checks pass. That suggests the gradient's last step renders slightly brighter on this macOS version than where the test was written, rather than a real seam.

Because the pre-push hook runs `swift build && swift test` whenever a push touches `frontend/` (counted from the remote branch's tip), it stops every push here that carries main's newer commits. For example, a rebased PR branch, where `frontend/` comes only from `main`. Contributors are told never to use `--no-verify`, so such a branch can't be pushed from this Mac until the test passes.

### What you expected

The test passes on macOS 27.2, or has a tolerance that allows for small rendering differences between macOS versions and displays (for example, 21 or 22, or checking that the brightest row past the fade stays below a margin, not each row at 20).

### NX2Apple version

Source checkout of `main` at 9821bf2c (`swift test` in `frontend/`), not a release build.

### This is

A problem

### What happens, or what you would like

Five problems with controller navigation on iOS (iPad, Japanese UI, one controller connected):

1. **The focus ring's corners and size do not match the button.** On the controller button at the top right, the ring is a larger rounded shape around the round button. On the Play button (プレイ), the ring is a rounded rectangle with smaller corners than the capsule button and stands off from it.

   | Controller button | Play button |
   | --- | --- |
   | ![Focus ring on the controller button](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Haseenesss/NX2Apple/assets/pr-screenshots/pr-screenshots/ios-focus/controller-button-ring.jpg) | ![Focus ring on the Play button](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Haseenesss/NX2Apple/assets/pr-screenshots/pr-screenshots/ios-focus/play-button-ring.jpg) |

2. **The gear at the top right cannot be focused.** Moving right from the controller button does not reach the Settings gear, so Settings cannot be opened with the controller from that row.

3. **Some rows flicker in Settings when moving with the D-pad.** In the Settings sheet (設定), pressing up and down moves the ring between ゲームデータ, クラウドセーブを有効にする, タッチ操作 and パフォーマンスオーバーレイ. While it moves, the ring flashes on rows that are not focused, and パフォーマンスオーバーレイ keeps showing a ring while another row has the focus.

   ![Settings rows flickering while moving with the D-pad](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Haseenesss/NX2Apple/assets/pr-screenshots/pr-screenshots/ios-focus/settings-flicker.gif)

4. **The game language setting cannot be focused.** Press X on a game to open its settings (ゲームの設定). The ring skips the game language setting, so it cannot be changed with the controller.

5. **The button mapping page cannot be left with the controller alone.** Once the button mapping page is open, there is no way back with only the controller: the page has to be closed by touch. Its RESET button is also styled as a touch control and does not fit controller use; it should look and work like the other controller-focusable buttons (focus ring, a button hint).

### What you expected

- The ring follows each button's own shape: a circle around round buttons, a capsule around capsule buttons, with the same gap on every side.
- The gear at the top right can be focused like the controller button next to it.
- Only the focused row shows a ring in Settings, with no flash on the others.
- Every setting in a game's settings, including the language, can be reached with the D-pad.
- The button mapping page can be closed with the controller (for example with B), and RESET can be focused and pressed like the other buttons.

body:
### Idea

Add adjustable stick deadzones to NX2Apple's existing controller settings, with independent left/right values, named profiles and a live stick preview.

A drifting stick can continuously move the camera even when the controller is untouched. Different controllers need different thresholds, including two controllers of the same model. The goal is to make those controllers usable without a separate utility or driver.

### Proposed experience

- Select a controller, then select its profile. The profile is assigned immediately when that model is uniquely connected.
- Adjust two sliders beneath live stick circles. The shaded area shows the deadzone, orange shows input and green shows filtered output.
- Create, duplicate, rename and delete profiles in the same window. Both sliders are available on first launch.
- Use scaled radial deadzones, independently for each stick. The prototype supports 0–90% in one-percentage-point increments, with 10% for new profiles. The higher range is useful for badly worn sticks.
- Configure profiles in the Mac launcher and select or adjust them in a running game's Controllers menu.
- For identical models without a reliable persistent device identity, select each device and its profile inside the game for that session. Never guess physical identity from connection order.

### Design and alternatives

A local prototype already exists. The launcher owns profile editing, while the game host applies the filter per physical controller before player inputs are merged. An active custom profile replaces the existing software deadzone on the generic HID / Switch Pro paths to avoid double filtering. Disabling profiles restores the original input path.

The prototype shares a versioned JSON file through atomic writes and event-driven file notifications. The game never waits for a launcher response and the launcher can be closed during play. Missing, invalid or unsupported configuration retains original controller behavior.

A launcher-only preview would not change gameplay. A system-wide virtual controller would add substantial platform and device-hiding complexity. A socket service would keep an extra process in the input path without being necessary for these settings.

Existing Mac games must be rebuilt with the modified host. This is an NX2Apple game feature, not a system-wide controller remapper. Qt and iOS interfaces are outside this initial proposal.

### Prototype evidence

- A physical PS4 / DualShock 4 connected over Bluetooth was tested on an Apple M5 MacBook Air running macOS 26.6.
- With left/right thresholds of 10% / 65%, the tester confirmed that the resting right-stick drift disappeared in a rebuilt Mario Kart World app.
- In a separate input-monitor test, all 50 right-stick samples produced exactly zero with the 65% filter. This capture is separate from the gameplay confirmation.
- Automated tests cover filter boundaries and full output, profile persistence and assignment, identical-model handling, filtering before merge, original-input fallback and live configuration reload.

PS5 / DualSense and Switch Pro are intended targets through the existing controller paths. Their physical USB/Bluetooth behavior, PS4 USB and mixed-controller multiplayer still need hardware testing. Synthetic tests are not a substitute for those checks.

### Done when

- The controller/profile workflow and shared configuration contract are agreed with maintainers.
- Custom deadzones affect each device before merge and preserve full stick output.
- Unassigned devices, paused profiles and invalid configuration use original input.
- Controller selection, profile switching, reconnection and identical models have regression coverage.
- Before/after UI captures and an explicit hardware coverage matrix accompany the implementation.
- The engine contribution is coordinated with seedds/nxnative, with a temporary NX2Apple patch only as agreed with maintainers.

Would this fit the project's controller settings roadmap, and is a shared-file profile contract the preferred integration point? I can adapt the prototype to the agreed design before submitting the implementation.

## Environment
- Launcher: NX2Apple 1.2.3 (macOS), engine commit `88c7e03f51e3934dc227089ea81ec64fcd525b03` (2026-11-06), shader chain `adec7d81d970`
- Build: `DmShell.app`, Release-iphoneos arm64, min iOS 26.0
- Devices (both reproduce identically):
  - iPhone 18 Pro Max (iPhone19,7), iOS 27.2
  - iPad Pro 11-inch (M4) (iPad16,3), iPadOS 27.2
- Signing: Personal Team (free, 7-day profile), dev-signed; `com.apple.developer.kernel.increased-memory-limit` = true and **active** (`runningboardd: Memory Limits: active 6144 inactive 6144`); Developer Mode is on; `amfid` validates the main binary and `DmGame0100000000010000.framework` with no rejection
- Game: base NSP only, title `0100000000010000`, display version 1.0.0, build id `3ca12dfaaf9c82da064d1698df79cda1`. No 1.4.1 (v393216) update available to test with. `romfs.img` is 5.13 GB in `Documents/games/0100000000010000/`, found by the shell as "SUPER MARIO ODYSSEY"

## What happens
Tapping the icon: the app starts, no window ever appears, and the app is back on the home screen after ~3–13 s with no alert.

Not a crash-report case: there is no `.ips` for `DmShell` on the device, no jetsam entry for it, and the 20 s launch / 19.94 s scene-create watchdogs never fire. SpringBoard only records `Scene commit was unsuccessful for sceneID:org.nxnative.shell.CY4M2HS3HR-default`.

## Evidence — `Documents/log.txt` (identical on two consecutive launches)

```
[dm] >>> nninitInitializeSdkModule
[dm] init takeover: nndiagStartup (no-op)
[dm] init takeover: oe::Initialize (no-op)
[dm] init takeover: aoc::Initialize (no-op)
[dm] init takeover: pctl::Initialize (no-op)
[dm] init takeover: diag::InitializeApplicationAbortObserver (no-op)
[dm] >>> nninitStartup
[dm] [mem] heap 3.12 GB (heap region 3.25 GB)
[dm] [mem] guest memory: memory pool 3.21 GB, room to the memory limit 7.95 GB, DM_GUEST_FILE unset: anonymous
[dm] guest AS 0x7000000000 +0x100000000  heap 0x7010000000 alias 0x70f0000000 stack 0x70e0000000
[dm] SVC 0x15 x0=0x1746aae58 x1=0x7012400000 x2=0x6000000 (placeholder returns success)
[dm] CRASH sig=11 addr=0 pc=sdk+0x14f778 lr=sdk+0x14f768 sp=0x1746aaea0
[dm] bt: main+0x536f80 guest_main+0x160 dm_main+0x10c boot_thread+0x44 _pthread_start+0x74 thread_start+0x8
```

`Documents/log.prev.txt` (the run before it) ends with the same four lines, byte for byte: same SVC, same PC.

`Documents/shell-log.txt`:

```
shell: free space 323839508220 bytes
shell: framework DmGame0100000000010000.framework
shell: Metal's HUD is ready, each game's Performance HUD setting turns it on at Play
shell: game 0100000000010000 SUPER MARIO ODYSSEY at DmGame0100000000010000.framework
```

The generated `profile.tsv` (39 rows) says `display_version  3ca12dfaaf9c82da064d1698df79cda1  1.0.0`, i.e. the profile was regenerated for the v1.0.0 dump, and the cheat lookup agrees: `no file for build 3CA12DFAAF9C82DA`.

## Reading
`SVC 0x15` is `svcCreateTransferMemory` (x1 = address 0x7012400000, x2 = size 0x6000000 = 96 MB — matches). The host answers it with a placeholder that reports success, so the handle the game receives is not a real transfer-memory object; the SDK dereferences it immediately afterwards and takes SIGSEGV at address 0.

So the game never reaches its first frame, and the failure is inside the host's SVC layer, not in the game data, entitlements, signing or memory budget (3.21 GB pool with 7.95 GB of headroom).

## Questions
1. Is `svcCreateTransferMemory` implemented on the iOS host path, or is this the known placeholder? If a real implementation exists, which engine commit carries it — the launcher's engine channel check would then fix this.
2. Is base-only v1.0.0 supported for this title, or is the 1.4.1 (v393216) update actually required (the profile regenerated cleanly, so the launcher did not object)?
3. Is there any `DM_*` switch, profile row or build option that avoids the transfer-memory path for this game while a fix lands?

Logs attached: `log.txt`, `log.prev.txt`, `shell-log.txt`, `shell-log.prev.txt`.

body:
### This is

A problem

### What happens, or what you would like

While a game is building, the update sheet's main button does nothing visible. Found while looking into #1010.

Steps:

1. Start a game build.
2. While it runs, click the update icon in the top bar (it opens the sheet at any time), or let Check for updates open the sheet.
3. Click **Update now**, or **Restart now** if the update has already been downloaded.

What happens:

- **Update now:** `AppUpdateStore.performUpdate()` stops at `guard mayInstall` and only sets `status` to `app.waitForBuild` ("A build is running: the update waits until it is done"). `UpdateSheet` shows `blocked` and never `status`, so the sheet stays as it was. The message appears only as the footnote of the App card in Settings, which is not on screen.
- **Restart now:** the sheet calls `updates.install(relaunch: true)` and then `dismiss()`. `AppUpdate.install` refuses during a build, `install` sets the same `status` and returns false, and the sheet closes anyway. To the player it looks as though the restart was accepted and then nothing happened.

The build itself is not affected: nothing is installed or relaunched while it runs. The problem is only that the player is not told why.

The Settings buttons (`AppCard`) already handle this: Update and Restart now are disabled while `buildRunning`. The sheet is the one place that does not.

### What you expected

# Description

NX2Apple stops during the update packing stage because three `.bntx.zs` files do not start with the expected Zstandard magic bytes.

The error is:

```
[RED] v131072: 3 file(s) whose bytes do not start as their names promise
```

Affected files:

All three files exist in the extracted update:

`updates\131072\romfs\Tex`

The update contains 20,667 files.

The three files have substantial nonzero data, but contain zero-filled prefixes:

| File | Size | Zero prefix |

body:
### Idea

The library scan of the Mac launcher reads a package's title ID only from its file name (`Game [0100000000010000][v0].nsp`). A renamed file, such as `Mario.nsp`, is not a game of the library, and an update or DLC with such a name is not found beside its game. The title ID is also in the package itself: the NCA headers name it, and `header_key` from prod.keys decrypts them. With the keys saved in Settings (#996, #1009), the scan has the keys it needs.

Suggested by @Absenti in #996.

### Plan

- The library scan reads the title ID of an NSP or NSZ whose name has none from the package: the program ID of its meta NCA, decrypted with `header_key` of the keys saved in Settings. The launcher already reads and decrypts NCA headers for the key check (`KeyCheck`).
- A name that holds a title ID wins, as today. Without saved keys, or for an XCI (its NCAs are behind a card header), the scan reads names only, as today.
- Each package is read once per scan, a few kilobytes. Key values are never logged or shown.
- Choosing or removing the saved keys scans the library again.
- A build of such a game stays the library's entry for it, instead of adding a second entry keyed by the file's path.

### Done when

- A renamed base NSP with the keys saved shows as its game in the library, with its renamed update and DLC.
- Without saved keys, or with a header_key that does not open it, nothing changes.
- Tests cover a renamed base, update and DLC, no keys, a wrong key, and a name that wins over the header.
title: Library: recognize game files whose name has no title ID, from their NCA headers

body:
### Idea

The first start of a freshly built game app waits for macOS for a long time, often minutes, before anything shows. Every rebuild brings the wait back. The launcher can take that wait off the player: as the build's last step it opens the new app once, in the background, so macOS verifies it while the build page is still open.

### Why the first start waits

- The packed game app is signed ad hoc (`codesign -dv` shows `flags=0x2(adhoc)`) and carries no quarantine attribute.
- The first time it is opened through LaunchServices, `syspolicyd` scans the whole bundle: the code signature and a malware scan of every file. `romfs.img` is several GB, so this takes minutes. The process sits in `ps` with STAT `U` (uninterruptible wait) the whole time, and no window shows.
- macOS remembers the result by cdhash. A rebuild makes a new cdhash, so the scan runs again on the next first start.
- Starting the binary directly (`posix_spawn` of `Contents/MacOS/...`) does not trigger the scan. Only an open through LaunchServices (`NSWorkspace.openApplication`, `open`, a double click, the Play button) does, so a preflight has to go the same way.

### Plan

1. **Engine (patch, and the same change to seedds/nxnative).** In `dm/mac/launcher.c`, `main` returns 0 at once when `DM_PREFLIGHT` is set, right after `_NSGetExecutablePath`: before it reads Info.plist, renames the log to `.prev.log`, creates the save folders or shows any window, and without starting `dmhost`. The open does nothing but let macOS verify the bundle.
2. **Launcher.** When a Mac app build finishes, `BuildStore.finishMacApp` adds a last stage, "Verify first start", and opens the new app through `NSWorkspace.openApplication` with `DM_PREFLIGHT=1`, `activates = false`, `hides = true` and `addsToRecentItems = false`, then waits for it to exit (at most 10 minutes). The stage ends done or failed. A failure is only logged: the build still counts as done.
3. No special case for a rebuild that changed nothing: the same content gives the same cdhash, macOS answers from its cache, and the stage takes a second.
4. A switch in Settings, App card: "Verify the first start after a build", on by default, with a note that it can take a few minutes and runs in the background.

### Not done, and why

- Removing the quarantine attribute (`xattr -d com.apple.quarantine`): the app has none, the scan is not Gatekeeper's quarantine check.
- `codesign --verify --deep` or `spctl --assess`: they check the signature in their own process and do not fill `syspolicyd`'s cache for the LaunchServices open, so the first start still waits.
- A real start of the game in the background: it would roll the log, touch the saves and start `dmhost`.
- Console mode (`Console*.swift`) shows the new stage through the shared build stages as is. A console banner for it is a separate issue.

### Done when

- After a build of a large game, the build page's last stage "Verify first start" takes the minutes, and pressing Play right after starts the game without the wait.
- The game's log and saves are untouched by the preflight.
- The switch in Settings turns the stage off.
title: Build: verify the new app's first start as the build's last step

body:
### Idea

Console mode (#816, draft #901) tells the player about things in three unrelated ways: the build chip in the top bar (the desktop is building), a toast at the top centre (a controller connected, Identify, a failed cheat write), and the centred questions. Some things it does not tell at all: a build finished or failed, the app's update is ready to restart into, a controller's battery is low, a cloud save was not sent (#957), a game is paused in the background (#952).

One queue, `ConsoleNotice`, with two weights that share the build chip's look (`consoleGlass`):

- **Chips** stay in the top bar while something runs: a build (as now), an update downloading, a game paused in the background. The build chip's bar shows the whole build's progress, `(k - 1 + frac) / n` from the script's stage events (`BuildStore` already reads `n`), and its text the current stage, so the bar no longer runs 0 to 100 once per stage.
- **Banners** slide out under the top bar for a few seconds and go: a controller connected or gone, a build done, an update ready, a battery at 20 %, a save waiting to upload. A banner with something to do shows the Y glyph at its end (Start the game, Restart); Y is borrowed only while the banner is on screen, and the banner says so.

Rules: notices never take the focus or move the page; same-kind notices merge (two controllers connecting read as one banner); one banner at a time, the rest queue; nothing shows while a game is starting or a question is open. Texts come from what the desktop already has (`BuildNotice.text`, `ConsoleAppUpdate`), so the two modes say the same thing. Icons are the SF Symbols the app already uses.

Why the top bar and not the top centre: the toast there covers the controller chips when several are connected, and on a notched Mac in console mode it sits under the camera housing.

The "build done" banner comes after the build's last stage verifies the app's first start (its own issue and PR, from `main`), so Y then starts the game with no wait.

### Plan

Each step its own PR, on top of #901's top bar:

1. The model and queue (`ConsoleNotice`, a pure `ConsoleNoticeQueue` with tests), with today's toast and build chip moved onto it and no visible change.
2. The banner view under the top bar, replacing `ConsoleToastView`.
3. Build done, update ready, low battery; the chip's whole-build progress.
4. Cloud save results and the paused game, once #961 and #952 are in.

Nothing here touches the desktop or the engine.

### Done when

- Every non-blocking message in console mode goes through the one queue; `ConsoleToastView` is gone.
- A build's end, a ready update and a low battery each show a banner, in all seven languages, without moving the focus.
- The build chip's bar is the whole build's progress.
- Offscreen captures (`NX_CONSOLE_CAPTURE_DIR`) show the banner under the top bar at 1920×1080, 1280×800 and the compact size.

A design note with the model, the triggers table and mock-ups is with the author; it goes into the first PR's description.
title: Console mode: one notice system (chips in the top bar, banners under it)

### Which step failed

Rewrite (the game's code)

### The message

### What happened
With **Use experimental builder** on, building Advance Wars 1+2: Re-Boot Camp (`0100300012F2A000`, base v1.0.0, no update needed) for iPhone fails right after extraction. The rewrite step stops with an error about a **different game's** patch file, Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity (`01002B00111A2000`).

```
[RED] nxb rewrite: unsupported: ../games/01002B00111A2000/patches.py changed since the patch snapshot was made
✗ The build failed (nxb exit code 1).
```

I have not edited any files in the engine. The engine is the one the app installed on the Stable channel.

### Expected
Advance Wars builds, or nxb only checks the patch file of the game being built.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Settings → Build tools → turn on **Use experimental builder**
2. Build Advance Wars 1+2 (`0100300012F2A000`, base only) for iPhone / iPad
3. Extraction completes (`extract v0`), then the rewrite fails with the error above

body:
### Idea

Red Dead Redemption (`01007820196A6000`, base 1.0.0 and update 1.0.4, SDK 15.3.2, Rockstar's RAGE in Double Eleven's port, NVN) plays on the Mac. It needs a reader for its archives in the shader split, a profile, and two rendering fixes for the engine that were found while playing it:

- Flickering light 8×8 blocks in the sky over distant hills and trees. The cloud fog samples the depth attachment its render pass has just written, and on Apple's GPUs that read returns partly stored tiles.
- Characters a few metres away are drawn as their hats and props only. The game reads its character occlusion queries from a samples-passed counter it never resets, and the host counted only from a reset, so every query read 0 and every character counted as hidden.

### Plan

- Carry the work as patches here (`pending`) and send the same changes to seedds/nxnative as pull requests:
  - the shader split's readers for Rockstar RPF6 archives, RAGE `rgxd` effects and Double Eleven `.pkdswitch` packs;
  - the game's profile and note, the 1.0.4 archive key and the registration of 1.0.4;
  - the depth fix (`DM_NVN_FB_DEPTH=0` turns it off);
  - the occlusion fix (`DM_NVN_OCC_IMPLICIT=0` turns it off).
- The movies' second audio renderer needs nothing of its own: upstream's support for several renderers (from Mario & Luigi: Brothership) covers it.

### Done when

- The patches are on `main` with this issue in their `Issue:` line, and each engine fix has its upstream pull request named in `Upstream-Status`.
- A Mac app built from the dump with `main`'s engine plays from Armadillo with distant characters drawn whole and no blocks in the sky.

### Idea
Adding two or three games to the shared app means building them one by one and exporting the IPA after each, and waiting at the Mac between builds. 
The same list helps on the Mac too (suggested in the comments): building several games as Mac apps today means starting each build by hand.

- On the Builds page for iPhone and iPad, a "Several games" card lists the library's games that have a base package or a game folder, each with what the library found beside it (update, number of DLC, base only, game folder). The player ticks games and starts "Build and export".
- The games are built one after the other with their update and DLC, each only into the shell's library (no IPA per game). A game that fails is marked with the reason, and the next one is built. Stop ends the list.

### This is

An idea

### What happens, or what you would like

Context : A created a feature to compile multiple game directly (futur issue), and I came across an issue with the IPA creation for "shared app".

### Idea
The shared app (#416) holds every game built for it, and a SideStore install keeps it signed with one app slot. Two steps of
"Export as IPA" still work per game:
- Step 1 only builds. To make the IPA again (to add a game built earlier, or after a profile fix), the only button builds the selected game first, which takes from minutes to an hour. Its label, "Export IPA", does not say it builds.
- Step 3 sends the data of the game just built. The other games of the app have their romfs.img on the Mac too, but the player has to build each one again to send its data.


### Plan
- Under step 1, a row "Export these games" that lists the games of shell.json whose framework is still there and makes the IPA from them, with no build. It stays after an export. Step 1's own button says what it does: "Build and export".
- Step 3 sends the data of every game of the app that has it (to the device or to a drive, one progress for all), and names  the games whose data the launcher cannot find. A game's data folder is found from shell.json (the folder recorded at build time, now stored there) or from the game library (output folder, source folder, the base package's folder).
- The library's stale-shader prompt asks before an export without a build, as before a build.


### Done when
- The IPA can be made again from the games built before, without a build, and after another export.
- Step 3 sends the data of all the app's games in one go, and says which games have none.
- Tests cover the export without a build (empty and incomplete library), the data lookup and the multi-game send.

body:
### Idea

Add Brazilian Portuguese (`pt-BR`) as an interface language for the Mac launcher, the Qt/Windows launcher and the iOS/iPadOS shell. Today the UI has en, zh, sv, de, fr, it, ja. Brazilian Portuguese is missing, even though the code already knows it: the game language list includes `pt-BR` (`frontend/Sources/NXCore/RomFSLanguages.swift`, `frontend-qt/nspb_qt/romfs_languages.py`) and `en.json` already has `launch.opt.DM_LANG.pt-BR`.

Implementation is one new file, `frontend/l10n/pt.json`, with `_language` (`name`: "Português (Brasil)", `locales`: `pt`, `portuguese`, `português`). The README says a new language is one file: no Swift change, the picker, device detection and iOS shell pick it up. Plus the generated catalogs from `tools/l10n_shell_catalogs.py`.

### Why Brazilian Portuguese

- **Size.** Brazil has about 200 million people and is the largest Portuguese-speaking country. Portuguese is its only official language. An English-only launcher asks these users to read every build step, error and setting in a second language before they can use it.
- **Local builds fit the Brazilian user base.** The launcher's whole model is a build on your own Mac from your own dumps. Users who tinker with their own hardware and setups are the ones this app serves, and the build flow is where translation matters most (unpack, rewrite, shaders, pack, errors). This is the maintainers' reasoning, not survey data; a Brazilian user can confirm or correct it in the comments.
- **Covers pt-PT devices too.** A `pt` locale prefix in the file would also select it for Portugal devices, which currently fall back to English. pt-PT wording can be a separate file later if they want their own.
- **Cheap to maintain.** Translations are one JSON file. The shell texts are machine translated now (see the v1.2.0 notes) and wait for a native review. A Brazilian reviewer closes that gap directly.
- **Already half there.** Game language `pt-BR` already works in the build. Only the UI is missing, so this is a small step with visible value.

### Plan

1. `frontend/l10n/pt.json`: copy of `en.json` with every key translated and a `_language` entry. Shell texts (`ios.*`) included, since every language file must have them.
2. `python3 tools/l10n_shell_catalogs.py` to regenerate the Xcode catalogs.
3. Tests: `tools/tests/test_l10n_shell_catalogs.py`, `tools/tests/test_launcher_texts.py`, `swift test --package-path frontend`.
4. Screenshots of the launcher in pt-BR for the PR (before/after per the contributing guide).

### Done when

- Device set to Português (Brasil) shows the launcher and iOS shell in Portuguese; Settings > Language can pick it.
- Catalog and key checks pass with no missing `ios.*` keys.
- A native pt-BR speaker has reviewed the texts.

Happy to open the PR once there is a go on this issue. I can start the translation draft in the meantime.
title: Add Brazilian Portuguese (pt-BR) interface language

body:
### This is

A problem

### What happens, or what you would like

On a physical iPhone Duo, custom touch-control positions in the layout editor, settings preview and running game do not agree. When ZR is placed sufficiently low in the editor, the running game can reject its position and put it back in the default top-right corner.

Reproduction with the shared iPhone shell:
1. Build Hades II through NX2Apple 1.2.3 and export the shell IPA.
2. Install on iPhone Duo and hold it landscape.
3. Open shell settings, touch controls, Arrange.
4. Choose 3D and overlay, move ZR down beside the face buttons, then finish editing.
5. Compare the editor, settings preview and running game.

The original settings preview uses a Pro Max geometry, while the editor derives geometry from the device. Fixing only that mismatch made editor and preview agree, but the runtime still shifted the right-side controls and could reset ZR.

### What you expected

The editor, settings preview and runtime should use the same placement geometry at the same screen size and orientation. A position accepted by the editor should remain accepted in the game.

### NX2Apple version

1.2.3, installed macOS GUI app. Engine pin 88c7e03f51e3934dc227089ea81ec64fcd525b03, packaged engine directory suffix 46919438b5de.

### Computer and OS

Build Mac: Apple M4, 32 GB, macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27.2.
Test device: physical iPhone Duo. Exact iOS version has not been collected.

### Copy diagnostics

The generated shell project resolves its Swift package to the installed application's Resources/frontend-ios directory. The shell was tested with Hades II 0100A00019DE0000, version 1.0.131248. The game version is outside the profile's registered update, but the failure concerns the shell's touch geometry.

No phone console or runtime safe-area measurements were collected. The diagnosis below separates source findings from the device-tested result.

### Investigation and tested candidate

Source findings:
- TouchPadPreviewGeometry uses the fixed 932 x 430 Pro Max screen.
- TouchLayoutScreens estimates rotated safe-area insets even when the window is already landscape, losing actual asymmetry and bottom inset.
- The game controller hides the status bar. DmGamepad recomputes geometry from its runtime safeAreaInsets, which can differ from the shell/editor placement area. This is a suspected source of the remaining mismatch, rather than a measured device trace.
- The runtime rejects custom positions that fail its bounds/overlap rules.

Candidate patch:
- Pass the same device screen geometry to settings preview and editor.
- Preserve actual landscape insets instead of estimating rotated phone insets.
- Snapshot the shell window bounds and safe-area insets before starting a game. Pass them through DM_TOUCH_LAYOUT_SCREEN and use that placement area in DmGamepad only while the game bounds still match. Fall back to UIKit's current insets after a size/orientation change.
- Validate the transferred dimensions/insets and add a diagnostic log line.

The first candidate containing only the Swift preview/editor fixes was tested on the Duo. Editor and preview agreed, but the game still differed.
The second candidate also rebuilt the game framework with the placement-area handoff. The device owner has now confirmed that this second build works correctly.

This is a tested candidate for maintainer review. The retained-snapshot approach is limited to the starting window size. Rotation after launch, split layouts, external display, other devices and other games remain unverified.

### Validation

- frontend-ios swift test passed, including duoLandscapeKeepsActualSafeAreaAndPreviewGeometry.
- python3 -m unittest dm.ios.tests.test_pad_geometry passed.
- Hades II game framework rebuilt successfully.
- iOS shared shell Release build succeeded.
- codesign --verify --deep --strict passed on the signed app.
- git diff --check passed for both trees.
- Physical iPhone Duo landscape with Hades II, confirmed by the device owner.

## Environment
- NX2Apple 1.2.3, engine `88c7e03f51e3934dc227089ea81ec64fcd525b03`, macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), Apple M4 Pro
- Xcode 27.2 (27B52), Metal 32023.922 (matches the pin), iOS SDK 27.2
- Game: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, `0100F2C0115B6000`, update v720896 (1.4.3)
- Target: iPhone build, work folder on an external exFAT volume (256 GB)

## What happened
After the app was installed on the iPhone, the card "Spieldaten kopieren" showed
`1/1 · 4:28` and `0%` for the entire transfer of `romfs.img` (17.0 GB). It stayed at
0% for at least eight minutes and then the step completed.

## Why it matters
The transfer takes eight minutes at best and much longer on a slow cable, and 0% is
the display of a stall. I checked the device by hand with
`xcrun devicectl device info files` while it ran and saw `romfs.img` growing
(12.6 GB at that moment), so the copy was fine and only the display was wrong.

## Likely cause
`devicectl device copy to` reports per file, not per byte, and a single 17 GB file is
one file, so a byte-based percentage has nothing to read. Reading the destination may
also fail while the copy runs: right before, both `devicectl device info files` and
`devicectl device copy from` failed on that container with
`CoreDevice.ActionError error 3` and `CoreDeviceError error 7000`.

## Request
Show either an indeterminate state ("Kopiere 17.0 GB, Gerät entsperrt lassen") or a
size that grows, so that 0% does not read as a failure. A spinner with the elapsed
time would already be enough.
title: iOS: the game data copy shows 0% for its whole run (17 GB), so it looks stuck

## Environment
- NX2Apple 1.2.3, engine `88c7e03f51e3934dc227089ea81ec64fcd525b03`, macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), Apple M4 Pro
- Xcode 27.2 (27B52), Metal 32023.922 (matches the pin), iOS SDK 27.2
- Game: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, `0100F2C0115B6000`, update v720896 (1.4.3)
- Target: iPhone build, work folder on an external exFAT volume (256 GB)

## Problem
A build can run for hours and then fail only because the work volume is full. In my
case `[5/7] iOS shaders` died after 4h10m at 19,007 of 28,669 shaders, with nothing
before it that pointed at the space. The failure message was a traceback, not a
statement about the disk (see the companion issue).

## What the same folder used, measured
- 19,007 finished shaders: `cas.db` 3.2 GB, iOS library folder 15 GB, Mac outputs 10.8 GB
- the stage's temporary folder at its peak: 27 GB (211,423 intermediate files)
- after a complete run: `cas.db` 5.37 GB, packed libraries 2.25 GB and 2.85 GB

So the stage needs roughly 50 GB of scratch for 28,669 shaders on this title, before
the pack and the IPA.

## Request
1. Before the shader stage (and before the build starts), estimate what it will need
   from the shader count and the target, compare it with the free space on the work
   volume, and stop in seconds with a clear message naming both numbers, instead of
   after hours.
2. When a stage does stop for space, say that the progress is kept and what the next
   run will reuse. Here it was `19,007 of 28,669 shaders in the cache`, and after
   freeing space the rerun reported `shader cache: hit 19007, rebuilt 9662`, which
   turns a four hour loss into 1.5 hours of remaining work. The current message reads
   like a failure with nothing to keep.
title: Warn about the free space a build needs before it starts, and say that a stopped stage keeps its progress

## Environment
- NX2Apple 1.2.3, engine `88c7e03f51e3934dc227089ea81ec64fcd525b03`, macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), Apple M4 Pro
- Xcode 27.2 (27B52), Metal 32023.922 (matches the pin), iOS SDK 27.2
- Game: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, `0100F2C0115B6000`, update v720896 (1.4.3)
- Target: iPhone build, work folder on an external exFAT volume (256 GB)

## What happened
`[5/7] iOS shaders` ran 4h10m and had published 19,007 of 28,669 shaders when the
volume filled. The log printed the intended line and then the stage died:

```
[RED] the shader compile cache .../shader/cache/cas.db cannot be written,
the build goes on without it: database or disk is full

File ".../dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_build.py", line 1580, in fin
    if result[1] == 'ok': publish_cache(key, digests[key], rule_fps[key], CODE_FP)
  File ".../dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_build.py", line 392, in publish_cache
    with STORE.batch():
  File ".../dm/tools/shader_cache.py", line 99, in batch
    else: self.db.commit()
sqlite3.OperationalError: database or disk is full
```

## Why
`Store.put()` catches `sqlite3.OperationalError`, sets `self.full` and prints one
`[RED]` line, which is the documented behaviour ("a full drive is one [RED] line").
`publish_cache()` wraps its puts in its own `with STORE.batch()`, so the commit runs
at that context's exit, outside `put()`'s handler. The exception escapes
`publish_cache()` -> `fin()` -> `ThreadPoolExecutor.map()` and the whole stage exits 1.

## Expected
A full volume should cost the cache, not the run. Either `publish_cache()`'s batch
belongs under the same handler, or `Store.batch()` catches `OperationalError`, sets
`self.full` and swallows the failed commit.

## Evidence that only the crash is wrong
After freeing space, the same folder reran and reported
`shader cache: hit 19007, rebuilt 9662`, then `shaders 28669: ok 28669`.
The cache did its job; the stage should not have exited.
title: iOS shaders: a full volume aborts the stage with `sqlite3.OperationalError: database or disk is full` instead of going on without the cache

### What happens, or what you would like
On macOS 27.2 the launcher does not come back from the Dock once its only window has been closed.

2. Close the window with the red close button. The app stays in the Dock, which is intended: a build and its log outlive the window that started them.
3. Click the app's Dock icon, or run `open -a NX2Apple.app`.

The app activates (its menu bar comes up) but no window appears, so the launcher looks dead. ⌘N (File → New NX2Apple Window) opens a window at once, so the app itself is healthy.

What the app does at that point, read on the installed 1.2.3 build with lldb: after the close the window is off screen; after the reopen `NSApp.windows` is empty and `NSApp.isActive` is YES. The reopen does reach the app: AppKit calls `SwiftUI.AppDelegate.applicationShouldHandleReopen(_:hasVisibleWindows:)` (the app's own `AppDelegate` implements only `applicationDidFinishLaunching`), it returns YES, and no window is made.

A minimal SwiftUI app on the same machine does not show this. It has a WindowGroup with `.windowStyle(.hiddenTitleBar)`, `.defaultSize(width: 1280, height: 900)`, `.windowResizability(.automatic)`, the same `NSApplicationDelegateAdaptor` (activation policy regular and `activate(ignoringOtherApps:)` in `applicationDidFinishLaunching`) and an `NSViewRepresentable` that sets `titleVisibility`, `titlebarAppearsTransparent`, `fullSizeContentView` and `isMovableByWindowBackground`; it still opens a window from the Dock after its window is closed. So the scene setup alone is not the trigger. I could not find what in the launcher keeps SwiftUI from making the window, so this is as much a "why" as a "please fix".

A change that restores the behaviour here (v1.2.3 plus the patch below, macOS 27.2): `applicationShouldHandleReopen` performs the File menu's New Window item when SwiftUI has made no window after a turn. Close then Dock click gives one visible window (`NSApp.windows` count 1), and repeated close/reopen cycles do the same. The item is found by its Command-N key equivalent because its title follows the interface language.

```diff
--- a/frontend/Sources/NX2Apple/NX2AppleApp.swift
+++ b/frontend/Sources/NX2Apple/NX2AppleApp.swift
@@ -52,4 +52,30 @@
         NSApp.setActivationPolicy(.regular)
         NSApp.activate(ignoringOtherApps: true)
     }
+
+    /// The Dock icon once the last window was closed. The app stays running on purpose (a build and its log outlive the window
+    /// that started them), but SwiftUI's own reopen makes no window for this app: the app comes forward with no window at all
+    /// (`NSApp.windows` empty), so the app looked dead from the Dock. The File menu's New Window does open one, so the reopen
+    /// performs that item unless SwiftUI made a window by itself in the meantime.
+    func applicationShouldHandleReopen(_ sender: NSApplication, hasVisibleWindows flag: Bool) -> Bool {
+        guard !flag else { return true }
+        DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 0.15) {
+            guard !NSApp.windows.contains(where: { $0.isVisible && $0.canBecomeMain }) else { return }
+            Self.openMenuNewWindow()
+        }
+        return true
+    }
+
+    /// The first menu item with the Command-N key equivalent that has an action: SwiftUI's New Window of the launcher's
+    /// WindowGroup, whose title follows the interface language and so cannot be matched by its text.
+    private static func openMenuNewWindow() {
+        guard let main = NSApp.mainMenu else { return }
+        for top in main.items {
+            guard let submenu = top.submenu else { continue }
+            for (index, item) in submenu.items.enumerated() where item.keyEquivalent == "n" && item.action != nil {
+                submenu.performActionForItem(at: index)
+                return
+            }
+        }
+    }
 }
```

### What you expected
The Dock click shows the launcher window again, as it did before.

### NX2Apple version
1.2.3 (release). `frontend/Sources/NX2Apple/NX2AppleApp.swift` is the same in `v1.2.3` and `main`, so a build of `main` should behave the same.

### Computer and OS
Apple M4 Pro, macOS 27.2 (build 26B123), Xcode 27.2

### Copy diagnostics
Not pasted: the app was in the windowless state and Settings was not opened. The rest of the environment: ad-hoc signed release build in /Applications, engine `88c7e03f51e3934dc227089ea81ec64fcd525b03-46919438b5de` (stable).

body:
### Idea

Before a game starts with cloud saves on, the launcher checks the cloud's save first. If it and this Mac's save differ, the player chooses which one to play with. Nothing in the cloud is replaced before that choice.

### Why

A save that is in iCloud does not always reach the game, and the way it can fail puts the cloud's save at risk. What I found on a Mac (M2, macOS 27.2):

- **The folder is set per game.** Only one of my four built games has a cloud saves folder. The other three never read iCloud: their logs have no `save sync:` line. That part is #864.
- **The saves in iCloud Drive are often only listed.** Every `save.dmsync` in my folder is `dataless`: iCloud keeps the content in the cloud until something reads it. On a Mac, the engine reads the cloud's file with a plain copy and waits at most 10 s for it (`FETCH_MS` in `dm/host/save_sync.c`), at the game's first save mount.
- **When the download takes longer, the game plays on with this Mac's save.** At the game's next save, the sender reads the cloud again. If the cloud's save differs from the last one synced, it is moved into a local backup folder, and this Mac's save replaces it in the cloud. The player is not told, and the launcher does not show that backup folder.
- **On a first play on this Mac, this replaces real progress.** With no save here and a slow download, the game starts a new save, and its first save replaces the cloud's progress in the cloud.
- **When both sides changed, the newer save time wins without asking** (`ss_decide`), and when the cloud's file is not found at all, it counts as no save in the cloud.

So a player who saves before the cloud's save has arrived can lose it from the cloud, which is the opposite of what cloud saves are for.

### Plan

- **Check before the start.** With cloud saves on, the launcher reads the cloud's save before it starts the game. It downloads a file iCloud has only listed and shows "Getting your save from iCloud…" with Cancel. There is no time limit that gives up without telling the player.
- **Compare.** It compares the cloud's save with this Mac's: each side's hash and save time, the device that saved it, and the last synced save, which the engine keeps in `<save>.sync`.
- **Ask when they differ.** If they are the same, the game starts. If they differ, a dialog asks: **Use the cloud's save** (from <device>, saved <time>), **Use this Mac's save** (saved <time>), or **Cancel**. The save not chosen is kept as a backup that the player can find.
- **Ask when the cloud cannot be read.** If the cloud cannot be read (offline, or the download fails), the dialog offers **Try again**, **Play with this Mac's save** or **Cancel**. Playing with this Mac's save does not send it until the two have been compared.
- **The engine follows the choice.** It brings the cloud's save in or sends this Mac's, as chosen, and never replaces a cloud save it has not compared against. That part is in `save_sync.c`, so it is a patch here and a pull request to seedds/nxnative.
- **Both modes.** The check and the dialog work on the desktop and in console mode (#816, #901), with a controller.

### Done when

- A game whose cloud save iCloud has only listed starts with that save, after a download the player can see.
- When the cloud's save and this Mac's differ, the player chooses before the game starts, and nothing is replaced without that choice.
- When the cloud cannot be read, nothing in the cloud is replaced until the player has chosen.
- Tests cover the comparison: the same, only the cloud's changed, only this Mac's changed, both changed, none in the cloud, and the cloud unreadable.

### Open question

When only one side changed since the last sync (the other is still the synced one), the right save is clear. Should that case still ask, or bring it in or send it without a dialog? I would ask only when both changed or the last sync is unknown, but I am glad to ask every time if you prefer.

Related: #499 (the cloud saves folder on the Mac), #864 (one folder for every game), #490.
title: Idea: check the cloud's save before a game starts, and ask when it and this Mac's differ

body:
## Summary

On NX2Apple **1.2.3**, the Mac build of Minecraft Dungeons II stops at a black screen after the Xbox Game Studios logo movie. Backporting upstream nxnative `51cc8bc` (`nn::vi::ListFrameHistory`) into the local engine pin `88c7e03` fixes that: the game now reaches first control and is playable. An **intermittent yellow screen** remains; quitting and relaunching the app clears it.

## Game and environment

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Game / title ID | Minecraft Dungeons II, `0100A7C01B792000` |
| Base / update | base v0 (sparse), update 1.1.3.0 / v131072; only the update is packed |
| Target | Mac app (built for This Mac), window mode |
| Device | Apple M3 Pro, 18 GB |
| OS | macOS 27.0.1 (26A434) |
| Installed / run | the app the launcher built, started by double-clicking it |
| NX2Apple version | 1.2.3 (`CFBundleShortVersionString` and `CFBundleVersion`) |
| Launch options | defaults (`DM_FULLSCREEN=0`, `DM_PSO_MTL4=1`, `DM_PSO_PREBUILD=1`, `DM_PRESENT_SNAP=0`) |

## What happens, and when

1. **Black screen (resolved locally).** Right after the logo movie the picture stays black while logo audio and game logic continue; the `longframe` counter stops at frame 33. Upstream `51cc8bc` describes exactly this: UE5's Viewport Thread learns of each flip from `nn::vi::ListFrameHistory`, and the old host answered with 0 entries, so `FFrameEndSync` / `FlushRenderingCommands` waited forever. Applying that commit's three-file change (`dm/gfx/hle_vi.c`, `dm/gfx/nvn/hle_nvn.c`, `dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m`) to the engine store and rebuilding `dmhost` fixed it.
2. **Intermittent yellow screen (open).** With the game playable, a yellow screen appears on some runs. Relaunching the app restores normal rendering. It is not reproducible on demand, and I have not yet established whether it is a flat full-screen colour or a warm tint over the scene, or whether audio and input keep running.

## Expected

A stable picture, as in upstream's verification of this title.

## What was already ruled out

- **Not a bad dump.** Every NCA's SHA-256 matches its content ID / `.cnmt.xml`. The earlier `[RED] the NSP is damaged … nx_extract exit code 3` during `--html` came from reading a 16 KB sparse base HtmlDocument NCA on its own; that stage now exits 0 with 29 offline HTML files.
- **Not a failed build.** The host tool builds with 0 errors, `DMSH_CHAIN` was unchanged by the backport (no shader rebuild), and the game reaches in-game control.
- `dmsh_build.log` has no `F32FtzRn`; it does report 249 shaders with an undecoded binding slot and one deleted bindless access (`ccd515f16b0f63a6`).
- The local profile is the script-generated provisional one and is missing `tex_dyn_slots on`, which upstream's `dm/games/0100A7C01B792000/game.tsv` requires. I have not rebuilt the shader chain for it.

## Why the engine pin looks relevant

1.2.3 uses engine `88c7e03`. `main`'s `.upstream-ref` is `b2d46b8`, 11 commits after `51cc8bc`, so a build from current main should no longer have the black screen — this part may already be fixed for the next release. The yellow screen happened on the old pin, which still lacks several upstream rendering / present fixes, notably:

- `5636e7a` — detect macOS revoking a process's GPU access. Its description says every later present takes a drawable that nothing draws while sound and logic keep running (an uninitialised Metal drawable commonly shows as a flat colour).
- `490859e` — at a 30 fps target on a fixed-rate screen, keep the display link at 60 Hz (this game runs at 30 fps).
- `d4c11e2`, `48d0b37`, `a631295` — present-thread texture uploads, bound render target lifetime, compressed-texture alias copies.

Upstream's own note for this game was measured on an M4 Pro in a window at 1920x1080 / 30 fps and explicitly covers only the start of the first level; later levels and saves across boots are untested, and `pso_manifest.tsv` is empty.

## Not in this report yet

The Game problem form asks for **Settings > Copy diagnostics**, the build log's game-profile lines, and the whole game log of an affected run. No run log was persisted for the yellow-screen runs (neither `log/<title ID>.log` beside the app nor `~/Library/Logs/nxnative/<title ID>.log`), so I cannot attach one yet. I will capture it on the next reproduction, append it here, and confirm the exact appearance and whether audio/input continue. No game files, keys or extracted data are attached.

## Related

- Upstream pull request for the extraction-stage finding: seedds/nxnative#1769 (`nx_extract --html`: stop on a sparse base HtmlDocument NCA without its update).
- Upstream `51cc8bc` — "Minecraft Dungeons II plays on the Mac to first control in its first level at 30 fps".
title: Minecraft Dungeons II (0100A7C01B792000): black screen on 1.2.3's engine pin, intermittent yellow screen after 51cc8bc

body: ### Idea Make console mode work like a console's home menu while a game runs: Home in a game pauses it and brings up a menu over it, from which the player can resume, change the volume or the controllers, go back to the home screen with the game kept in the background, or end it. Back on the home screen, the running game's card says so, and A goes back to it without loading it again. ### Why Today a game started from console mode is a separate app. There is no way back to console mode except quitting the game, no way to end a game from the couch, and holding Home to quit does not work with many controllers: they switch off when Home is held. A game that was played once and quit has to load again from the start. Embedding the game's window in the launcher is not possible on macOS (one process cannot host another's window). Instead the game stays its own app and the launcher talks to it: ### Plan - Engine (patches, and a PR to seedds/nxnative): a game started by the launcher can be suspended, resumed and given a volume through distributed notifications, using the suspend path the host already has for a minimized window (focus out, audio paused, GPU suspended). It writes its last picture for the menu. On the Mac a press of Home hands the game to the launcher instead of the hold to quit. - Launcher: console mode keeps the game in the background (one at a time). The game menu shows over its last picture: Resume, Volume, Controllers, Button mapping, Home, End game (asked first; it ends the game properly, and at once if it has not quit after a few seconds). Playing another game asks to end this one. ### Limits - A paused game keeps its memory, several GB for a big game, so one game runs at a time. - Resuming without loading works while the game process is alive; after it quits, crashes or the Mac restarts, the game starts from its save as now. Saving the whole game state to disk is not part of this. - Some games react to losing focus in their own way and need checking one by one. - Home reaches the game only when macOS's Home button setting lets the app decide (a per-app override in System Settings). ### Done when - Home in a game opens the menu over it; Resume returns to the same moment. - Home from the menu shows console mode with the game's card marked as running, and A returns to it. - End game ends it; starting another game asks first. A working branch exists with the engine patches and the launcher side, not tested enough with real controllers to open as a PR. Screenshots below: the game menu and the home screen with a game in the background (demo data).
title: Console mode: a game menu on Home, the game kept in the background

body: ### Idea Show the game being built in the library from the moment its build starts, as a greyed card with the build's progress, and bring it to colour when the build is done. On the desktop and in console mode. ### Why When a build starts, nothing in the library says which game it is for. With the Built filter on, or in console mode with "only built games", the game is not in the row at all until the build ends, and it can take tens of minutes. The cover and the title are known from the start (the game's own data), so the card can be there the whole time. ### Plan - The card of the game a build makes shows from the start of the build, under Built too. - Its cover is grey with the build's progress along its bottom edge: the same figure as the activity bar on the desktop and the build chip in console mode (#901). It comes to colour when the build is done. - A game without a build is grey as well, so colour means "has a build". A game built again keeps its colour and shows the progress. - One look (`CoverLook`) draws it for both the desktop and console mode. ### Done when - Starting a build shows its game's card at once, greyed with progress, with Built on and in console mode. - The card comes to colour when the build ends, without a restart or a rescan. - Nothing changes for games that are not being built. A working branch exists (on top of #901 and #937, so not opened as a PR yet). It depends on the fix for builds that end in console mode, #950. Screenshots below: console mode with a game being built, and the desktop library.
title: Show the game being built in the library from the start of its build
