### Which step failed

Install to an iPhone or iPad (Xcode, devicectl)

### The message

## Environment
- NX2Apple Windows build v1.2.3 (NX2Apple-windows-x64.zip), Windows 10 x64, Python 3.12
- Game: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, title ID 0400486024DEC000, built from a .nup (update v131072, 24.4 GB unpacked)
- Build mode: iPhone / iPad, "Shared app" export
- Device: iPhone on iOS 27.3, free Apple ID
- Installers tried: Sideloadly 0.72, AltServer for Windows, AltStore on the phone

## Build result (all stages finished)
- shader split: 42,854 shaders
- iOS shaders: 42,845 of 42,854 ready (9 failed, see dmsh_build.log)
- IPA pack: ZeldaOcarinaOfTime.ipa, 3.6 GB
- The archive tests clean (Python zipfile testzip() returns None), top level is only Payload/, forward slashes.

## Problem
The IPA contains one very large entry. Largest entries by uncompressed size:
- 7,083,527,740 bytes  Payload/DmIOS.app/msl/b-adec7d81d970.img
- 109,591,488 bytes    Payload/DmIOS.app/DmIOS
- everything else is under 20 MB

Every installer fails on that file:
- Sideloadly: signing and upload succeed, then the phone reports
  "0 PackageExtractionFailed (Could not extract archive)" on every retry.
- AltServer (Windows): "Could not install ...ipa to iPhone. The app could not be found."
  (also NSCocoaErrorDomain 4 "The app could not be found")
- AltStore on the phone (IPA saved in Files): 
  "The file 'b-adec7d81d970.img' couldn't be opened. NSPOSIXErrorDomain Code=12 Cannot allocate memory"
  with the path .../tmp/.../App.app/msl/b-adec7d81d970.img

Control test: a copy of the same IPA with only msl/b-adec7d81d970.img removed (about 110 MB)
installs fine with Sideloadly. The two IPAs differ only by that one file.

The same installers handle a small IPA fine (a Balatro build installed with both Sideloadly and AltServer).

## After installing the stripped copy
The app boots and loads main/subsdk0/sdk. log.txt shows:
  [RED] boot: This app's game file identity (romfs.id) cannot be read; install the app again.
        Expected: 0400486024DEC000 1.0 (build v131072, 26247576430 bytes, index 0000000000000000).
  boot: no game data yet (Documents/romfs.img, Documents/romfs or <App>/romfs)
- Payload/DmIOS.app/romfs.id IS present in both IPAs (101 bytes).
- RomFS.img from the work folder is 26,247,576,430 bytes (matches the expected size).
- I sent it to Documents/romfs.img. The app then logged:
  [RED] boot: Documents/romfs.img is not the image this build needs (verdict 2); not used
- "Copy game data" writes a single file, romfs (about 25,632,399 KB), into <chosen folder>\0400486024DEC000\.
  It does not write a separate identity file there.
- The app's per-game settings page has no Game data row. launcher.json (4,314 bytes) lists only the
  15 display/control/performance settings and has nothing about shader or data locations.
- The settings page shows "Memory available: 3.27 GB" (Sideloadly install, so I assume no Increased Memory Limit entitlement).

## Questions
1. Can msl/*.img be kept outside the IPA (like romfs.img), or split into pieces under 4 GB, so the IPA installs on iOS?
2. Is the shared-app IPA expected to work for games with tens of thousands of shaders (the msl image for this game is 7 GB; Fire Emblem Engage's was about 7 GB for 9,335 shaders)?
3. Why would romfs.id be unreadable when it is in the bundle? Is the identity check tied to the missing shader image, or to how Sideloadly re-signs the bundle?
4. Is a Windows build expected to work with Switch 2 / NUP games on iPhone?

body:
### Idea

After an engine update, the player has to start every rebuild by hand. A setting can make the launcher do it in the background at low priority, so the games have the update's fixes the next time they are played and the Mac stays usable in the meantime.

### Plan

- A new switch in Settings, next to the automatic engine update: "Rebuild outdated games in the background". Off by default.
- When it is on and the engine changes, the games marked as needing a rebuild (#944) are added to the build queue (#943) by themselves.
- The build processes of these entries run at low priority: `Process.qualityOfService = .background` for the build and its children, or `taskpolicy -b`, so CPU and disk I/O give way to the player's own work.
- The background queue pauses:
  - while a game is running (no stutter while playing),
  - in Low Power Mode, or when `ProcessInfo.thermalState` is serious or critical,
  - and, with a second switch "Only on power adapter", on battery.
  It goes on when the condition ends.
- Before each entry, the free disk space is checked. When it is too low, the queue pauses with a note instead of failing one build after another.
- A background build never waits on a prompt:
  - stale frameworks, the shell copy and signing for iPhone/iPad are not asked, and the entry waits for the player instead;
  - the first version rebuilds only games whose last target was the Mac. An iPhone/iPad game stays marked and is left for the player.
- A rebuild keeps the game's mods, launch options and artwork.
- When the background queue ends, one notification says which games were rebuilt.

### Done when

- [ ] With the switch on, an engine update starts the rebuilds of the marked Mac games by themselves, at background priority.
- [ ] The queue pauses while a game runs, in Low Power Mode, under thermal pressure and (with the second switch) on battery, and goes on afterwards.
- [ ] Low disk space pauses the queue with a note.
- [ ] No prompt blocks a background build. iPhone/iPad games stay marked and are not rebuilt.
- [ ] Tests for the pause conditions and for skipping entries that would need a prompt.
- [ ] Strings in en, zh, de, sv, fr, it, ja, and screenshots of the Settings section.

Depends on #943 and #944.
title: Settings: rebuild outdated games in the background at low priority after an engine update

body:
### Idea

Many engine updates fix how a game looks: wrong colours, missing effects, flicker, broken lighting. Most of these fixes are in the host and in the shader translator. A game's shaders are translated and compiled into shader libraries when the game is built, so a game built before the update keeps the old shaders and the old bugs. The fix reaches the game only once it is rebuilt: the build then sees that the shader translator changed and rebuilds the shader libraries once (the "Rebuilding the shaders" notice, `shaders_stale`).

Players do not know this. They update, start the game, and the bug is still there. The launcher should tell them on the home page which games need a rebuild to get the fixes, and let them rebuild them in one step.

Two gaps today:

- Since #65, a game built with older build tools shows "Built with older tools" on its card and hero. The check (`ToolsAge`) runs `git diff` between the engine commit recorded at build time (`LibraryGame.toolsCommit`) and `engine/`'s HEAD. The engine of a release app is a tree from the engine store with no git history, so in the release app, which most players use, no game is ever marked.
- The marker only shows on each game's own card. After an engine update, nothing says "these games need a rebuild" in one place.

### Plan

**1. Know which games need a rebuild, also in the release app**

- At the end of a build, record what the game was built with, next to `toolsCommit`: the engine version (the engine id of `EngineSelection`), the shader chain (`StaleFrameworks.currentChain`), and a digest of the engine files the build reads (`ToolsAge.buildInputs`, plus the game's own `dm/games/<title ID>/`).
- A git engine keeps its `git diff` check. An engine tree compares the digest, worked out once when the engine is installed or synced, not on every check.
- A game built before these fields existed is not marked, as now.
- Each marked game has a reason: "the shader translator changed" (the shader chain is different: the rebuild rebuilds the shader libraries, and the game may compile shaders again on its first start), or "the engine changed files this game uses" (the host, the graphics layers, its profile).

**2. A notice on the home page**

- When at least one game is marked, the home page (the library and console mode) shows a notice, for example: "The engine update has fixes for 3 of your games. Rebuild them to get the fixes."
- Its actions:
  - "Rebuild all": adds every marked game to the build queue (#943).
  - "Show": filters the library to the marked games, each with its reason.
  - "Not now": hides the notice until the engine changes again.
- A marked game whose input files are gone is counted apart ("1 game can't be rebuilt: its files were moved"), and Rebuild all skips it.

### Done when

- [ ] In the release app, a game is marked after an engine update that changes the shader chain or files its build reads, and is not marked after one that does not.
- [ ] A checkout keeps its current `git diff` check.
- [ ] The home page shows the notice with the count, and Rebuild all puts the games in the queue.
- [ ] "Show" lists the games with their reason. "Not now" holds until the next engine change.
- [ ] Tests for the digest comparison, a changed shader chain, an engine tree and a game built before the new fields.
- [ ] Strings in en, zh, de, sv, fr, it, ja, and screenshots of the notice.

Depends on #943 for Rebuild all. Follows #65.
title: Home page: say which games need a rebuild to get an engine update's fixes, also in the release app

body:
### Idea

Only one build runs at a time, and while it runs, Build and Rebuild do nothing (`BuildStore.startBuild()` returns when `running` is set). To build several games, the player has to wait for each build to end and then start the next one by hand.

A queue lets them add builds while one runs. When a build ends, the next one starts by itself.

### Plan

- While a build runs, Build (on the build page) and Rebuild (in a game's Manage menu) add the build to a queue instead of doing nothing. An entry keeps what the build needs at the time it was added: the inputs, the target (Mac or iPhone/iPad), the launch options and the mods. For a rebuild, these come from the library entry (`LibraryGame.inputs`, `lastTarget`, `launchOptions`, `mods`).
- When a build ends, the next entry starts, whether the build succeeded or failed. A failure does not stop the queue. Stop stops only the running build. A separate "Cancel all" clears the queue.
- An entry whose input files are gone (a moved or deleted NSP/XCI) is skipped with a note. It does not fail the queue.
- The build page and the home page show the queue: the running build with its progress, then the waiting builds. A waiting build can be removed or moved up or down.
- When the queue empties, one notification (`BuildNotifications`) sums up what was built, what failed and what was skipped. There is no notification for each build.
- An engine update that waits for the running build (`EngineSyncStore.pendingEngine`) is installed between two entries. The entries after it build with the new engine.
- The queue is saved. After the launcher restarts, it asks whether to go on with the builds that were waiting.
- Prompts during a build (stale frameworks, the shell copy, signing) still show for the running build. The queue waits while a prompt is open.

### Done when

- [ ] Starting a build while one runs adds it to the queue, and it starts by itself when the running build ends.
- [ ] A failed or skipped entry does not stop the queue. A summary notification comes once the queue is empty.
- [ ] The queue can be seen, reordered, shortened and cleared on the build page and the home page.
- [ ] A pending engine update is installed between entries, not in the middle of a build.
- [ ] The queue survives a restart of the launcher.
- [ ] Tests in `frontend/Tests` for the order, a failed entry, a skipped entry and Cancel all.
- [ ] Strings in en, zh, de, sv, fr, it, ja.

Out of scope: the Windows launcher (`frontend-qt/`), which can follow later.

### The message

Build stops at the rewrite stage:

nxb rewrite: unsupported: patch_nso.py of the engine (~/Library/Application Support/NX2Apple/engine/f25fa9562ee96d06f1e6412dbb91aab2b7035ec1-c65b42ce7e50/dm/tools) differs from the version this rewriter was checked against (pinned sha256 6ca3aeeda9cb608f2298926f546b7ab3488afba9dcd23ebcce0077fe2b84f009, engine sha256 d4ad73740f6c93b7708426c59d6d04421e962e94be0288a4b420152e29d10e38): the engine changed, the rewriter must be checked against it and the pins updated

nxb exits 1 here, so the launcher does not hand the game to the NSP script: that fallback is only for exit code 4. Turning "Build with nxb" off builds this game with the script, so this is not blocking me — I am reporting it so 1.3.0 does not ship this.

What I checked, in case it saves you the trip:

- nxb 0.9.1 carries a hardcoded sha256 table for 12 files in dm/tools. I compared all 12 against the engine the launcher downloaded for engine_id f25fa9562ee96d06f1e6412dbb91aab2b7035ec1-c65b42ce7e50:

- The engine copy is not modified. dm/tools/patch_nso.py at seedds/nxnative f25fa9562ee96d06f1e6412dbb91aab2b7035ec1 hashes to d4ad73740f6c93b7708426c59d6d04421e962e94be0288a4b420152e29d10e38, the same bytes the launcher downloaded.

Golden Gate 27.2

From the launcher

1.2.3

### What happens, and when

When starting the game from the launcher with default settings, the game crashes before the title launch. It happens every time. 
Just before the crash, Metal printed this error:

MTLTextureDescriptor has height (32768) greater than the maximum allowed size of 16384.

The game asked for an image  32,768 pixels tall. The M2 Pro can only create images up to 16,384 pixels tall, so macOS aborted the program. The crash trace points to the code that translates the game’s graphics for Metal, so it’s a bug or missing workaround in NX2Apple’s graphics layer

Game launches as expected

None

### This is

An idea

### What happens, or what you would like

Following how NX2Apple Library view currently is on v1.2.3, as well as the redesign proposed by @Haseenesss as part of #901, it would be nice to get the feature to manually re-organize the game collection in the Library view via a re-order button toggle that puts the Library UI into re-order mode and as you select a game to move after highlighting it over hover it displays left and right arrows. As you approach the furthermost left or right edges, the appropriate arrow disappears in that direction indicating re-order direction limit.

At the moment the order the games display in are tied to when they were built. So games you might be actively playing now are pushed further down the Library whereas games you might have stopped playing are at the very front. This would allow users to bring their most played games to the front and push their unplayed/backlog games towards the back for later.

Alternatively the most recently played games can be pushed to the front after quit as default functionality and the potential manual re-ordering will override the automatic-to-front Library feature as part of this proposed idea.

body:
@ComicBit, these are my Ocarina of Time findings from 2026-11-07. A6 in the nxkit runtime plan is yours, so I hand them over here. I move to Breath of the Wild (B1 to B5).

Game: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, `0400486024DEC000` (Switch 2 NUP). Mac: M2 Max, 32 GB, macOS 27.2. Host: NX2Apple `main` with patch 0096. Related: #856, #892.

### Fixed: GPU page fault in the grass scenes

A mesh draw with no task shader used more than 1024 workgroups as the Metal mesh grid. Metal does not allow that, and the GPU faulted on the first draw of the scene. The fix splits such draws into grids of at most 1024.

- Fork: #925 (patch 0096, `forwarded seedds/nxnative#1708`)
- Upstream: seedds/nxnative#1708

### Frame time in the grass scene

Measured with `DM_NVN_GPUPROF=every:600` at frames 1200 and 1800. The encoder sum is about 20 ms per frame, and the whole frame is about 26 to 28 ms GPU. Three parts repeat in every profile:

| part | GPU time | content |
|---|---|---|
| compute and copy encoder 0 at the start of the frame | about 7 ms | 93 to 126 dispatches, most of them 1x1x1 |
| render pass 128x128 with depth | 3.6 to 4.3 ms | about 230 to 246 draws |
| main pass 683x384 | 2.8 to 4 ms | 349 to 673 draws |

The most frequent dispatches in encoder 0 at frame 1800 are `d8417253d976c110` (19 times), `059e8d63a659ccf4` (10), `50d3050cfa7cded5` (7, 2x1x1), `b9c1a507c34d6890` (8) and `96fb5825db712d65` (5). The larger grids are `e7798c202c2c1c44` (32x32, 5 times), `66c383579c983d46` (43x12), `5473fbd870e70a60` (22x24), `f4a0f6e622caa08d` (64x16), `c109d8aafce9a7f3` (384x1) and `eacb0fb5db476ba8` (32x32). Four dispatches are indirect: `f85fe64924e7e6f5`, `ef4bdc971d323ee0`, `e855420a39e60874` and `cee08c634ef1f343`. The time of each single dispatch is not measured yet. That needs timestamps inside the shared encoder.

Which pass the 128x128 one is (shadow or something else) is not checked.

### The image is washed out because of dynamic resolution

The game renders at 683x384 in the grass scene. Its dynamic resolution drops there because the GPU frame takes 26 to 28 ms. The output is then scaled up and looks soft.

Hookshot fixes the resolution with a patch of the game code at `main+0x805BD0` (the "Max Resolution" patch, credited to Lichii). It sets a fixed scale of 100, 75, 67 or 50 percent. It only applies after about 30 frames. Before that, the 3D image stays black. For us this would be a rule in the game's `patches.py`, or a module setting. A fixed full resolution makes each frame more expensive, so it trades sharpness for frame time.

### Tried without effect

- Fewer barriers: the `draw_barriers game` setting does nothing in this game, because it uses image heaps. I built a variant that relaxes barriers with image heaps too. It removed about 6,800 full barriers per 300 frames. An A/B run in the same scene gave the same GPU time (base 25.9 to 28.2 ms, variant 26.4 to 28.3 ms). The barriers are not the cost.
- Hookshot has no fix for the mesh cost. Their GPU time is about 10 ms on desktop GPUs. Their only mesh fix is the indirect argument layout, `{count, first}` to `{count, 1, 1}`.

### Open: GPU hangs after 1 to 2 minutes

The host from `main` with patch 0096 stopped with `kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorHang` in 3 of 3 runs, 1 to 2 minutes into the grass scene. The failed command buffer only had 35 to 45 ms of GPU time. Its rarest shaders were different each time. Switching the window focus is not the cause. One run hung while the game window kept focus.

An earlier build with my local diagnostics (GPU watchdog, fault map, sub-recording) ran 14 minutes without a fault on the same base. These diagnostics change the timing, so that run does not prove a cause. The next step is a longer run of both hosts in the same scene. The kernel log shows many `IOGPUCommandDescriptor::prepare preparedBytes != requiredBytes` lines in these runs. I did not check whether they belong to the hang. #856 reports a GPU firmware lockup on an M2 Pro and may be the same thing.

### Notes for measuring

- `DM_NVN_DISPATCH_OWN=1` crashes under Metal 4 (AGX `performEnqueueKernel` from `mtl_sub_fill`).
- `DM_NVN_PASSGPU` does nothing under Metal 4.
- `DM_NVN_PASSDUMP` turns off the mdx path, so it changes what is measured.
- `python3 dm/tools/gpuprof.py <log> --frames N --by class` summarizes a GPUPROF log.
title: Ocarina of Time: frame time, dynamic resolution and GPU hangs (findings for A6)

- Metal Developer Tools 6.2 (Windows), `metal 32023.850 (metalfe-custom-windows)`
- Windows x64; the 13-item dependency probe is fully green (cross-compile / cross-link / Metal compile probes all pass)

**What happens**

Every Unreal title I tried stops at the shader split, after extract and rewrite succeed:

```

      in a form shader_split.py does not read; locate them (docs/agents) and add a reader
```

This is **not** the Mac-host path. The Mac-host steps degrade gracefully on Windows in the same builds: `✓ [5/9] heap estimate (no Mac host)` and `✓ [6/10] address regions (no Mac host): skipped: needs the Mac host`. The split itself runs and simply reads nothing.

**Games** (stock NSP/XCI, prod.keys v22.5.0, same machine, same build folder reuse)

| title ID | title | engine | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 010029F01BA3E000 | Xuan Yuan Sword 7 | UE4 (pak) | 9.4 GB extracted, 177 files |
| 010062E01FE0C000 | Digimon Story Time Stranger | UE5 | update v1.2.2, 14 DLC extracted |
| 010066101A55A000 | Little Nightmares III | UE5 | update v1.2.1 |
| 0100B1A023F18000 | Sands of Aura | UE4 | |
| 0100BD401D18A000 | Under Night In-Birth II Sys:Celes | UE4 | |
| 0100CDB01E748000 | REYNATIS | UE4 / KT-renderer UE | |

For contrast, on the same install a KTGL title runs end to end, so the Windows toolchain is not the problem:

```
main has 45 GLSLC compiler output magics (0x19866891): shader_split.py takes those that are whole outputs
✓ [6/9] shader split (0:13): 2,945 shaders
✓ [7/9] iOS shaders (3:16): 2,945 of 2,945 shaders ready
✓ [8/9] game framework (0:16): DmGame010082F015576000.framework
```

**What would make these buildable on Windows**

Either:

1. a `shader_split.py` reader for the Unreal containers (UE4 `.pak` and UE5 IoStore: `ShaderArchive` / `GlobalShaderMap` in `.uasset`/`.ubulk`/`.utoc`), or
2. a documented "bring your own shaders" route — let the split accept a pre-decoded shader set / shader map file instead of reading the container, so a game whose shaders are decodable by other tooling can still be built.

**Question**

Is a UE pak / IoStore shader reader planned, or are UE titles on Windows considered out of scope? If out of scope, it would help a lot if the docs (and the front ends' "supported games" hints) said so explicitly, because right now a UE title gets through extract/rewrite and only dies 30 seconds later at the split, which reads like a bug rather than a known limitation.

body:
Hi! Ocarina of Time (0400486024DEC000, build E0F3CCFAF50065AE) runs on my M2 Max with NX2Apple 1.2.3.

There's already an ultrawide mod for this exact build: https://github.com/craftycorvid/oot-mod
It widens the 3D view to 21:9 / 32:9 and keeps the HUD and videos at 16:9. It's an exefs IPS patch, and the Mods screen says exefs mods aren't supported.

Two asks:
1. Support exefs IPS patches in the Mods folder, applied when the game is built.
2. A Mac picture shape wider than 16:9 (DM_SCREEN_ASPECT above 1.77), so a 21:9 game fills an ultrawide screen instead of being squished.

I play on a 21:9 LG ultrawide (same shape as 3440x1440), so I'm happy to test.

Thanks for NX2Apple!

### Which step failed

Mac shaders or iOS shaders

### The message


### Pokémon Pokopia — iOS Build Failure & Cache Recovery

I encountered an issue when building Pokémon Pokopia for iOS using NX2Apple. After several hours of shader compilation, the build failed before generating the game framework.

### Build Details

| Item | Result |
|---|---|
| Game | Pokémon Pokopia |
| Title ID | `0400A3A01EE4C000` |
| Game version | v655360 |
| Xcode | 27.2 |
| Shader chain | `adec7d81d970` |
| Shaders | 131,410 / 131,426 succeeded |
| Shader directory | 137 GB |
| Final framework | 27 GB (after manual recovery) |

### Issue

After shader compilation completed, the GUI build failed with:

```text
cp: .../dm/games/0400A3A01EE4C000/pso_manifest.tsv:
No such file or directory

FAIL: copy shader tables
build_ipa.sh exit code 1
```

The active engine profile was missing `pso_manifest.tsv`.

After manually creating a minimal manifest, restarting the GUI build caused the lengthy shader build process to run again instead of continuing from the failed framework stage.

I experienced this twice.

### Workaround

I verified that the existing packed iOS shader library matched the active shader chain and game profile.

Then I ran `build_ipa.sh` directly with `DM_FRAMEWORK_ONLY`, reusing the compiled shaders.

Result:

```text
xcodebuild (Release, unsigned, the game framework
DmGame0400A3A01EE4C000 with its own host)

done: .../DmGame0400A3A01EE4C000.framework
(27G; build_shell.sh embeds it in the shell)

FRAMEWORK BUILD SUCCESS
```

This successfully generated the 27 GB game framework without recompiling the shaders.

The framework has not yet been tested on an iPhone.

### Suggestions

1. Could NX2Apple handle a missing `pso_manifest.tsv` automatically instead of failing after hours of shader compilation?
2. Could the GUI support resuming from the failed framework stage when a valid compiled shader library already exists?

Thanks for your work on NX2Apple!

I run the app the launcher built.

1.2.3

### What happens, and when

The Mac app starts and the loading screen is drawn. About 72 frames (under 2 s) after the first frame, the first command buffer fails with a GPU page fault. macOS then ignores every later submission from the app, so the picture stays on the loading screen for good while the game and its audio keep running. It happens on every run. I never get past the loading screen.

First failure (fence 83, frame 72):

[RED] command buffer error details fence=83: Error Domain=MTL4CommandQueueErrorDomain Code=1 ...
  Error Domain=MTL4CommandQueueErrorDomain Code=2 "Caused GPU Address Fault Error (0000000b:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorPageFault)"

From fence 84 on, every submission fails with:
Code=5 "Ignored (for causing prior/excessive GPU errors) (00000004:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorSubmissionsIgnored)"
This repeats until I stop the app (more than 1,500 frames, up to fence 1555). The host does not crash; it exits cleanly on SIGTERM.

Earlier in the same log there is one other [RED] line:
[RED] shader 1156eacb8bf7c705_b writes output 1 and a pipeline blends with it as the second source, but it has no dual-source entry point ...

The symptom looks like seedds/nxnative#1289 (Splatoon Raiders: a GPU address fault, then the picture freezes while the game keeps running). I do not know whether the cause is the same.

### What you expected

The loading screen to finish and the game to reach the title, as in the game's README for 1.8d.310c (60 fps in a Classic Match on the Mac).

none (for the attached log I started the app's own `nxnative` binary with DM_LAUNCHER=0, which only hides the settings window; there is no env.txt for this title)

[00:46:23] FAIL: the frameworks in DM_SHELL_FRAMEWORKS (above)

### Build log

```text
game framework: ~/Downloads/Switch Rom/0100E65002BB8000_build/shell-framework/DmGame0100E65002BB8000.framework
[准备共用应用] /bin/bash ~/Library/Application Support/NX2Apple/engine/f25fa9562ee96d06f1e6412dbb91aab2b7035ec1-7b57c0235df8/dm/ios/tools/build_shell.sh --prepare-xcode
[RED] ~/Library/Application Support/NX2Apple/shell/frameworks/DmGame0100E65002BB8000.framework: built without a host in the framework (loader 'FR'). Rebuild this game for the shared app.
[00:46:23] FAIL: the frameworks in DM_SHELL_FRAMEWORKS (above)
```

### Root cause analysis

1. Since upstream's per-framework host change (#451), `dm/ios/tools/build_ipa.sh` sets `FW_LOADER=FH` when `FRAMEWORK_ONLY` (`--shell-framework`) is non-empty, links `dm/host` into `DmGame<titleID>.framework/DmGame<titleID>` (exporting `_dm_*` host symbols), and passes `--loader FH` (plus `"launcher": "dm/launcher.json"`) to `gen_manifest.py`.
2. `dm/ios/tools/build_shell.sh` line 55 enforces:
   ```python
   if m.get('loader') != 'FH': sys.exit(f'[RED] {p}: built without a host in the framework (loader {m.get("loader")!r}). Rebuild this game for the shared app.')
   ```
3. However, the bundled `nxb 0.9.0` (`Contents/Resources/nxbuild/nxb` in `v1.3.0-rc2`) still builds `--shell-framework` using the pre-#451 M1 container layout:
   - `DmGame<titleID>.framework/DmGame<titleID>` only exports `_dmgame_image_marker` without the `dm/host` symbols;
   - `DmGame<titleID>.framework/game.manifest.json` is written with `"loader": "FR"` and `"app binary": "dm/launcher.json"` instead of `"loader": "FH"` and `"launcher": "dm/launcher.json"`.
4. As a result, any iOS game built for the shared shell app with `nxb 0.9.0` enabled fails at `build_shell.sh --prepare-xcode`. Turning off the experimental `nxb` builder in Settings (falling back to `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py`) produces a valid `loader: "FH"` framework.

body:
With nxb as the default builder (v1.3.0), an iPhone / iPad build for the shared app produces a framework the shared app refuses. The install stops with:

```
The shared app could not be prepared: .../NX2Apple/shell/frameworks/DmGame0400486024DEC000.framework:
built without a host in the framework (loader 'FR'). Rebuild this game for the shared app.
```

```
launcher ──▶ nxb build <nup> --progress json --work-dir <work> --shell-framework <work>/shell-framework --team-id <team>
               │  exits 0
               ▼
           DmGame<id>.framework   game.manifest.json  "loader": "FR", no host linked in
               │
build_shell.sh:55  (patch 0077, #451)  loader != 'FH'  ─✗  refused
```

Root cause: nxb 0.9.0 builds the upstream route C framework, a pure module container. `crates/nxb-build/src/ios/manifest.rs` writes `("loader", s("FR"))` with no option to change it, and the binary links no host. Its only exports are `_DmGame0400486024DEC000VersionNumber`, `_DmGame0400486024DEC000VersionString` and `_dmgame_image_marker`, with no `dm_glue_start_game` from `ShellGlue.m`. The fork's patch 0077 makes the NSP script build `--shell-framework` with `FW_LOADER=FH` (`build_ipa.sh:218`) and makes `build_shell.sh` refuse anything else. nxb doesn't implement that patch, and it doesn't exit with code 4 for `--shell-framework`, so the launcher never falls back to the script.

| | NSP script | nxb 0.9.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `--shell-framework` loader | `FH` (host linked in) | `FR` |
| `ShellGlue` / `dm_glue_*` in the binary | yes | no |
| accepted by `build_shell.sh` | yes | no |

Workaround: Settings, turn off **Build with nxb**, and build the game for iPhone / iPad again.

Possible fixes, either one works:
- The launcher sends `--shell-framework` builds to the script until nxb builds an `FH` framework (`BuildStore+Run.swift`, next to the exit code 4 fallback).
- nxb returns exit code 4 for `--shell-framework` until it links the host, so the existing fallback picks it up.

Seen on: NX2Apple 1.3.0 built locally from `a04ccf12` (engine `f25fa956`), bundled nxb 0.9.0, macOS 27.2, Ocarina of Time `0400486024DEC000` v131072, iPhone target.
title: Shared app refuses games built by nxb: --shell-framework gives loader FR, no host

`sparse_gpu_wrote` (`nvn_mtl.m`) needs a validity/generation check before dereferencing the texture object, matching the magic check in the `RED_ONCE` at line ~3465.

body:
### Idea

When several people play on one Mac, they share one save per game, so one player's progress overwrites another's. The engine has a single Switch user (`dm/host/hle_account.c` always lists one `Uid`), and the Mac app keeps one save folder per game: `~/Library/Application Support/nxnative/<title ID>/save`, or `<library>/save/<title ID>` beside a library folder.

The launcher could keep a list of players and start every game with the chosen player's own save folder. No engine change is needed for this: `dm/mac/launcher.c` keeps a `DM_SAVE` that is already set, so the launcher's Play can hand the game a different one.

### Plan

- **A player picker in the top bar** (next to search): the current player's name, and a menu to switch players, add a new one, rename the current one or remove one. The choice is remembered.
- **Player 1 is the save you already have.** The default player adds nothing to the environment, so nobody's saves move and nothing changes for anyone who never adds a second player.
- **Every other player gets `DM_SAVE=<usual save's parent>/profiles/<player>/<usual name>`**, for example `…/nxnative/<title ID>/profiles/ana/save`. The host's `.work`, `.new` and `_device` folders land beside it, inside the player's folder.
- **Shared pipeline list.** `DM_PSO_USER` points at the game's usual `pso_user.tsv`, so what the game learned about its shaders is not learned again for each player.
- **Cloud saves stay with Player 1.** A cloud save is one per game (`dm/host/save_sync.c`), so other players start with `DM_SAVE_SYNC=0`. A later step could give each player their own cloud subfolder.
- **Removing a player keeps their folder on disk.** Adding a player with the same name brings the saves back.
- Both Play paths use it: the desktop Play button and console mode (`GameStart.environment`).

Later, in separate steps:
- Saves sheet (copy to and from a device) and "Open saves folder" follow the current player.
- The iOS shell gets the same picker (`DM_SAVE` in `main.m`).
- Optional: several Switch users in `hle_account.c`, for games that show a user picker (upstream, seedds/nxnative).

### Done when

- Two players can each play the same game on one Mac, and neither overwrites the other's save.
- Player 1's existing saves and cloud saves work as before.
- Switching players needs no restart of the launcher.
- Tests cover the save folder and environment for each player, and the store (create, rename, remove, persistence).

A working prototype of the Mac part is on the branch `feat/player-profiles`, ready to become a PR if the idea gets a yes.
title: Idea: players in the launcher, each with their own saves

body:
### Idea

The library shows the name from the Mac app's bundle (`CFBundleDisplayName`). The packing script takes it from `control.nacp`, the first non-empty title, which is usually American English and for some games Korean or Japanese. A player with the launcher in Chinese sees an English or Korean name for a game that has an official Chinese name.

### Plan

1. Engine (a patch here, a pull request to seedds/nxnative in parallel): `dm/tools/nacp.py` gets `names()`, the title of each of the 16 languages of the title area. `dm/mac/pack_app.py --control` writes them into Info.plist as `DMTitleNames` (`{"en-US": …, "ja": …, "zh-Hans": …}`), and the NSP script passes the control data that lists the game's languages. Offline, from the game's own data, no new download.
2. Launcher: the library reads `DMTitleNames` and shows the name of the launcher's language (Chinese: Simplified, then Traditional, Traditional first on a Traditional Chinese system; English: en-US, then en-GB; the others by their code). The library, the hero, the sheets and the console mode show it, and the search finds a game by either name. `name` in `library.json` stays the bundle name, the names are only what is shown. A game whose app has no `DMTitleNames` (built before this) or no name in that language shows the bundle name as before.
3. Later, optional: for apps built before this, a lookup by title ID in titledb's regional lists (as the artwork already does with US.en), which are large, so only when the player turns it on.

### Done when

A game built after this shows its own name in the launcher's language when its control data has one, and switching the launcher's language switches the name.

body:
## Game and title ID

CHRONO CROSS: THE RADICAL DREAMERS EDITION, `0100AC20128AC000`. Update `v131072` (1.0.2). The source package contains program 0 (collection menu), program 1 (CHRONO CROSS), and program 2. Program 0 main build is `ebec2b1f2c43c4f35447aa8098786cf5`. Program 1 main build is `7a54fb69872aa45a58e58e80f8672f9a`.

## Where it runs

iPhone shared App, installed through NX2Apple. Reproduced on iPhone Duo, iOS 27.3, with NX2Apple 1.2.1 (build 1.2.1), engine `7249ee9f95ed728aff9a86395330d10d4c91fb5c-537c69b35c23`, framework loader FH, and shader chain `b-223f10d34f97`. The Mac host reproduced the same exit.

## What happens, and when

1. Build the collection into the shared iPhone App.
2. Launch the collection menu and choose Start for CHRONO CROSS.
3. The game exits. The phone and Mac logs both show that program 0 requested program 1, which the packed host did not have.

```text
[dm] [RED] oe::ExecuteProgram(1, 0 bytes of parameters:): the host has only this program; it ends
[dm] received oe::ExecuteProgram: graceful exit
```

Expected: Start launches program 1 and its data within the shared App. The Mac reproduction exited with status 0 after the switch request.

## Verified workaround and current source

Building the source title with `--title-id 0100AC20128AC000 --program 1` and packaging `0100AC20128AC001` as a separate library entry let the user launch CHRONO CROSS directly on the iPhone. This verification covers the direct launch.

On source review of NX2Apple `00e67a11`, the shared framework build still requires separate RomFS storage, while the multi-program packing path expects the programs and their data in one app. The reproduction above is from 1.2.1. Related multi-program work is tracked in [#483](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/issues/483) and [#484](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/pull/484). This report focuses on the shared iPhone App.

- [x] Nothing attached contains keys, game files, or extracted game data.
title: CHRONO CROSS: Start exits when program 1 is missing from the shared iPhone app

body:
### This is

An idea

### What you would like

Add Korean (`ko`) to the launcher languages, next to en, de, fr, it, ja, sv and zh. Today a Mac, PC, iPhone or iPad set to Korean shows the launcher and the shell in English.

### Plan

Follow the Japanese PR (#866) and its issue (#718):

- Add `frontend/l10n/ko.json` with every key of `en.json`, in the same order, with the same placeholders, and a `_language` block (`한국어`, locales `ko` and `korean`).
- Generate the iOS shell catalogs from it with `tools/l10n_shell_catalogs.py`.
- Add Korean to the same places #866 touched: `CFBundleLocalizations` in `build-mac-app.yml`, `tools/try-local`, the iOS demo `project.yml` and `Info.plist`, and a fork-only engine patch for `dm/ios/project-shell.yml` (like 0086); the language list tests in Swift, Qt and `tools/tests`.
- Some tests use `ko-KR`, `ko_kr` and `Korean_Korea` as the example of a language without a file (`LanguageListTests.swift`, `test_i18n_detect.py`, `test_language_list.py`). They would move to another language without a file, for example Portuguese (`pt-BR`, `pt_br`, `Portuguese_Brazil`), and a new check would say that `ko-KR` picks Korean.
- Capture the changed views in Korean with `NX_LAUNCHER_CAPTURE_DIR` / `NX_CAPTURE_LANG=ko` (Mac) and the shell captures (iPhone and iPad) for the PR.

How the file is made: an AI tool writes the first draft, a second pass checks terms and placeholders across all keys, and I (a Korean speaker) read it in the captures and on my own iPhone and iPad, and correct what reads wrong. I would say so in the PR.

### Questions

1. Do you want Korean in the launcher?
2. Is a file drafted by a tool and read by one Korean speaker enough?

The game consistently force-closes approximately 2–3 seconds after launching.

I expected Donkey Kong Bananza to launch successfully, initialize the game, and reach the title screen without force-closing.

### What happens, and when

Two engine bugs stopped Devil May Cry (build 883F54C67475ABAE). I fixed both and the game now runs on my Mac. I can't open the upstream PR myself, so I'm attaching the fix as a diff against seedds/nxnative main (b2d46b8), with a test for each bug.

1. The rewrite stopped at "jump table 2082ac". The bounds check is folded into a conditional compare: and w18,w8,#0x7fffffff; ccmp w18,#0xc,#2,ne; b.hi; ldrsw x18,[x11,x18,lsl #2]; add x18,x18,x11; br x18. I added jump_ccmp_guard to patch_nso.py, tried after every other form, so other games' output is unchanged. It only accepts when the failed-condition nzcv takes the b.hi (C set, Z clear), the run is straight-line with no branch landing inside it, and the table base has a single adrp+add writer. Test: CcmpGuard in dm/tools/tests/test_jump_copies.py (14 cases on synthetic code, no game data).

2. After the intro movie the game calls StopAudioOut and then FlushAudioOutBuffers. The host did not take over Flush, so the SDK version searched its own audout session table, found nothing and read address 0 (SIGSEGV at sdk+0x93684), the same class of bug as SetAudioOutVolume in STEINS;GATE. I added it to hle_audio.c: stopped returns false and does nothing; started returns true and sends the unplayed buffers back as released, with the backend stopped and restarted around it. Test: test_flush in dm/host/tests/t_audio.c.

What I checked: the game converts and plays on an M4 Max (the stopped path of Flush). My own checker passes all 14 jump table cases. I could not run t_audio myself; it needs a Mac build. The started path of Flush is covered by that test but no game I have exercises it.

However, the opening cinematic exhibits severe graphical corruption, audio/video desynchronization, and progressively slower video playback. During testing, macOS experienced a GPU firmware lockup followed by a WindowServer watchdog timeout, returning me to the login screen. Steps to reproduce Import the game's NUP file into NX2Apple. body:
### Game and title ID

No Man's Sky, 0100853015E86000

### Base game and update versions

v0 + update v5177344 (display version 7.3.0), SDK 20.5.17, NVN, Havok, Wwise

### Where it runs

Mac app (built for This Mac, `--gpu none`)

### Device, chip and RAM

MacBook / Mac with Apple M4

### NX2Apple version

v1.2.1 (engine 7249ee9f95ed, shader chain 223f10d34f97), with the local changes listed below

### What happens, and when

There is no profile, so the game uses the provisional profile from the survey. With the changes below it boots, shows the title and renders the "SELECT GAME MODE" menu correctly at 30 fps. After a mode is chosen (about 83 s, frame ~3100), the main thread spins forever in the texture streamer and no further frame is presented.

### What I changed locally to get this far

1. **Shaders: HGPAK reader** (`shader_split.py` `hgpak_shaders`, `profile_guess.py` `oodle_hgpak`)
   - The game keeps everything in `NMSARC.*.pak`, which is Hello Games HGPAK version 2:
     - Header: magic, version, file count, chunk count, compressed flag, data start.
     - Per file: 32 bytes, made of a 16-byte hash, a virtual offset and a length.
     - Then one u64 compressed length per chunk.
   - Chunks are 16-byte aligned, Oodle Kraken (decoded with the game's own decoder through `DM_OODLE_SERVE`), and each decodes to exactly 0x20000 bytes. The last chunk is zero-padded; passing the shorter length makes the game's Oodle abort the host.
   - File 0 is the manifest, one name per line in index order.
   - The shaders are `NMSARC.Shaders.pak` → `shaders/code/bin/switch/*.nvb`. Each holds a u64 header length, then blocks of a 0x20-byte block header (0x20, hash, 0, length) followed by the data: the control section first, then the code area.
   - Result: 20,933 shaders, 10,251 unique, all passing `check()`.
2. **Boot SIGBUS at `main+0x12edc0`** (`dm/host/main.c`): the game upper-cases `argv[0]` and its `-`/`+` options in place. `g_argv` points at read-only literals, so they are now `strdup`'d before `SetHostArgv`.
3. **`nvnMemoryPoolMap` on a CPU_NO_ACCESS pool** (`hle_nvn.c`): NMS maps its 61 GB virtual pool (flags 0x221) and memcpys texture data into it (`main+0x2429264`). The host's memory is now returned instead of NULL.
4. **No first frame** (`hle_nvn.c` `nvnSyncWait`): before its first frame the game polls (~5,000/s) a sync that was never fenced. A never-fenced sync now reports ALREADY_SIGNALED. On hardware its syncpoint threshold 0 is already reached (my assumption). Behind `DM_NVN_SYNC_FRESH=signaled`, on by default for this title only.
5. **Crash `-[NvPkg parentTexture]: unrecognized selector`** in `image_prepare` (`nvn_mtl.m`): `tex_mtl` can return the NvPkg holder. Its `->tex` is now used.
6. **Compute writes dropped** ("texture bound to an image slot lacks the shader-write usage", sparse textures with flags 0x20 and no IMAGE flag): `image_prepare` upgraded `tex_mtl` of the image flavour, while `img_binding` binds the `tex_fast_rid` object. That object is now checked and upgraded too.
7. **`virtual pool: more than 1024 separate mapped runs`**: `NVRUN` was raised to 16384 and the run scratch buffer made static.
8. **Diagnostics**: `DM_PROBE_POLL=main+<offset>`, `kill -TERM` writing `DM_HLECOUNT` plus all NVN call counts (`DM_NVN_COUNT=1`), and `DM_NVN_SIZELOG=N`.

Still unimplemented and seen: `nvnDeviceRegisterFastClearColorui`, `nvnCommandBufferSetControlMemoryCallbackEnabled`, and primitive type 8 (patches: 8 draws skipped).

### The open hang (texture streaming pool exhausted)

- **Pool:** the streamer uses a physical pool of 0x19000000 bytes (400 MB = 6400 × 64 KB pages, flags 0x10a). Its free-page count is at `main+0x41673b0 + 0x8858` and starts at 0x1900. Over 83 s it is decremented about 4,100 times and never incremented:
  - Page alloc `main+0x23ae90c`: 10,126 calls.
  - Page free `main+0x23aebe4`: 0 calls. It is reached only through `0x1631900` (page resize).
- **Who holds the pages:** at `0x2429ea8`, 2,964 textures took 6,102 pages for their base data (texture + 0x1f8 sub-struct). These are mostly sparse 256×256 / 256×512 BC textures of 0x10000–0x60000 bytes. The host's storage sizes look right to me (for example, 256×256, 5 levels, format 0x4e → 0x20000).
- **The loop:** `main+0x16f63e0` evicts streamed mips when free KB < `*[GOT 0x3130810]` (0x3c00) or < the request (0xc000). Every one of the ~3,200 textures in its list fails the first check: streamed mips (+0x258) = 0. So nothing can be evicted, the caller `0x2429a80` retries, and the frame never ends.
- **Same in handheld mode** (`DM_OPMODE=0`).

My guess is that the game loads more base textures than it does on hardware, or that the menu/space scene's textures should be released when the mode starts. I did not find which. Notes with all addresses: happy to attach them.

### Which step failed

Shader capture or shader split

### The message

There is no error message and no red line. The step never finishes and never fails: it freezes, with CPU activity at zero.

Stage lines from one run (a terminal run of the same engine with J=8, NX2Apple 1.1.0, Tears of the Kingdom), progress frozen from 5:10 on:

```
[11:46:08] [4/7] shader split · splitting: 94%, 285,600/304,243 files, 4:40 · ETA 0:42
[11:46:38] [4/7] shader split · splitting: 99%, 303,856/304,243 files, 5:10 · ETA 0:00
[11:47:08] [4/7] shader split · splitting: 99%, 303,856/304,243 files, 5:40
...
[11:54:10] [4/7] shader split · splitting: 99%, 303,856/304,243 files, 12:42
```

Each game stalls at its own fixed count, run after run:
- Tears of the Kingdom: exactly 303,856 / 304,243 (every run, on 1.1.0 and 1.2.2, with 24 workers and with J=8). The 387 files left are the last 25 batches of 16.
- The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (0400486024DEC000): exactly 170,960 / 186,587 on both 1.2.2 and 1.2.3 (about 977 batches unfinished), so it is not always the end of the list.
- A third game left running overnight never got past about 5% of its shader split.

Possibly related: #489 (same game and update, also stalls at 99%). The signature is different: in #489 one worker is busy at about 98% CPU on one heavy batch and the build finishes after roughly 9 minutes. Here every process is at 0% CPU, every worker is blocked in write(), and it never finishes (the logs below sat on the final count for roughly 28 and 37 minutes before I stopped them).

State while frozen (sampled with `sample`):
- All processes at 0.0% CPU, state S. No crash reports.
- shader_split.py: main thread waiting on a lock, one thread in poll(), one thread blocked in write() for the whole sample.
- Every pool worker sampled (all 8 in the J=8 run): main thread blocked in write() for the whole sample.
- build_ipa_from_nsp.py: main thread blocked in read(), waiting for the next line.

```
shader_split.py, 5 s sample
  main thread : _PyMutex_LockTimed -> __psynch_cvwait   (waiting on a lock)
  thread 2    : select.poll -> poll
  thread 3    : os.write -> write                       (blocked the whole sample)
pool worker (all 8 in the J=8 run, 2 s sample each)
  main thread : os.write -> write                       (blocked the whole sample)
build_ipa_from_nsp.py
  main thread : TextIOWrapper.readline -> read          (waiting for the next line)
```

Other things I tried: the default 24 workers and J=8 (same freeze point), and updating the app (1.1.0, 1.2.2, 1.2.3: same freeze). The last Tears of the Kingdom files in the split's list (index 303,856 onward) are small (`VolumeStats/*.vsts.zs`, `WorldMgr/WorldParam/*.bgyml`, all under about 26 KB), so it does not look like one oversized file. I could not tell which pipe the workers are writing to. I have the full process samples and can attach them or run anything else that helps.

### The message

我在 Windows 上使用 NS Port Builder 打包多款游戏，多个不同游戏都出现同一条红色提示：
[RED] this game compiles its shaders at run time, and upstream captures them by booting the game in the Mac host — which needs a Mac, or a Mac virtual machine on this PC. The game's files are extracted, so a Mac can finish the build from the same work folder (its shader/ and extract/ are reused).
我没有 Mac，也没有 Mac 虚拟机。
这些游戏大多是虚幻引擎或者 LÖVE 引擎，都是运行时编译着色器。
想问下：
1. 是否存在不需要 Mac、在 Windows 上直接捕获这类着色器的方案？
2. 或者有没有地方可以获取这些游戏对应版本的着色器缓存文件？
谢谢。

body:
### Idea

When I add game files to the Mac library, the displayed name comes from the file or folder name. These names can contain IDs, version numbers and other details, so the library is harder to read and search.

The launcher already uses TitleDB to find artwork by title ID. Could it also use the game name from TitleDB when the ID is known?

For example, a file named `World War Z [0100A17016974000].nsp` could appear as `World War Z` in the library.

### Proposed behavior

- Look up the name by title ID and use it in the library.
- Prefer the base game when TitleDB lists several products for the same ID, as the artwork selector does in #632.
- If the game is missing from the US list, try another regional list. For example, the Japanese version of World War Z is in the Japanese list.
- Keep the existing name if no match is found or the database is unavailable.
- Cache the results so the library still works offline.

The lookup should also consider names from built apps and avoid replacing a more accurate name with the wrong edition or bundle.

### Related work

- #403 and #632 use TitleDB for artwork and describe cases where one title ID has multiple products.
- #688 and #824 cover sorting the library by its displayed names.

I tested a local prototype with my library, including the Japanese version of World War Z. I would be happy to work on this if the idea fits the project and a maintainer adds it to a milestone.

body:
### Idea

Console mode works, but it is still a list of games with a few sheets. I would like to take it to the level of Steam's TV mode: something you use from the couch with only a controller, from picking a game to changing its options, managing it and coming back after it quits or crashes.

Before writing any code, I made a mockup and a playable prototype, and I would like your go (or your changes) on the direction first.

### Try it

**https://koshindai.github.io/NX2Apple/**

- Controller: Chrome or Safari, press any button once. Firefox-based browsers on a Mac see the controller but get no input.
- Keyboard: arrows to move, return for A, esc for B, X and Y, Q and E for L and R, M for the main menu, V for the quick menu, H for Home.
- The bar at the top switches the button glyphs (Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo) and restarts the prototype.

It is a mockup: games and numbers are placeholders, and nothing touches your library.

### Watch it

[![The prototype driven with a controller: Home, a game page, Launch options, Manage, the main menu, the Library filters, then starting a game](https://koshindai.github.io/NX2Apple/shots/console-mode.gif)](https://koshindai.github.io/NX2Apple/shots/console-mode.mp4)

A 40-second walkthrough: Home, a game page, Launch options, Manage, the main menu, the Library and its filters, then starting a game and coming back to its page. [Full size video (MP4)](https://koshindai.github.io/NX2Apple/shots/console-mode.mp4).

### Screens

**Home.** The game in focus fills the background. Rows for Continue playing, Ready to play and Needs attention. Up reaches Search.

![Home](https://koshindai.github.io/NX2Apple/shots/1-home.png)

---

**Game page.** Play, with last played, play time and saves. Then Controls, Launch options and Manage, and the tabs on LB and RB.

![Game page](https://koshindai.github.io/NX2Apple/shots/2-game.png)

---

**Launch options.** The game's existing settings, changed with left and right. A dot marks what differs from the tested defaults, and a setting that depends on another says so.

![Launch options](https://koshindai.github.io/NX2Apple/shots/3-launch-options.png)

---

**Main menu**, opened with Menu over the Library. The sections of console mode, back to the desktop and quit.

![Main menu over the library](https://koshindai.github.io/NX2Apple/shots/4-main-menu.png)

### What changes (phase 1, the launcher only)

- **Home**: Continue playing, Ready to play and Needs attention rows, with the focused game's artwork behind.
- **Library**: filters on L and R (All, Ready on Mac, Not compiled, Needs game data), sort and display options on Y.
- **Game page**: Play with last played and play time, then Controls, Launch options and Manage, and tabs for Overview, Saves, Build and Cheats.
- **Launch options**: the existing settings, changed with left and right, with what differs from the tested defaults marked, and a reset.
- **Manage**: compile again, saves, cheats, artwork, remove, delete. Actions that need the desktop (Show in Finder, Show log, importing cheats) say so and switch to it.
- **Confirmation** before anything that loses something, with the safe choice focused.
- **Search** with an on-screen keyboard, **Builds** with Stop, **Controls** per game (layout and All controllers are player 1).
- **Main menu** on Menu/+ (Home, Library, Builds, Search, Settings, back to the desktop) and **quick menu** on View/− (controllers, frame rate overlay).
- **Settings**: start in console mode, offer it when a controller connects, vibration, button glyphs, the Home button step on macOS 27.
- **After a crash**: what happened, the last save time, Play again.
- Navigation follows Steam's: sections from the main menu, L and R only for tabs inside a screen, A opens, X plays now, B goes back, hints in the glyphs of the controller in use.

### Later (phase 2, the engine)

A short press on Home opens a menu over the running game (Resume, Quit, then frame rate and controllers). This would be a separate proposal once phase 1 is settled. See "What the engine would need" below.

### What it needs

Most of the data is there already: launch options, cloud saves state and last session, cheats, controller layouts and players, battery, builds and Stop, delete and remove, start in console mode.

New in the launcher:
- the new console mode UI (screens, focus navigation, menus over a screen);
- session tracking: last played and play time per game (the Mac launcher records no sessions today);
- shader progress on the Starting screen from the live game;
- search with an on-screen keyboard, library sort and filters, console mode settings.

Still to check: the step details of a running build, and the Recently compiled and Size on disk sorts.

### What the engine would need (seedds/nxnative)

Phase 1 can ship without any engine change. These would make it sturdier. Each would go to seedds/nxnative as a PR first, and here as a patch, as CONTRIBUTING.md asks.

1. **A clean-exit signal**, for the "The game stopped" screen. The game ends with `exit(0)` both when the guest finishes and when its window closes (`front_mac.m`), and a crash leaves nothing the launcher can read: today only `.cheats-running-<title>` (`hle_cheats.c`) survives an unclean exit, and only with cheats on. Proposal: the host writes a run marker when the game starts and removes it on every clean exit (or writes how the run ended). The launcher shows the screen when the marker is still there.
2. **Start progress the launcher can read.** The pipeline prebuild runs in the game process before the first frame and logs `pipeline prebuild: N of M pairs` (`nvn_mtl.m`). The launcher can parse that line, but a small status file (stage, done, total) would not break when the wording changes.
3. **A "first frame on screen" signal.** The launcher ends its Starting screen when it loses the focus to the game, or after 20 seconds (`LiveConsoleDriver.swift`). The same status file could say when the window is up and the first frame is shown, so Starting ends exactly then.

No engine change needed for:
- the frame rate overlay in the quick menu: the existing Performance HUD (`DM_METAL_HUD`), already a launch option;
- last played and play time: the launcher sees the game start and quit;
- rumble, language, console mode, render scale, cheats, cloud saves, controller layouts and players: existing `DM_` switches (`DM_RUMBLE`, `DM_LANG`, `DM_OPMODE`, `DM_RENDER_SCALE`, `DM_CHEATS`, `DM_SAVE_SYNC`, `DM_HID_MAP`, `DM_PAD_MERGE`).

Phase 2, later and in its own proposal: the in-game menu on a short Home press, built on hold-to-quit (`front_mac.m`, `home_quit.h`). The host already takes the Home button, tells the game it lost the focus (`dm_focus_set`) and blocks its input while the prompt shows. The iPhone build's in-game menu (patches 0068 and 0069) is the model for how it behaves. Related: #617.

This list comes from a first read of the code. Going through each screen in detail will likely find more, and the development plan will list it.

### How should I send it?

I work from a fork, so I cannot stack PRs the way you do: a PR from my fork can only target a branch of this repository, never the branch of another of my PRs. This is a large change, and I would like to send it in small steps you can review one at a time (the navigation shell first, then each screen, then session tracking). Which way do you prefer?

1. You create a branch here (for example `console-mode`). My PRs target it one step at a time, and a last PR merges it into `main`.
2. One PR at a time into `main`, with the new console mode behind a setting that is off by default, so a half-built screen never reaches users and each step stays small.
3. Each PR built on the previous one and still aimed at `main`: it carries the earlier commits, says which PR it depends on and which commits to review, and I rebase it once the one below is merged.
4. One PR with one commit per step.

The engine parts would go to seedds/nxnative first, as CONTRIBUTING.md asks, each as a patch here too. Tell me if you would rather have them in a separate issue.

### Done when

- You say whether this direction is a go, and what to change before it is.
- We agree on how the work comes in (above).
- Then I write the development plan, and the issue goes into a milestone.

### This is

A problem

### What happens, or what you would like

On a Mac whose `python3` is the one macOS ships (`/usr/bin/python3`, Python 3.9.6), the pre-push hook stops a push that touches `frontend/l10n/` or `frontend/Sources/`, even when no Python file changed:

```
python3 -m unittest discover -s frontend-qt/tests
FAILED (errors=9, skipped=36)
```

The 9 errors are all in `frontend-qt/tests/test_win.py` and come from Python 3.10 features:

- 5 × `TypeError: write_text() got an unexpected keyword argument 'newline'`, from `nspb_qt/win/shim.py` line 700 (`sc.write_text(body, encoding='utf-8', newline='\n')`). `Path.write_text(newline=)` was added in Python 3.10.
- 4 × `TypeError: 'staticmethod' object is not callable` (`VenvWheelsTest`, `InstallFailureHintTest`): calling a `staticmethod` object directly also needs Python 3.10.

The same tests pass with Python 3.14 (`325 tests, OK, skipped=37`).

`frontend-qt/README.md` says two things: the table at line 15 says **Python 3.9+**, the setup steps at line 134 say **Python 3.10+**. The hook runs plain `python3`, so with the system Python a contributor cannot push a launcher change, and the message does not say why.

Found while preparing #798, which changes no Python file.

### What you expected

One of:

- the README says 3.10+ everywhere, and the hook (or `tools/githooks.py`) checks the version and says "Python 3.10 or newer is needed for the Qt front end tests" instead of 9 errors; or
- the code and tests keep working on 3.9 (`write_text` without `newline=`, `open(..., 'w', newline='\n')` instead; call the function through the class instead of the raw `staticmethod`).

### NX2Apple version

main at 6f577f43 (after v1.2.1)

### Computer and OS

Apple M2, macOS 27.0.1, `/usr/bin/python3` 3.9.6 (Command Line Tools)

Not needed: the problem is in the repository's pre-push check, not in the app.

### Which step failed

Prepare Xcode, app build or IPA pack

### The message

## Summary

Building Hollow Knight: Silksong fails deterministically at the "game framework" step. The shader step completes successfully and produces `shader/ios/b-223f10d34f97.img` (plus a `.key`), but the framework step then tries to copy the shader libraries from a directory `shader/ios/b-223f10d34f97/` that does not exist, rsync fails, and the build aborts with `FAIL: copy the shader libraries` / `build_ipa.sh exit code 1`.

## Environment

- NX2Apple 1.2.1 (latest; app reports up to date)
- Engine: tried both the Stable and Experimental channels — identical failure on both
- Mac: MacBook Air (Mac16,13), Apple silicon
- macOS 26.6.2 (25G83)
- Xcode 27.2 (Metal compiler 32023.922 / metalfe-32023.922.4, per build log)
- Target: install on device (iPhone 17), personal signing team

## Game

- Hollow Knight: Silksong, version 1.0.30000
- Title ID 010013C00E930000 (org.nxnative.010013c00e930000)
- Base NSP (v0) + update v655360

## Steps to reproduce

1. Add the Silksong base NSP and the v655360 update in NX2Apple.
2. Build the game (Install on device).
3. All steps pass through "iOS shaders" (2,450 of 2,450 ready).
4. The "game framework" step fails within seconds.

## Expected

The framework step copies the shader libraries that the shader step produced, and the build proceeds to the Xcode compile.

## Actual

`build_framework.log` in full:

```
[22:36:10] app: Hollow Knight: Silksong 1.0.30000 (org.nxnative.010013c00e930000), language en-US, frame-rate counter on
[22:36:10] generate Gen/ (host sources, embedded modules, tables)
[22:36:10] launcher: DM_OPMODE DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE DM_LANG DM_PICTURE_FIT DM_SHOW_FPS DM_TOUCH_HAPTICS DM_RUMBLE DM_RUMBLE_GAIN DM_RUMBLE_MIN DM_PRESENT_SNAP DM_PSO_MTL4 DM_PSO_PREBUILD DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD DM_METAL_HUD
[22:36:10] no pipeline archive (DM_PSO_GPUS=none)
[22:36:10] app icon: .../010013C00E930000_build/extract/v655360/icon.jpg
[22:36:10] framework: Gen/framework (modules main subsdk0 sdk, profile.tsv, game.manifest.json)
[22:36:10] xcodebuild (Release, unsigned, the game framework DmGame010013C00E930000 with its own host)
rsync(22027): error: /Users/nikogriggs/Local Files/010013C00E930000_build/shader/ios/b-223f10d34f97/: (l)stat: No such file or directory
[22:36:24] FAIL: copy the shader libraries
```

After the shader step, `shader/ios/` contains only:

- `b-223f10d34f97.img` (76,596,854 bytes)
- `b-223f10d34f97.key`

No `b-223f10d34f97/` directory is ever created.

The shader build itself finishes cleanly. The end of `dmsh_build.log` reports:

```
shaders 2450: ok 2450
shader cache: hit 0, rebuilt 2450
lost without failing: nothing
```

## What I tried

- Rebuilt with the cached shaders — same failure.
- Built fresh in a second build folder — same failure, same shader build id `b-223f10d34f97`.
- Full fresh rebuild (re-extract, re-rewrite, all 2,450 shaders recompiled) — same failure.
- Switched the engine channel from Stable to Experimental and rebuilt — same failure, byte-identical log.
- The app is on the latest version (1.2.1).

A different game (title ID 0100F43008C44000) built successfully end to end on this same Mac on 2026-11-01, producing a working IPA, so the machine, Xcode install and signing setup are known-good.

## Notes

- The log line `no pipeline archive (DM_PSO_GPUS=none)` appears just before the framework step in every failing run. If the shader library directory is normally produced by the pipeline archive step, that step being skipped for this game may be why the copy has nothing to copy.
- Full `build_framework.log` and `dmsh_build.log` are attached.

### Game, title ID and versions

Sid Meier's Civilization VII, 0100C3601518C000, base 1.0.0, update 1.5.0 (v1638400). The failure is not specific to the game: it happens for every NVN game built for the shared app.

### Built for

iPhone / iPad

### Game files

Several of these, or a base game with updates and DLC

### Computer and OS

MacBook Pro M5 Pro, macOS 27.2 (26B123), NX2Apple 1.2.0 (also seen on 1.2.0-rc5)

### Fork patches line

The 46 patches of 1.2.0 (engine pin seedds/nxnative 7249ee9). The build also carried local patches, but the failure reproduces on a clean `tools/engine.py sync` of main a19205e0 (the regression test above fails there).

### Cause

seedds/nxnative 7249ee9 (the engine pin of 1.2.0, #761) packs an NVN game's iOS shader libraries into the one file `shader/ios/b-<chain>.img` (`dm/tools/shader_lib.py`) and removes the folder `b-<chain>/`. Upstream's own readers handle both forms (`lib_has`/`lib_path` in `build_ipa.sh`, `pack_ipa.py`'s `library_map`, `stage_resources.sh`'s `sync_libraries`). The fork's `DM_FRAMEWORK_ONLY` step (patch 0050 `route-c-shell`) still runs `rsync -a --delete "$MSL_IOS/$MSLDIR/" "$OUTFW/msl/$MSLDIR/"`, and that folder no longer exists. The patch applied cleanly in the bump because the block is fork-only code. Vulkan and GL games (`vk/`, `gl/`) still have folders and are not affected.

The host already reads `b-<chain>.img` from `DM_MSL_DIR` (`nvn_mtl.m`), and the shell sets `DM_MSL_DIR` to the framework's `msl/` (`frontend-ios/Sources/ShellHost/EngineLaunchPlan.swift`), so the fix is only the copy. A PR follows.

### This is

A problem

### What happens, or what you would like

In the default iPhone route (only the game's framework, installed into the shared shell app), the build's `--env-file` never reaches the running game, so the **"Older devices (A15 / A16 and earlier)"** switch can't take effect:

- `engine/dm/ios/tools/build_ipa.sh` removes `Gen/framework/dm/env.txt` when it builds the framework.
- The shell's launch environment (`ShellHostModel.launchEnvironment` → `EngineLaunchPlan.make`) is built from the player's settings and the `env.txt` files in Documents, not from a build env file.

Super Mario Bros. Wonder (010015100B514000) was built with the switch on for an iPhone 13 Pro (A15, iOS 27.0.1). The game's log showed:

```
boot: DM_ENV_FILE_KEYS=
[dm]   more stdalloc_cap 0 key_skip 0+0 bc_cpu 0 ue_pool 0 enc_thread 0
[dm] [nvn-mtl] FATAL the Metal device Apple A15 GPU has no BC texture formats, ...
```

The app then quit itself with exit 134 when Play was pressed.

The switch also wrote the wrong variable name (`DM_TEX_BC_CPU` instead of `DM_PROF_TEX_BC_CPU`). That part is fixed in #778, but it only helps one-game IPAs while the shell route drops the file.

**Workaround:** put `DM_PROF_TEX_BC_CPU=1` in `Documents/games/<title ID>/env.txt` on the device. With that (and #776), the game runs.

**Possible fixes (your call):**
- The framework carries the switch: keep a build env file in the framework, or write `tex_bc_cpu 1` into its `profile.tsv`.
- The shell offers it as a per-game setting that sets `DM_PROF_TEX_BC_CPU`.
- The launcher writes the game's `env.txt` when it sends the game to the device.

### What you expected

With "Older devices" on, the installed game starts with `bc_cpu 1` and decodes BC textures on the CPU.

### NX2Apple version

1.1.0 (engine 641d1480021a57840b7acc15f92cbd86ecfae611-de8d83152878). The same `build_ipa.sh` line and shell code are on main at a19205e0.

Mac with Apple M1 Max, macOS 26.7.2. Device: iPhone 13 Pro (A15), iOS 27.0.1.

body:
### Idea

Today a game's picture in the library is the eShop banner titledb lists for it, or one file chosen with **Manage > Change artwork**. The same picture serves two places with different shapes: the hero (about 2.9:1 in a full-width window) and the collection card (1.8:1). Two things are missing:

- **Choice.** titledb also lists up to six 1920×1080 screenshots for most games (82 % of them in the US list). Some banners carry a promotion or show the wrong product (#403 fixed the product, not the promotions). A screenshot is often the better picture, but there is no way to pick one.
- **Framing.** The hero crops a 16:9 image by about 13 %, from the centre. When the character or the logo sits near an edge, it is cut, and nothing lets the player say which part to keep.

### Plan

**Change artwork…** opens a panel beside the library instead of a file picker:

- Two tabs, **Hero** and **Thumbnail**. Each shows the banner and the screenshots, plus **Choose file…** (or drop an image on the panel).
- The thumbnail follows the hero until another image is picked for it.
- **Framing**: a point to keep visible, placed with a click, a drag or the arrow keys. The preview shows the band the hero keeps.
- The library stays visible as a live preview. While the panel is open, the hero is drawn at its real size and scaled down, so what you frame is what you get after Save.
- **Reset**, **Cancel**, **Save**. Keyboard and controller work in the panel.
- A chosen file is copied into the launcher's own folder and resized, so moving or deleting the original changes nothing.

**Left out on purpose: the app icon.** The panel was first designed with a third tab for the built app's icon (the game's icon or the eShop one, 1024×1024). It is not in this proposal because:

- upstream's `DM_ICON` only reaches the IPA, so the Mac app's icon needs an engine patch, which should go to seedds/nxnative first;
- a new icon only shows after a rebuild, which needs its own flow;
- the game's own icon is often not available, as the extraction is not kept after a build.

It can come later as its own change.

**Related:** #403 (which product's banner, fixed by #632) and the open PR #661 (custom covers: formats, animation, install). This proposal changes how a custom image is stored (a copy per slot instead of the chosen file's path), so the two need to agree on that.

### Done when

- The panel picks and frames the hero and the thumbnail from the eShop images or a file, and Save shows the result in the library and console mode.
- Libraries saved by earlier versions keep their picture.
- Texts in the six languages, tests, before and after screenshots.

body:
## Problem

Preparing the shared app from the NX2Apple UI fails when the selected game's profile was generated provisionally by `build_ipa_from_nsp.py` and lives outside `dm/games/`.

The UI invokes `dm/ios/tools/build_shell.sh --prepare-xcode` without `DM_GAMES_DIR`. The script selects the first framework's title ID as `GAME`, then `gen_build.py` runs `make ... game_profile`; make searches `dm/games/` and the unset `DM_GAMES_DIR`, and stops with:

```text
no game profile <title ID> (neither in dm/games nor in DM_GAMES_DIR)
```

The profile does exist under the game's build folder at `profile/<title ID>/game.tsv`, and the embedded framework carries a runtime `profile.tsv`.

## Expected

The UI build should make the selected frameworks' profile roots available to `build_shell.sh` (including provisional profiles), or the script should derive them from the framework metadata before compiling the host.

## Workaround

Set `DM_GAMES_DIR` to the build's `profile/` directory when invoking `build_shell.sh`.
title: UI shell preparation fails for games with provisional profiles

### Idea

nxbuild is a new build tool in Rust. It reproduces parts of the NSP script byte for byte and is much faster there. On Wonder the extraction and the shader split take about 15 s instead of 3.5 minutes. I want players to be able to try it from the Mac launcher, as an option that is off by default.

### Plan

- The NSP script stays the driver. With `DM_EXPERIMENTAL_BUILDER=1` and `NXB_BIN` (the path of the `nxb` binary) it hands a stage to nxbuild where nxbuild supports the case. The stage names, the JSON events, the work folder and the reuse keys stay the same.
- First stages: the extraction (`nxb-extract`) and the shader split (`nxb-split`). The split is only taken when its tables have the data rows of the profile's tables.
- Everything else runs as today. A stage nxbuild does not support (a defined exit code), fails or gets wrong falls back to the Python step, with a note in the build log.
- The engine side is a patch here and a pull request to seedds/nxnative in parallel.
- The launcher gets a setting "Use experimental builder" in Settings, Tools, off by default. It passes the two variables and the path of the binary. For now the path is set by hand. A download of a signed nxbuild release with a checked SHA-256 comes once that release exists.
- Not part of this step: the shader step, the pipeline archive and the Mac app. nxbuild has them, but they do not fit the script's step one to one yet (the shader cache list, the launcher build, the icon). They follow later.

### Done when

- The option is off by default and a build without it is unchanged.
- With the option on, a Wonder build runs the extraction and the split through nxbuild with the same outputs and events as the Python run.
- Any case nxbuild cannot do falls back to the Python step and the build still finishes.
title: Experimental builder (nxbuild)

body:
## Problem

While testing `v1.1.1-rc1` on a non-APFS disk (#595), building a Mac app into a folder that already holds `<title ID>.app` immediately stops before the build starts with:

> This disk cannot replace an old Mac app.

## Cause

- PR #651 added a pre-build check in `BuildStore+Run.swift` that stops a Mac app build when `OutputVolume.supportsAppReplace` is `false` and `<title ID>.app` already exists, and prints `msg.volumeNotAPFS` on the first build.
- PR #654 (and upstream `seedds/nxnative#1190` / `5061b2a`, included in the `777a5f6c` engine pin) fixed `dm/mac/pack_app.py` so `replace_app` falls back to `swap_by_moves` when `renamex_np(RENAME_SWAP)` returns `ENOTSUP` (`Errno 45`).
- Because the pre-build stop from #651 remained in `BuildStore+Run.swift`, the launcher blocks the second build before the engine's `swap_by_moves` fallback can run.

## Fix

Remove the pre-build `appReplaceCheck` block from `BuildStore+Run.swift` so Mac app builds on non-APFS volumes proceed to the engine's `swap_by_moves` replacement, while keeping the log classifier rule for `[Errno 45]` as a fallback if a volume still fails at the OS level.
title: Mac app: the pre-build APFS check stops a second build before swap_by_moves can run

body:
### Idea

When both halves of a Nintendo Switch Joy-Con pair are connected to a Mac over Bluetooth, Apple's `GCController` framework merges `Joy-Con (L)` (`0x057E:0x2006`) and `Joy-Con (R)` (`0x057E:0x2007`) into one combined controller and drops the rail `SL` and `SR` buttons. Two people sharing one Joy-Con pair on a Mac cannot use the two halves as Player 1 and Player 2 sideways controllers as on a Switch. Meanwhile macOS already switches both Bluetooth devices into standard `0x30` 49-byte input report mode at 60 Hz, where `IOHIDManager` sees both halves separately with their full button bits, 12-bit stick axes and battery level.

### Plan

- Add a `Split Joy-Con pair into two controllers` toggle (`ControlLayout.joyconSplit`, passed to games as `DM_JOYCON_SPLIT=1`) in desktop `Settings -> Controls` and in the console mode `Controllers` sheet.
- In `LiveConsoleDriver`, when `joyconSplit` is enabled and a Joy-Con pair is present, list `Joy-Con (L)` and `Joy-Con (R)` as two separate sideways controllers with their battery levels from the `0x30` HID report and independent player slot assignments instead of the single combined `GCController` entry.
- In `dm/host/`, add `pad_joycon.h` and `pad_joycon_mac.h` (wired into `front_mac.m` when `DM_JOYCON_SPLIT=1`) so the host ignores the merged `GCController` Joy-Con entry and reads `0x057E:0x2006` and `0x057E:0x2007` non-exclusively via `IOHIDManager`, giving each half its own player slot in `g_slots` with a 90-degree sideways stick rotation and button mapping (`SL` and `SR` mapped to `L` and `R`).

### Done when

- Toggling `Split Joy-Con pair into two controllers` persists in `ControlLayout`, exports `DM_JOYCON_SPLIT=1` to the game environment, and splits a connected Joy-Con pair into `Joy-Con (L)` and `Joy-Con (R)` in the Controllers sheet.
- With `DM_JOYCON_SPLIT=1`, `dmhost` assigns separate player slots to `Joy-Con (L)` and `Joy-Con (R)` and decodes sideways sticks and buttons (`SL`, `SR`, rotated face/directional buttons and sticks) from `0x30` reports.
- Engine C unit tests (`t_pad_hid`) and Swift unit tests cover the sideways report decoder, setting plumbing and controller list splitting.

### Idea

Overcooked! 2 has no game profile in `dm/games`, so it can only be built from a provisional profile. It builds and plays on an iPad Pro 13-inch (M4), iPadOS 27.2, in the NX2Apple 1.1.0 shell with a provisional profile, but at its native 30 fps. A proper profile with the frame-step treatment — the host pacing presents at 60 fps, as the registered 30 fps games in `dm/games` do — would make it match the Mac/PC experience. If a full profile is not warranted, a documented frame-step cut for this build would help the next person.

### What the provisional survey shows

- Title ID `01006FD0080B2000` (US), update v1245184 (display 1.0.19), from the owner's own dump.
- Modules: `main` (build `616640f27b9362502d1ce10bf01eb9a6`, 65.4 MB text), `subsdk0` (NintendoSDK_movie), `sdk` (nnSdk), `rtld`.
- SDK 20.5.14; NVN; Unity IL2CPP; FMOD; NPLN 1.41.
- RomFS: 3,377 files, 4.39 GB; 1,677 UnityFS bundles.
- A provisional profile was guessed, the shell framework built, and the game ran on the device; the only visible limit is the 30 fps frame limiter.

### Plan

- Find the engine's frame limiter (the busy spin on the system tick, as in the documented cuts for other 30 fps games) in this build's `main`, and add a `FRAME_STEP` cut so the host's present pacing can drive 60 fps.
- If the limiter is beyond a clean cut, a note in GAMES.md saying so helps the next person.
- I can build, install and test on a Mac and on an iPad Pro 13-inch (M4), and provide logs and screen recordings.

### Done when

- Overcooked! 2 plays at 60 fps from a profile (Mac and/or iPad) with its logic at normal speed, verified; or
- a note records that this engine's limiter does not allow the frame-step treatment.
title: Idea: a profile and a frame-step patch for Overcooked! 2 (01006FD0080B2000)
