NX2Apple 1.1.0 (engine `641d1480021a` / `de8d83152878`), iOS, iPad mini 6 (iPad14,1, A15 GPU), `tex_bc_cpu` enabled. This is the other half of #719: once the toggle actually reaches the host, the CPU decode path does not work either.

**Symptom**

Two failures, in the order you hit them.

First, an abort on the first draw that creates a texture view:

```
[nvn-mtl] texture upgraded to allow format views ser=386 base format 30 → view format 142
_mtlValidateArgumentsForTextureViewOnDevice:1877: failed assertion
  texture view pixelFormat (MTLPixelFormatInvalid) not castable.
  source texture pixelFormat (MTLPixelFormatRG8Unorm) not compatible with texture view pixelFormat (MTLPixelFormatInvalid)
[dm] CRASH sig=6 … tex_by_id → encode_args → draw_ → mtl_exec → hNVNQueueSubmitCommands
```

(30 = `RG8Unorm`, 142 = `BC5_RGUnorm`. A15 has no BC hardware, so Metal maps BC5 to `MTLPixelFormatInvalid`.)

Get past that and the game runs at 60 fps, but every 3D surface is 1–2 pixel colour noise: geometry, UVs and draw order are all correct, and every uncompressed 2D element (HUD hearts, button prompts) renders fine. Zooming in on a floor tile shows per-pixel random colour with no 4×4 or 8×8 block structure, i.e. block bytes being read as pixels rather than a decode error.

**Root cause**

The decode is wired into `tex_desc` only; the two paths that consume that texture still assume it is compressed.

1. `dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m:1968` — `tex_desc` already creates the Metal texture in the *unpacked* format: `if (g_bc_cpu && nvn_bc_unpacked(t->d.format, &bc_unpacked, &bc_bpp)) pf = bc_unpacked;` So the base texture is RGBA8/RG8/RGBA16F, not BC.
2. `dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m:2385` — the upload path picks the GPU deswizzle branch without testing `bc_cpu`: `int use_gpu = !rb_shift && !sparse && g_nvn_deswz_gpu && mtl_addr(...)`. That branch blits the still-compressed block data at block-row pitch into the uncompressed texture (BC1 writes 2w bytes per row into a 4w-byte row). `nvn_bc_decode` is therefore never called — hence the noise. (`RED_ONCE(40)` at `:2386` fires on the fallback and is misleading here.)
3. `dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m:4609` — view formats are mapped straight through, so a BC5 view is created on an RG8 texture: `if (!(r.has_v && r.v.set_format && nvn_fmt_to_mtl(r.v.format, &view_pf, fsw) && view_pf)) …`. Same shape at `:3477` (render-target views) and `:11173` (clear views). On a Mac or an A19+ device `g_bc_cpu` is 0, the base texture *is* BC, view == base, and none of this triggers — the bug exists only on the path that exists only for A15/A16.

**One reproducible piece of evidence**

Same build, same save, `bc_cpu 1` in both cases; only the two conditions above differ.

Before (3D noisy): texture uploads report a duration no CPU decode could fit, and no decode ever runs:

```
[dm] [nvn-mtl] BC textures: this GPU has no BC support, decoding them on the CPU (profile tex_bc_cpu)
[dm] [longframe] frame 386: … texture uploads 26 first, 2.4 MB / 0.9 ms
```

After (correct 3D), the decode itself shows up, and it is cheap:

```
[dm] [nvn-mtl] BC on the CPU #0: 1100x480 format 0x4b levels 1, 2 bytes per pixel
[dm] [nvn-mtl] BC on the CPU #1: 62x62 format 0x48 levels 1, 4 bytes per pixel
[dm] [nvn-mtl] BC on the CPU #100: 128x128 format 0x4b levels 1, 2 bytes per pixel
[dm] [gl] frame 8187: … GPU 11.2 ms
```

165 s session, 8187 frames, GPU frame time p50 4.1 ms / p90 12.3 ms / max 28.5 ms, 181 lazy decodes totalling 271 ms, clean exit from the in-game quit prompt. Zelda: Echoes of Wisdom is playable at 60 fps on an A15 through the CPU decoder.

**Workaround**

Three hunks in `dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m` (patch applied locally to verify; source backed up first):

```c
// :2385  the GPU path cannot be used when the block data has to be expanded per pixel
int bc_cpu = g_bc_cpu && nvn_bc_unpacked(t->d.format, &bc_pf, &bc_bpp);
int use_gpu = !bc_cpu && !rb_shift && !sparse && g_nvn_deswz_gpu && mtl_addr(...);
// :2386
if (g_nvn_deswz_gpu && !bc_cpu && !use_gpu && !sparse && !rb_shift) RED_ONCE(40, "…");

// :4609 / :3477 / :11173  a view of a decoded texture must ask for the decoded format
uint32_t f = r.v.format;
if (g_bc_cpu) { uint32_t up; int bpp; if (nvn_bc_unpacked(f, &up, &bpp)) f = up; }
```

**Suggestions**

1. Gate `use_gpu` on `!bc_cpu` (first hunk). This alone fixes the noise.
2. Route view formats through `nvn_bc_unpacked` at `:4609`, `:3477` and `:11173` when `g_bc_cpu` is set (second hunk). This alone fixes the abort.
3. Better than patching call sites one by one: resolve the format inside `nvn_fmt_to_mtl` when `g_bc_cpu && nvn_bc_unpacked(fmt, …)` succeeds. Every caller then gets the decoded format for free, and no future caller can reintroduce either failure.
4. Keep `nvn_bc_unpacked` per-format, not "BC means RGBA8": BC4 decodes to R8, BC5 to RG8, BC6H to RGBA16F. All three appear in this title (`0x4b`, `0x48`), and a single hard-coded target format would only move the corruption.
5. Worth a CI check: build one title with `tex_bc_cpu` on and run it on an A16-or-earlier device or simulator, asserting no `MTLPixelFormatInvalid` view. Today nothing exercises this path, which is why both faults shipped.

**Severity**

Not urgent under the current support policy — A15/A16 devices are refused by default, so nothing regresses for supported hardware. But `tex_bc_cpu` is the only mechanism that lifts that refusal, #719 is needed to reach it at all, and with the two fixes above it goes from "cannot run" to "60 fps on an iPad mini 6 with the frame data in the log above". The two issues are one feature and are worth fixing together.

The install base is also larger than the support matrix suggests. A15/A16 is iPhone 13 through iPhone 15 and every iPad mini 6 — and a spare older phone or tablet is a common second device, which is exactly the hardware people are willing to hand over to something experimental. Right now that hardware is turned away one key name and two format lookups short of working.
title: tex_bc_cpu on a GPU without BC: every GPU-deswizzled upload skips the decode, and texture views still ask for the BC format

### Idea

This is a documentation suggestion. 

Please consider documenting an additional SideStore installation option in [ENTITLEMENTS.md](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/blob/main/ENTITLEMENTS.md): a tested third-party SideStore build that enables Increased Memory Limit automatically when the source IPA already requests it.

Repository: https://github.com/Silverhza/SideStore

IPA release: https://github.com/Silverhza/SideStore/releases/tag/memoryfix-2026.11.05

### Context

The existing guide correctly describes the two requirements: the entitlement must be in the executable signature, and the App ID/provisioning profile must authorize it. In the SideStore version embedded in the LiveContainer + SideStore build from [LiveContainer PR #1695](https://github.com/LiveContainer/LiveContainer/pull/1695), native IPA installation could lose the entitlement because the App ID capability was not enabled through the modern API. The same underlying issue is recorded in [SideStore #1616](https://github.com/SideStore/SideStore/issues/1616).

The change is in SideStore's provisioning path. NX2Apple's existing entitlement request can be preserved by fixing the sideloader.

### Solution and validation

The patched SideStore enables `INCREASED_MEMORY_LIMIT` through Apple's JSON capability API after legacy feature/app-group updates, then downloads and checks the provisioning profile. It repeats the capability step during later provisioning refreshes, and falls back to the source IPA's request when an older cached profile lacks the key.

The repository includes the source, regression tests, build instructions, packaging script and upstream references. The release provides a standalone SideStore IPA and a LiveContainer + SideStore IPA that retains PR #1695's iPhone Duo support.

I tested the combined build on-device and it worked well, with no issues observed. 

Apps whose executable signature already lost the entitlement need reinstalling from the original IPA once; profile-only refresh does not repair that signature.
title: Document a tested SideStore fix for retaining Increased Memory Limit

NX2Apple 1.1.0 (engine `641d1480021a` / `de8d83152878`), iOS build target, iPad mini 6 (iPad14,1, A15). The launcher's **兼容老设备 (A15 / A16 及更早)** toggle was switched on for this build.

**Symptom**

With the toggle on, an A15 device still aborts at start:

```
[dm] [nvn-mtl] FATAL the Metal device Apple A15 GPU has no BC texture formats, which the games' textures use and the host does not decompress: an iPhone needs an A17 Pro or later, an iPad an M1 or later
```

There is nothing the user can do about it from the UI: this toggle is the only control that mentions the case, it is visibly on, and the build shows no trace of it — the boot dump prints `bc_cpu 0`.

**Root cause**

1. The toggle writes `DM_TEX_BC_CPU=1` into `dm/ios/Gen/dm/env.txt`. The host reads only `DM_PROF_TEX_BC_CPU`: the key table at `dm/host/hle_profile.c:268` holds `TEX_BC_CPU`, and the variable name is built as `DM_PROF_%s` at `:273` (called from `:283`). `DM_TEX_BC_CPU` exists nowhere else in the tree, so the value is inert even where the file is read.
2. The file is not shipped anyway. The shell stages `Gen/dm` as a resource folder (`shell/project/project.yml:33`), and that folder ends up containing only `font/`, so the built bundle has no `dm/env.txt` and the boot log shows `boot: DM_ENV_FILE_KEYS=` (empty).
3. The value the check actually reads is a third spelling: the compiled `DM_GAME_TEX_BC_CPU` (`dm/host/hle_profile.c:162`), consumed by `dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m:405` and by the iOS pre-check at `dm/ios/Sources/main.m:209`. Nothing in the GUI writes it.

**One reproducible piece of evidence**

Drop `DM_PROF_TEX_BC_CPU=1` into the app's `Documents/env.txt` and launch the same build — it passes the check with no other change:

```
$ xcrun devicectl device copy to --device <UDID> --source env.txt \
    --domain-type appDataContainer --domain-identifier org.nxnative.shell.5H7KU27CWQ \
    --destination Documents/env.txt
$ xcrun devicectl device process launch --device <UDID> --console org.nxnative.shell.5H7KU27CWQ

boot: DM_ENV_FILE_KEYS=DM_PROF_TEX_BC_CPU
[dm]   more stdalloc_cap 0 key_skip 0+0 bc_cpu 1 ue_pool 0 enc_thread 0
[dm] [gl] frame 600: draws 14360, passes 600, uploads 0 (0 by blit), command buffers 300 (since the last record, 300 frames); pipelines so far 8
```

600 frames rendered, saves committed, clean exit. Balatro is playable on an A15 through the CPU decoder.

**Workaround**

After installing, put `DM_PROF_TEX_BC_CPU=1` in `<app>/Documents/env.txt` (command above). `boot_env()` reads that file on every launch, so it survives relaunches; it is lost when the app is deleted.

**Suggestions**

1. Write the key the host reads — `DM_PROF_TEX_BC_CPU=1`, not `DM_TEX_BC_CPU=1`.
2. Ship the file: copy `dm/ios/Gen/dm/env.txt` into the shell's `Gen/dm` staging, or put the variable into the launch environment instead of a file.
3. Better still, take the toggle out of the per-game path. `dm/tools/docs_patches.py` already classifies `tex_bc_cpu` as `goal: host` with the reason "a device capability, not a game choice: the host could decode wherever supportsBCTextureCompression is false, for every game". Enabling it whenever the device lacks BC support removes the failure mode outright, and the setting only remains as an opt-out.
4. If the toggle stays, print one line in the build log when it is applied, so a user can tell whether it reached the profile.

**Severity**

Not urgent for the current support policy — every A15/A16 device is refused today, so nothing regresses. But this toggle is the one path someone with an older device will take, it is one key name and one file copy away from working, and with it a whole device generation (iPhone 13/14/15-class and iPad mini 6) goes from a hard refusal to a playable game.
title: "兼容老设备 (A15/A16)" toggle does nothing: its env file is never shipped and its key is not the one the host reads

body:
### Idea

Add Japanese (`ja`) to the launcher languages, next to en, de, fr, it, sv and zh. Many of the games people run are Japanese releases.

### Plan

Follow the Italian PR (#528) and the request in #547:

- Add `frontend/l10n/ja.json` with every key of `en.json` and the same placeholders. CI checks both.
- Generate the iOS shell catalog from it with `tools/l10n_shell_catalogs.py`.
- Add Japanese to the same places #528 touched: the language list tests, the iOS demo `project.yml` and `Info.plist`, `frontend-qt/tests/`, the Mac build workflow, `tools/try-local`, and the engine patch that lists the language in `CFBundleLocalizations`.
- Capture the changed views with `NX_LAUNCHER_CAPTURE_DIR` for the PR, in Japanese.

How the file is made: the first draft is written with an AI tool, then I read and correct every line myself. I would say so in the PR. If a second Japanese reader turns up, I would ask them to read it before it merges.

### Questions

1. Do you want Japanese in the launcher?
2. Is a file that is drafted by a tool and checked by one reader enough, or should it wait for a second reader?
3. Japanese and Chinese share many characters but draw some of them differently. Should the launcher tell the system the text is Japanese, so it picks Japanese glyphs and not Chinese ones? I would check this in the captures.

### Done when

- `frontend/l10n/ja.json` covers every key in `en.json`, and CI passes.
- Japanese can be picked in Settings on the Mac, Windows and iOS launchers.
- The PR shows the changed views in Japanese.
title: Add Japanese (ja) localization

### The message

Environment

NX2Apple: v1.0.2

Mac: Apple M1

Installed update: v720896

Initial issue

The XCI contains two program title IDs (010097F018538000 and 01005EC01E6A4000). The GUI build failed with:

The folder holds more than one game

Successful workaround

I used the underlying build script with:

--title-id 010097F018538000

The Mac app built and launched successfully. I subsequently built all 39,659 iOS shaders, generated the iOS framework, and installed the game on my iPad Pro M4.

The game launches and runs on the iPad. The initial loading time appeared to be approximately 3–4 seconds (informal observation).

Remaining concerns

The build uses a provisional game profile.

A Mac address-region check reported an alias-space warning during the earlier build.

Long-term stability has not yet been verified.

Request

Could the GUI allow the user to choose a program Title ID when an XCI contains multiple programs, rather than stopping the build?

Thank you for NX2Apple!

body:
When the same game is built for both Mac and iOS, the build generates `romfs.img` twice, once per target. The image itself is target-independent — it is the packed RomFS from the same input set (base + update + DLC); the per-target work is the executable rewriting and the shader compilation, which live outside the image.

For a large game this is one of the slowest stages of the build (Tears of the Kingdom: ~17 GB of extraction and packing), and keeping both targets doubles the disk usage for identical data.

Proposal: before the extract/pack stage, check whether a `romfs.img` for the same game identity (title ID + update version) already exists from the other target's build — the shell already matches games by the identity of `romfs.img`, so the notion exists. If the input set matches exactly (base, update version, DLC), reuse that image and continue with the target-specific stages. On any mismatch, fall back to a normal full build.

Workaround today: keep one copy manually and point both sides at it, which works because both the Mac launcher and the shell locate game data by the image itself.
title: Build: reuse the other target's romfs.img instead of generating it twice

### This is

An idea

### What happens, or what you would like

Hi, and thank you for NX2Apple. The launcher is great.

What I would like
I would like to add any Mac app to the NX2Apple library, not only the games built by NX2Apple. That way NX2Apple becomes the one launcher for everything I play, and my Mac works like a game console: I turn it on, open NX2Apple, and all my games are there.
Examples of apps I would add
- LAS Recomp, a recompilation of The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening that I use to play that game.
- Zelda 64: Recompiled, a recompilation of Majora's Mask (Nintendo 64).
- Any other recompilation or Mac app, from Switch or from other platforms.


### What you expected

How it could work (simple version)
- An "Add app..." button or a Manage menu entry.
- I pick a .app on my Mac (from /Applications or anywhere else), and optionally a cover image and a name.
- The app appears in the library like the other games, and Play simply opens it.
- No special launch options are needed for these external apps.
What I tried
- I put the app path in the game's entry in library.json (appPath). The path is kept, but the game still shows "Not built yet".
- I also changed the copy's bundle identifier to org.nxnative.<title ID> and re-signed it. No change.
- A launcher build has dm, msl, pso and romfs.img in Contents/Resources, and these apps have none of them, so I assume the launcher checks for the nxnative runtime inside the app.
Why it would help
I already use NX2Apple for my Switch games. Being able to launch my other recompilations and Mac apps from the same place would be much more convenient than keeping them in different folders.

Thank you!

body:
### Idea

#693 narrows the engine's all-languages row of a game with no language list to the languages in its RomFS. The tests carry that row as a copied string (`fallbackLangRow` in `MacAppLanguageTests.swift`, `fallbackRowJSON` in `RomfsLanguagesTests.swift`). If seedds/nxnative changes the row's shape or its note, or adds a 17th language, no test fails. The narrowing then does nothing, quietly, until someone regenerates the string after a pin bump.

Found in the review of #693. Smaller points from the same review:
- The Mac `launcher.json` inside the `.app` is not rewritten, only the iOS framework's file is. Someone who opens the app without NX2Apple still sees 16 languages and the note.
- With `appReadsStore`, `launcher.c` reads a saved language itself. A saved choice that the narrowing dropped (for example `pt-BR`) still applies there, while the launcher shows the default.

### Plan

- Add a test or a step of the "Patch queue" job that runs `dm/games/settings.py` from the pinned engine for a game without control data and checks that the row it writes is recognised by `isFallbackRow`.
- Decide whether the `.app`'s `launcher.json` should be narrowed on disk too, as the iOS framework's is.

### Done when

A change of the engine's row after a pin bump turns a test red.

Follows from #693 and #668.
title: Language row: a test that follows the engine's own row, and narrowing on disk for the Mac app

### Idea

The Picture row "Fill" of #575 scales the 16:9 picture up and crops the edges, so health bars, subtitles or maps near the edges can be cut off (#545). A real full-screen picture without cropping needs the game to render a wider view. Upstream has started this with a picture shape (`DM_SCREEN_ASPECT`): the new pin (#689) has it for Breath of the Wild and Animal Crossing: New Horizons, and the launcher shows it as "Picture shape".

### Plan

- Check with a taller screen such as the iPhone Duo's whether the Picture shape of the two games looks right, and what the iPhone shell should offer next to Fill and Fit.
- Collect the games that need their own patch for a wider view, one by one, and send each to seedds/nxnative first.

### Done when

The games that matter for phones have a wider picture, and the shell's Fill is only used for the others.

Follows from #545 and #575.
title: Full-screen picture without cropping on phones, game by game

### Idea

The Switch 2 launcher work of #445 is in (#603 to #610). These parts are not done:

- **iPhone and iPad shell.** The shell shows no Switch 2 mark and no memory warning. It needs a `console` (and maybe `min_memory`) field in `game.manifest.json`, which the engine writes (patch 0050). That is engine work.
- **Profile keys upstream** (`console`, `tested`). The launcher tells a Switch 2 game by the first line of its profile. This check moves to the keys once they exist upstream.
- **The Qt launcher's footer** still says the base game and the keys are missing when a folder is refused.
- **Onboarding** still asks for keys. A player with Switch 2 games only could skip that step.

### Plan

Take them in this order: the Qt footer text and the onboarding skip (small), then the manifest field with a seedds/nxnative PR, then the shell mark.

### Done when

Each item is done or crossed out here. Nobody has built or played a Switch 2 game through the launcher yet, so the real test is by whoever owns one of the five games.

Follows from #445.
title: Switch 2 in the launcher: what #445 left open

### Idea

#633 puts the Controllers and Settings chips and Back in a narrow column next to the screen of the iPhone Duo, placed by the areas the system reserves (#622). @jonochocki pointed to Apple's guidance for the Duo: the space is shared with the system, and standard navigation, toolbar and tab bars avoid the status bar and the camera on their own. Native SwiftUI bars would replace our own positioning of the column.

### Plan

- Try the launcher's controls in a native `NavigationStack` toolbar on the Duo and compare it with the column, in the Simulator and on a real Duo if someone can run it.
- Decide for one of the two. Remove the column if the native bars do the job.

### Done when

The launcher's controls on the Duo sit where the system keeps its own, with the least code of our own.

Follows from #622. The column is only checked in the Simulator so far.
title: iPhone Duo: native bars instead of our own side column

body:
### Idea

"One game, all inside" (#540) puts the game data into the IPA. A ZIP holds at most 65,535 entries without the ZIP64 extension. SideStore refuses an IPA with more entries (#587), and #593 packs the shader tree into one file so a shared IPA installs. A game with a very large data tree inside the IPA can still hit the limit, and we do not know the size where an IPA stops installing with each tool.

### Plan

- Find out which installers read a ZIP64 IPA (SideStore, AltStore, Sideloadly, Xcode, `devicectl`) and at which size or entry count each one fails.
- Pack the game data of "One game, all inside" in a way that keeps the entry count low, as #593 does for the shaders.
- Say the limit in the export step when a game is close to it.

### Done when

A player knows before the export whether the IPA installs with their tool, and a large game packs under the limit.

Follows from #587 and #593.
title: One game, all inside: the ZIP64 limit of the IPA

body:
### Idea

The "Tool tests" job in `.github/workflows/tests.yml` runs every engine test file through `tee`, so the job stays green when a file fails. Found while bumping the engine pin (#689): three files fail the same way on main today. They are `test_env_switches` (rows for the `DM_TOUCH_*` switches of our touch patches are missing), `test_shell_build` (no Swift package at `engine/frontend-ios`) and, only in CI, the gfx tests that need Metal.

### Plan

- Make the job fail when a test file fails, for example with `set -o pipefail` or by collecting the exit codes.
- Fix or skip the three failing files first, so the job is not red from the start. The `DM_TOUCH_*` rows belong to the touch patches, `test_shell_build` needs the front end tree or a skip.

### Done when

A failing engine test file turns the "Tool tests" job red, and main is green.
title: Tool tests job stays green when an engine test file fails

body:
### Idea

The problems behind the ideas #672, #673, #674, #677, #679, #681, #682, #684 and #685 of the discussion #589. We take the problems and not the designs shown there. Each one gets a small change in the current style of the launcher, the smallest first. Thanks to @zatteogit, who named them.

### Plan

- [ ] **Finding a game in a large library** (#673, #682): the library keeps the order in which games were added, so a new game lands at the end. Sort by title or add a plain sort menu, and give the existing search Cmd+F.
- [ ] **Two buttons called "Build game"** (#677): the hero button of an unbuilt game fills the form with that game's files, the button at the top right empties it. Give the hero button its own name.
- [ ] **Progress shown twice during a build** (#679): the build bar and the Builds page both show it, and the form stays locked. Hide the bar on the Builds page and fold the locked cards while a build runs.
- [ ] **A game ready on the Mac and on a device** (#681): the hero offers only Play on the Mac, so the start on the device is out of reach. Add "Open on <device>" as a second action or an entry in Manage.
- [ ] **The version of the built package** (#672): the launcher shows no game version. Show the version of the built package beside Play, so a player sees whether a newer update is already in the build. No DLC count.
- [ ] **No feedback under the pointer** (#684): cards and custom buttons do not react to the mouse. A slight brightening and a hand cursor.
- [ ] **Top bar at the minimum width** (#685): no wrap has been shown yet. It needs a screenshot of a long language at the minimum width before anything changes.

### Not taken

The grid and list views with a detail panel (#673, #674) and the design of the library shown in the pictures stay out. The carousel and the hero stay.

### Done when

Each item is closed by its own small pull request, or crossed out here with the reason.
title: Library and build page: problems to solve in our own design

body:
### What happened?

A game built from a dump folder (`scripts/pack_dump.py`) or a NUP without control data has no `control.nacp`, so `dm/tools/nacp.py`'s `languages()` returns `[]` and `dm/games/settings.py` omits the `DM_LANG` (Game language) setting from `launcher.json` even when the game's RomFS ships multiple languages (for example Donkey Kong Bananza `040074A01BF12000`, which ships 15 Horizon languages in `Mals/` and `System/RegionLangMask.txt`).

### Fix

1. **Upstream (`seedds/nxnative#1208`)**: teach `dm/tools/nacp.py` to fall back to `System/RegionLangMask.txt` or `Mals/<Tag>.Product.*` in the sibling RomFS when `control.nacp` is absent.
2. **Launcher side (`frontend/` and `frontend-ios/`, zero engine patches)**: while `seedds/nxnative#1208` is under review (and for already-built `.app` bundles and iOS frameworks), read `System/RegionLangMask.txt` or `Mals/` directly from the game's `romfs.img` (`DMROMFS1` index) or `romfs/` folder when `launcher.json` has no `DM_LANG` row.

body:
## Summary

Persona 5 Royal runs fine at a locked 30 fps on iPhone 17 Pro for about **5 min 33 s**, then the process **aborts itself (SIGABRT)** inside the shader prefetch path:

```
-[_MTLFunction newArgumentEncoderWithBufferIndex:reflection:functionReflection:]:11352:
  failed assertion `bufferIndex 0 does not identify an argument buffer'
```

This is **not** the vnode-limit kill from #665 — that one is a jetsam kill with `reason: vnode-limit`; here jetsam reports the process with **no reason at all**, i.e. the abort came from our own code.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Device | iPhone 17 Pro (iPhone18,1, A19 Pro) |
| OS | iOS 27.0 (24A5418b) |
| Shell | NX2Apple 1.1.0, `org.nxnative.shell.LN5TP352NZ`, upstream ref `641d1480`, shader chain `e047be1b6829` |
| Game | Persona 5 Royal, US `01005CA01580E000` |
| Config | `DM_PSO_MANIFEST=off`, Metal 4 **off** (`DM_PSO_MTL4=0`), prebuild **on** (`DM_PSO_PREBUILD=1`), `pso/applegpu_g18p.mtl4a` (60 MB) present but unused while Metal 4 is off |
| Save sync | iCloud folder, active |

## Log excerpt (`Documents/log.txt`, the only launch in that file)

```
[dm] [nvn-mtl] display link up to tick 5432: ticks 300, presents 5400, empty ticks 31 ...
[dm] [nvn] present thread time-constraint policy (period 33.333 ms, computation 7.217 ms) set
-[_MTLFunction newArgumentEncoderWithBufferIndex:reflection:functionReflection:]:11352: failed assertion `bufferIndex 0 does not identify an argument buffer'
[dm] CRASH sig=6 addr=__pthread_kill+0x8 pc=__pthread_kill+0x8 lr=pthread_kill+0x10c sp=0x16bdb23e0
...
[dm] bt: abort+0x94 err+0 <redacted>+0 MTLReportFailure+0x344 <redacted>+0xa4
          shader_load+0x1568 __mtl_prog_prefetch_block_invoke+0x34
          <redacted>+0x20 <redacted>+0x10 <redacted>+0x284 <redacted>+0x138
          <redacted>+0xf8 <redacted>+0x280 _pthread_wqthread+0x124 start_wqthread+0x8
```

The crashing thread is a GCD worker (`_pthread_wqthread`), not the render thread:

```
[dm] thread 0x1017 ... waits:running/not waiting ... lr=sdk+0xe2efac
[dm] handle table use 22 / 4096, threads created so far 23
```

Immediately before, the frame that compiled new pipelines:

```
[dm] [longframe] frame 5258 (328.90 s) whole frame 82.7 ms, submit+present 81.6 ms, GPU 11.8 ms;
     new pipelines 2 + shader libraries 0, 79.9 ms in all
[dm] [longframe] frame 5385 (333.13 s) whole frame 47.5 ms, ...
```

So: 2 new pipelines at 328.90 s → ~4 s later the background prefetch thread creates an argument-buffer encoder and Metal asserts.

## Why this is not #665 (vnode-limit)

| | this crash | #665 |
|---|---|---|
| Signal | `sig=6` from `abort()` via `MTLReportFailure` | jetsam kill, `reason: vnode-limit` |
| Jetsam entry | `JetsamEvent-2026-11-04-222007.ips`, DmShell listed with **no** `reason` field | `reason: vnode-limit` |
| Frames reached | 5400 (333.13 s) | 1,959–2,849 |
| rpages at death | 1593 MB | 344 MB – 2098 MB |

Health at the moment of the crash — nothing is starved:

```
frame time p50 33.34 / p95 33.71 ms; GPU p50 11.58 / p95 14.52 ms;
on-screen 300 frames, dropped 1; footprint 1824 MiB; CPU 53 %
```

(For calibration: the same title survives 11+ minutes in one earlier run today before a pure vnode-limit kill — `pid 10998` alive at 11:59:51 with 1574 MB, killed at 12:10:54 with 2098 MB. That run never hit this assertion, so the assertion is a separate, earlier ceiling.)

## Probable cause

`__mtl_prog_prefetch_block_invoke` → `shader_load()` calls
`newArgumentEncoderWithBufferIndex:reflection:functionReflection:` for **buffer index 0 unconditionally**, assuming binding 0 of every prefetched function is an argument buffer. P5R binds argument buffers on some stages and plain `device` / `constant` buffers on others, so a function compiled by the background prefetch can have a non-argument-buffer at index 0, and Metal's assertion fires.

Suggested guard (Metal API):

```objc
id<MTLBinding> b = reflection.bindings[idx];
if (b.type == MTLBindingTypeBuffer && b.isArgumentBuffer) {
    /* newArgumentEncoderWithBufferIndex:... */
}
```

or skip argument-encoder creation entirely when
`reflection.argumentBuffersSupport == MTLArgumentBuffersTierNone`
(this exists on `MTLStructType`; on newer SDKs the equivalent is `MTLFunctionReflection` / per-binding `isArgumentBuffer`).

## Repro

1. NX2Apple 1.1.0 shell, game `01005CA01580E000`, config exactly as above.
2. Launch, play normally (opening sequence, first area).
3. At ~5:20–5:35 of wall clock, right after a small pipeline compile, the process aborts.
4. Deterministic in the only run that survived long enough to reach that point (earlier runs of the day died at 60–100 s from #665 and never got here).

## Ask

1. Is unconditional argument-encoder creation in the prefetch path intentional (i.e. the engine guarantees index 0 is an argument buffer for prefetched functions)? If not, can it be guarded as above?
2. Does the prefetch path need to stay on for playability? If we could disable it, would P5R fall back to plain per-draw compilation and survive to the #665 ceiling instead of aborting at 5.5 min?
3. Would you expose a runtime switch for the background prefetch (something we can set in `Documents/env.txt`), so this can be A/B tested without rebuilding the shell? Right now `env.txt` only accepts a whitelist (`DM_PSO_MANIFEST`, `DM_FD_LOG`, `DM_PSO_ARCHIVE`), so we cannot test `DM_PSO_PREPARE` / `DM_PRELOAD` from the device.

Happy to run any build you want tested on this device — logs and full thread dump available on request.

---

## 中文摘要

**现象**：iPhone 17 Pro / iOS 27.0 上，Persona 5 Royal 稳定跑 30 fps 到 **5 分 33 秒**，然后在着色器后台预取线程里被 Metal 断言打死（`sig=6`），不是被系统杀：

```
-[_MTLFunction newArgumentEncoderWithBufferIndex:reflection:functionReflection:]:11352:
  failed assertion `bufferIndex 0 does not identify an argument buffer'
bt: MTLReportFailure ← shader_load+0x1568 ← __mtl_prog_prefetch_block_invoke
```

**和 #665（vnode-limit）是两回事**：这次 jetsam 记录里 DmShell **没有 reason 字段**（自己 abort），死时 rpages 1593 MB，帧时间 p50 33.34 ms / GPU 11.58 ms，完全不是资源耗尽。同一台机器今天中午还有一次**纯 vnode-limit** 的死亡，那个进程活了 11 分钟以上，也从没碰到这个断言 —— 说明这是另一条更早的天花板。

**触发条件**：frame 5258（328.90 s）刚编了 2 条新管线，约 4 秒后预取线程建 argument buffer 编码器时断言。看起来是 `shader_load()` 对 buffer index 0 无条件调用 `newArgumentEncoderWithBufferIndex:`，而这个函数的反射里 0 号绑定根本不是 argument buffer。

**建议**：调用前判断该 binding 是 buffer 且 `isArgumentBuffer`，或反射 `argumentBuffersSupport == None` 时整体跳过。

**想请你确认三件事**：① 预取路径无条件建 encoder 是有意为之吗，能不能加守卫；② 预取关掉会不会只是退回 #665 的上限（也就是能不能活到 11 分钟）；③ 能不能把预取开关加进 `Documents/env.txt` 白名单，现在只认 `DM_PSO_MANIFEST` / `DM_FD_LOG` / `DM_PSO_ARCHIVE`，我们没法在设备上 A/B。

需要什么版本我这边都能装测。
title: iOS 27 / A19 Pro: Persona 5 Royal aborts (SIGABRT) at ~5.5 min — MTLFunction newArgumentEncoderWithBufferIndex: assertion in the shader prefetch path (bufferIndex 0 is not an argument buffer)

body:
## Summary

On an iPhone 17 Pro (A19 Pro, iOS 27.0), Persona 5 Royal (`01005CA01580E000`) boots and renders correctly at ~30 fps, then the whole app disappears after **60–100 s**, in every configuration I tried: Metal 4 on or off, with or without the bundled `--gpu g18p` pipeline archive, with the prewarm list on or off.

iOS writes no `.ips` for the app. A **system `JetsamEvent`** lands at the same second every time, and its reason is `vnode-limit`, not memory: the event purges 500–1,981 other processes with the same reason (`addressbooksyncd`, `driverkitd`, `tailspind`, `AppSSODaemon` …), so the device's vnode table is being exhausted system-wide.

## Environment

- App: NX2Apple 1.1.0; engine `641d1480021a57840b7acc15f92cbd86ecfae611-de8d83152878`, shader chain `e047be1b6829`
- Device: iPhone 17 Pro (`iPhone18,1`), A19 Pro (`applegpu_g18p`), iOS 27.0 (24A5418b), Developer Mode on
- Build Mac: M5, macOS 26.6.2, Xcode 27.2
- Route C shell (`build_shell.sh`) with three frameworks; P5R built with `build_ipa_from_nsp.py --platform ios --shell-framework …`
- Installed from Xcode with a free team (same bundle ID, in place), not SideStore
- Game: base + update 1.0.2 (`v65536`), US/`01005CA01580E000`. `profile.tsv` as shipped (`pso_mtl4 0`); Metal 4 was turned on for the archive test with the per-game setting (boot line `DM_PSO_MTL4=1`)

## Evidence (system flight recorder, not the host log)

`JetsamEvent-*.ips`, parsed from `/vendor/…/systemCrashLogs`:

| capture | DmShell reason | rpages (16 KB) | other processes killed with `vnode-limit` | `largestProcess` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 21:17:37 | `vnode-limit` | 46,880 (732 MB) | 782 | bili-universal |
| 21:18:35 | `vnode-limit` | 103,660 (1.62 GB) | 1,931 | DmShell |
| 21:20:11 | `vnode-limit` | 47,139 (737 MB) | 781 | DmShell |
| 21:51:36 | `vnode-limit` | 22,003 (344 MB) | 500 | Aweme |
| 21:56:02 | `vnode-limit` | 118,482 (1.85 GB) | 1,982 | DmShell |
| 21:59:43 | `vnode-limit` | 23,999 (375 MB) | 939 | DmShell |
| 22:07:17 | — (DmShell largest) | 101,856 (1.59 GB) | 1,961 | DmShell |

The rpages column rules out a per-process memory kill (344 MB–1.85 GB; `memoryStatus` shows free pages, not a shortage). `largestProcess` being `bili-universal` or `Aweme` in two of them shows the pressure is not "DmShell is just the biggest" — the vnode table itself is full and the killer works down the list.

Same phone, same evening: Breath of the Wild and Rhythm Heaven Groove (100 `metallib`) run for as long as you like with no such event.

## Scale of this game

- `DmGame01005CA01580E000.framework/msl/b-e047be1b6829/`: **88,792 `.metallib` + 30,646 `.json` = 119,439 files**, 1.3 GB
- 30,646 shader keys (29,526 pixel, 1,114 vertex, 6 compute), 3,342 cover pairs (its `dm/games/…/README.md`)
- `Documents/games/<title ID>/pso_user.tsv`: **25,714 lines** on this device
- prewarm line: `pipeline prepare: 25,692 lines (24,826 shaders, 864 render pipelines, 2 compute pipelines) in 2.61 s on 6 workers before the first frame`

## What we tried (all die at the same ceiling)

| configuration | what the log says | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Metal 4 off, prewarm on | prepare 25,692 lines in 2.61 s; then `new pipelines 0 + shader libraries 0` on almost every frame | **frame 2,754 / 96.7 s**, then a `vnode-limit` event |
| Metal 4 off, `DM_PSO_MANIFEST=off` | no prepare, shaders load lazily | **frame 1,959 / 67 s** |
| Metal 4 on + bundled archive, prewarm on | `pipeline archive bundled with the app: …/pso/applegpu_g18p.mtl4a, 59.9 MB, opened in 24.3 ms`; `prepare: 5,192 of 25,714 lines done after 0.5 s` | **~1 s**, during prepare |
| Metal 4 on + bundled archive, `DM_PSO_MANIFEST=off` | archive opened; no prepare | **frame 2,849 / 100.2 s** (the best of the four) |

So the bundled archive is **not** #640 here: it opens (24.3 ms) and `pso_mtl4 1` is honoured (`switches … pso4 1`). It just does not raise the ceiling — with Metal 4 the same number of lines is fatal sooner (~5,000 lines ≈ 1 s), which suggests the cost per pipeline is what fills the table, not the number of shader files touched.

`DM_PSO_MANIFEST=off` and `DM_FD_LOG=<seconds>` do come through `Documents/env.txt` (`boot: DM_ENV_FILE_KEYS=` lists them); `DM_PSO_MTL4` does not, as in #640.

## Suspicion

`lib_from_file` (`dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m`) maps the `.metallib` and closes the fd immediately, which is the right call — but the mapping lives as long as the library's `dispatch_data` does, and a `MTLFunction` retains its library while the shader table keeps one `NvShader` per key with its functions. So every shader the prewarm loads leaves its `.metallib` mapped for the rest of the run: 24,826 mappings here. Breath of the Wild's 4,829 pipelines / 1,818 bases sit under whatever the ceiling is; 25,714 pipelines / 24,826 shaders do not.

## Ask

1. Is there a supported way to release a shader's library (and its mapping) once its pipelines are built — e.g. dropping the cached `MTLFunction`/`MTLLibrary` for a key whose uses are all built already, and re-loading on a miss? For a game with 30k shaders that would cap live mappings at the working set instead of the whole library.
2. If not, is this a known iOS limit we should document for big-library games (`docs/` has nothing on vnode or per-process mapping counts)? If it is, the framework's `README.md` line "iOS and later battles have not been tested" could say what kills it, so the next person does not spend an evening on it.
3. Is there a way to log the number of live shader mappings? `DM_FD_LOG` counts descriptors, and `lib_from_file` closes them, so the growth is invisible in the log while being the thing that kills the app.

Happy to run anything you want measured on this device (iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 27.0, A19 Pro) — it reproduces in 100 s every time.
title: iPhone 17 Pro (A19 Pro, iOS 27.0): Persona 5 Royal is killed by the system's vnode limit after 60-100 s in every configuration (Metal 4 on or off, bundled g18p archive or not)

body:
### Idea

On iOS and iPadOS, the Controllers panel and the shell settings panel (the gear) slide out less smoothly than a game's settings pane when they close. The difference is easy to see with a controller: press B on either panel, then on Game settings.

Found while testing #660 on an iPad with an Xbox controller. That PR keeps both panels above the library while they leave (`.zIndex`), so the slide out is now visible. It is still not as smooth as the settings pane.

### Why they differ

In `frontend-ios/Sources/ShellUI/LibraryView.swift` (as of #660):

- **Game settings** is always in the view tree. `settingsPane(...)` is placed with `.offset(x: settingsOpen ? … : pane + 40)` and `.opacity(settingsOpen ? 1 : 0)`, and `.animation(.smooth(duration: 0.3), value: settingsOpen)` animates the open and the close. Nothing is inserted or removed, so the content, its layout and its focus targets stay put, and only the offset changes.
- **Controllers** and **shell settings** are inserted and removed: `if controllersOpen { Group { … }.zIndex(3) }` and `if shellSettingsOpen { Group { … }.zIndex(4) }`, with `.transition(.move(edge: .trailing).combined(with: .opacity))`. On close, SwiftUI removes the view and plays the transition on a snapshot of it. At the same moment the focus moves back to the library (`focus.id = "lib.controllers"` / `"lib.shellSettings"`) and the library's focus targets change, so the exit competes with that relayout.

### Plan

1. Present `ControllersView` and `ShellSettingsView` the way the settings pane is presented: always in the tree, moved off screen with `.offset(x:)` and faded with `.opacity` when closed. Keep the dimming layer behind each one as it is now.
2. When a panel is closed, hide it from input and accessibility: `.allowsHitTesting(open)`, `.accessibilityHidden(!open || …)`, and `.isModal` only while it is open.
3. Keep its focus targets out of the library's while it is closed. #660 already filters targets at use time with `isLive(_:)` and the `ctl.` / `shs.` prefixes. Check that a closed panel's targets are not live, so the D-pad cannot reach a panel that is off screen. If needed, add a `settingsArrived`-style flag so the focus ring only shows once the slide in has finished (see how `settingsArrived` gates `\.shellFocus` on the settings pane).
4. Keep the edge swipe back (`EdgeSwipeBack`, `edgeDrag`) working on both panels: the offset becomes `open ? edgeDrag : panelWidth + 40`.
5. Keep Reduce Motion: no slide, as now (`.animation(reduceMotion ? nil : …)`).
6. Watch the cost: an always-present `ControllersView` keeps observing the controllers. If that costs anything while it is closed, build it lazily on first open and keep it after that.

### Done when

- With a controller and with touch, opening and closing Controllers and the shell settings slides as smoothly as Game settings, in portrait and in landscape, on iPhone and iPad.
- Fast A / B / A / B on either panel does not jerk, flash or leave the panel half open.
- After a close, the focus ring is on the button that opened the panel (Controllers or the gear), and the D-pad cannot move into the closed panel.
- The edge swipe back still works on both panels, and VoiceOver does not read a closed panel.
- Reduce Motion still turns the slide off.
- The fixes in #660 still hold: A on a focused control does not start the game, and the delete-saves switch does not flip by itself.
title: iOS shell: Controllers and shell settings slide out as smoothly as Game settings

body:
## Summary

On an iPhone Air (A19 Pro, iOS 27.0), a game whose shell framework carries the offline pipeline archive (`--gpu g18p`) crashes at boot with SIGSEGV inside Metal, while the host opens that archive. Both games I built this way crash the same way: Metroid Dread (`010093801237C000`) and Hollow Knight: Silksong (`010013C00E930000`). Zelda: Echoes of Wisdom (`01008CF01BAAC000`) is in the same shell app, has no bundled archive and runs fine with Metal 4 on.

The archive passes the host's container check (`arch_file_ok`) and Metal still crashes, so the check does not catch it.

## Environment

- Device: iPhone Air (A19 Pro, `applegpu_g18p`), iOS 27.0
- Build Mac: MacBook Air M4, macOS 27.0 (26A428), Xcode 27.2 (27B52)
- NX2Apple `7ef881b9`, engine commit `b9e6e4084e3c`, shader chain `b7cd656abd7c`
- Route C shell (`build_shell.sh`), three game frameworks. Unsigned IPA (ad-hoc signed with the memory-limit entitlement), installed with SideStore
- Frameworks built with `build_ipa_from_nsp.py --platform ios --shell-framework … --gpu g18p`. Both profiles have `pso_mtl4 off`, so the archive was requested explicitly; Metal 4 is turned on with the per-game toggle in the app (`DM_PSO_MTL4=1` in the boot lines)

Bundled archives (`archive.tsv`):

| Game | arch | platform | toolchain | bases |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Metroid Dread | applegpu_g18p | ios 27.0 | AIR-TT 32023.922 | 659 (33.9 MB) |
| Silksong | applegpu_g18p | ios 27.0 | AIR-TT 32023.922 | 1171 (21.4 MB) |

## What happens

The app exits with code 139 right after the first frames. Silksong's `log.txt`:

```
boot: DM_PSO_BUNDLE=/private/var/containers/Bundle/Application/…/App.app/Frameworks/DmGame010013C00E930000.framework/pso
boot: DM_PSO_MTL4=1
boot: DM_PSO_PREBUILD=1
…
[dm] CRASH sig=11 addr=0x20 pc=<redacted>+0x458 lr=<redacted>+0x438 sp=0x16f429c40
[dm] bt: <redacted>+0x1b8 <redacted>+0x94 <redacted>+0x1e4 <redacted>+0x10c <redacted>+0x3c <redacted>+0x48 __pso4_init_block_invoke+0x35c <redacted>+0x10 <redacted>+0x20 fn_spec+0x238 shader_load+0x7d8 __mtl_prog_prefetch_block_invoke+0x34 <redacted>+0x20 <redacted>+0x10 <redacted>+0x284 <redacted>+0x138 <redacted>+0xf8 <redacted>+0x280 _pthread_wqthread+0x124 start_wqthread+0x8
```

Metroid Dread crashes at the same spot: same `addr=0x20`, same `pc` / `lr` offsets, same backtrace.

Neither log has the `pipeline archive bundled with the app: …` line or the line for the device's own `pso_archive` folder, so the crash comes before both. In `pso4_init` that points at `pso_bundle_open`, most likely `newArchiveWithURL:` on `applegpu_g18p.mtl4a`. Since the `<redacted>` frames are inside Metal, this is an inference from the missing log lines.

## Workaround that confirms it

An empty `Documents/games/<title ID>/pso/` folder (`EngineLaunchPlan` prefers the per-game `pso` folder over the framework's) makes `pso_bundle_open` find no `applegpu_g18p.mtl4a` and fall back to the device. Both games then start, with Metal 4 still on, and the device builds its own bases quickly:

```
Silksong:      pipeline archive: 1171 new pipeline bases written to p00001.mtl4a (21.0 MB, 3209 ms)
Metroid Dread: pipeline archive: 659 new pipeline bases written to p00000.mtl4a (32.6 MB, 4095 ms)
```

## Also: no way to turn the bundled archive off from `env.txt`

My first try was `DM_PSO_BUNDLE=off` in `Documents/env.txt`. It has no effect, because `EngineLaunchPlan.make` sets `DM_PSO_BUNDLE` whenever the framework has a `pso/` folder, and `env.txt` keys only apply `where env[key] == nil`. A user hit by a bad bundled archive has no switch short of rebuilding the app or the folder trick above.

## Suggestions

- If Metal cannot open an offline archive made by this toolchain on this device and OS, the host should fall back to building on the device instead of crashing. If a crash inside `newArchiveWithURL:` cannot be caught, a stamp check could do it: the archive's `platform` / `toolchain` against the running OS build, or a one-time open in a probe before trusting the file.
- Let `DM_PSO_BUNDLE=off` from `env.txt` (or a per-game setting) win over the launch plan's default.

I am on an older checkout (`7ef881b9`, 2026-11-02). I did not find a commit or issue about this since then, but I have not retested on the latest version.
title: iOS: the bundled offline pipeline archive (--gpu g18p) crashes Metal at boot on iPhone Air (A19 Pro, iOS 27.0)

Opening Button mapping from the iOS shell's library shows a card. In landscape the card is too small for the controller drawing, so the drawing is cut off.

Instead of a card, Button mapping could open as its own full-screen view: the controller drawing on the left and the current list of buttons on the right. The drawing then always has room, and the rows stay usable with a controller as they are now (the D-pad moves through the rows, A picks, B closes).

### Plan

- Button mapping opens as a full-screen view in place of the card, in landscape and on iPad.
- Left: the controller drawing, whole at every size. Right: the existing grouped rows, the picker and the footer, unchanged.
- The rules from #576 stay: the view takes no controller state, the drawing is no focus target, and trying buttons stays in the button test.
- On a narrow portrait screen, the drawing can go above the list or be left out.

### Done when

- In landscape on an iPad (tested on an iPad mini, A17 Pro), the drawing shows in full beside the list.
- A controller moves only through the rows, A picks and B closes, as now.
- The captures show the new view in landscape and portrait.

### Game and title ID

Donkey Kong Country: Tropical Freeze, 0100C1F0051B6000

### Base game and update versions

base 1.0.0 [v0] (cartridge dump), update 1.0.2 [v131072]

### Where it runs

iPhone or iPad (built for iPhone / iPad)

### Device, chip and RAM

iPad Pro 11-inch (M5), iPad17,1

### macOS or iOS / iPadOS version

iPadOS 27.2 (24B119); Mac on macOS 27.2, Xcode 27.2

### How it was installed

The launcher's shared app (`NSPortBuilder --install-shell`), Xcode signing with a free Personal Team

### NX2Apple version

1.0.2, engine 65501fbbaf85

### What happens, and when

Constant clicks / crackle in the sound, every time, from the menus on and in game, mostly heard in the music (built-in speaker). 60 fps throughout.

The output side is healthy: `audio session: sample rate 48000 Hz, I/O buffer 5.00 ms (asked for 5 ms)`, and every `audio #0 device callbacks` line reads `240–240 frames each, 4.0 blocks queued on average at callback; in these 2000, 0 underruns, 0.0 ms zero-padded`. But `catch-up renders so far` grows by about 600 per 2000 frames (581, 1181, 1781, 2381 …), about one in 3.3, where the audio reference expects a few dozen.

**Cause (traced):** with `DM_AUDREN_TRACE=1` the game updates twice in a row every video frame: pairs 0.02 ms apart, 16.7 ms between pairs (of 199 traced updates, 99 gaps round to 0 ms and 88 to 16–17 ms). The second update of each pair finds nothing rendered since the first and renders a catch-up frame. `render_main` checks the catch-up queue outside `g_render_mu`, and the update hook stores `g_cq_tail` only after `render_once` has released the lock. When the render thread's check lands inside a catch-up render, it sees an empty queue, waits on `g_render_mu`, renders the *next* frame after the catch-up and plays it first; the catch-up frame plays one slot later. Two 5 ms blocks swap order, a click, several times a second with this update pattern.

**Fix (tested on the device: the clicks are gone):** hold `g_render_mu` across the render thread's queue check with its own render, and across the catch-up render with its `g_cq_tail` store; `render_once` leaves the lock alone when its thread already holds it (a `__thread` flag). The queue head moves only after the frame is copied out, still under the lock. The lock order stays `g_render_mu` → the SDK update lock in both paths.

```c
// render_main
pthread_mutex_lock(&g_render_mu);
uint32_t h = atomic_load(&g_cq_head);
if (h != atomic_load(&g_cq_tail)) { src = g_cq[h % CQ]; got = g_cq_n[h % CQ]; }
else { g_frame_n = 0; t_render_mu_held = 1; exec(g_handle[0], g_handle[1]); t_render_mu_held = 0; src = g_frame; got = g_frame_n; }
/* copy into the output buffer as before */
int popped = src != g_frame;
if (popped) atomic_store(&g_cq_head, h + 1);   // the slot is free only once its frame is copied out
pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_render_mu);
if (popped) cq_popped();

// h_ars_Update, catch-up branch
pthread_mutex_lock(&g_render_mu); t_render_mu_held = 1;
if (t - atomic_load(&g_cq_head) < CQ) { render_once(sys, g_cq[t % CQ], &g_cq_n[t % CQ]); atomic_store(&g_cq_tail, t + 1); }
else render_once(sys, NULL, NULL);
t_render_mu_held = 0; pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_render_mu);

// render_once
if (!t_render_mu_held) pthread_mutex_lock(&g_render_mu);
/* … */
if (!t_render_mu_held) pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_render_mu);
```

Not run: `regress.py` and the host tests. This was a patch to the launcher's downloaded engine copy, not a git checkout. The race is in the general renderer path, so it should reach any game that updates twice between two renders, not only this one; it probably belongs upstream in seedds/nxnative as well.

### What you expected

Clean sound, as after the fix.

### Launch options changed from the defaults

none

### Copy diagnostics

```markdown
Not pasted from the launcher. By hand: NX2Apple 1.0.2, engine 65501fbbaf8526f7aab0a1edd028135888590f8e, bundled Python 3.13.18, .NET SDK 10.0.403, Xcode 27.2 (27B52).
```

### Game profile lines from the build log

```text
none (the 1.0.2 build printed no `[RED] this …` line; the earlier 1.0.1 build did, which is why it was rebuilt with 1.0.2)
```

### The game's log

Relevant lines quoted above (from `log.prev.txt` and the `DM_AUDREN_TRACE=1` run's `log.txt`). I can attach the whole logs if useful.

### Crash report

no crash

### Fork patches line

fork patches: runtime-profile,ios-game-data-folder,ios-slim-ipa,nsp-dotnet-home,nsp-chain-changed-note,bc-cpu-decode,mac-keymap,mac-library-folder,hades2-update-profile,env-switches-verify,ios-probe,fork-docs,…

---

**Two more things seen in the same setup** (happy to file them separately):

1. **`nx_extract` fails on repacked updates:** `ResultFsInvalidArgument (2002-6001)` in `Aes128CtrExStorage..ctor` for updates repacked with key generation 18 (New Super Mario Bros. U Deluxe 1.0.2, Pokémon Legends: Z-A 1.0.1). Their patch sections are `AesCtrEx` with an empty encryption table (`EncryptionTreeSize 0`, a BKTR header with 0 entries), which LibHac 0.19 refuses. Relabelling such a section `AesCtr` and recomputing its FS header hash makes the merged RomFS read cleanly with `IntegrityCheckLevel.ErrorOnInvalid` (NSMBU 1.0.2: 2090 files, 2.5 GB; Z-A 1.0.1: 22 files, 4.1 GB).
2. **The launcher stores a path as the title ID:** some library entries had `"titleID": "/Volumes/…/Captain Toad Treasure Tracker.nsp"` (a game added from a folder whose files have no `[title ID]` in their names). The iPhone / iPad install then looked for `shell-framework/DmGame<path>.framework` and stopped with "The game's framework was not found". Seen for Captain Toad, Luigi's Mansion 3 and DKC: Tropical Freeze.

body:
**Pull request: #630**, everything below but forwarding patches 0071 and 0072 to seedds/nxnative.

### Idea

The launcher can only build a game that its engine supports. Supporting a new game often means changes to nxnative: the game's folder `dm/games/<TitleID>/` (its profile, memory addresses, shader handling) and sometimes changes to shared engine files. Until those changes are in an engine release, a player can't build the game. The build fails, or the app crashes at runtime.

A **game engine file** (`.nxgame`) carries one game's support from a developer to a player. With it, the Mac launcher builds the game with that support, without an engine update.

### What a .nxgame file is

It's a ZIP file named `<TitleID>-<name>.nxgame`. It contains:

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `manifest.json` | The game (title ID, name, the update versions its `game.tsv` registers), the engine it was made against (`engine_id`, or the base commit and upstream pin), the commits, the engine files the patch changes, the author, a note for the player, and the SHA-256 of every other file |
| `game/dm/games/<TitleID>/...` | The game's folder, as it is in the developer's last commit |
| `engine.patch` | The game's changes to shared engine files (`git diff --binary`). It's absent when the game only needs its own folder |

It holds one game only, and it's bound to that game's title ID. Docs, tests and the files `tools/engine.py sync` generates are left out, because a player's build reads none of them. The same commits always make the same bytes.

### Making one (developer)

1. In the engine repository, which is `engine/` of an NX2Apple clone or an nxnative fork elsewhere on disk, make a branch for the game. In `engine/`, branch from `nx2apple`. Never use `nx2apple` or `main` itself.
2. Do the game's work there, test it, and commit it.
3. Run `python3 tools/game_archive.py <TitleID>` from the NX2Apple clone. Add `--engine PATH` for another repository, `--notes "…"` for a line for the player (what was tested), and `--name` or `--author` to replace the defaults.
   - The tool takes the commits of the current branch that are on no other branch and no remote. It lists the commits, and the files it puts in and leaves out.
   - It stops on uncommitted changes (`--allow-dirty` leaves them out instead), on a merge in the branch, on a change to another game's folder, and on a repository that isn't nxnative.
4. Check the file with `python3 tools/game_archive.py --show FILE`, then share it. Don't commit it to NX2Apple: it contains engine files.

**Or with an AI agent.** Have an agent (Claude Code, Codex, …) do the work in an NX2Apple clone. For example: "Add support for <game> (<TitleID>)." You don't need to name the tool. The fork's `AGENTS.md`, which `CLAUDE.md` points to, has the rule "A new game ends with its game engine file". It tells the agent to:

- commit the game's changes on a branch of their own in the engine repository, never on `nx2apple` or `main`;
- run `tools/game_archive.py <TitleID>` when the work is done;
- check the file with `--show`, and say where the file is.

The tool's checks apply the same way to an agent. The agent uses `--allow-dirty` only with your agreement, and it doesn't commit the file. Check the file with `--show` before you share it.

**Sharing it.** The `.nxgame` file can be distributed on its own, for example attached to an issue, posted in a chat, or put on a download page. Players need only the file and the Mac launcher: no clone, no engine repository and no engine update.

### Using one (player, Mac launcher)

1. In the build card, under the optional files, choose the file in **Game engine file**. The row shows the game, the engine it was made for and its author. The launcher keeps a checked copy, and selects it again the next time that game is built.
2. Before the build:
   - **Blocked:** a damaged file, or a file for another game than the chosen base game.
   - **Warning you can continue past:** a file made for another engine version, or for another update than the chosen one.
   - **First use of a file:** the launcher shows the author, the engine files it changes, and a reminder that it runs code on this Mac. Use only files from people you trust.
3. The build runs from a copy of the launcher's engine with the file applied. The installed engine is never changed. The copy is deleted after a build that succeeds, and kept after a failure for a look (the log names it).

It works for the Mac app, for "One game, all inside", and for the shared app.

### The shared app needs a host of its own for some games

The shared app (Route C) runs every game on its built-in host, which is built from the launcher's engine. A game's framework is built from the engine copy, but changes that `engine.patch` makes to the engine's sources (`dm/host`, `dm/ios`, and so on) never reach the host. Scott Pilgrim (0100D59022590000) crashed on iPhone this way: its code for Epic Online Services and its Vulkan changes weren't in the shared app's host.

### Plan

- **The game engine file, built** (in #630: `tools/game_archive.py`, the build card row, the checks, the engine copy).
- **Patch 0071, a host of its own for the game.**
  - When the game engine file has an `engine.patch`, the build also makes `DmHost<TID>.framework`: the whole host, built from the patched engine copy (`dm/ios/tools/build_host.sh`, `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py --shell-host`).
  - The shared app embeds it next to `DmGame<TID>.framework`. At Play, `ShellMain.m` loads it with `dlopen` and starts the game through its glue (`dm_glue_*`, checked with `DMGlueVersion`).
  - The host reads its own image (`__dso_handle`) instead of the main executable's.
  - The other games keep the shared app's built-in host, and there is still one game per process.
- **Patch 0072, an Engine setting.** Under Game, a game with its own host gets an **Engine** setting: "This game's engine" (the default) or "The shared app's engine". `DM_SHELL_HOST=shared` makes the app skip the game's host, to compare the two or to work around a broken one.
- **The Mac launcher.**
  - It passes `--shell-host` for a game engine file with an `engine.patch`.
  - It mirrors, checks and removes the host along with the game's framework.
  - It stops with a message when the engine is too old to build a host.

### Done when

- A game engine file makes a game build and run that fails without it, on the Mac and on the iPhone.
- In the shared app, a game whose file changes the engine's sources starts with its own host. `shell-log.txt` says so, and the other games in the app are unaffected.
- The Engine setting appears only for such a game, and "The shared app's engine" starts it on the built-in host.
- The engine tests (`dm/ios/tests/test_shell_build.py`, `test_framework_build.py`, `dm/tools/tests/test_launcher_settings.py`) and the launcher tests (`GameArchiveTests`, `BuildStoreTests`, the shell mirror, export and install tests) cover the file, the host build, the embedding, the setting and the mirror.
- Patches 0071 and 0072 are forwarded to seedds/nxnative.

### Tested

Tested on a Mac and on an iPhone. Each game below fails without its game engine file: either the build fails or the app crashes at runtime. With the file, it builds and runs.

| Game | What its file holds |
|---|---|
| Mina the Hollower (0100DCD01F306000) | Only its `dm/games` folder: memory addresses, and shader handling specific to this game |
| Dispatch (01008BA02525A000) | Only its `dm/games` folder |
| Scott Pilgrim (0100D59022590000) | Its folder and an `engine.patch`. The patch adds code for Epic Online Services and changes the Vulkan code, so in the shared app the game runs on its own host |

### For future consideration: the security of a file from an untrusted source

A `.nxgame` file is code, not data, and this needs a discussion before game engine files are shared widely.

**What a file can run:**

- **On the Mac, during the build.**
  - A game's folder can hold Python (`patches.py`, which 22 games have today), and the build runs it.
  - `engine.patch` can change any engine file, including the build scripts the launcher runs.
  - Either way, the file runs code with the user's rights on the Mac: their files, their keys and their network.
- **On the iPhone or the Mac, at runtime.**
  - The build compiles the file's changes into the app (the game's framework, and for the shared app the game's own host).
  - That code runs on the user's device, inside the app: with its data, its saves, the other games of the shared app, and the network.

**What the launcher does today:**

- It checks the SHA-256 of every file against the manifest. That shows the file isn't damaged, not who made it: anyone can edit a file and rewrite its manifest.
- On a file's first use, it asks for confirmation, showing the author (as written in the manifest), the engine files it changes, and a reminder to use only files from people you trust.
- The installed engine is never changed, but the build itself isn't sandboxed.

**Options to discuss:**

- **Signed files.** An author signs a file with a key the launcher trusts, as the engine releases are signed (`engine-signing.pub`). Then: who holds the keys, and what does the launcher do with an unsigned file? Refuse it, or warn louder?
- **A reviewed source.** Files from a place where maintainers review them (an issue or a PR here, a catalog), with the launcher showing where a file comes from.
- **Showing what it changes.** Before the first build, show the full `engine.patch` and the game folder's Python, not only the list of files.
- **Limiting what a file may change.**
  - A file with only the game's data files (`.tsv`) would be lower risk than one with Python or an `engine.patch`, and the launcher could tell the two apart.
  - An `engine.patch` could be limited to some paths, or refused when it changes the build scripts.
- **A sandboxed build.** Run the build with `sandbox-exec` or a separate user, with no access to the user's files beyond the build's inputs and outputs.
- **The runtime side.** None of the above limits what the compiled code does on the device once the build has finished, so a trusted source matters most there.
title: Game engine files (.nxgame): build a game the launcher's engine doesn't support yet, with a host of its own in the shared app

### What happens

A tester of v1.1.0-rc2 reports that "Exit Game" in the in-game menu on iPhone and iPad leads to the Home screen and not back to the launcher.

### Cause

The iOS shell runs one game per process. After "Exit Game" the app closes, and iOS does not let an app start itself again. The launcher screen comes back when the app is opened again. This is how #421 works, but nothing says it.

### Plan

- Say it in the quit prompt: the app closes and you open it again to get back to the launcher. The texts are shell texts, so they go into all six languages.
- Say it in the notes of the next release.
- Going back to the launcher without closing needs several games in one process. That is an architecture change and not part of this issue.

### Done when

The quit prompt tells the player what happens next.
title: iOS Exit Game: the quit prompt does not say the app closes

### This is

An idea

### What happens, or what you would like

The Windows Qt build (`build-qt.yml`) produces an app **without an engine tree**. The only way a Windows player gets one is the repo route: download the repository, install PortableGit, run `tools/engine.py sync`. That route needs git, breaks on symlinks (the SDK's `.tbd` aliases), leaves empty folders on a failed sync, and pulls untested code from main.

The Mac release app carries its own engine (`Contents/Resources/engine`) and never touches git. The Windows build should work the same way: `build-qt.yml` runs `tools/engine.py tree`, and the zip carries the engine tree alongside the app. The Qt app finds it and skips the repo/sync path entirely.

The repo route stays for developers who edit the source, but it is no longer the only path for a player.

**Source handoff:** [final patches, licence, reproduction steps and validation notes](https://gist.github.com/zatteogit/42e0bab63638f547ecf0e6ed3e38ee39). The combined prototype and the independent Italian, inventory and icon patches are listed separately.

## This is
A problem

## What happens
Some custom launcher controls have visual labels and pointer handling without equivalent native accessibility behaviour. The source baseline inspected was `6a3d130d325b1969bd911e51a8327faf090b4253` (the combined local prototype was originally developed on `c15b057`).

Reproduction routes to check on that baseline:
1. Open game launch options and inspect a slider with Accessibility Inspector or VoiceOver. A custom drag gesture alone does not expose native slider adjustment, bounds and keyboard behaviour.
2. Inspect custom switches and repeated reset-arrow buttons. Each should expose a switch value or a label identifying which setting it resets.
3. Open a custom Manage/choice menu. Keyboard focus and accessibility focus should remain with the menu, with Escape closing it and no actions firing behind it.
4. Enable Reduce Motion and inspect custom segment, toggle and disclosure transitions.

## Expected
Native roles/values and keyboard adjustment, meaningful per-control names, a clear selected state, accessible modal menus, and reduced-motion behaviour.

## Local changes for review
The prototype uses a native slider, a native switch accessibility representation, setting-specific reset labels, selected/heading traits and modal-menu accessibility handling. It also uses distinct selected navigation styling and measured foreground/background contrast pairs in light and dark appearances. Hover feedback is supplementary and does not replace keyboard focus or selection.

These changes are included in `01-final-launcher-prototype.patch` in the source handoff. That patch is a combined prototype, not a focused accessibility PR; the fixes should be extracted into smaller changes if wanted. The catalogue-only Italian patch is independent.

## NX2Apple version
Source comparison: `6a3d130d325b1969bd911e51a8327faf090b4253`. Local installed test app: `1.0.2-local`, based on `c15b057` plus the prototype.

## Computer and OS
MacBook Pro, Apple M3 Max, 64 GB, macOS 27.0.1.

## Evidence and limits
Native accessibility-tree inspections and selected component/layout/contrast checks were performed. This is **not** a completed VoiceOver spoken-navigation certification or a full keyboard-only audit. Increased Contrast and every Reduce Transparency combination still need manual end-to-end testing. New hover styling has been compiled and is available for pointer review; the automation does not expose a standalone mouse-move action.

## No keys, no game files
- [x] Nothing in the source handoff contains keys, game files or extracted game data. The existing licence is retained. Credit may use **Zatteo**.

Validation detail: the expanded launcher/model suites passed, but the full run has one failing, unchanged Python-venv logging test in NXCore. `VALIDATION.md` records this and the remaining manual checks. The handoff is not CI-approved.

Source baseline note: main had advanced to `c1cf03b6e6edf3e25a2e46bc0189249d207675d1` when this was posted. The handoff is pinned to the earlier, explicitly tested `6a3d130d325b1969bd911e51a8327faf090b4253` snapshot; it has not been retested on the newer tip.

body:
### Idea

A player exports the shared app as an IPA, signs it with another tool (Feather, Flarestore) and installs it. Step 3 "Send the game data" to the device then fails. In #491 the player copied the game data with Finder instead, and that works: the device in the Finder sidebar, the Files tab, the game data dragged onto the app.

The launcher should say what happened in plain words and offer the Finder way as a second option. Only after the copy to the device did not work. The automatic send stays the one way by default.

What I believe, but have not verified on a device: `devicectl device copy to --domain-type appDataContainer` writes into an app only when the app allows it, for example with `get-task-allow`. An app that another tool signed may not. The launcher should not state this as fact. It says that the device refused the copy and keeps devicectl's own words behind Details.

### Plan

- When the device refuses the copy into an app it listed, step 3 says so in one sentence and shows a button "Copy with Finder". A copy error is always a refusal there, even when its words sound like a missing app, because the device listed the app.
- When the device lists no copy of the shared app, the sentence says to install the IPA first, or to copy with Finder if it is installed already (another tool may have changed its bundle ID).
- "Copy with Finder" opens a Finder window with the game's folder selected (`games/<title ID>`, which holds `romfs.img` and the add-on content) and shows three short steps: connect the iPhone and select it in the Finder sidebar, choose Files and drag the folder onto the app, on the iPhone tap the game, then "Choose game data", and pick that folder.
- An app list the device does not give (locked, not connected) gets a plain sentence too, without the Finder way.
- Texts in `frontend/l10n` for every language.

### Done when

- The refusal and the missing app show the sentence and "Copy with Finder", nothing else changes for a send that works.
- The mapping from the end of a send to the state step 3 shows is a pure function with tests, and so is the folder Finder shows.
- Before and after screenshots are in the PR.
title: Send game data: show the Finder way when the copy to the device is refused

body:
### Idea

@Haseenesss suggested this in #495. Controllers like the Xbox Elite or the DualSense Edge have back paddles. Today the shell cannot show them and a game cannot use them, because the engine does not read them and `DM_PAD_MAP` has no source for them.

### Plan

- Engine: read the paddles from GameController (`GCXboxGamepad` and `GCDualSenseGamepad` expose them as extra buttons) and give each one a name as a source in `DM_PAD_MAP`. A paddle sends nothing until it is mapped. This goes to seedds/nxnative as a PR first and lands here as a patch.
- Shell: the button test gets a back view and lights the paddles of a controller that has them. The mapping card gets rows for the paddles, only when a connected controller has them, where each paddle can send any Switch button or nothing.

### Done when

- On an Elite controller or a DualSense Edge, the button test shows each paddle when it is pressed.
- A paddle mapped to a Switch button presses that button in a game, and an unmapped paddle does nothing.
- The engine change is merged in seedds/nxnative or carried as a forwarded patch.
title: Controller back paddles: read them and map them

body:
### Idea

When a game has no resolution setting, the settings sheet of the Mac launcher says nothing. The player looks for a scale slider or a resolution box and finds none (#534, Xenoblade Chronicles 2). A short note in the sheet, for example "This game has no resolution setting yet", would say why.

### Plan

- Show the note in the game's settings sheet when the game's build has no render scale row.
- Same words in all languages the launcher has.
- Name what is available instead: Console mode and Upscaling, when they are shown.

### Done when

- A game without a render scale hook shows the note, and a game with one does not.
- A test covers both cases.
title: Game settings: say why there is no resolution row

body:
### Idea

Let the player delete a game from the launcher on the Mac and from the iPhone and iPad app. Today the only way is to delete files by hand in Finder or in the Files app. On iOS the game stays listed after that, as reported in Discussion #556.

### Plan

- Mac: a "Delete" action on a game in the library. It asks first and says what goes away: the game's app or framework, its build folder and, as a separate choice, its saves.
- iPhone and iPad: a "Delete" action on a game in the shell. It removes the game's data in `Documents/games/<title ID>` and takes the game off the list. Whether the game's framework inside the shared app can be removed without a new IPA is not checked yet.
- Saves are never deleted without an explicit choice.
- The wording and the confirmation are the same on both.

### Done when

- A game can be deleted on the Mac and on iOS from the launcher, without touching files by hand.
- The saves stay unless the player chooses to delete them too.
- A test covers what is removed and what stays.

Discussion: https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/discussions/556

body:
### This is

An idea

### What happens, or what you would like

The shared iPhone/iPad shell (`NX2Apple`, one app that holds every built game) reads one environment file for the whole app and applies it to whichever game is launched:

- `dm/ios/Shell/ShellApp.swift`, added by [`patches/0050-route-c-shell.patch`](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/blob/main/patches/0050-route-c-shell.patch), in `EngineGameLauncher.launch`: `let envFile = try? String(contentsOf: documents.appendingPathComponent("env.txt"), encoding: .utf8)`
- [`frontend-ios/Sources/ShellHost/EngineLaunchPlan.swift#L23-L57`](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/blob/main/frontend-ios/Sources/ShellHost/EngineLaunchPlan.swift#L23-L57): those keys are merged into every game's launch environment, after the per-game settings.

So a per-game switch has no per-game scope. Example: a mod enabled through `DM_ROMFS_OVERLAY=<dir>` in `Documents/env.txt` stays set when another game starts. To play the other game without it, the player has to open the Files app and comment the line out — and while it stays in, every RomFS read of every game consults the other game's overlay first (a path collision silently serves the wrong file). The same applies to every other `DM_*` switch that is not a row in the game's `launcher.json`, since `Documents/env.txt` is the only way to set those.

The shell already has a per-game folder: `Documents/games/<title ID>/` holds the save, temp, an optional per-game profile (`profile.tsv`) and `cheats/`. A per-game env file fits that layout. The Mac launcher already keeps mods per game and passes them for one game's Play ([`frontend/Sources/NX2Apple/Library.swift#L183-L239`](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/blob/main/frontend/Sources/NX2Apple/Library.swift#L183-L239), `modEnvironment`), and the engine takes `DM_ROMFS_OVERLAY` per process ([`dm/host/hle_fs.c`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/main/dm/host/hle_fs.c)), so nothing is needed upstream: upstream's single-game iPhone app has one app per game, so its one `Documents/env.txt` is already per game.

Proposal:

1. Read `Documents/games/<title ID>/env.txt` in addition to `Documents/env.txt`, with the per-game file winning over the shared one (the explicit launch environment still wins over both). Passing both texts into `EngineLaunchPlan.make` and merging them in that order should be enough.
2. Optional follow-up: mods parity with the Mac launcher — `Documents/mods/<title ID>/<mod>/`, per-game toggles in the existing suite (`dev.nx2apple.shell.game.<title ID>`), and `EngineLaunchPlan` building `DM_ROMFS_OVERLAY` the way `modEnvironment` does on the Mac.

### What I expected

A mod, and any other `DM_*` switch typed in an env file, stays with the game it belongs to. Switching games needs no edit of a shared file.

### NX2Apple version

v1.0.1 installed (v1.0.2 is current; `main` still reads only `Documents/env.txt`).

### Computer and OS

MacBook Pro (MacBookPro18,4), Apple M1 Max, 64 GB, macOS 27.2 (26B123).
Device: iPad mini (A17 Pro) (iPad16,1), iPadOS 26.7.2 (23H128).
Shared shell app: `org.nxnative.shell.9PRS9BN7AA` v1.0, holding The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild (`01007EF00011E000`) and Hades II (`0100A00019DE0000`).

### Copy diagnostics

Not needed for an idea, per the form. The behavior above is read from `main` (c15b057).

### No keys, no game files

- [X] Nothing attached here contains keys, game files or data extracted from a game.
title: iOS shell: one Documents/env.txt for every game — add a per-game env.txt (a mod via DM_ROMFS_OVERLAY leaks into other games)
