## Reproduced

Just Dance (0100BEE017FC0000) with base v0, update v983040 and five DLCs. Reusing a provisional profile generated from v0 silently packed 1.0.0 despite the update being present and detected by the build-ID lookup. Explicit --package v983040 was refused because the cached provisional profile registered only v0. Using a separate --profile-out generated a profile for the actual update and produced a 25.0.3 Mac app.

## Expected

A selected update should be built, or the desktop should stop with an actionable mismatch notice. Cached provisional profiles must not silently pin a previously surveyed base version. Preserve old profiles/caches while deriving or surveying the selected version.

## Offline import request

Allow explicit import of a local save seed and indexed cache-storage directories, with backups, separate writable runtime storage, no overwrites of existing saves, capacity checks, provenance/compatibility warnings and first-run progress. Do not bundle DBI: it is a Switch transfer tool, not runtime game content.

## Engine prerequisites and validation limits

The installed engine lacks nn::fs::GetCacheStorageMax (Just Dance 25.0.3 null-dereferences the uninitialized SDK service at sdk+0x34fb44) and reports no cache entries. A diagnostic host reading NACP cache limits and enumerating actual cache directories reports nine entries, mounts indices 0–8 and reads OfflineSaveNx.txt. This establishes file access, NOT offline songs/playability. The supplied offline catalog identifies itself as a third-party mod, so compatibility must not be assumed from the version string alone.

A portable packaging candidate is still under validation; no desktop UI changes or screenshots are claimed here. No keys, game binaries, song assets or saves attached.
title: Just Dance: cached provisional profile ignores supplied update; offline save/cache import needs explicit support

body:
### Idea

Add a launcher setting **"Downsample BC HDR textures"** (`DM_BC6H_RGB9E5`) under the **Performance** section.

On pre-A17 Apple devices (e.g., iPhone 14 Pro, iPhone 13, iPad 9/10 with A15/A16 and earlier chips), hardware BC texture compression is unsupported (`[MTLDevice supportsBCTextureCompression] == NO`), requiring block-compressed textures to be decompressed on the CPU. For BC6H HDR textures, standard decompression expands them from 1 B/px into 8 B/px (`RGBA16Float`). In heavy scenes of games like *The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom* and *Breath of the Wild*, this 8× expansion inflates texture memory past the iOS process jetsam ceiling (~3.5–4.0 GB) and triggers an OS out-of-memory termination.

This setting decodes BC6H textures into `RGB9E5Float` (4 B/px instead of 8 B/px), halving the RAM footprint of HDR textures with virtually indistinguishable visual difference on mobile displays.

### Where it shows

* **Launcher (Mac SwiftUI & Windows Qt)**:
  * Section: **Performance**
  * Title: `Downsample BC HDR textures`
  * Note: `Save RAM by slightly reducing the quality of some textures`
  * Values: `1` (on, default on devices lacking BC compression), `0` (off)
* **iPhone Shell (`LauncherSettings.swift`)**:
  * Shows under the **Performance** section of the in-game / launcher settings.
  * **Dynamic visibility**: Automatically hidden if the device supports native BC compression (`MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice()?.supportsBCTextureCompression == true`), so users on A17 Pro+ / M-series Macs are not presented with an irrelevant setting.

### Plan

1. **Launcher UI & Localization**:
   * Add `DM_BC6H_RGB9E5` toggle under `Performance` in `dm/games/settings.tsv`.
   * Add localized strings for English, Chinese (`zh`), Swedish (`sv`), German (`de`), and French (`fr`) in `frontend/Sources/NXCore/Localization.swift` and `frontend-qt/nspb_qt/localization.py`.
   * Wire visibility check in `dm/ios/Sources/LauncherSettings.swift` to hide on native BC devices.
2. **Engine / NVN layer**:
   * In `nvn_mtl.m`, when `g_bc_cpu` is active and `DM_BC6H_RGB9E5 != 0`, select Path 3 (`BC_PATH_CPU_RGB9E5`) during `mtl_init()`.
   * Decode BC6H blocks to `RGB9E5Float` (Metal `MTLPixelFormatRGB9E5Float`), using unpacked format `0x3c` (`RGB9E5Float`) in `nvn_bcdec.c`.
3. **Tests**:
   * Verify with `t_bcdec` (BC6H RGB9E5 decoder accuracy and range clamping).
   * Verify with `LaunchOptionsTests` and `test_launcher_settings.py`.

### Done when

- [ ] `DM_BC6H_RGB9E5` toggle is present under Performance in Mac, Qt, and iOS launcher settings.
- [ ] Dynamically hidden on devices with hardware BC support (`supportsBCTextureCompression == true`).
- [ ] Default is `1` (enabled) on pre-A17 devices, reducing HDR texture RAM by 50%.
- [ ] All launcher localization and test suites pass.
title: Idea: Downsample BC HDR textures setting (DM_BC6H_RGB9E5) under Performance for pre-A17 devices

body:
### Idea

Export as IPA (#416, #531) makes the shared app as one IPA, and the game data goes over afterwards (to the app on the device, or to a drive). Some sideloading tools can only install an IPA and cannot copy data into an app. Players with such a tool have no way to get the game data in.

So the export gets a second kind of IPA: one game with everything inside, its game data (RomFS) and add-on content included. One IPA per game, nothing to send afterwards.

### Plan

- The shared app stays the default. The new kind is a choice in the Export card, never picked for the player.
- Under "Install or export", when Export as IPA is on, a row "IPA contents" with two choices: "Shared app" (today's three steps) and "One game, all inside".
- With "One game, all inside" the card shows two steps: export the IPA, install it with your own tool. Step 3 (send the game data) is gone, because the data is inside. The row's note says what this costs: the IPA is as large as the game, and the game's saves stay in that app.
- The build runs the engine's own one-game IPA path, the one upstream builds by default: `build_ipa_from_nsp.py --platform ios --romfs bundle -o <folder>/<title ID>.ipa`. The game's files go to `<App>/romfs` and `<App>/aoc`, which the engine's app reads when Documents has no image. `pack_ipa.py` writes zip64 for files and offsets above 4 GB. No engine patch, no change to the iOS shell.
- The IPA lands next to the game's build folder (the output folder, else the game's folder), named `<title ID>.ipa`, with bundle ID `org.nxnative.<title ID>`.

### Not verified

- Whether every sideloading tool installs an IPA of 10 GB and more. The engine's own build_ipa.sh warns that a large game's full package can exceed what iOS extracts. I have not measured where that limit is.
- How long AltStore or SideStore need for such an IPA on the device.

### Alternatives I looked at

- The shared app with one game and its data inside: needs a change in the iOS shell (it reads game data from Documents only, never from its bundle) and its own bundle ID per game. More work for the same result.
- Keeping only the shared app: leaves players without a data copy tool stuck.

### Done when

- The Export card has the choice, with the shared app as default, in all five required languages.
- One game, all inside builds one IPA with the RomFS inside and shows it in step 1.
- Before and after screenshots in the PR.
title: Export: one IPA per game with the game data inside

body:
### This is

A problem.

### What happens, or what you would like

A game whose input file name carries no title ID builds fine, then fails after the build with:

```
The game's framework was not found: /…/The_Legend_of_Zelda_Breath_of_the_Wild-7603d90e_build/shell-framework/DmGameThe_Legen…
```

The build itself succeeded and wrote the framework under the title ID name (`game framework ✓ DmGame01007EF00011E000.framework` in the stage list). The failure is the handoff to the shell app right after the build.

Why: the launcher derives the framework path from the build **key**, not from what the build wrote (`ContentView.swift:1450`):

```swift
let tid = Self.buildKey(self.basePath)
let fw = ShellInstall.frameworkPath(workDir: self.effectiveWorkDir, titleID: tid)
```

`buildKey` (`ContentView.swift:1216`) prefers a 16-hex-digit title ID parsed from the file name, and otherwise falls back to the cleaned file name plus a hash. The engine side always names the framework after the **real** title ID it read from the game data (`build_ipa.sh`: `FW_NAME=DmGame$(echo "$GAME" | tr 'a-z' 'A-Z')`, and `build_ipa_from_nsp.py` mirrors that). On a file name like `The_Legend_of_Zelda_Breath_of_the_Wild-7603d90e` the parse fails (`-7603d90e` is 8 hex digits, and `titleID()` needs `01` + 14 more), so the launcher looks for `DmGameThe_Legend….framework`, which the build never wrote. Games whose file names carry `[01007EF00011E000]` or a bare `01…` ID are unaffected, which is why this hides.

Reproduction: pick an NSP or folder named without a parseable title ID, build to the shell (iPhone/iPad target), and the build finishes, then the install step reports the framework was not found.

### What you expected

The install step should embed the framework the build actually wrote, regardless of what the input file is called.

### Fix direction

- After the build, use the path the script printed (`game framework: <path>`) or take the one `DmGame*.framework` in `<work>/shell-framework/` — a build folder holds exactly one. `buildKey` stays only what it is good at: the work folder name.
- A test covers the handoff with an input name that has no title ID (the framework path comes from the build, not from the name).
- No visible change, no capture needed.

A player-side workaround until then: rename the input to carry the title ID, e.g. `The Legend of Zelda Breath of the Wild [01007EF00011E000].nsp`. That changes the work folder, so the build runs again from an empty cache.

### NX2Apple version

Seen on the build a player ran on 2026-11-02 (version not captured in the report). The code path quoted above is on `main` today.

### Computer and OS

macOS, Apple silicon (the player's Mac). Exact version not captured; the failure is deterministic from the code path, not environment-dependent.

### Copy diagnostics

Not captured. The build log lines in the report show the mismatched lookup path after a green build:

```
[17:14:09] game framework ✓ DmGame01007EF00011E000.framework
The game's framework was not found: /…/The_Legend_of_Zelda_Breath_of_the_Wild-7603d90e_build/shell-framework/DmGameThe_Legen…
```

(The two `[RED]` lines above it in that log are a separate matter: the game's build version is not one the profile registered, so function patches may not apply. They do not cause this error.)

### No keys, no game files

Nothing attached here contains keys, game files or data extracted from a game. Only file paths, log lines and code references.
title: Shell install: a game whose file name has no title ID fails after the build ("The game's framework was not found")

body:
### Idea

Switch 2 titles reach the fork as an **already-extracted dump folder**, not as an NSP/XCI:

```
<game folder>/
  base/exefs/{main, main.npdm, sdk, rtld, subsdk*}
  base/romfs/
  updates/458752/{exefs, romfs}        the version as a decimal number
  dlc/040074a01bf13001/<n>/romfs/      the DLC title ID in hex
```

The engine already builds from that layout (`scripts/pack_dump.py`, `build_ipa_from_nsp.py <folder> --platform mac-app`, seedds/nxnative `99947471`): the title ID comes from the ACI0 program ID in `main.npdm`, no `prod.keys` are needed, and the update's RomFS is the patched tree, packed on its own.

The launcher cannot take it. Its input rows are file pickers and `InputStaging.gameExtensions` is `nsp/xci/nsz/xcz`, with no dump branch anywhere in `NXLauncher`. Picking a dump folder finds no `.nsp`, so the game is silently "not recognised" — which is what happened with Donkey Kong Bananza (`040074A01BF12000`, update `458752`, DLC `040074A01BF13001`), the first title that exists only in this form. A dump that scans correctly with `pack_dump.scan()` therefore cannot be built from the app at all.

### Plan

- A fifth input row, **Game folder (dump)**, using a directory picker instead of a file picker.
- Validate on pick with the engine's own test (`base/exefs/main.npdm` is a NMDM and `base/romfs` is a directory), then show what was found: the title ID from the program ID, the update versions and the DLC title IDs. A folder that fails the test says which piece is missing rather than "nothing found".
- With that row filled, pass the folder as the script's positional argument and disable the base/update/DLC/keys rows: a dump needs no keys, and there is no separate update or DLC file to pick. Clearing the row restores the package path.
- Refuse a folder that also holds packages beside the dump (`dump_folder()` ignores the dump when a `.nsp/.xci/.nsz/.xcz` sits in it) and name the conflicting file, instead of failing later inside the script.
- Keep the existing staging for the package path unchanged, and keep `<dump folder>/<title ID>_build` as the build folder so a repeat build reuses it.

### Done when

- Picking a dump folder shows its title ID, update and DLC in the rows, and Start build runs the script with the folder and the chosen target, with no keys.
- The Donkey Kong Bananza dump builds to a Mac app end to end from the launcher.
- A folder without `base/exefs/main.npdm` is refused with the missing piece named, and a dump carrying NSPs names the conflicting file.
- The package path is unchanged: the existing tests and a package build still pass.
title: The launcher takes a game's dump folder: Switch 2 titles arrive as folders, not packages

### This is

A problem

### What happens, or what you would like

![The game row on the iPhone Duo outer screen, with the third card (Hades II) cut at the right edge](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f98d061b-7616-4d87-b788-2f069735abea)

On the **iPhone Duo outer screen**, with four games in the shell, the "Your games" row cuts the third card (Hades II) at the right edge of the screen. The cover and the title are sliced mid-card, there is no 24 pt margin and no rounded right edge. The hero at the top also shows a thin slice of the next picture at the right edge.

The row is built by `PortraitLibrary.coverSize` (`frontend-ios/Sources/ShellUI/PortraitLibrary.swift`). Its own comment says the layout shows whole cards only and the screen edge must fall in the gap between cards, never through a name or a status. The screenshot shows the edge inside a card, so the card width does not match the width the row actually gets on this screen.

The inner and outer screens of the iPhone Duo have the same aspect ratio and differ only in width, so the likely cause is the width-dependent card count or the `wide`/`short` branch. Two games fit, and the problem starts with the third.

### What you expected

- Up to two games: two whole cards, same margin on both sides.
- Three or more: whole cards only, so the screen edge falls between cards, or a horizontal scroll whose next card shows its rounded edge and the right margin. No title cut in half.

### NX2Apple version

Not shown in the report (1.0.1 era).

### Computer and OS

iPhone Duo, outer screen. The iOS version is not in the report.

Not available for this report.

### This is

An idea

### What happens, or what you would like

The Builds page already explains under **Save to** that the output folder is also the build cache. It does not say that an external drive makes a first build much slower, and players who keep their games and output folder on a USB drive run into it without knowing why.

Measured on this Mac (1,500 files of 32 KB, then 6,000):

| | internal APFS | external exFAT over USB |
|---|---|---|
| create | 0.12 ms per file | 1.7 ms per file, 14 times slower |
| delete | 0.06 ms per file | 0.87 ms per file, 16 times slower |
| `._` sidecar files | none | one per file (`com.apple.provenance` becomes an AppleDouble file on exFAT) |

A shader-heavy game makes this visible: Tears of the Kingdom has 28,669 shaders, so the shader step writes about 71,621 libraries plus 28,669 reflection files, and the build creates and deletes a few hundred thousand small files. That is roughly 5 to 15 minutes more on a first build on an external SSD, and worse on exFAT or a mechanical drive. Small games barely notice it.

Add one sentence to the existing hint, in all five languages:

Chinese: 当「输出目录」为外置硬盘时，首次构建会明显变慢（exFAT 或机械硬盘更明显）。
English: When the output folder is on an external drive, a first build is noticeably slower (worse on exFAT or a hard disk).

This follows the existing `msg.workdirHint` text, so it shows whenever the hint shows. No detection code, no new key, no layout change.

### What you expected

A player who picks an external output folder knows before the first build why it is slow, and can move the folder to the built-in disk.

### NX2Apple version

1.0.1

### Computer and OS

MacBook Pro, Apple M1 Pro, 16 GB, macOS 26.6.2, Samsung T7 as `/Volumes/Samsung` (exFAT, USB)

### Idea

The Mac launcher has no place to see or set a game's cloud saves folder, and no sign that a save is syncing. The engine does the sync (`DM_SAVE_SYNC`, one `<title ID>/save.dmsync` file per game). The player can only reach it through a line in the game's `env.txt`. The iPhone launcher has a Cloud saves row. #490 shows the result: the Mac kept an old folder, the iPhone used another, and nothing on screen said so.

### Plan

- A Cloud saves row in each game's settings on the Mac. It shows the folder (`DM_SAVE_SYNC` from `env.txt`, else the app's `cloudSaves.folder`), with Choose a folder and Turn off.
- A sync state next to it, read from the `save sync:` lines of the game's log: in step with the cloud, a newer save brought in, a save sent, offline, or an error with its text. It shows the time of the last result.
- A notice when the folder does not exist or holds no `<title ID>/save.dmsync` for the game, so a wrong folder is visible before the first play.
- Strings in all language files, a test that reads sample logs and gives the state, and a capture of the row.

### Done when

- A player can see and change the cloud saves folder of a game without editing a file.
- After a play session the row says whether the save was sent, with the time.
- A folder that nobody else writes to is shown as such.
- The row is covered by tests with sample `env.txt` files of older versions.
title: Mac launcher: show and set the cloud saves folder, and show when a save syncs

body: ### Idea The iOS shell (`frontend-ios`) has no way to change what a physical controller's buttons send in games. Players with an Xbox or PlayStation controller often want A and B swapped, and some games want a single button moved or turned off. ### Plan - A global button mapping in the Controllers page (the controller button at the top right), with a one-tap Swap A and B and a row per button (any button or none). - A per-game mapping in each game's settings. It follows the global one by default and can override single buttons or turn the swap off for that game only. Per button, the game wins over global, global over default. - The shell passes the merged result to the engine as `DM_PAD_MAP` at launch. The iOS host (`dm/ios/Sources/DmGamepad.m`) applies it to physical controllers, as the Mac host already does (a patch in `patches/`, upstream in parallel). Shell menus keep A to confirm and B to go back. Touch controls are unchanged. - The mapping opens in a card of its own, laid out like the language list. - A Button test in the Controllers page: an Xbox-style controller drawing that lights up each button, trigger and stick as it is pressed. ### Done when - Swap A and B in the Controllers page swaps A and B in every game. - A game set to "Off" keeps A and B unswapped while the others swap. - The Button test shows every press of the first controller. - Shell navigation is not affected by the mapping.

### This is

A problem

### What happens, or what you would like

![The launcher fails at 准备共用应用: 你不能保存文件"NX2Apple-shell"，因为"Macintosh HD"是只读卷](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/14da9229-57bd-4ab5-9a91-6f877dd8b4c8)

A user's iPhone build ran through extraction, rewrite, GL capture, the game framework and packing the game data, and then failed at the last step:

> 无法准备共用应用：你不能保存文件“NX2Apple-shell”，因为“Macintosh HD”是只读卷。

The build log above it already named the folder:

> library: 0100217023F6C000's framework could not be mirrored at /NX2Apple-shell/frameworks/…, it stays at …
> banner: 0100217023F6C000 /Users/lily/Library/Application Support/NS Port Builder/artwork/…

so the shell root was `/NX2Apple-shell`, the root of the read-only system volume.

**Cause.** `ShellLibrary.resolveRoot` (`frontend/Sources/NX2Apple/ShellInstall.swift`) computes `<parent>/NX2Apple-shell` and saves it in the `shellRoot` default on the first call. `parent` is the output folder, else the folder that holds the game files. When the function runs before a game is chosen — the Settings page shows the shell cache path, `BuildModel.shellCachePath` — the parent is `""`, and `("" as NSString).deletingLastPathComponent` is `""`, so the root becomes `/NX2Apple-shell`. From then on every build uses that saved value; the write fails on the read-only system volume only at the last step, after the whole build.

**Workaround for anyone who hits it:** quit the launcher, run `defaults delete org.nxnative.NSPortBuilder shellRoot`, reopen it and pick the game before opening Settings. The finished build folder is kept (the extraction, the split and the framework are reused), so the rebuild goes quickly to the last step.

### What you expected

The shell root is never the root of a volume; a saved value like `/NX2Apple-shell` is repaired; and an unwritable shell folder stops the build before it starts, with a message that says which folder to change.

### NX2Apple version

Not shown in the report (1.0.0 / 1.0.1 era; the shell cache row in Settings arrived with #398)

### Computer and OS

The reporter's Mac (macOS, user folder `/Users/lily`); the model is not in the report

Not available for this report.

body:
### This is

A problem

### What happens, or what you would like

Building **The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom v1.4.3** (title ID `0100F2C0115B6000`, base + update `v720896`) for iPhone / iPad, the Builds page sat at `着色器拆分 · splitting · 304,227 / 304,243 files` (99%) for about **8 minutes** with no movement.

It was not a hang. Sampling the process at the stall showed:

- 8 worker processes; **one** at 98.4% CPU and 1.2 GB RSS, the other seven idle;
- the one busy worker had `backports.zstd` (`_zstd.cpython-313-darwin.so`) loaded — it was decompressing zstd data;
- when it finished, the count jumped straight to `304243/304243` and the step reported `shaders: 28669 (compute 257, pixel 13646, vertex 14766); ... variation pairs 20016`.

The whole shader split took about 9 minutes, so the frozen tail was almost the entire stage.

**Why the count freezes.** `dm/gfx/tools/shader_split.py` reports progress per finished **batch**, not per file: `pooled(..., chunk=16)` prints `progress: <done>/<total>` where `done` counts whole 16-file batches (`cf.wait` over batch futures). `304,243 - 304,227 = 16`, i.e. exactly one batch was still running. Inside a batch there is no progress, and inside one file there is no parallelism. Tears of the Kingdom keeps 15,080 `Pack/*.pack.zs` files compressed with zstd dictionaries (the docstring in `shader_split.py` says so); one heavy pack in that batch means minutes of single-threaded decompress + scan while the UI says 304,227.

**Why it matters.** To a player this looks like a freeze, not work. The natural reaction is to force-quit and start over, which loses the extraction and the whole split and makes the build feel broken. Any game with a big archive can hit this, not just TotK.

**Options (for v0 to judge against the build-speed work):**

1. Count completed **files**, not batches: a shared counter (`multiprocessing.Value`) incremented per file in the worker, so the stage moves per file. The last file still stalls, but at `304242/304243` instead of `304227/304243`, which reads as work rather than a hang.
2. Publish the **current file** per worker (a shared dict or a small progress file) and show `splitting · Pack/<name>.pack.zs` in the stage line. The count may stand still, but the user sees it is reading something specific.
3. **Stall hint** in the launcher: when a stage has not advanced for 60 s, add "large archive, still working" with the elapsed time. UI-only, no engine change.
4. Skip files that cannot carry shaders by extension (`.webm`, audio containers): small gain and a risk of missing a source, so probably not worth it.
5. Parallelise inside an archive (split a pack's members across workers): the real speedup, but a much larger change. This is the one that overlaps the build-time work.

1 and 3 would remove the "it hung" impression cheaply; 2 helps most when a single file is minutes long; 5 is the only one that makes the stage shorter.

### What you expected

The progress reflects something that is still moving (or names the file being worked on), so an 8-minute heavy archive does not look like a frozen 99%.

### NX2Apple version

v1.0.1-local (a local test build of v1.0.1-rc2 with build-timing instrumentation; the shader split code itself is unmodified), engine `cd859c38a8f8`

### Computer and OS

MacBook Pro, Apple M1 Pro, 16 GB, macOS 26.6.2

### Copy diagnostics

Not included: this was a local test build without an update manifest. The build folder is `~/Downloads/Switch Rom/0100F2C0115B6000_build`; `logs/shader_split.log` is the log quoted above.

title: Shader split: progress sits at 99% for minutes on one heavy 16-file batch (Tears of the Kingdom), and users read it as a hang

body:
## Environment

- macOS 27.2, Xcode 27.2 (27B52)
- NX2Apple 0.7.5 (release app)
- iPad `iPad16,1`, iPadOS 26.7.2 — wired USB, Trust set, **Developer Mode enabled**
- iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 27.2 — paired over Wi-Fi

## Symptom

The device picker shows **no device at all**, so a build cannot be installed to a device from the app. The devices are there:

```
$ xcrun devicectl list devices
Name         Identifier                         State                Model
Ordis-mini   00008130-001E60C43C33803A (UDID)   available (paired)   iPad16,1
Ordis_17p    00008150-0002483E3A38401C (UDID)   available (paired)   iPhone18,1

$ xcrun devicectl device info details --device 00008130-001E60C43C33803A
    • Device Reality: physical
    • Developer Mode Status: Enabled (1)
    ...
```

`idevice_id -l` lists the iPad as well.

## Cause

Since Xcode 27.2, `xcrun devicectl list devices --json-output` **does not fill `hardwareProperties.reality` for iOS devices any more**. The JSON carries a `_deprecationNotice` (`hardwareProperties` / `deviceProperties` / `connectionProperties` → `properties`), and for this iPad and iPhone neither the deprecated block nor `properties.hardware` contains `reality`. The paired Apple Watch in the same output still has `"reality": "physical"`.

`frontend/Sources/NXCore/Devices.swift:72` requires it:

```swift
guard hardware["reality"] as? String == "physical", hardware["platform"] as? String == "iOS",
      connection["pairingState"] as? String == "paired",
      let udid = hardware["udid"] as? String, !udid.isEmpty else { return nil }
```

so every iOS device is dropped silently by `compactMap`. The Watch is dropped by `platform`, leaving an empty list.

## Suggested fix

A missing `reality` means a paired physical device; only an explicit `"simulated"` should be excluded:

```swift
let reality = hardware["reality"] as? String
guard reality != "simulated", hardware["platform"] as? String == "iOS",
      connection["pairingState"] as? String == "paired",
      let udid = hardware["udid"] as? String, !udid.isEmpty else { return nil }
```

The existing cases still behave: the simulator JSON in `frontend/Tests/NX2AppleTests/` has `"reality": "simulated"` (still rejected) and the unpaired case has no `pairingState` (still rejected). A test with the Xcode 27.2 shape (no `reality`, `pairingState: paired`) would cover the regression.

If you would rather read the newer field first, `properties.hardware.reality` can be consulted when present — but under 27.2 `list --json-output` does not fill it for iOS either.

## Verification

I patched a local build with the guard above and both devices parse from the same JSON; the app lists the iPad and the iPhone again and installs work. Happy to open a PR with the change and a test if that helps.
title: No device listed on Xcode 27.2: devicectl list omits hardwareProperties.reality for iOS devices

### Notes

exFAT has no native extended attributes, so macOS keeps each file's xattrs (`com.apple.provenance`, quarantine) in an AppleDouble file named `._<name>` beside it. `dm/mac/pack_app.py` does not expect them, and the pack breaks in three places:

1. the input globs (`MODULE_FILES`, `MSL_FILES`, `PSO_FILES`, `*.ttf`) match `._main.patched.bin` / `._..._b.metallib` as if they were modules and shaders, and `._x.patched.bin` then fails the fixups check;
2. `shutil.copy2` of the host cannot set the flags of the copy on exFAT (`chflags: Operation not permitted`), and `cp -R` carries the sidecars into the app (`DMModuleFiles` in the built `Info.plist` lists 18 `._*` entries);
3. `codesign` reads `Contents/MacOS/._nxnative` as a nested code object that is not signed and refuses the whole bundle.

On APFS the same build is fine, which is why this only shows up with a build folder or an app on an external exFAT drive.

Workaround without a code change: put `--work-dir` **and** `-o` on the same APFS volume. Putting only the output on APFS is not enough, the input step fails first.

`defaults write com.apple.desktopservices DSDontWriteUSBStores -bool true` does not help here, it only stops Finder writing `.DS_Store`; the `._` files come from the kernel when an xattr is set.

A fix follows in a pull request: skip those names in the input globs, copy without extended attributes (`cp -X`, `shutil.copy` instead of `copy2`), and strip what is left from the staged bundle before `codesign` reads it.
title: Mac app: a build or output folder on exFAT breaks the pack (._ sidecar files reach the inputs, the copies and codesign)

### Game and title ID

### Where it runs
Mac app

Mac, Apple M4 Pro, 24 GB

### macOS or iOS / iPadOS version
macOS 27.0.1

### How it was installed
Built from my own dump with NX2Apple

### NX2Apple version
0.7.5, engine with the patches below on top

### What happens, and when
Tracking issue for the fixes that take the Ezio Collection from a black screen to playable AC II. Each one is a fork patch (`Upstream-Status: pending`):

- **0055 Shader split: Scimitar .forge archives.** The shaders live in Ubisoft's Scimitar `.forge` archives (Oodle Leviathan / Mermaid entries), which the shader split did not read, so the title screen and menus drew nothing. Also: raw control sections in `main` that start off a 4-byte boundary.
- **0056 Mac app: multi-program applications.** The collection is four programs, and its menu starts each game with `ExecuteProgram`, which was a stub. The build now packs every program, and the Mac app switches programs in one window, as the Switch does.
- **0057 nvn-mtl: stage keeps a finalized program's shaders.** AC II finalizes a program that another stage still has bound, then reuses its memory. The host crashed in `keys_hash` (Desmond flickered in the Animus, then the game crashed).
- **0058 nvn-mtl: image buffer textures below 16-byte alignment.** AC II's occlusion culling writes "object visible" flags into buffer textures at pool offsets 8 mod 16. Apple GPUs address such views from the 16-byte boundary below, so the flags landed two objects early and walls and floors flickered in and out. Writes now go through an aligned shadow buffer. Checked in the game: the flicker is gone.
- **0059 DM_CTL diagnostics.** `shots <n> <folder>` captures consecutive frames, and `DM_NVN_VIS_ALL` can now be toggled while the game runs.

One more change is needed and cannot be a fork patch because it touches the shader chain: `dmsh_build.py` `vertex_ab` must accept a type-0 vertex shader whose c1 sits between parts A and B. 478 of Brotherhood's and Revelations' 2,238 VertexA/B shaders are like this. It belongs in a pull request to seedds/nxnative.

### What you expected
AC II plays without crashes or flicker; Brotherhood and Revelations start from the menu.

None

n/a (tracking issue for fixes)

No profile yet (provisional)

Available on request

title: [Crash] Hogwarts Legacy (0100F7E00C70E000) crashes after splash art / Preparing Pipelines

body:
### Idea

Every engine bump takes many upstream commits in. The last one, to `cd859c38`, was 53. nxnative has no releases and no changelog, so nobody tells us which commits change what a front end or a player depends on. We found out about the shader chain, the Xcode pin and the new NSP script messages only because they broke something or because we read the commits by hand. The backslash change in saves (`7c23cc0`, #461) shows that a diff does not always say it.

Part of the answer is upstream, see seedds/nxnative#905. The other part is ours: a step in the bump that lists the commits that probably matter, so a person reads those and not all 53.

### Plan

A script, run with `tools/engine.py bump` and in the `sync/upstream-<sha>` pull request, that lists the commits between the old and the new pin which touch:

- `dm/gfx/nvn/dmsh_chain.h`, `dmsh_chain.lock` and `own_compilers.py`: a shader chain move or a new requirement (a rebuild of every game, see #449).
- `docs/env_switches.tsv`: removed or changed lines, and changed rows for settings our launcher shows (`launch.set.*`).
- `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py`: arguments, the setting block, exit codes and error texts that our failure rows match.
- `docs/frontends.md`, `dm/launcher.json` and the JSON event fields: the interface the launchers read.
- Binary layouts without a version (the RomFS image entry), `game.manifest.json`.
- Files that our patches hook, found from the patch headers.

The list goes into the bump pull request as a table with the commit, the file and one line, and a place to write "handled" or an issue number. It is a list of candidates, not a verdict. A commit with a `Breaking:` or "For front ends" line from upstream, if seedds takes that up, is listed first.

The first run is the reading of the 53 commits of the v1.0.1 pin (v1.0.0 pin `bbc3b737` to `cd859c38`). It found these that matter to us: the shader chain and Xcode 27.2 (handled in #449, #450, #447), new NSP script messages (handled in #444), a new free space check in `pso_offline` (no failure row yet, see the issue for it), new inputs we do not use yet, and the Switch 2 work (#445).

### Done when

- `tools/engine.py bump` prints the candidate list for a pin move, and a test covers it with a fixture of upstream commits.
- The `sync/upstream-<sha>` pull request holds the table.
- It is used for the pin bump before v1.0.2-rc1.
title: Pin bump: list the upstream commits that change what the front ends and players depend on

body:
### Idea

Upstream now stops the iPhone and iPad build before the Metal archive step when the disk is too full (seedds/nxnative `68e8dc23`, #790). `pso_offline` checks the free space, needs at least 2 GB and about 96 KB per base, and says so before `metal-tt` runs. A failure of `metal-tt` on a full disk is named as well.

The Mac launcher and the Qt front end have no failure row for this message, so the build ends with the raw line and no hint. It is a clear problem with a clear answer, free space on the disk the build folder is on.

### Plan

- Add a failure row for the `pso_offline` free space message to `BuildFailure.swift` and `build_failure.py`, in all five languages, with the same wording in both front ends. The row says how much space the build needs and to free it or move the build folder.
- Check the message text against the engine (`scripts/pso_offline.py` at the pin) so the row matches it.
- Fixture in `build_failures.json` and a test in both front ends.
- Look at `FreeSpaceView` and the free space estimate for the iPhone and iPad build. If it can use the same figure (96 KB per base, 2 GB at least), the launcher warns before the build starts.

### Done when

- A build that stops on the free space check shows a row that names the missing space and the way out, in the Mac launcher and in the Qt front end.
- A test covers the message in both front ends.

Found while reading the 53 upstream commits of the v1.0.1 pin bump.
title: A failure row for the pso_offline free space check, in both front ends

### Where it runs

Mac app (built for This Mac)

### Device, chip and RAM

Macbook air M5, 24Go

### macOS or iOS / iPadOS version

MacOS 27.0.1

### How it was installed

run the app the launcher built

### NX2Apple version

v1.0.0

### What happens, and when

In a camp scene (a large drill or rig, a yellow tent, lit hangar windows) the picture flickers at the game's 30 fps. Bright and emissive things (tent cloth, windows, lantern) alternate between two brightness levels on every game frame; the rest of the picture changes much less (block means differ by at most about 15%). It happens every time, with no crash and, with the default settings, no [RED] line in the log.
The two states follow the swapchain texture the game renders into: frames drawn into window texture #2 are bright, frames drawn into #3 are dark (12 of 12 texture dumps). In the dark frames, four 640x360 RGBA16F targets (the half-resolution scene used by the glow pass) hold nothing at the end of the frame. The draw that fills two of them (fragment shader 521e75edb4abd1e5_b, a 3-vertex full-screen draw) receives the same textures and the same 8,704-byte uniform block in both frames. Only a 2-float anti-aliasing jitter differs. The cause is therefore probably on the replay side: hazard, view cache or ordering, not data.

### What you expected

The picture keeps a steady brightness from one frame to the next, as on a Switch. Only animated things such as clouds and grass should move.

### Launch options changed from the defaults

No in-game launch option was changed in the later runs; Upscaling was MetalFX with the Metal HUD on in the earliest runs, then off, with the same flicker. These engine settings were each tried alone in env.txt, in the scene where the flicker shows. None changed it.

Setting | Result
-- | --
DM_NVN_UB_DEFER=0 | still flickers
DM_NVN_FB_SNAP=0 | worse: flickers on every movement
DM_NVN_GEO_HOIST=0 | still flickers
DM_NVN_UB_LAZY=0 | still flickers
DM_NVN_DIRECT_UPLOAD=0 | still flickers
DM_NVN_STORAGE_FIRST_USE=0, alone and with DIRECT_UPLOAD=0 | still flickers
DM_NVN_DIRTYCHECK=1 | still flickers; missed 0 (cumulative), so no CPU-written texture change was missed
DM_NVN_SLICE_MERGE=0 | still flickers
DM_NVN_CUT=0 | still flickers
DM_NVN_CS_HOIST=0 | still flickers
DM_PSO_MTL4=0 | still flickers
DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=off (MetalFX off, off, bilinear) | still flickers

Also checked: shared-texture storage takeovers are only 2 in 1,500 frames, so aliasing evictions do not cycle per frame. The 64x64x192 probe atlas (serial 1340) is updated six layers per frame and those layers are not black (mean 1 to 55).
Settings window left on defaults, except the saved language (DM_LANG=fr).

### This is

An idea

### What happens, or what you would like

Following the suggestion in [discussion #435](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/discussions/435#discussioncomment-19337223), I would like to propose a small first step: **one profile-tested “Optimized defaults” preset per game**, using the existing per-game settings contract. Thank you for clarifying the intended scope.

Today the individual settings are available through `launcher.json` and saved as `launcher.<VAR>` choices. A user still needs to know which combination the profile has actually tested and select those values individually. A named group would make that known configuration easy to inspect and apply.

The initial feature could:

- Show one optional “Optimized defaults” action for a game/profile that supplies tested values, with the actual values visible before applying them.
- Apply only supported, allowlisted settings already exposed by that game. Include relevant engine settings in the group when tested, rather than changing resolution while leaving an unspecified engine configuration behind.
- Preserve language, controller mapping, rumble, window/fullscreen and other personal preferences.
- Show Custom after a user changes a value belonging to the preset; retain that manual choice.
- Continue using the existing per-app preference and temporary-override behavior. Validate a saved group against the current game/runtime capabilities and preserve incompatible older settings for recovery.

A profile could supply a short note identifying the tested game/build and configuration. A game without such data would keep its current settings interface. “Optimized defaults” would mean a profile-tested starting point, not an automatic benchmark or a promise of maximum performance on every Mac.

The local prototype and current source files are in [discussion #435](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/discussions/435). [Configuration and UI](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/discussions/435#discussioncomment-19335517) · [Installer/helper and fixture tests](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/discussions/435#discussioncomment-19335519).

### What you expected

Select a game, inspect the explicit values in its tested preset, apply them once, and keep my personal preferences. Changing one of those tested values should leave it as a custom configuration.

For this first issue, the requested deliverable is the single preset layer. The broader standalone UI prototype, multiple preset cards and read-only package/version/DLC information can serve as examples for later discussion. The Odyssey-specific resolution/HDR backend remains a separate engine experiment in [seedds/nxnative#885](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/issues/885).

The prototype's native tests cover preset application, preservation of personal preferences, manual-change detection, legacy settings, overrides and incompatible package data. These checks exercise the local prototype; integration with NX2Apple's frontend is still to be designed. No pull request is proposed yet.

### NX2Apple version

0.7.5, from the installed application's Info.plist. Local prototype checkout: `df713726c682cc936ac47d8ea17fa35fa522acb1` with local changes; standalone launcher revision `2.2-local`.

### Computer and OS

MacBook Pro, Apple M3 Max, 64 GB RAM; macOS 27.0.1 (26A434). The native launcher prototype was compiled with the macOS Swift toolchain for `arm64-apple-macos26.6`.

Not required for an idea by the issue form. This is a launcher feature proposal, with local prototype sources and fixture tests linked above.

body:
## Problem or idea

After an engine update the shader chain moves, and **every** framework built before it is refused:

```
[RED] …/DmGame0100A00019DE0000.framework: built for shader chain b-e65a4ebd3322, this checkout is b-b7cd656abd7c: build the game again
```

#449 (the up-front prompt and the offer to rebuild the stale ones) makes that survivable. It does not remove the cause: the host lives in the shell, so all games share one shader runtime, and a chain move makes every installed game stale at once. Rebuilding is dominated by the shader step — hours for a large game — which is exactly what the owner hit while testing v1.0.1-rc1.

## Proposal: the host travels with the framework

Today:

- the **shell** carries the host (HLE, the NVN to Metal runtime, the shader loader) — the `DmShell` binary is 7.3 MB including the SwiftUI UI
- each **framework** carries the game's modules, the rewrite tables, `profile.tsv` and the precompiled shader libraries (`msl/b-<chain>/`, 3.7 MB of a 110 MB framework)

Move the host into the framework, and the shell becomes the UI plus a loader:

1. `build_ipa.sh` links the host into the framework next to the game's modules; the framework's `dm_main` is the entry.
2. `build_shell.sh` stops linking the host; the shell `dlopen`s the chosen framework and calls into it, as it already does for the modules.
3. The framework's manifest gains the host's identity (engine pin, chain) as **information**; the shell no longer refuses a framework for a chain mismatch, because each game brings the runtime its shaders were built for.
4. Consequence: an engine update reaches **newly built** games only. Installed games keep working, unchanged, with the engine they were built with.

**Size:** the host is a few MB against a framework that is already ~110 MB — about 6 percent per game (7 games: ~45 MB).

**The trade-off to state plainly:** a host fix (crash, compatibility) then reaches an old game only when that game is rebuilt. That is inherent to pinning; the alternative is the current behaviour, where every engine bump forces every game to be rebuilt.

## The design problem this must solve first

The host owns the game window today (`front_ios.m` creates it); the shell owns the UI window. The port needs an explicit surface handoff: the shell passes the view or CA layer and the environment in, and the framework's `dm_main` draws into it and returns when the game exits. `dm_main`'s contract (`argc`/`argv` plus the environment) is otherwise unchanged, and `hle_profile`/`profile.tsv` reading stays inside the framework.

## Alternatives considered

- **Several hosts in the shell, dispatched by `manifest.chain`**: +7 MB per chain, shared by the games of that chain; needs every past host archived and buildable. Same memory as the proposal for one extra chain, but a second build matrix to keep alive.
- **Relax the chain check and load old shader libraries into the new host**: only safe when the chain moved for reasons that do not touch the ABI the libraries use; unsafe as a product feature.
- **Keep the `b-<V>` caches on disk for every chain** (worth doing whatever else we choose): switching an engine back then costs no recompile.

Suggested for v1.1.0. @v0lumehi the surface handoff is the part I would want your read on first — it decides how much of `front_ios.m` moves into the framework.
title: Let each framework carry its own host, so an engine update stops invalidating every installed game

body:
### Idea

After the engine moved to a new shader chain, adding one more game to the shared iPhone and iPad app fails at the last step, and the message does not say what to do. @LNPANDY found it while testing v1.0.1-rc1 and asked for a prompt that tells the player up front.

What happened, from the build log of a Chinese-language launcher (paths shortened):

```
[Prepare shared app] build_shell.sh --prepare-xcode
[RED] <NSP folder>/NX2Apple-shell/frameworks/DmGame0100A00019DE0000.framework: built for shader chain b-e65a4ebd3322, this checkout is b-b7cd656abd7c: build the game again
FAIL: the frameworks in DM_SHELL_FRAMEWORKS (above)
```

The launcher then shows "Cannot prepare the shared app" with the same text. The new game itself was built. The old game's framework in the shell folder was built with the previous engine's shader chain, and the shared app takes only frameworks of one chain. The engine bump in v1.0.1 changes the chain, so every player who already has games in the shell meets this the first time they add a game after the update. The games already on the device keep running, but no new one can be installed until the old frameworks are gone.

@LNPANDY's proposal: a prompt that says installing a new game requires rebuilding the previously installed games, with two choices:

- **Stop the build.** Nothing is touched.
- **Continue.** The existing games will be removed. The local framework cache is deleted and the build goes on.

### Plan

- Check before the long steps, not after them. At the start of a build for the iPhone or iPad, compare the shader chain of each framework in `<NSP folder>/NX2Apple-shell/frameworks/` with the chain of the engine the build will use. Find the cheapest source for both: the framework records its chain (the message above reads it), and the engine knows its own chain (`dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_chain.py`, the `b-<chain>` folder name). If the launcher cannot read them, the build script can print a short list and exit with a code the launcher understands.
- Only when at least one framework has another chain, show the prompt with the two choices. Say plainly: the games that are already installed in the shared app have to be built again, and Continue removes them from it. List their names (the library knows them by title ID).
- **Stop** ends the build before it starts. Nothing is deleted.
- **Continue** deletes only the frameworks whose chain differs, and the build goes on. Frameworks with the current chain stay. If all of them differ, that is the whole cache.
- The same on the Windows launcher if it builds for the iPhone or iPad with the shared app, and the same texts in English, Chinese, German, Swedish and French.
- A failure at the last step stays as it is for the case that the check cannot decide. Its row says what to do: "Build the games listed again, or remove them from `NX2Apple-shell/frameworks`."

### Done when

- A build with stale frameworks asks before the shader build starts, with the games named and the two choices.
- Stop leaves every file as it was. Continue removes the stale frameworks and ends with a shared app that holds only games of the current chain.
- Without stale frameworks nothing is asked.
- A test covers a shell folder with one current and one stale framework, for Stop and for Continue.
- The prompt has screenshots in English and Chinese in the pull request.

Found with v1.0.1-rc1. It needs a new candidate before the final release, so I put it in v1.0.1.
title: Adding a game after an engine update fails at the last step: ask first, then remove the stale frameworks

body:
### Idea

seedds/nxnative now runs a first Nintendo Switch 2 game, Donkey Kong Bananza, on the Mac. This issue collects what upstream has, with the evidence, and plans how the launcher takes it in. It follows the research question in #417.

The player brings their own game files. The launcher never bundles, downloads or looks up keys or games, and it does not explain how to get them. For a Switch 2 game the engine needs no `prod.keys` at all (see below).

Everything below was checked against upstream main at [`cd859c38`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/cd859c38a8f8890ddbb57a23d6f45e23ba9e6651) on 2026-11-01. Our pin is still [`bbc3b737`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/bbc3b73784751d2a706932dc69fd67627e3445d4), which has none of it. #444 moves the pin to `cd859c38`.

### What upstream has now

#### What "Switch 2 support" means

- **Native Switch 2 titles.** That is what is new. The engine tells a Switch 2 game by its `sdk` module, whose spec string reads `Ounce` (`dm_sdk_ounce` in `dm/host/dm.h`, set in `loader.c`).
- **The "Nintendo Switch 2 Edition" of a Switch 1 game is not part of it.** The host still answers `nn::pl::IsRunningOnOunce` with false ([`dm/host/hle_sdk16.c` line 152](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/cd859c38a8f8890ddbb57a23d6f45e23ba9e6651/dm/host/hle_sdk16.c#L152)). Super Mario Bros. Wonder 1.2.1 runs as on a Switch 1, as #417 found.

#### Titles and status

| Title | Title ID | Status upstream | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| Donkey Kong Bananza | `040074A01BF12000`, update v458752 | Plays on the Mac (M4 Pro), 60 fps with drops to 30 in busy scenes. Tested through the first level's opening areas only. iPhone and iPad untested. Profile header says "In bring-up". | [profile note](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/cd859c38a8f8890ddbb57a23d6f45e23ba9e6651/dm/games/040074A01BF12000/README.md), in main |
| Mario Kart World | `0400C3F00006E000` | Title, menus and free roam on the Mac, by the PR author. Ground drawn as flat patches, `DrawMeshTasks` draws nothing, movies and 32 shaders do not lower. | seedds/nxnative#834 by `@robertzsun-dev`, closed on 2026-11-01. Its profile, `dm/host/hle_nx2.c` and `dm/gfx/tools/nx2_lower` are not in main at `cd859c38`, so it was not taken (yet). |

No other Switch 2 title has a profile. I found no upstream issue or roadmap item about Switch 2 games, only about Switch 2 controllers (seedds/nxnative#646, seedds/nxnative#867, PR seedds/nxnative#645).

#### The commits

All landed on main on 2026-11-01:

- [`8dd0c98a`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/8dd0c98a) boots into the frame loop. Adds `scripts/pack_dump.py`, the SDK version string's variant form, `GetInfo` 33 and 29 to 32, NVN2 API 231.30 with 197 NVN2 names, stubs for Switch 2 services (hid Jcms, `oe` graphics scale, audio volume auto-tune, streamplay, `vi` HDR and VRR).
- [`d3995ca4`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/d3995ca4) translates Ampere shaders natively (`dmsh_xlate` arch `sm86`, `dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_ampere.py`). Supported Xcode becomes 27.2.
- [`a7bd05f4`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/a7bd05f4), [`fdb3710d`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/fdb3710d), [`5b2d4606`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/5b2d4606), [`5251763d`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/5251763d), [`c4b0618c`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/c4b0618c), [`4de40e62`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/4de40e62): tensor instructions (HMMA through `simdgroup_matrix`), the Switch 2 GOB order for textures (`nvn_gob_switch2`), the `nn::codec` video decoders, mesh geometry, the 31.25 MHz system tick, NVN2 device values.
- [`99947471`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/99947471) lets `build_ipa_from_nsp.py` build from a folder of the game's files, with no `prod.keys`.
- [`d76c45f7`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/d76c45f7) pins the toolchain to Xcode 27.2.

#### Files, containers and keys

- A Switch 2 game is built **only from a folder of its files**, never from NSP, XCI, NSZ or XCZ. The layout ([`scripts/pack_dump.py`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/cd859c38a8f8890ddbb57a23d6f45e23ba9e6651/scripts/pack_dump.py)): `base/exefs/` (with `main.npdm`) and `base/romfs/`, optional `updates/<version as decimal>/exefs` and `romfs`, optional `dlc/<DLC title ID>/<n>/romfs`.
- An update's RomFS in that folder is the patched tree and is packed on its own, not laid over the base.
- The files are not encrypted, so **no key set is needed**. `-k` is ignored for such a folder.
- The title ID comes from the program ID in `base/exefs/main.npdm`.
- The folder has no control data, so the app gets **no icon**, and the name comes from the profile.
- The script packs such a folder **only for a game with a profile**. The survey and provisional profiles read NSPs, so an unknown Switch 2 game stops with an error.
- I found no code that reads a Switch 2 NSP or XCI. The packed update, DLC handling and `nx_extract` paths are the Switch 1 ones.

#### CPU, OS and GPU

- CPU: the game's code is AArch64 and goes through the existing rewrite. The fixes are in the host's services and kernel answers, not in a new CPU layer.
- GPU: NVN2 (API 231) is served by the same NVN on Metal layer, with Switch 2 branches (`dm/gfx/nvn/hle_nvn.c`). Shaders are Ampere code (128-bit encoding). The translator decodes it natively and the build splits NVN2 control sections (`shader_split.py`, `dmsh_build.py`).
- Bananza builds 22,852 shaders. A full shader build takes about 75 minutes on the Mac from an empty cache. The first start without a pipeline archive builds pipelines for about 4 minutes, once.
- Mac only: the profile note says iOS is untested. Nothing in the code blocks an iPhone build of a dump folder, but nothing was run there.

#### Memory and disk

- Profile [`game.tsv`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/cd859c38a8f8890ddbb57a23d6f45e23ba9e6651/dm/games/040074A01BF12000/game.tsv): `app_pool 0x240000000` (9 GiB) and `mem_reserve 0x270000000`. The note says a Switch 1 pool (3.2 GB) did not fit the game's heaps.
- For comparison, Tears of the Kingdom uses `app_pool 0xCD500000` (about 3.2 GiB), and our [ENTITLEMENTS.md](ENTITLEMENTS.md) shows it at 3,342 MB resident with 33 MB headroom on a device with Increased Memory Limit. An iPhone 15 Pro has 8 GB of memory in total.
- The update's RomFS is 80,273 files and 8.6 GB. The DLC is 8,000 files and 0.9 GB. The script estimates the disk need for a folder as the RomFS trees plus 6 GB.

#### What did not change

- `docs/launcher.schema.json`, `docs/frontends.md` and `docs/settings.md`: no change between our pin and `cd859c38`.
- The Bananza profile has no `launcher.json`.
- `docs/env_switches.tsv`: no Switch 2 switch. The new switches (`DM_NVN_INDLOG`, `DM_NVN_PREFETCH`, `DM_HID_*`) are general.
- No machine-readable field says "this is a Switch 2 game" or "tested on Mac only". That is only in the profile's comments and README.
- New build stages: `pack <version>` and `pack DLC` replace `extract <version>` and `extract DLC` for a folder, and the nx_extract build stage is left out.

#### Not found

- Which key set a Switch 2 NSP or XCI would need: the engine does not read them. I looked in `scripts/`, `dm/tools/nx_extract` and the open and closed PRs and issues.
- Any iOS measurement of a Switch 2 game, and any minimum device. I looked in the profile note, README, `docs/` and the PRs.
- An upstream plan for Switch 2 on iOS, or for more titles. `docs/` at `cd859c38` has no roadmap file. I searched the issues and PRs for "Switch 2", "NVN2", "Ounce", "Bananza" and "Mario Kart World".
- Why seedds/nxnative#834 was closed. It has no comment.

### Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Player picks a folder] --> B{Folder kind}
    B -->|NSP, XCI, NSZ, XCZ| C[Slots base, update, DLC, keys]
    C --> D[KeyCheck on NCA headers]
    B -->|base/exefs/main.npdm and base/romfs| E[NEW: Switch 2 folder]
    E --> F[NEW: title ID from main.npdm]
    F --> G{NEW: engine has pack_dump.py and a profile for it}
    G -->|no| H[NEW: message, update the engine or not supported yet]
    G -->|yes| I[NEW: keys slot shows not needed]
    D --> J[build_ipa_from_nsp.py --progress json]
    I --> J
    J --> K[Builds page stages]
    K -->|NSP| L[extract version, extract DLC]
    K -->|folder| M[NEW: pack version, pack DLC]
    L --> N[split, shaders, app]
    M --> N
    N --> O{Target}
    O -->|Mac app| P[Library card, NEW Switch 2 badge and icon fallback]
    O -->|iPhone or iPad| Q[NEW: blocked or warned until upstream tests iOS]
    Q --> R[Shell reads game.manifest.json]
    R --> S[NEW: memory and device check before Play]
```

#### Mac launcher (`frontend/`)

- **Input.** `BuildModel.inputFiles(in:)` in `ContentView.swift` walks at most 8,000 entries and `classify` knows only `.nsp .xci .nsz .xcz`. A Switch 2 folder has 80,000 and more files and no package. The folder must be recognised first, with the same rule as `pack_dump.is_dump`, before the walk. `FoundInputs` gets a folder kind. The base, update and DLC slots show the folders, the keys slot shows "not needed".
- **Staging.** `InputStaging` links files by name for packages. A Switch 2 folder is passed to the script as it is.
- **Keys.** `KeyCheck` reads NCA headers and does not apply. It reports "no keys needed" for a folder. The build drops `-k` (`ContentView.swift`, the `args` for the script). `BuildFailure` must not classify a missing keys file for a folder.
- **Builds page.** `Stage.localizedName` maps `extract <name>`. It needs `stage.pack` (with the version) and `stage.pack_dlc`, in every language of `Localization.swift`, or those two stages show in English. `BuildFailure` gets rules for the script's folder errors ("a dump folder packs only a game with a profile", "is not a DLC of", "no base/exefs/main.npdm").
- **Target.** Mac app only for a Switch 2 game until upstream reports iOS. `BuildTarget` hides or disables iPhone and iPad with the reason.
- **Library.** `Library.swift` groups by `tid & 0xFFF`, which also fits `04…` title IDs and their DLC. The card gets a "Switch 2" mark and an icon fallback, as the folder has no icon (`Artwork.swift`). `FreeSpace` uses the RomFS trees plus 6 GB, as the script does.
- #420 splits the launcher into NXCore, NXModel, NXLauncher and NX2Apple. These steps should land after it, or name the new module of each type.

#### iOS shell (`frontend-ios/`)

- `GameManifest` (schema 1) has no console and no memory field. A reader ignores unknown keys, so an optional `console` and `min_memory` field keep schema 1.
- `HostEnvironment` in `GameCatalogue.swift` checks the chain and the OS only. It gets the device memory, and `GameCatalogue` marks an entry the device cannot run, before Play, in words without numbers the player cannot act on.
- `DataLocator` and `romfs_identity` work the same for a Switch 2 image. A 9.5 GB image makes the slim IPA (patch 0004) and the data folder (patch 0003) the normal path.
- `LauncherProfile` needs no change: the schema did not change.

#### Windows and Qt launcher (`frontend-qt/`)

- `inputs.py`, `input_staging.py` and `build_failure.py` mirror the Mac rules. They get the same folder rule and messages. The strings are generated from `Localization.swift`.

#### What the engine must tell the launcher

1. **That a game is a Switch 2 game.** Today only the `Ounce` spec in the `sdk` module says so, at run time. Upstream first: a profile key in `game.tsv` (for example `console switch2`) and a `console` field in the manifest the build writes. Until then the launcher can use the folder kind. The `04` prefix of both known title IDs is an observation, not a rule, and should not be used.
2. **Where it is tested.** Upstream first: a key such as `tested mac`. Until then a list in our launcher, kept with `GAMES.md`.
3. **What memory it needs.** The profile's `app_pool` holds it. The build can write it into the manifest as `min_memory`. This is ours in patch 0050 (Route C shell), or upstream if the manifest moves there.
4. **What the engine can do.** An older engine has no `scripts/pack_dump.py`. The launcher checks for that file in the engine tree, which needs no new field in `latest.json`.

#### Older engines and channels

- The `stable` channel keeps the release's engine. A launcher on an engine without `pack_dump.py` says "this engine does not build Switch 2 games, update the engine" and builds nothing.
- `experimental` gets the support after #444 merges and the nightly sync publishes it (`sync-upstream.yml`).
- `latest.json` (`EngineManifest.Manifest`) ignores unknown keys, so a capability list can be added later without breaking older launchers. For now the file check is enough.

### Plan

Each step is one PR unless noted. Ours unless marked upstream.

| # | Step | Blocks | Size |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Merge #444 (pin `cd859c38`). Move CI from Xcode 27.1 to 27.2 (`tests.yml`, `build-mac-app.yml`) if #444 does not | everything | 1 to 2 PRs |
| 1 | `GAMES.md`, README and zh-CN: a Switch 2 section, Bananza on the Mac, from a folder of the game's files, nothing about how to get it | none | 1 PR, docs |
| 2 | Mac: recognise a Switch 2 folder, title ID from `main.npdm`, slots, no keys, no `-k`, staging pass-through. Tests with a synthetic folder | 0 | 1 to 2 PRs |
| 3 | Mac: stage names `pack` and `pack DLC`, folder errors in `BuildFailure`, all languages | 2 | 1 PR |
| 4 | Mac: target limited to Mac app for Switch 2, engine file check with message | 2 | 1 PR |
| 5 | Mac: library mark, icon fallback, free space estimate | 2 | 1 PR |
| 6 | Upstream: profile keys `console` and `tested`, manifest field `console`. Fork patch in parallel | none, 7 uses it | 1 upstream PR, 1 patch |
| 7 | iOS shell: optional `console` and `min_memory` in `GameManifest`, memory check in `GameCatalogue` | 6, and an upstream iOS report | 1 to 2 PRs |
| 8 | Qt: the same folder rule and messages | 2, 3 | 1 PR |
| 9 | Allow iPhone and iPad targets for Switch 2 | an iOS test on a device | 1 PR |

About 9 to 11 PRs of ours and 1 upstream. Steps 1 and 6 can start now. Steps 2 to 5 follow 0. Step 9 waits on a real game on a real device.

Patches and bumps: 10 of our patches touch `build_ipa_from_nsp.py`, `hle_nvn.c` or `loader.c` (0001, 0005, 0006, 0018, 0040, 0041, 0045, 0047, 0051, 0053), the files the Switch 2 work changes most. #444 already had 9 conflicts. Expect more on each bump while the Switch 2 code moves.

### Tests and verification

- **Without a game:** a synthetic folder (a minimal `main.npdm` with an ACI0 program ID, an empty `romfs/`) in the Swift tests covers detection, slots, title ID, staging and the missing `-k`. Captures (`NX_LAUNCHER_CAPTURE_DIR`) cover the keys slot, the stages and the card. Manifest decoding with and without the new fields. A fake engine tree with and without `pack_dump.py`.
- **With a real title:** a Mac build of Bananza from the tester's own folder, played to the first level, the Build log and the game log attached without game data. This needs a maintainer who owns the game.
- **On a device:** step 9 only, after upstream reports an iOS result.

### Risks

- **Memory on iPhone and iPad.** Bananza reserves a 9 GiB pool. Tears of the Kingdom with a third of that is already close to the limit on a device. Whether any iPhone or iPad can run it is unknown, and upstream has not tried.
- **A moving engine.** All of the Switch 2 work landed in one day. One title is in main and is "in bring-up". Mario Kart World was closed without being taken. Our patches sit in the same files, and upstream moved to Xcode 27.2 while our CI is on 27.1.
- **Input and legal facts.** Switch 2 games come only as a folder of the game's files, with no keys. The launcher shows the folder layout and nothing on how to obtain it. If seedds/nxnative#834 or its successor lands, `nx2_lower` is GPL-3.0-or-later inside an MIT engine, and our release zip ships the engine tree. That needs a look at `NOTICE` and the release then. No legal advice here, only the fact.
- **Time and disk.** About 75 minutes of shader build, about 9.5 GB of game images, and a RomFS too large for a plain IPA. The Builds page and the free space check must say so before the build starts.
- **Performance.** On an M4 Pro the game measures 17 ms a frame (p90 24 ms) by its own controller and drops to 30 fps in busy scenes. Smaller Macs are not measured.

### Open questions

For `@LNPANDY` and me:

1. Do we take Switch 2 into v1.x on the experimental channel, or keep it for the v2.0.0 milestone of #417?
2. Do we offer Switch 2 builds while only one title is in main and in bring-up, marked as experimental in the launcher?
3. iPhone and iPad targets for a Switch 2 game: hidden, or shown with a warning, until upstream reports iOS?
4. Do we ask upstream for the `console` and `tested` profile keys (step 6), or keep that list in the launcher?
5. Icon for a folder build: a picked image, or the plain placeholder?
6. Who owns Bananza and can run the real test on a Mac (step 2 to 5 sign-off)?

### Proposal

Proposal, not a decision. Answer per line.

**1. v1.x on the experimental channel, or the v2.0.0 milestone?**

- Proposal: v2.0.0. The Mac path (steps 2 to 5) merges when it is ready and reaches players through the experimental engine channel first. It is not announced as stable before a release candidate test with a real title.
- Why: one title in main, all of it landed in one day ([`8dd0c98a`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/8dd0c98a) to [`4de40e62`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/4de40e62)), and the profile header says "In bring-up". The v1.x milestones (v1.0.2 to v1.6.0) already hold 57 open items with other themes. v2.0.0 is the milestone that already holds #417.
- Alternative: put steps 2 to 5 into v1.2.0 (build and install flow). Cost: they change the same input code as #378 (merged NSPs and XCIs, `classify` in `ContentView.swift`) in the same release, and that release grows by 4 to 5 PRs.
- Consequence: steps 2 to 5 (4 to 5 PRs) and steps 7 to 9 go into v2.0.0. Step 0 (#444) stays in the v1.0.1 candidate where it already is. No v1.x milestone changes.

**2. Offer Switch 2 builds while one title is in bring-up?**

- Proposal: yes, on the Mac only, marked "Switch 2, experimental" on the card and in `GAMES.md`.
- Why: the script already refuses a folder without a profile (`build_ipa_from_nsp.py` around line 2424), so the launcher cannot start a guessed build. Bananza plays at 60 fps on an M4 Pro per its profile note.
- Alternative: wait until upstream has two titles out of bring-up. Cost: no launcher work lands, and changes to the folder input upstream go unnoticed until then.
- Consequence: the mark is part of step 5. No extra PR.

**3. iPhone and iPad targets for a Switch 2 game?**

- Proposal: shown but disabled, with one line why ("Switch 2 games are tested on the Mac only"). Not hidden, so the player sees why.
- Why: the pool is 9 GiB (`app_pool 0x240000000` in `game.tsv`). An iPhone 15 Pro has 8 GB in total. Tears of the Kingdom with about 3.2 GiB is already at 33 MB headroom ([ENTITLEMENTS.md](ENTITLEMENTS.md)). Upstream says iOS is untested.
- Alternative: shown with a warning. Cost: a player spends about 75 minutes of shader build and about 9.5 GB of disk for an app that most likely does not start, and we get the reports.
- Not decidable yet: whether any iPad or iPhone can run it. To find out: ask upstream in the issue that tracks it, or a test on an iPad with 16 GB by someone who owns the game. Default meanwhile: disabled.
- Consequence: part of step 4. Step 9 stays blocked.

**4. Profile keys upstream, or a list in the launcher?**

- Proposal: ask upstream. One PR to seedds/nxnative with `console` and `tested` keys in `game.tsv`, the fork patch in parallel. Meanwhile the launcher uses the folder kind and a short list next to `GAMES.md`.
- Why: today nothing machine-readable says Switch 2 or Mac only, only comments in `game.tsv` and the README. Outside contributors already send Switch 2 profiles (seedds/nxnative#834), so a list kept only by us goes stale with each bump.
- Alternative: keep the list in the launcher only. Cost: an edit on every bump that adds a title, and the iOS shell cannot read it.
- Consequence: step 6, 1 upstream PR and 1 patch. It unblocks step 7.

**5. Icon for a folder build?**

- Proposal: the launcher's existing key art by title ID first (`ArtworkStore` in `Artwork.swift`), the plain placeholder when there is none. No new image picker for now.
- Why: a folder has no control data, so the build has no icon ([`99947471`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/99947471)). The library already looks up key art by title ID.
- Not decidable yet: whether that title list has the Switch 2 title IDs. To find out: a cheap check of the two known title IDs in the list `ArtworkStore` reads.
- Alternative: let the player pick an image. Cost: a change to how the launcher looks, so an issue first, then 1 more PR.
- Consequence: part of step 5. No extra PR.

**6. Who runs the real test?**

- Proposal: steps 2 to 5 merge on the synthetic tests and the captures. The real title is checked at the release candidate test, by whichever of `@LNPANDY` and me owns the game.
- Why: CI cannot hold game files. Everything up to the build start can be tested with a synthetic folder.
- Not decidable yet: whether `@LNPANDY` or I own Bananza. To find out: we say so in this issue. If neither of us does, the mark stays "experimental" and we ask a player in Discussions for a report with the Build log.
- Consequence: no PR. It decides when the "experimental" mark comes off.

**Milestone.** I recommend v2.0.0. I did not set it.

**Proposed order**

1. First: merge #444 (pin `cd859c38`) and move CI to Xcode 27.2 if #444 does not.
2. Now: step 1, the Switch 2 section in `GAMES.md` and README.
3. Now, in parallel: step 6, the `console` and `tested` keys as a seedds/nxnative PR, the patch here.
4. After #444, #420 and #378: steps 2 to 5, the Mac path.
5. After steps 2 and 3: step 8, the Qt launcher.
6. Wait for an upstream iOS result: steps 7 and 9.
7. Leave to upstream: more titles (Mario Kart World), reading Switch 2 NSP or XCI, the iOS bring-up, the Switch 2 Edition behaviour.
8. No for now: Switch 2 targets on iPhone and iPad, builds of a Switch 2 game without a profile, telling by the `04` title ID prefix, and anything about how to get the files.

### Recommendation

Merge #444 first. Then do the Mac path only (steps 1 to 5), behind the engine file check, with the iPhone and iPad targets disabled for Switch 2 and a plain note why. Send the profile keys upstream in parallel. Leave iOS (steps 7 and 9) until upstream has a result on a device, because the 9 GiB pool makes it uncertain.

### Done when

- The Mac launcher takes a Switch 2 folder, builds a Mac app with no keys, and shows every stage in the player's language.
- The library card marks the game as Switch 2.
- iPhone and iPad targets say why they are not offered.
- An older engine gives a clear message instead of a failed build.
- `GAMES.md` lists Donkey Kong Bananza as Mac only.
- The synthetic tests pass in CI, and one maintainer built and played Bananza from their own files.
title: Switch 2 games: what nxnative supports now and how the launcher integrates it

body:
## What is broken

The shell-level game-data folder (#400, the row in the shell settings page) is effectively dead for its purpose. `DataLocator.locate` checks the chosen folder against **each game's own manifest**:

- `<folder>/romfs.img` must be non-empty and, when the manifest carries `romfs_identity … size=N`, **exactly N bytes** (that check exists to reject a copy cut off mid-transfer, and it is right to keep it)
- a folder holding the `romfs_marker` tree counts too

One folder can hold **one** `romfs.img`, and its size can match **one** game. So with several games installed, picking a folder helps at most one of them; every other game silently falls back to `Documents/games/<titleID>/` and still says 'Needs game data'. Nothing in the page can fix the other games, which is the whole point of setting it once.

There is also no title-ID descent anywhere on the global path: `DataLocator.holder(of:)` inspects the picked URL and `<picked>/romfs` only.

## What it should be

Look up the game inside the chosen folder by title ID, the layout the Mac launcher already copies and the external-drive case needs:

```
<chosen folder>/
  01007EF00011E000/
      romfs.img            (complete: the manifest's size= when it names one)
      aoc/0.img, aoc/1.img (optional DLC; the file name is the DLC index, a directory aoc/<n>/ also works)
  0100F2C0115B6000/
      romfs.img
```

Order per game: game's own bookmark, then `<shell folder>/<titleID>`, then (compatibility) `<shell folder>` itself for the single-game layout, then the app's `Documents/games/<titleID>/`. The completeness rule stays exactly as it is; only the search grows a path. The source shown in the game's settings row should stay 'from Settings' for the title-ID case, and the page's note should say the folder holds one `<title ID>/romfs.img` per game so players know what to copy to an external drive.

## Why it matters

The owner's reason for the shell folder was copying games' `romfs.img` to an external drive once and pointing the launcher at it — with a multi-game library that only works if the folder is per-title-ID. Today it works for exactly one game, so the setting reads as broken (it is).

@v0lumehi the change is in `DataLocator.locate/holder` (frontend-ios/ShellHost/GameCatalogue.swift) plus the note in the settings page; tests can extend `CatalogueStateTests.theShellFolderBacksTheGameAndSaysSo` with a two-game folder. Owner-approved, suggested for v1.1.0.

body:
### Idea

The text of the release notes is written by hand or by an agent. I want the Copilot CLI to write them, and CI to publish them in the release without a manual step. It follows the pattern of the issue triage (`issue-triage.yml`): the model only reads and never holds a write token, and a strict check sits between its answer and the release.

### Plan

- A job `notes` runs in the build of a final tag, before the step that creates the release. A first part without secrets gathers the inputs: the row of this version in `CHANGELOG.md` and `CHANGELOG.zh-CN.md`, the merged pull requests since the previous final tag (number, title, author, labels), and `.github/release_notes_template.md`.
- The model part runs the Copilot CLI the way the triage does: read-only, an empty directory, `--available-tools=view`, no shell, no write, no URLs, the `COPILOT_TOKEN` secret, no write token. It answers one text in the form of the template, English part first, then Chinese. It may only use the gathered inputs, and every claim must come from them.
- The release job downloads that text and runs `tools/release_notes.py check` on it (#432). Only a text that passes goes into the release, through `tools/release_notes.py build`, with the generated block of contributors and the Full Changelog link below it. If the model job fails, the secret is missing or `check` fails, the release gets the short body and a warning, as in #432. A problem with the notes never stops a release.
- A reviewed `release-notes/vX.Y.Z.md` in the repository, if one exists, wins over the model text (#432).
- The model is a repository variable `RELEASE_NOTES_MODEL`, passed as `--model` like `TRIAGE_MODEL`. The triage uses `claude-haiku-4.5`, which is fine for labels. The notes need a stronger model for the Chinese and the English text, a Sonnet class model. The first step is to list the model ids the CLI accepts on our subscription and pick the newest Sonnet.
- The release page can still be fixed afterwards with `gh release edit <tag> --notes-file <file>` (RELEASING.md, "Release notes").

### Done when

- A final tag gets notes in the form of the template, written by the model from the inputs only, with the generated contributors block, and `check` passed on them.
- With no `COPILOT_TOKEN`, a failed model job or a failed `check`, the release gets the short body and a warning.
- A reviewed `release-notes/vX.Y.Z.md` is used instead of the model text when it exists.
- One release was written this way and compared with hand-written notes of the same release.

This builds on #431 and #432.
title: CI: the Copilot CLI writes the release notes of a final release
