### Idea

The iOS shell speaks Chinese everywhere except in a game's settings. In the Chinese screenshot of `README.zh-CN.md` the section headings (GAME, CONTROLS), the labels and notes ("Play mode", "Show frame rate"), the options ("Handheld", "Docked") and the rows from the game's launcher profile ("Language", "American English") are still English.

I think this is the cause, from the code. The shell draws these rows from each game's `launcher.json` (`docs/launcher.schema.json`: `label`, `note`, `section`, option labels), and `LauncherProfile` shows those strings as they are. They are English. The Mac launcher translates the same rows with its own keys, 92 `launch.set.*` entries with Chinese in `Localization.swift`. The shell has no such table. I have not checked this on a device, only in the code and in the screenshot.

### Plan

- The shell looks up a translated section, label, note and option text by the setting's `DM_*` name and the system language. When there is none, it shows the English text from `launcher.json`, so a new setting never shows an empty row.
- The texts live in the same per-language JSON files as the other shell strings, so the Mac launcher and the shell share one source for the setting texts. This builds on #388, step 5 (the shell's keys move into the JSON files). It needs the answer to the open question there about the key form.
- The Demo app's sample rows go through the same lookup, so the screenshots show it.
- A test fails when a setting that the Mac launcher translates has no Chinese text in the shell.

### Done when

- A device set to Chinese Simplified shows every row of a game's settings in Chinese, as far as the Mac launcher has a Chinese text for it.
- A setting without a translation shows its English text.
- The Chinese screenshots in `README.zh-CN.md` (`frontend/screenshots/ios-library-zh.webp` and `ios-cover-flow-zh.webp`) are captured again from the fixed app and replaced.
title: iOS shell: a game's settings are English on a Chinese device

## Problem or idea

The owner's decision after seeing where the shell cache landed: `NX2Apple-shell` is created **inside the game output folder** (his: `~/Downloads/Switch Rom/NX2Apple-shell`) — the one place a player habitually cleans. The cache holds the frameworks (a deleted one costs a full rebuild), `shell.json` (the library ledger) and the banner cache. Important-and-hard-to-regenerate must not live next to things players delete.

## The agreed direction (owner + @v0lumehi)

1. Default location: `~/Library/Application Support/NX2Apple/shell/` — the macOS home for app-owned data players do not touch, beside the engine tree.
2. **Migration**: an existing `shellRoot` moves to the new location automatically on first run — `shellRoot` updates, `shell.json`'s internal paths are rewritten, the old folder is removed after a verified move.
3. The Settings cache row gains a **Move cache folder…** button: pick a new location, the folder moves, the root updates — a player who wants the cache on an external drive (frameworks are hundreds of MB per game) is not pinned to the first location.
4. With the cache as the framework's primary copy (#406), #232 (delete the build folder after a build) loses its risk and can be implemented.

Owner-approved, suggested for the v1.1.0 milestone. `ShellLibrary.resolveRoot` is the contract that changes; the Settings cache row (#400) is where the Move button goes.
title: Move the shell cache out of the game output folder into Application Support

### Idea

In the iOS shell library, a tap on a game under Recently played does not start it. It only selects the game: `PortraitLibrary.recent` calls `select(detail.id)`, which makes it the game in the hero at the top. The row ends in a chevron, which says "open", and I expected the game to start. The chevron has no clear job today.

The rows also sit too tight. The hairline between two games has no space around it, so the title of the lower game touches it. On my phone the Zelda row sticks to the line above.

### Plan

- A tap on a Recently played row does what the Play button does for that game. That covers the games that need game data or an app update, where Play offers the fix instead of starting. The same goes for A on a controller (`lib.recent.<id>`).
- Drop the chevron, or replace it with a glyph that matches the action. A chevron on a row that starts a game is wrong.
- Add vertical space around the hairline between the rows, about 10 pt above and below. The row keeps its minimum height.
- Check the other layouts (Cover Flow, iPad grid) for the same Recently played rows and change them the same way.

### Done when

- A tap on a Recently played game starts it, or opens the same fix as Play does.
- The chevron is gone, or shows the real action.
- The title of a row has clear space to the hairline above it.
- The PR has before and after screenshots of the library in English and Chinese.

body:
## Problem or idea

Follow-up to #406. The owner measured three on-disk copies of one game's framework:

1. `<id>_build/shell-framework/` — the build script's own output (433 MB), kept as the build's incremental cache
2. `NX2Apple-shell/frameworks/` — the mirror, the shell's primary copy (#406, an APFS clone of #1: no extra space until either side changes)
3. `NX2Apple-shell/derived-data/…/DmShell.app/Frameworks/` — the copy xcodebuild embeds into the signed shell (unavoidable: it is part of the app)

**#2 and #3 are by design and cost (almost) nothing.** #2 is a clonefile (copy-on-write, blocks shared until a side changes), #3 is the signed app itself. **#1 is the real duplicate** — and the build script will happily regenerate it from its other caches when the folder is missing.

## Proposal

In the `DM_FRAMEWORK_ONLY` path, after the framework is produced and handed over, let the build **reuse the cache as its output location**: if `NX2Apple-shell/frameworks/<id>/` already exists, build straight into it (or clone from the build output and delete the build-side copy at the end of the script). The build keeps whatever incremental state it actually needs (Gen/, derived data), not the final framework.

The caveat to weigh: the build folder is per-game and the cache is per-install-root — a player who uses two output folders would build the framework once per root. @v0lumehi your call on where this belongs (build_ipa.sh's FRAMEWORK_ONLY path vs. the launcher passing a flag).

## Measured on the owner's disk

- Mario Kart 8 (installed through an rc with #406): all three copies present; the mirror is an APFS clone.
- Captain Toad (built, install not completed): **only the build-side copy exists** — the mirror appears at install time, which is by design, but also means the disk spike happens before the player sees anything.
title: Build folder's shell-framework copy: make the build reuse the cache instead of keeping its own 400 MB copy

body:
## Problem or idea

Companion to #336 (the Mac's controller quit). On the iPhone there is no keyboard and no Cmd+Q, so a running game needs its own way back to the launcher. Written down per the owner's request, with the options and their trade-offs — the choice decides engine work, so it should be deliberate.

**The architecture fact behind every option:** the engine runs as `dm_main` on a big-stack thread inside the shell's process (one game per process today; the shell relaunches to switch games). So 'quit to launcher' = end that thread's host cleanly, tear down the game view, and hand the window back to `LibraryView`. A crash-style exit works but must never be the *designed* path.

## The options (from how touch-era shells do it)

**A. Floating return orb (Delta, Dolphin iOS, PPSSPP).** A small circle parked at the screen edge; drag it to the centre to arm, tap to show a confirm. Pros: always visible, works with fingers only, movable out of the way of any game's HUD. Cons: one more overlay over the game's picture; the arm-by-drag is the anti-mis-touch cost.

**B. Controller Home long-press (Steam Link, Delta; mirrors #336's Mac proposal).** Hold the logo button ~2 s → 'Quit game?' → A confirms. Pros: zero learning for controller players, one implementation serves the Mac too. Cons: nothing for touch-only players; needs the engine's input loop to watch the button while the game runs.

**C. A gamepad combo (RetroArch: L3+R3 or Start+Select).** Same audience as B, cannot collide with any game's mapping as long as the shell reserves the combo. Cons: discoverable only if told; still nothing for touch-only players.

**D. An in-game 'Exit' switch inside the shell's per-game settings overlay.** The shell already renders an overlay over the running game (the same panel that shows game settings); an Exit row there is one tap. Cons: reaching it mid-game is the same problem it solves.

## The recommendation to discuss

**B + A together**: Home long-press for controller players (shared with #336's Mac work, one design), the floating orb for touch-only players (the only group with no other path). Both land behind one 'Quit game?' confirm. The engine-side work — a clean host shutdown on demand — is the real cost and serves either choice.

@v0lumehi the engine-side shutdown design is the part I would like your read on: what a clean `dm_main` teardown needs today, and whether the progress hook (#0052) is the right place for a 'host wants to exit' channel.
title: iOS shell: how a running game hands control back to the launcher (exit paths for the touch era)

We want to know whether NX2Apple can run Nintendo Switch 2 games. The answer decides whether this becomes a feature. Nothing is promised yet.

## What the engine does now

Checked in the engine at `9c426b89`.

- The engine runs Switch 1 games only.
- The host answers `nn::pl::IsRunningOnOunce` ("is this a Switch 2") with false (`dm/host/hle_sdk16.c`). A game with a Switch 2 Edition, such as Mario 1.2.1, runs as on a Switch 1.
- seedds/nxnative has issues about Switch 2 controllers (seedds/nxnative#646, seedds/nxnative#867). It has none about Switch 2 games.

## Questions

None of these is checked yet.

1. Can `nx_extract` read a Switch 2 game dump, and which keys does it need?
2. Is a Switch 2 game's code AArch64 that the existing rewrite handles?
3. The Switch 2 has a different GPU generation from the Switch 1. How much of the shader translation still applies?
4. Which new SDK services does a Switch 2 game call that the host does not answer?

## Result

A comment on this issue that answers each question, with how it was checked. It ends with one of three outcomes: Switch 2 games are possible with the current engine and some work, possible only with large changes to nxnative, or not possible.

A test uses a Switch 2 game the tester owns and dumped from their own console.

The Mac launcher cannot build an IPA without installing it. An iPhone / iPad build needs a paired device and a signing team. Without them the build stops before it starts, with "The shared app needs a device and a signing team. Choose them under Install on first."

Players who sideload with their own tool (AltStore, SideStore, a re-signing service) have no way to get an IPA from the Mac launcher.

### What is still there

- `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py` packs an unsigned IPA when it runs without `--prepare-xcode` and `--shell-framework`. It prints `output IPA: <path>`.
- `frontend-qt` still builds an IPA. On a Mac it uses the same script, on Windows `nspb_qt/win/build_app.py`.

### What removed it

`c198d056` ("Launcher: iPhone / iPad is the shared app, the per-game IPA target is gone", part of #226) removed the per-game IPA target from the Mac launcher, with its build path and strings.

The comment above `installDevice` in `frontend/Sources/NSPortBuilder/ContentView.swift` still says "Without a device or a team the build stays an unsigned IPA, as before". That is no longer true.

### Expected

- The Mac launcher can build an unsigned IPA for a game without a device or a signing team.
- The finished build shows where the IPA is, with a button that reveals it in Finder.
- The IPA installs with a sideloading tool and the game starts.

### Open questions

- Is the IPA built when no device is chosen, or is it a separate choice on the iPhone / iPad card?
- Does the IPA carry the RomFS, or is it slim with the game files copied to `Documents/romfs` by hand, as the Windows build in `frontend-qt` can?

body:
@LNPANDY reported that cloud saves are stored as one packed file. A player who wants to bring a save from a Switch cannot drop the files in.

### What happens today

The cloud folder holds one file per game, `<folder>/<title ID>/save.dmsync`. The engine packs the committed save (`DM_SAVE` and `DM_SAVE_device`) into it on purpose. iCloud replaces a single file as a whole. It syncs a folder file by file, so a folder could end up half from the iPhone and half from the Mac. The reasoning is in `engine/dm/host/save_sync.h`.

The local save is already plain files. On the iPhone it is `Documents/games/<id>/save/`, which the Files app shows. On the Mac it is `save/<id>` in the app's folder. A Switch dump (`Profile1.sav`, `Profile1.sjson`, `GlobalSettingsNX64.sjson` and so on) can be copied there by hand.

### Problem with copying by hand

On the first sync with changes on both sides, the newer save wins. The engine takes the newest modification time of the files. Copied Switch files keep their old dates. The cloud save could then win, and the imported save would only be kept in `<DM_SAVE>-backups/`. I have not tested this.

### Proposal

An "Import save" button in the per-game settings on the iPhone and in the Mac launcher. It copies the picked folder into the game's save folder, keeps the current save as a backup first, and makes sure the imported save is sent to the cloud at the next sync. The packed cloud format stays as it is.

An "Export save" button that writes the plain files to a picked folder would cover the way back to the Switch.

### Open questions

- Does the engine need a call to mark an imported save as the one to keep, or is touching the file dates enough?
- Should import be possible while a cloud folder is set but the cloud copy is newer?
title: Import and export a save as plain files, for saves from a Switch

### This is

A problem

### What happens, or what you would like

The macOS launcher shows an idle Builds page with no progress or log, while the build it started is still running and compiling shaders at high CPU usage.

Observed during a Mac app build of The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom (0100F2C0115B6000, update 1.4.3). The library says the game is not built yet. On the Builds page, the normal "Build game" button is visible rather than the active build controls. Expanding the build log shows only the placeholder "构建日志会显示在这里" (the build log will appear here).

At the same time, the process tree was:

```text
PID 2368  PPID 1     /Applications/NX2Apple.app/Contents/MacOS/NSPortBuilder
PID 3729  PPID 2368  python3 .../engine/scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py ... --progress json --work-dir ~/Desktop/Games/0100F2C0115B6000_build --platform mac-app -o ~/Desktop/Games/0100F2C0115B6000.app
PID 36342 PPID 3729  python3 .../engine/dm/gfx/tools/own_compilers.py .../shader/pkg .../shader/cache
multiple metal compiler children of PID 36342
```

The main build had been running for about 26 minutes, and the shader compiler wrapper for about 20 minutes. Several Metal compiler children used roughly 59–93% CPU each in one sample. `logs/dmsh_build.log` continued to grow (approximately 4.0 MB at 20:37 and 4.4 MB at 20:39 local time). This was active compilation, not simply an idle UI after the build exited.

Steps to observe the affected state:

1. A build started from the launcher is running in the background.
2. Open the launcher, select Builds and expand Build log.
3. The page looks idle and the log is empty, even though the launcher's child build process and its Metal compiler children are still active.

The exact action that originally caused the UI to lose the task state is unknown. Closing/reopening a window has NOT been verified as a reproduction step. No second build was started during diagnosis.

Possible investigation direction, not a confirmed root cause: in the inspected checkout, `RootView.Shared` owns a per-window `BuildModel`; its progress/log/running state lives in memory, while process-group tracking is static. The build's pipe and termination callbacks capture the model weakly. Please check whether a window/model lifecycle change can leave a running build without a corresponding UI model, and whether an existing build can be reattached or surfaced in a newly created window.

### What you expected

While a launcher-owned build is active, the launcher should show its current stage, progress, log and stop control. If the owning window is recreated, the running task should remain visible or the launcher should clearly indicate that an existing build is still active, rather than presenting an empty idle build page.

### NX2Apple version

0.7.5 (installed app, both CFBundleShortVersionString and CFBundleVersion)

### Computer and OS

MacBook Air (Mac17,3), Apple M5, 10-core CPU, 16 GB RAM. macOS 27.0.1 (26A434). Launcher UI language: Chinese.

### Copy diagnostics

The Settings > Copy diagnostics output was not captured. The following information was collected directly from the installed app, system and local checkout instead:

- Installed app: `/Applications/NX2Apple.app`, version 0.7.5.
- Local launcher checkout: `a4efa44` (not asserted to be the installed binary's source revision).
- Local engine checkout: `2291093`.
- Build target: Mac app.
- Build script: `~/NX2Apple/engine/scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py`, launched with `--progress json`.
- Python: the interpreter bundled inside NX2Apple.app.
- Work directory: `~/Desktop/Games/0100F2C0115B6000_build`.
- Launcher PID 2368 was still the parent of build PID 3729 during the observed mismatch.
- No complete build log is attached; the empty UI log and active process tree are the relevant evidence for this launcher issue.

### No keys, no game files

- [x] Nothing attached here contains keys, game files or data extracted from a game.
title: macOS launcher loses build progress and log while its shader compilation continues in the background

Hi, could the Mac launcher produce apps named after the game, such as `Mario Kart 8 Deluxe.app`, instead of `0100152000022000.app`?

The numerical name is visible in Finder when moving, sharing or launching a compiled app outside NX2Apple. The apps examined already have the correct game title in `CFBundleName` and `CFBundleDisplayName`; the request concerns the outer `.app` directory name.

## Current behavior and code

With a recognized Title ID, [ContentView.swift at a4efa44e](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/blob/a4efa44ea92d980d0b16938c694a63fd7ce7dd4e/frontend/Sources/NSPortBuilder/ContentView.swift#L1369) constructs `<output>/<ID>.app` and passes it through `-o`.

The engine script already has `mac_app_name()`, obtains the display name from the NACP or an explicit app-name setting, and defaults to a game-title-based `.app` name when no explicit output is supplied:
[build_ipa_from_nsp.py](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/main/scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py).

The library also has a numeric-path assumption in [rememberInputs](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/blob/a4efa44ea92d980d0b16938c694a63fd7ce7dd4e/frontend/Sources/NSPortBuilder/Library.swift#L502), so changing only the name passed to `-o` would need corresponding path tracking and rediscovery checks.

## Proposed behavior

- Use a validated game display title for the outer app directory, with Finder-safe filename sanitization. For example:
  - `Mario Kart 8 Deluxe.app`
  - `Princess Peach - Showtime!.app`
  - `The Legend of Zelda - Tears of the Kingdom.app`
- Keep stable Title IDs for bundle identity, save-data identity and `<ID>_build` work/cache directories.
- Record and reopen the actual resulting app path throughout the library, build-completion handling and discovery.
- Handle titles that sanitize to the same filename without overwriting another game's app; appending the Title ID when needed would be one option.
- Continue recognizing existing `<ID>.app` bundles and preserve manually named apps. Any migration should retain their library links and existing build state.
- Retain a safe ID-based fallback when a game name is unavailable.

The goal is a readable app name while continuing to reuse the same extraction, shader and pipeline caches.

## Related issue

[#382](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/issues/382) was fixed by [#386](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/pull/386). That addressed the shared `game_build` / `game.app` fallback when the launcher failed to parse an ID. This request is different: with a correctly recognized ID, the launcher still deliberately uses the numerical ID as the app filename.

## Validation status

This is an investigated feature request. No launcher naming patch has been applied or validated locally yet.

Useful checks for an implementation would include punctuation and Unicode in titles, colliding sanitized names, rebuilds of existing numerically named apps, library relinking, and confirmation that the work/cache and save-data identities stay unchanged.

No keys, game packages or extracted game code are included.
title: Use human-readable game titles for compiled Mac .app filenames while keeping Title ID-based caches

body:
Hi, while organizing a local Switch-game collection in NX2Apple, I found two artwork problems that can make the library misleading:

- The cover belongs to a different shop product, such as a Nintendo Switch 2 edition or a game + Nintendo Switch Online subscription bundle.
- The correct game's official banner contains promotional overlays such as “Demo Available” or an awards ribbon.

## Observed examples

| Game | Cover selected automatically |
| --- | --- |
| Splatoon 3 | Game + 3-month Nintendo Switch Online membership |
| Super Mario Bros. Wonder | Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Meetup in Bellabel Park |
| Kirby and the Forgotten Land | Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Star-Crossed World |
| Tears of the Kingdom, Divinity: Original Sin 2, Hollow Knight | Nintendo Switch 2 edition artwork |
| Mario vs. Donkey Kong, Princess Peach: Showtime!, Metroid Dread, Cadence of Hyrule, Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity | Demo or other promotional overlays |

The collection contains the original Nintendo Switch releases. Having an update installed does not by itself establish that a separate edition or its additional content is present.

## Likely cause of the wrong-product selection

In [Artwork.swift at a4efa44e](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/blob/a4efa44ea92d980d0b16938c694a63fd7ce7dd4e/frontend/Sources/NSPortBuilder/Artwork.swift#L82), entries are reduced to a Title ID → banner URL dictionary. The first encountered entry for an ID wins.

The [TitleDB US English list](https://github.com/blawar/titledb/blob/master/US.en.json) can contain multiple shop products with the same `id`, but different `name`, `nsuId` and `bannerUrl`. For example, the list examined during this investigation contains:

| Title ID | Original Switch product / NSU ID | Other product / NSU ID |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0100C2500FC20000` | Splatoon 3 / `70010000046395` | Splatoon 3 + 3-month membership / `70010000066990` |
| `010015100B514000` | Super Mario Bros. Wonder / `70010000068688` | Switch 2 Edition + Meetup in Bellabel Park / `70010000115567` |
| `01004D300C5AE000` | Kirby and the Forgotten Land / `70010000046405` | Switch 2 Edition + Star-Crossed World / `70010000096829` |

A Title ID match alone therefore does not establish that a cover represents the edition or bundle the player actually has. Retaining product information and using an explicit, deterministic selection rule would avoid dependence on dictionary iteration order.

This is separate from promotional overlays: even the correct base-product banner can contain “Demo Available”, so product filtering alone will not solve that part.

## Manual workaround verified locally

I replaced 11 covers using the existing **Manage → Change artwork…** action. I downloaded complete official artwork variants, inspected each one, and confirmed the replacements in the GUI and their saved `artworkPath` values. The collection's other game metadata remained unchanged.

This is a verified manual workaround, not an implemented fix to the automatic artwork selector.

### Where the clean images came from

Eight are media assets served by Nintendo's European website; three are served by Nintendo's official eShop image CDN. TitleDB was used as a community-maintained index to locate the appropriate eShop product URLs; the image files themselves came from Nintendo.

| Game | Clean image used |
| --- | --- |
| Mario vs. Donkey Kong | [Nintendo Europe](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/10_share_images/games_15/nintendo_switch_4/2x1_NSwitch_MarioVsDonkeyKong_image1600w.jpg) |
| Princess Peach: Showtime! | [Nintendo Europe](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/10_share_images/games_15/nintendo_switch_4/2x1_NSwitch_PrincessPeachShowtime_image1600w.jpg) |
| Metroid Dread | [Nintendo Europe](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/10_share_images/games_15/nintendo_switch_4/H2x1_NSwitch_MetroidDread_image1600w.jpg) |
| Splatoon 3 | [Nintendo Europe](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/10_share_images/games_15/nintendo_switch_4/2x1_NSwitch_Splatoon3_image1600w.jpg) |
| Super Mario Bros. Wonder | [Nintendo Europe](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/10_share_images/games_15/nintendo_switch_4/2x1_NSwitch_SuperMarioBrosWonder_image1600w.jpg) |
| Kirby and the Forgotten Land | [Nintendo Europe](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/10_share_images/games_15/nintendo_switch_4/H2x1_NSwitch_KirbyAndTheForgottenLand_onlylogo_enGB_image1280w.jpg) |
| Tears of the Kingdom | [Nintendo Europe](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/10_share_images/games_15/nintendo_switch_4/2x1_NSwitch_TloZTearsOfTheKingdom_Gamepage_image1280w.jpg) |
| Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity | [Nintendo Europe](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/10_share_images/games_15/nintendo_switch_4/H2x1_NSwitch_HyruleWarriorsAgeOfCalamity_enGB_image1280w.jpg) |
| Hollow Knight | [Nintendo eShop CDN](https://img-eshop.cdn.nintendo.net/i/4643fb058642335c523910f3a7910575f56372f612f7c0c9a497aaae978d3e51.jpg) |
| Divinity: Original Sin 2 – Definitive Edition | [Nintendo eShop CDN](https://img-eshop.cdn.nintendo.net/i/f175e75e1685926eaad644e032010d776108041c44791a0daf6586ddd11fde0c.jpg) |
| Cadence of Hyrule | [Nintendo eShop CDN](https://img-eshop.cdn.nintendo.net/i/d98ff11f4ee342047b7812c9011425b0c41cc469a2418187ba2994212721ef0c.jpg) |

For the European assets, the original game pages and their `og:image`/media references are useful entry points—for example [Kirby](https://www.nintendo.com/en-gb/Games/Nintendo-Switch-games/Kirby-and-the-Forgotten-Land-2045110.html), [Tears of the Kingdom](https://www.nintendo.com/en-gb/Games/Nintendo-Switch-games/The-Legend-of-Zelda-Tears-of-the-Kingdom-1576884.html) and [Princess Peach](https://www.nintendo.com/en-gb/Games/Nintendo-Switch-games/Princess-Peach-Showtime--2444445.html). The asset filenames vary, so constructing one universal URL pattern would be fragile. An `og:image` candidate still needs inspection.

## How to choose the appropriate image

1. Match the actual game, platform and edition. Preserve the shop product name and NSU ID alongside the Title ID while comparing candidates.
2. Prefer the standalone original Switch product for a Switch-source build. Bundle or Switch 2 artwork should be an explicit match to the player's edition, rather than a consequence of a shared Title ID.
3. Inspect the downloaded image for baked-in demo, subscription, awards, upgrade or additional-content advertising. A product-name filter cannot detect all of these.
4. When its eShop banner is promotional, look for a clean official media variant on the original game page. Keep the game's actual logo and legitimate edition subtitle.
5. Keep a persistent user override as the final choice. NX2Apple already supports this, and it worked for all 11 replacements.

Could the automatic selector retain enough product information to avoid wrong editions/bundles, with a clean-artwork fallback or a curated override where necessary? An automated selection implementation has not been tested here.

All links above point to public official artwork. No keys, game packages or extracted game data are included.
title: Library artwork can select a different edition or bundle; prefer accurate, promotion-free game covers

When playing Persona 5 Royal, whenever shaders need to be compiled, the game experiences severe frame pacing issues.

title: Persona 5 Royal: Unstable frame pacing during shader compilation, dropping to ~20 FPS until window focus changes

body:
## Fix or feature

- [ ] Fix
- [x] Feature

## What and why

**The problem.** The shell's library (shell.json) and the banner cache live in `NX2Apple-shell/`, but every game's `DmGame<id>.framework` lives in that game's `<id>_build/shell-framework/`. A player who deletes a build folder loses that game from the shell: the next install's `dropMissing()` drops it, and the only recovery is a full rebuild (the shader cache helps, but it is still hours for a big game).

**Recovering from the device is possible but slow.** The frameworks are not compressed in the app bundle (each `DmGame<id>.framework` sits there as-built, one directory), so `devicectl device copy from` can pull them back and they can be re-embedded directly — but pulling hundreds of MB to GBs per game over USB, and re-verifying every file, is a worse experience than never losing them.

**The proposal (the cache wins):**

1. After a successful framework build, mirror it into `NX2Apple-shell/frameworks/<id>/` — a hard link when the build folder is on the same volume (zero extra space), a copy otherwise. `dropMissing()` then checks the mirror too, and the next install re-embeds from the mirror without touching the build folder. Deleting a build folder no longer removes a game from the shell.
2. A **Cache** row in Settings → Build tools: the name, the folder path beneath it, an *Open folder* button at the right, and a caption saying what lives there (the shell's frameworks, its library file, the banner cache) and what deleting it costs (every game reinstalls from its build folder; a game whose build folder is also gone must be rebuilt).

@v0lumehi this touches ShellInstall and the dropMissing contract you wrote — please review the design before it becomes a PR (especially: hard links across volumes, and whether the mirror should be the *primary* source with the build folder as the cache, not the other way around).

body:
## How translations work on main

Checked on main `41f7d6ba`.

- `frontend/Sources/NSPortBuilder/Localization.swift` has 4213 lines and holds every language. Chinese and English are pairs in one table with 1033 keys. Swedish, German and French are dictionaries in the same file.
- 283 Chinese rows are written as `\u{...}` escapes. Nobody can read or review them in a diff.
- The Windows launcher does not read translations itself. `frontend-qt/gen_localization.py` reads the Swift source with regular expressions and writes `frontend-qt/nspb_qt/localization.py`. The Swift string literal is in effect a data format.
- A new language touches 14 files. #352 (Italian) rewrites all of `localization.py` (+957/−956), adds to the `Lang` enums in Swift and Python, changes language detection in both, and adds its own test file in both front ends.
- Every PR that adds a language or a string conflicts with every other one. #274 and #275 needed a rebase over 84 duplicated lines in `Localization.swift`.
- 95 calls build their key at run time, for example `launch.set.\(variable)`. No tool can tell whether a key is still used.
- The iOS shell has its own texts in `Localizable.xcstrings` files. `ShellUI` has 70 keys and `ShellHost` has 59 keys, both in English and Chinese. `ShellDemo` has 40 keys in English only. The keys are the English text. `ShellLanguage.bundle` picks the language. Checked on main `80ed4026`.

## Target

### Files

`frontend/l10n/<code>.json`, one file per language, next to `frontend/fonts/`. Each file is a flat object, keys sorted, UTF-8 text without escapes. A `_language` entry holds the language's own name and the locale prefixes that select it.

```json
{
  "_language": { "name": "Français", "locales": ["fr"] },
  "app.checking": "Recherche de mises à jour…",
  "build.start": "Construire"
}
```

### The iOS shell

The shell's texts are in the same JSON files. A script generates the `Localizable.xcstrings` of `ShellUI` and `ShellHost` from them, so `String(localized:)` and `ShellLanguage.bundle` keep working. A test fails when a generated catalog differs from the JSON files. The shell offers every language that the files have.

### Rules

- English and Chinese have every key. A test fails otherwise.
- Every other language may miss keys. A missing key shows the English text.
- Placeholders (`%@`, `%ld`, `%1$@`) match English in count and order.
- A file has no key that English does not have.
- Every literal key in `t("...")` in Swift and Python exists in English.
- A key built at run time uses a prefix from one declared list, for example `launch.set.`. The test checks that every key with that prefix has a variable behind it.
- The language picker and the device detection read the language list from the files. Adding a language changes nothing outside `frontend/l10n/`.

### Loading

- The Mac app reads the files from `Contents/Resources/l10n`. `build-mac-app.yml` copies them there, like the engine and the bundled tools. SwiftPM resources (`Bundle.module`) are not used, because the workflow builds the bundle by hand and would leave the resource bundle out.
- `swift test` and `swift run` read them from the checkout.
- The Windows launcher reads the same files. `build-qt.yml` adds them with `--add-data`, as it does for `frontend/fonts`.

## Steps

The open translation PR #352 lands first. After the conversion, an open translation PR has to be redone in the new files.

1. A one-time script writes the five JSON files from the current tables. Swift and Python load them. `Localization.swift` keeps only the lookup and the language choice. `gen_localization.py` and `nspb_qt/localization.py` are deleted. The two build workflows copy the files.
2. The language list comes from the files. `Lang` stops being an enum in Swift and in Python. Windows locale names move into `_language`.
3. One test per front end checks every language against the rules. `GermanLocalizationTests.swift`, `FrenchLocalizationTests.swift`, `test_localization_de.py` and `test_localization_fr.py` are replaced by it. Rules that only one language has, such as German typography, stay as small tests.
4. The key checks: literal keys, the declared prefixes, and no unused keys outside them.
5. The shell's keys move into the JSON files. The script generates the shell's catalogs, and the test checks that they match.

## Done when

- `Localization.swift` contains no translated text.
- `gen_localization.py` and `nspb_qt/localization.py` do not exist.
- The released Mac app and the Windows build show all five languages. Checked by hand on a build from the workflow, not only in `swift test`.
- The catalogs of `ShellUI` and `ShellHost` are generated from the JSON files.
- The shell on an iPhone shows every language of the files. Checked by hand on a device.
- A new language is one new file under `frontend/l10n/`. Both launchers and the shell offer it without code changes.

## Open questions

- Do the shell's keys become dotted keys like the launcher's, for example `shell.settings.back`, or do they keep the English text as the key?
- The files then serve more than `frontend/`. Do they move to a top-level `l10n/`?

## Out of scope

- The catalog of `ShellDemo`. It holds sample data for the demo app.
- A translation platform such as Weblate. The flat JSON format works with one later.
title: One JSON file per language, read by the Mac launcher, the Windows launcher and the iOS shell

body:
`frontend/Sources/NSPortBuilder/ContentView.swift` has 3708 lines on main (`41f7d6ba`). About 2900 of them are `BuildModel`. `BuildModel` owns the language, the repository checkout, app updates, the engine sync, the dependency check, devices and signing, the build inputs, the build run and the build log.

## What this causes

- 13 views observe `BuildModel` with `@ObservedObject` or `@StateObject`. Most do it to call `m.t()` for strings. `LauncherView.swift` calls `m.t()` 74 times.
- Every `@Published` change invalidates all 13 views. During a build, `logTail` changes with every chunk the script writes. Each change invalidates the whole launcher, not only the log view. The cost of this is not measured yet.
- Pure logic lives in the UI model. `GameLibrary` calls `BuildModel.titleID` to read title IDs from file names.
- Threading is manual. `BuildModel` is not `@MainActor` and has 46 `DispatchQueue` hops.
- Processes are started in many places (`runQuiet`, `runCaptured`, `runOK`, `runTool`, `Process` directly). Tests replace them through loose properties such as `xcrunPath`.
- Everything is one SwiftPM target. Any file can use any other file, so nothing keeps a new feature out of `BuildModel`.
- The file changed in 166 commits in the last 30 days. Four open PRs change it.

The package targets macOS 13, so `@Observable` is not available. Small `ObservableObject`s, each observed only where it is needed, give the same effect.

## Target structure

Three SwiftPM targets, plus the app. Each target may only import the ones above it.

| Target | Holds | May import |
|---|---|---|
| `NXCore` | pure logic and services | Foundation |
| `NXModel` | stores | `NXCore`, Foundation, Combine |
| `NXLauncher` | views | `NXModel`, `NXCore`, SwiftUI, AppKit |
| `NX2Apple` (app) | entry point, wiring | all |

A store that imports SwiftUI or AppKit does not compile. Types shared between targets use the `package` access level, not `public`.

`NXCore` builds in the Swift 6 language mode, so the compiler checks data races there. This needs `swift-tools-version` 6.0. CI runs Xcode 27.1, which supports it.

### The app target is renamed to NX2Apple

The app is `NX2Apple.app`, but its code still uses an old name. The target `NSPortBuilder` becomes `NX2Apple`. The folder `Sources/NSPortBuilder` becomes `Sources/NX2Apple`. `NSPortBuilderApp` becomes `NX2AppleApp`, and the test target `NSPortBuilderTests` becomes `NX2AppleTests`. Workflows, tools and docs that name the old paths follow.

Three names stay, because players would lose data or updates otherwise:

- `CFBundleIdentifier` `org.nxnative.NSPortBuilder`. The settings in UserDefaults belong to it, and the updater rejects a bundle with another identifier.
- `CFBundleExecutable` `NSPortBuilder`.
- The data folder `~/Library/Application Support/NS Port Builder/` with the venv, the artwork and `library.json`.

### NXCore: pure logic

Value types and static functions. No state and no UI. They are tested directly.

- `TitleID`: parse, owner, update version.
- `GameInputs`: classify files, row mismatch, allowed file types.
- `BuildProgress`: stage lines, JSON events, durations, Xcode and install steps, failure info.
- `Toolchain`: Python, venv, dotnet and Xcode probing.
- App release parsing and version compare, from `AppUpdate.swift`.

### NXCore: services

They start processes and touch the file system. They have no `@Published` state. Each one is a protocol with one real implementation, so tests pass in a fake.

- `ProcessRunner`: the only place that starts a process. It handles process groups, environment and captured output.
- `GitCheckout`: clone, fetch, pull, behind count, adoption of a zip copy.

### NXModel: stores

Each store is `@MainActor`, is an `ObservableObject` and owns its own `@Published` state. It gets services and other stores through `init`.

| Store | Owns |
|---|---|
| `Localizer` | `lang`, `t()`. Passed as an environment object. |
| `RepoStore` | repository path, status, auto pull |
| `AppUpdateStore` | release check, staged update, update sheet, uninstall plan, `appVersion` |
| `EngineSyncStore` | engine selection, sync, engine failure |
| `DependencyStore` | deps, Python and dotnet paths, installs |
| `DeviceStore` | devices, teams, install target, shell copy flow |
| `BuildStore` | inputs, target, stages, running, failure, build anyway |
| `BuildLog` | the log text. Only the log view and the failure classifier read it. |

A store checks the conditions for its own actions. `BuildStore` decides whether a build may start. It gets what it needs from other stores through narrow protocols, for example a `DependencyStatus` with `allPresent`, not the whole `DependencyStore`.

Things the views need from AppKit, such as file pickers and opening Finder, reach the stores as closures. Several already do (`chooseKeys`, `revealFolder`, `openApp`).

### The app: wiring only

`BuildModel` is gone. The app creates the services and the stores, connects them and hands them to the views. It holds no logic and no `@Published` state.

### NXLauncher: views

`BuilderView` becomes one view per card: files, target, action, tools and log. Each view observes only the stores it shows.

## Guards against drift

- `frontend/ARCHITECTURE.md` describes the targets, what each may import, the store pattern and where a new feature goes. `AGENTS.md` points to it.
- `AppUpdateStore` is the first store and the reference. It has tests with a fake `ProcessRunner` and a fake release source. Later stores follow it.
- A test fails when a Swift file under `frontend/Sources` grows past 800 lines. Files above that today are listed with their current size and may only shrink.

## Steps

Each step is one PR. Behavior does not change, and tests stay green. Tests move to the new names in the same PR.

1. The three targets, the rename to `NX2Apple`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, the file size test. Only files that already fit their target move.
2. `Localizer` out of `BuildModel`. Views take strings from the environment. This cuts most of the dependencies.
3. `BuildLog` out. `LauncherPerformanceTests` gets a step that writes 1000 log lines during a build. Its budget is 0 game cards built.
4. Pure logic into `NXCore` (`TitleID`, `GameInputs`, `BuildProgress`, `Toolchain`).
5. `ProcessRunner` and `GitCheckout`.
6. `AppUpdateStore` as the reference store. `appVersion` moves with it. `build-mac-app.yml` line 187, `sync-upstream.yml` line 191 and `RELEASING.md` line 9 read it there.
7. One store per PR: repository, engine sync, dependencies, devices, build.
8. `BuilderView` split into cards. `ContentView.swift` is gone.

## Done when

- `BuildModel` and `ContentView.swift` do not exist.
- `NSPortBuilder` appears only in the bundle identifier, the executable name and the data folder.
- `NXCore` and `NXModel` do not import SwiftUI or AppKit.
- A log line invalidates only the log view. The performance test checks this.
- Every store has unit tests that run without SwiftUI.
- No Swift file under `frontend/Sources` is above 800 lines, except the listed ones.

## Open questions

- When does this start? It conflicts with most PRs that touch the launcher. Directly after v0.8.0 final looks best.
- Should `LauncherView.swift`'s `struct ContentView` be renamed to `LauncherView`? Twelve test files use the name.
title: Split BuildModel into layers the compiler enforces

### Idea

South Park: The Fractured But Whole (01008F2005154000, update 1.05 v327680, Snowdrop on NVN) has no profile. A build stops twice: the shader split finds no shaders, and the address region check reports a 12 GB reservation.

### Plan

- Shader split: the game's `.mcache` files are bare zlib streams in 64 KB blocks, without the 20-byte record header of the Mario + Rabbids games.
- Memory: Snowdrop's three-pool page allocator reserves 12 GB; cut its layout to 4 GB, sized from the pools' use measured on the Mac. The SDK build takes the Kingdom Battle node-area and alignment cuts.

### Done when

The game builds for the Mac from the NSPs and plays from boot to the first interactive scene.

### Idea

A merged NSP (base game, update and DLC in one PFS0), or an XCI with an update on the cartridge, holds more than one title. The NSP script takes such a package as the base game alone: the update and the DLC are left out, or the build fails. Mario Kart 8 Deluxe from one merged NSP was the case that showed it.

### Plan

- `nx_extract --contents <package>` lists every content meta in the package (type, title ID, version).
- The scan counts a merged package as base, update and DLC; the update is opened as a Patch and each DLC is picked by its title ID.
- The extraction progress counts the shared file once.

### Done when

A merged NSP or an XCI with base and update builds like the separate files, and `test_nsp_scan` covers it.

Princess Peach: Showtime! — 01007A3009184000

### How it was installed

Ran the Mac .app produced by the NX2Apple launcher (This Mac target), with the existing local engine checkout and generated provisional profile.

### NX2Apple version

0.7.5

### What happens, and when

**Working-title / build-success report.** Princess Peach: Showtime! 1.0.0 now completes its Mac build and starts. The initial hands-on check reports that it works; this is not a full-game compatibility certification.

The previous blocker was UE shader decode:
```text
PJ037/Content/Paks/PJ037-Switch.pak:
the index is encrypted and no window of main decrypts it
```
We narrowly backported the **existing upstream code_keys/find_key implementation and its synthetic tests**, already present in [nxnative at 2716f78f01e9](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/2716f78f01e90a9f9bbf0d09e7a798903525962f/dm/gfx/tools/uepak.py). **Credit belongs to upstream; this is not a newly written engine fix.** The local investigation/report was AI-assisted.

The reader previously searched contiguous 32-byte windows. In this title the engine copies the key from two separate 16-byte literals. The upstream reader recognizes the literal-load/store pattern and validates candidates against the pak index. No actual key was logged.

After this change:
- The version-11 pak index opened: **103,924 entries**.
- Two LZ4 shader archives decoded: **1,563 global + 55,311 game records**.
- The split produced **56,594 distinct shaders**, and the Mac build reports **56,594/56,594 OK** (10,068 vertex, 45,424 pixel, 1,021 compute, 81 geometry).
- Variant compilation reported **143,503 Metal compile operations + 8,724 reused**; the offline pipeline build produced **10,062 bases**. Those are separate counts from distinct shader keys.
- Existing extraction, provisional profile and rewritten modules were reused. Shader preparation ran for the first time after the archive blocker was fixed.
- The reader checks passed **13 tests** (three upstream key-search + ten existing IoStore), plus **11 documentation checks**.

Tested module build IDs:
- main: `928efe2954f680557b8b3839481c97db`
- subsdk0: `368f01d5cb42f06cd125dc739d036719`
- sdk: `8618895246b420329b77746b960a66ab`

The normal builder generated the provisional SDK-15 profile. Its Mac bring-up settings include `mem_alias 0x1000000000`, `mem_reserve 0x1028000000`, `mem_stack 0x10000000`, `app_pool 0xCD500000`, `sys_resource 0x5000000`. The 64 GiB alias region is a virtual-address reservation, not 64 GiB resident RAM or an iPhone recommendation.

**Remaining limits:** the short runtime log contains **13 texture-type mismatch warnings** (shader slot 128, declared Metal type 2, texture type 7), recorded in the runtime log. The game starts and the initial user test works, but rendering correctness throughout, level completion and iOS have not been verified.

The run used the existing local engine at **df713726c682cc936ac47d8ea17fa35fa522acb1 + dirty**, chain **87e2d75e6338**. That checkout has other local experiments; the test isolates the pak-reader backport and records the environment, but does not establish a clean current-main reproduction. A supported profile should be validated against the maintained engine version.

This may be useful as a new-game report and as evidence that the existing split-literal reader also handles Peach. Thanks for the upstream reader and the launcher.

### What you expected

Sharing a successful local Mac build / initial-run report, with the existing upstream fix clearly credited and the remaining warnings retained. A validated supported profile or independent reproduction would be useful; this is not a request to merge an untested profile.

### Launch options changed from the defaults

The supplied short runtime log records these saved choices: DM_LANG=it, DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=metalfx, DM_PRESENT_SNAP=1, DM_METAL_HUD=1. No comparison against default presentation settings was performed.

> Draft. There is no proposal yet. This issue collects what players report and the basic idea. A design follows once we have one.

## What players report

- The 3D layout has a right stick, but it is not drawn. It answers to a touch anywhere in the right third of the screen. Players think the stick is missing. On Pokémon Legends Z-A a player read the 3D layout as having no right stick at all ([seedds/nxnative#788](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/788)).
- The controls are large. On an iPhone Pro Max the left stick's ring is 154 points wide, as wide as the whole A B X Y diamond. Together the controls cover a lot of the picture.
- Players want to move, resize and hide single controls ([seedds/nxnative#740](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/issues/740)).

## How it works now

- The right stick is not drawn to keep the picture clear. `DmGamepad.m` places every control at the edges and corners for the same reason.
- Every size follows the screen height. `u` in `DmGamepad.m` is the height divided by 430 points, up to 1.3. A small phone gets small keys and a tablet gets large ones.

Two attempts ran as patches 0035 (a one-time text hint for the right stick) and 0036 (a layout editor opened by a long press). #345 removed both, because 0036 broke the layout. [seedds/nxnative#788](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/788) and [seedds/nxnative#811](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/811) were closed in favour of a new version here.

## The basic idea

- The picture comes first. A control covers the game only where a thumb needs it.
- A player finds every control without reading text.
- Controls have a size that fits a hand, not one that follows the screen. A larger screen gives the picture more room.
- Size and layout are changed in the app's settings, not through a gesture inside the game.
- Physical controllers are not affected.

## Open questions

- How does a player find the right stick without a drawn stick covering the picture?
- Which default size fits a thumb on a phone and on an iPad?
- Do layout changes apply to one game or to all games?
title: Touch controls: rethink the on-screen controls (draft)

### Game and title ID

Mario Kart 8 Deluxe, `0100152000022000`

### Base game and update versions

Base game `[v0]`; update 3.0.5 `[v1376256]`.

### Where it runs

iPhone or iPad (built for iPhone / iPad).

### Device, chip and RAM

iPad mini (6th generation, `iPad14,1`), Apple A15, 4 GB RAM.

### macOS or iOS / iPadOS version

iPadOS 27.0 (24A437).

### How it was installed

Installed with Apple `devicectl` using a local development signature. The installed app kept the existing bundle identifier and save data. No account credentials are included.

### NX2Apple version

Custom iOS build `3.0.12` (`CFBundleVersion 3.0.12`), based on commit `7d64131324dcfe2fff9d14b4cecbbcfe35a2cd15`.

### What happens, and when

On the A15 iPad, the game reached the menu but terminated every time during course loading with iOS Jetsam reason `per-process-limit`.

The first trace raised the application footprint from 1,968 MiB to 2,782 MiB in 0.422 s, including an 820 MiB graphics-ledger increase. A kernel trace then recorded `ActiveHard 2867 MB (fatal)` and `killing_specific_process ... DmIOS ... per-process-limit`. Fixing an independent Metal upload-staging lifetime issue reduced temporary retention, but the next run still reached 2,861 MiB with 5 MiB available and was killed at the same limit.

An opt-in BC1/2/3 → ASTC 4x4 path made the course fit. The first version reached gameplay but rendered the 3D scene magenta because it also compressed a GPU-generated 128×128×6 BC3 render target. Restricting ASTC to packaged uploads fixed that regression. In the final run, course loading completed at about 1,875 MiB resident with 991 MiB headroom, and the race, HUD and pause menu rendered with normal colors.

### What you expected

Course loading should remain within the process memory limit, and the scene and HUD should retain correct colors and rendering behavior.

### Launch options changed from the defaults

- `DM_TEX_BC_CPU=1`
- `DM_TEX_BC_ASTC=1`
- Pipeline prebuild disabled (`DM_PSO_PREBUILD=0`)
- `DM_OPMODE=0`

No game modifications were made.

### Copy diagnostics

The launcher's **Settings > Copy diagnostics** was unavailable because this is a manually built iOS app. The corresponding build, device, memory and Metal information is:

```text
Target: iPhone/iPad
App: DmIOS, CFBundleVersion 3.0.12
Engine commit: 7d64131324dcfe2fff9d14b4cecbbcfe35a2cd15
iOS build: Xcode 27.1 local development signature
Device: iPad mini (6th generation, iPad14,1), Apple A15, 4 GB RAM
OS: iPadOS 27.0 (24A437)
Increased-memory-limit entitlement: present; the measured process budget remained about 2,867 MiB
BC path: DM_TEX_BC_CPU=1
ASTC path: DM_TEX_BC_ASTC=1
Final gameplay memory: 1,875 MiB resident at frame 1500; 991 MiB headroom
Final render check: no compressed-format render-target warning; scene and HUD colors normal
```

### Game profile lines from the build log

None. The game log reports profile `0100152000022000`; no build-log line starts with `no game profile for`, `this IPA`, `this Mac app`, `this Mac build`, `this Xcode project`, or `[RED] this`.

### The game's log

Complete, privacy-sanitized logs are attached in [the attachment comment](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/issues/344#issuecomment-6554287685):

- [Successful ASTC gameplay run](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34232430/nx2apple-mariokart8-astc-gameplay-sanitized.txt) — reaches frame 3000 with normal rendering.
- [Pre-ASTC run that hit the memory limit](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34232433/nx2apple-mariokart8-pre-astc-jetsam-sanitized.txt) — the complete log up to the loading-time termination.

The logs had iOS App Group/container UUIDs and absolute paths replaced with placeholders. A follow-up scan found no API keys, tokens, email addresses, device UDIDs or decryption keys. The `key numbers` / `keys 268…` lines are engine patch-point indices, not key material.

### Crash report

No crash occurred in the final ASTC run. The earlier failure was a system memory termination (`per-process-limit`), not a renderer exception or Objective-C crash.

### Fork patches line

```text
fork patches: runtime-profile,ios-game-data-folder,ios-slim-ipa,nsp-dotnet-home,nsp-chain-changed-note,nsp-work-dir,bc-cpu-decode,mac-keymap,mac-library-folder,hades2-update-profile,env-switches-verify,ios-probe,fork-docs,ref-hle-hid-d2r,fork-patches-stamp,nsp-dotnet-root-verify,games-md-gallery,cheats-engine,cheats-mac-panel,front-mac-enter-fullscreen-once-the-app-is-activ,front-mac-dm-screen
```

### Screenshots and performance numbers

![Mario Kart 8 Deluxe gameplay on iPad mini 6 with the ASTC path enabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6487c8a5-294c-4651-a5dd-e5a05a58b990)

The final run sustained 60 fps: frame time was p50 16.88 ms, p95 19.52 ms, p99 20.47 ms; GPU time was p50 8.85 ms, p95 9.27 ms at frame 3000. Resident memory was about 1,899 MiB at frame 3000.

### No keys, no game files

- [x] Nothing attached here contains keys, game files or data extracted from a game.

### Root cause

Large BC1/2/3 atlases expand substantially when decoded to RGBA8. For example, a 4096-square BC1 atlas grows from roughly 8 MiB of encoded blocks to a 64 MiB Metal texture. Course data contains several atlases and many smaller BC textures, taking the process past the fixed iOS budget.

A second, independent lifetime defect caused autoreleased Metal upload objects to retain CPU staging until the enclosing rendering submission drained. Giving each upload its own autorelease pool reduced staging retention, but this alone did not fit the course into the device budget.

### Implemented fix

The local implementation adds opt-in `DM_TEX_BC_ASTC=1`, used together with `DM_TEX_BC_CPU=1`:

- Recompress packaged BC1/2/3 color slices to ASTC 4x4 using Arm astc-encoder 5.7.0.
- Decode and compress each mip level and array slice independently.
- Preserve linear/sRGB intent and follow the actual ASTC representation for texture views.
- Cache large converted slices with a content-sensitive SHA-256 key under `DM_TEMP`.
- Keep BC4/5 and BC6H on their existing expanded/HDR paths.
- Apply ASTC only to packaged uploads. GPU-only BC textures retain their expanded RGBA representation because they may be used as render targets.

The last point is essential. The initial version applied ASTC to every BC texture. During boot it produced:

```text
[bc-astc] encoded 1024x1024 format 0x46: 1024 KiB ASTC
[nvn-mtl] [RED] render target is a compressed-format texture (Metal format 204 128x128 layers 6, view format change 1 → NVN 0x2f): not attached; draws to this attachment are lost
[nvn-mtl] [RED] no render target could get an MTLTexture
```

The affected 128×128×6 BC3 environment cube then rendered as a magenta scene. The corrected eligibility rule leaves that GPU-only target in its expanded format.

Relevant implementation areas:

- `dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m` — `tex_desc`, `pkg_upload_`, texture-view mapping
- `dm/gfx/tex/nvn_bc_astc.{h,m}` — BC decode and ASTC transcode/cache
- `dm/gfx/tests/t_bc_astc.m` — production-path Metal regression

### Reproduction

1. Install Mario Kart 8 Deluxe on an A15 iPad without hardware BC texture support.
2. Select a course.
3. During course loading, resident memory rises rapidly and iOS kills the process at the per-process limit.

### Validation

- `check_t_bc_astc` passes 1,234 checks in each of the direct and deferred encoding runs with Metal validation.
- Coverage includes all eight guest BC color formats, odd dimensions, mips, 2D arrays, cube arrays, linear/sRGB sampling, nonuniform colors, transparency, cache reuse and the guard that a GPU-only BC render target stays expanded.
- `t_upload_budget` verifies that completed upload staging is released while preserving decoded pixels.
- Manual iOS build `3.0.12` loaded a course and reached gameplay.
- The race background, karts, HUD and pause menu rendered with normal colors; the compressed-render-target error did not recur.
- The signed app and archive passed `codesign --verify --deep --strict`; the IPA archive passed an integrity test.

### Limitations

- This path is lossy and intentionally opt-in; first-time loading is slower while textures are encoded.
- The cache consumes temporary disk space.
- Validation currently covers Mario Kart 8 Deluxe on an A15 iPad mini 6. Other BC-less devices and other games still need testing.
- The original RomFS and translated shader libraries are unchanged.
- This fix belongs in the engine: the GPU-only render-target exclusion must be part of the BC→ASTC implementation, not a game-specific workaround.
title: Mario Kart 8 Deluxe on iPad mini 6: BC-less course-loading jetsam is fixed by opt-in BC→ASTC, but GPU render targets must stay expanded

body:
## Problem

The engine is pinned to an upstream commit in `.upstream-ref`. Our `patches/` and `tools/` are not pinned. Both launchers follow `origin/main`:

- Mac: `ContentView.swift` pulls `origin/main` with `git pull --ff-only` when the app opens (`autoUpdateRepo`, on by default), and on Pull updates. Download repository clones `main`.
- Qt: `nspb_qt/model.py` fetches and pulls `origin/main` the same way.

So every commit on main reaches players within minutes. On 2026-10-31 a direct push broke the patch series for about an hour. A player pulled that state, the engine sync failed, and he could not build any more (#335).

## Proposal

The launchers pull a release tag instead of main. Players then only get tools and patches that went through a release candidate (#332).

- Check for updates compares the checkout with the newest release tag, not with `origin/main`.
- Pull updates and the automatic update move the checkout to that tag.
- Download repository clones that tag.
- Contributors who work on main keep their branch. The launcher only moves a checkout that it manages, as today.

## Open questions

- Which tag? The newest release, or the tag that matches the app's own version? The newest tag may need tools that an older app cannot run. The app's own tag never brings fixes without an app update.
- How do existing checkouts on `main` move to a tag without losing local changes? Today the automatic update only runs on a clean checkout on main.
- Is this blocked by #332, so a release is cheap enough to ship tool fixes quickly?
title: Launchers: pull the newest release tag instead of main

### What happens, or what you would like

Two ideas from #335 by @volcoice. #335 itself stays for the two bugs.

#### Always start in console mode

Today the launcher asks whether to switch to console mode each time it sees a controller. A setting starts NX2Apple in console mode every time instead. With the setting off, the launcher keeps asking as it does today.

#### Quit the game from the controller

Quitting a game needs Cmd+Q today, so a keyboard has to be close. Holding the Home button (the logo button on Xbox and PlayStation controllers) for about 2 seconds shows a "Quit game?" prompt, and A confirms. Players know Home from every console. The prompt keeps a game from closing by accident. After quitting, the launcher comes back in the same mode it started the game from. Home is the only way. There is no second button combination.

On macOS 27 and iOS 27 the game claims the Home button with `preferredSystemGestureState = .disabled`. The system respects this when the Home button setting for apps lets the app decide. The game reads that setting with `GCControllerHomeButtonSettingsManager`. If the system keeps Home for itself, the launcher shows a hint once in console mode. The hint has a button that opens the right Settings screen with `openControllerHomeButtonSettings(for: .customizeInAppAction)`. The player does not have to find the setting alone.

Before macOS 27 the game still sets `preferredSystemGestureState`, but Apple does not guarantee that the system respects it. If the Game Overlay still opens, Cmd+Q stays the way to quit.

#### Open questions

- What is the Home button setting for apps on a new Mac or iPhone with version 27? Does it let the app decide?

### This is

An idea

### What happens, or what you would like

I want to use an iPhone or iPad as a controller for a game that runs on the Mac. The NX2Apple iOS app is already on these devices, so the controller mode goes into the iOS launcher. There is no browser and no web server.

#269 built this with a web server inside the game process on the Mac. We declined it because the phone sent input over plain HTTP, a 4-digit PIN was the only guard, and the game parsed network data in about 2000 lines of hand-written C. This issue is the safe version of the same idea.

#### Security requirements

- The connection is encrypted and both sides are authenticated. It uses Apple's frameworks, MultipeerConnectivity with encryption required or Network.framework with TLS. There is no own crypto and no own HTTP or WebSocket parser.
- The first pairing needs a confirmation on the Mac. The Mac shows a code, and the user checks that the iPhone shows the same code. After that, both devices remember each other.
- A device that is not paired cannot send input. A pairing can be removed in the Mac settings.
- The Mac only listens while the controller mode is on. It is off by default.
- The network connection ends in the Mac launcher, not in the game process. The game only receives the button and stick state.
- Input messages have a small fixed format. Anything else closes the connection.
- The iOS app asks for local network access with a clear text that says why.

#### Open questions

- How does the input reach the game on the Mac? Does the engine need a second input source next to GameController devices, or can the launcher create a virtual controller?
- Can two iPhones be player 1 and player 2 at the same time?
- What is the latency over Wi-Fi compared to a Bluetooth controller?

### What you expected

Pairing an iPhone takes one confirmation on the Mac. After that the iPhone works as a controller for the running game. A device that was never paired cannot send any input.

## Game and build

Little Nightmares Complete Edition `01002FC00412C000`, 1.0.4 (v262144), Unreal Engine 4, SDK 3.5.1. Mac app from the provisional profile, M2 Pro, macOS 27.2.

## What happens

The lantern and Six's lighter light only one side of the room, with straight, sharp edges. The floor on the other sides and the base of the pillars stay dark as if in shadow, and Six casts no shadow on the floor. On the Switch the light is a soft round area around Six.

## Cause

- Every point light renders a one-pass cube shadow (geometry shader `ffc21034b958840b`, six faces at 512x512 D32F_S8). The game clears the cube in the pass that captures the vertex shader's output, and that pass is not layered.
- NVN clears every layer of the bound view, but the host's load-action clear covered only layer 0. Faces 1-5 kept zero depth, every fragment failed the depth test there, and the projection's comparison sampler read them as fully shadowed.
- A `texraw` of every face (the first commit of the fix) showed face 0 drawn and faces 1-5 all zero.

## Fix

### What happens, and when

The window opens, NVN and the audio renderer start, then the game exits with 42 on its first audio frame, every time:

```
[dm] audren: OpenAudioRenderer rate 48000 samples per frame 240 mix buffers 4 submixes 0 voices 64 sinks 1 effects 2 splitters 0 (original device 0 mode 0 → CPU / manual)
[dm] audren: render thread started (4 buffers in flight, paced by the output)
[dm] Break#1 reason=0 Result=0 svc at sdk+0xa9dec
[dm] bt: sdk+0x4305c sdk+0x43114 sdk+0x431a4 sdk+0x8799c sdk+0x17e694 render_main+0x1a0 sdk+0x8a8a8 sdk+0x8e958 dm_thread_enter+0x18

```

Symbolized against the game's `sdk`: `ExecuteAudioRendererRendering` (sdk+0x17e690) → `os::SignalSystemEvent` (sdk+0x87960) → `OnAssertionFailure` → `Break`.

Cause: SDK 3's CPU / manual `OpenAudioRenderer` keeps the `SystemEventType` in the handle (`handle[1]`) and the public `ExecuteAudioRendererRendering` signals it after each render. The game (Unreal Engine 4) reuses that object's memory right after opening the renderer (on Horizon the DSP open keeps no pointer to it). Dumping the object showed state 2 after `hle_bind_system_event`, then other data in it at the first render, where `SignalSystemEvent` checks the state byte at +0x28.

With the fix in the linked PR (SDK 3: the render thread passes NULL and signals the kernel event through its binding) the game boots, renders, takes input and plays sound.

The game to keep running past its first audio frame.

body:
`apply_series` in `tools/patches.py` can count a patch that does not apply as landed upstream.

When `git am -3` fails, the function looks at the worktree. If there are no unmerged files and the tree is clean, it calls the patch landed, unless `r.stderr` contains `Patch failed` or `patch does not apply`. `git am` prints `Patch failed at <n> <subject>` to stdout, not to stderr. A patch whose 3-way fallback cannot start (for example "could not build fake ancestor") leaves no unmerged files and a clean tree, so it ends up in `landed`.

What follows from it:

- `tools/engine.py check` reports the patch as "empty on the pinned upstream" and exits 1. CI fails, but the message points the wrong way.
- `tools/engine.py bump` and `sync` pass `landed` to `write_series`, which deletes the patch file. A conflicting patch disappears from `patches/` without a conflict report.

This came up while I rebased #226 and #288 onto a new pin. Several patches that conflicted were reported as landed.

### What to build

- A patch counts as landed only when `git am` says so (`No changes` / `already applied`) or when it applies and leaves the tree unchanged. Every other failure is a conflict.
- A test in `tools/tests` with a patch whose context is gone from the base. It must end up in `conflicts`, not in `landed`.
title: patches.py: a patch that fails to apply can be reported as landed upstream, and bump deletes it

body:
The launchers learn that cached shader libraries cannot be reused from a text marker. Patch `0006` adds a `[NOTE] chain-changed` line to the build script for this, and the Mac launcher and the Qt front end search the log for it. The patch is fork-only.

Upstream now reports the same news as a build event (seedds/nxnative#490, landed as `2716f78`). In `--progress json` mode the build script sends `shaders_stale` once per shader step, before it rebuilds the libraries. The event carries `reason`, `old`, `new` and `count`. `reason` is `chain` when the shader translator changed and `inputs` when the game profile's shader inputs changed. The fields are described in `docs/frontends.md` upstream. A `[NOTE] cached shader libraries cannot be reused` line follows the event in every progress mode.

### What to build

- The Mac launcher (`ContentView.swift`) shows its notice on the `shaders_stale` event instead of on the `[NOTE] chain-changed` text.
- The Qt front end runs the build with `--progress lines`, so it gets no events. It shows its notice on the upstream `[NOTE] cached shader libraries cannot be reused` line, or it switches to `--progress json`.
- The notice covers both reasons. A changed game profile also rebuilds the libraries, and today no notice is shown for it.
- The notice text is updated in every language in `Localization.swift` and `localization.py`.
- Patch `0006` is removed from `patches/` and `patches/series`.

### Depends on

The pin bump to `c5fe6b5d` in #319, which brings `shaders_stale` in.
title: Launchers: show the stale shader notice from the shaders_stale event and drop patch 0006

A problem

### What happens, or what you would like

The root Documents layout loads the base game but fails to discover DLC next to it. This is a runtime discovery gap, distinct from the earlier missing-export problem in #202: in this case aoc/2.img is already present on the phone. Related layout discussion: #99.

Game: FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE Asian release (0100B8A026F14000), base 1.0.0 + update 1.0.1 (v65536), selected DLC 0100B8A026F15002.

Reproduction:
1. Build the default slim iPhone IPA and install it through a separate signing tool.
2. Copy the exported romfs.img and the complete aoc folder into the game app Documents root through Finder file sharing.
3. Fully quit and relaunch the game.

Verified phone layout:
```text
Documents/
  romfs.img
  aoc/2.img
  save/
```
The DLC image is 106 bytes and contains the extracted content entry. It was independently listed on the device. Extraction succeeded; the build log says add-on content is alongside game data, outside the IPA.

Actual phone log, with the private container path removed:
```text
boot: game files <app-data>/Documents/romfs.img
[dm] aoc: reporting 0 add-on contents {} (no DM_AOC_DIR)
```

Verified workaround:
Create Documents/env.txt containing:
```ini
DM_AOC_DIR=aoc
```
Fully quit and reopen the app. The user confirmed this restored DLC functionality. No game, DLC, save or executable file was changed, and no reinstall was needed.

Code-path observation in the inspected engine/dm/ios/Sources/main.m: the per-game games/<id>/aoc path is handled when the per-game data layout is active, followed by bundled <App>/aoc; the root Documents/romfs.img fallback does not set its sibling Documents/aoc. A comment mentions Documents/aoc compatibility, but the inspected startup path did not provide it.

Please preserve explicit DM_AOC_DIR overrides and add discovery for the supported root layout, or clearly document and enforce a required per-game layout in the manual installation instructions. The workaround result establishes the observed case; the exact provenance of the re-signed installed binary was not independently verified.

DLC in Documents/aoc/<index>.img should be discovered automatically when the selected game data is Documents/romfs.img, without requiring a diagnostic env.txt edit.

### Game and title ID

Mario Tennis Aces, 0100BDE00862A000 (no game profile: a provisional one)

### Base game and update versions

Base 1.0.0 (v0); the build used v0

### Where it runs

Mac app (built for This Mac)

### Device, chip and RAM

MacBook Pro (Mac15,6), Apple M3 Pro

### macOS or iOS / iPadOS version

macOS 27.2

### How it was installed

Built with `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py --platform mac-app` from the NSP

### NX2Apple version

0.7.4 (engine at upstream f11018a1f312)

### What happens, and when

The game crashes about 0.3 s into `nnMain`, right after the shared fonts load and before the first frame:

```text
[dm] shared font (standard.ttf): /System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental/Arial Unicode.ttf (23278008 bytes, BFTTF 'decrypted' header + TTF as is)
[dm] CRASH sig=11 addr=0x38 pc=main+0x3eacbc lr=main+0x3eacbc
```

`main+0x3eacb8` calls a glyph lookup (`main+0x3ee4dc`) for `?` (0x3f) that returns null, and `main+0x3eacbc` reads `[x0, #0x38]`. The lookup asks each font engine `ScalableFontEngine::CheckGlyphExist`, and none has the glyph. With `DM_PROBE` after the `GetError` calls that follow `LoadFont` (`main+0x3ec17c`, `+0x3ec1b4`), the game's first engine loads the standard stand-in (error 0), but its extra engines fail with error 201. They get 50 KB work buffers each (`main+0x3ebf8c`: `0xc800` bytes to `Initialize`).

The engine is Monotype iType (`LoadFont` = `FSS_load_font`, `GetError` = `FS_error`). Arial Unicode (23 MB) does not fit 50 KB. A smaller stand-in does: with `DM_SHARED_FONT` set to macOS's Arial (0.8 MB) or Noto Sans Regular (0.6 MB), every `LoadFont` gives 0 and the game runs. A failed load also leaves the engine's buffer used up, so a second `LoadFont` into the same engine fails with 201 whatever the font, until the engine is initialized again.

### What you expected

The game reaches its title with the default stand-in fonts.

None (`DM_PROBE` and `DM_SHARED_FONT` only for the diagnosis above)

### Build log

The end of the launcher's Build log, and the full `logs/rewrite_main.log`:

```text
[09:27:57] reusing the extracted v0: ~/Downloads/0100BDE00862A000_build/extract/v0

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "~/NX2Apple/engine/dm/tools/patch_nso.py", line 1076, in <module>
    assert tgt, f'jump table {ins.address:x}'
           ^^^
AssertionError: jump table 35837c
[RED] patch_nso.py exit code 1 on main (full output: ~/Downloads/0100BDE00862A000_build/logs/rewrite_main.log)
```

The site, `main+0x35837c`:

```text
0x358360 cmp x8, #5
0x358364 b.hs #0x3583b4
0x358368 cmp w8, #4
0x35836c b.hi #0x3583b4
0x358370 and x18, x8, #0xffffffff
0x358374 ldrsw x18, [x16, x18, lsl #2]
0x358378 add x18, x18, x16
0x35837c br x18
```

The table base `x16` is `adrp x16` + `add x16, x16, #0xb68` at `+0x3581c4` / `+0x3581e8`. `jump_offsets` takes `and x18, x8, #0xffffffff` as a mask and looks for the same mask on the checked `w8`, finds none, and every other form fails too. The `and` only zero-extends `w8`, so `cmp w8, #4` bounds the index (5 entries: `+0x358380`, `+0x3581f4`, `+0x358228`, `+0x358280`, `+0x358328`, all in the function).

### Game and title ID

The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, 0100F2C0115B6000

### Base game and update versions

Base v0 + update 1.4.2 (v655360). The profile registers only 1.4.3 (v720896), so the build used a derived profile.

### Where it runs

Mac app (built for This Mac)

### Device, chip and RAM

MacBook Pro (MacBookPro18,2), Apple M1 Max, 32 GB

### macOS or iOS / iPadOS version

macOS 27.0.1 (26A434)

### How it was installed

I run the Mac app the launcher built.

### NX2Apple version

0.7.3

### What happens, and when

From the title screen on, everything moves at twice its normal speed: Link, the camera, animations. Sound plays at normal speed. Other games built the same way run at normal speed.

The cause, as far as I traced it:

1. 1.4.2's main is `5cb42b1cf25469fb0635fd046453d843`. The profile's `patches.py` has `FRAME_STEP` stubs only for 1.4.3's main `277178b7dba1b6d4949a84778d4abc58`, so the 1.4.2 main gets no frame step stubs and no frame step state page.
2. `derive_profile` in `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py` copies the profile's keys as they are, so the derived profile still has `fps_target 60`. The built app's settings list also offers Frame rate, with 60 as its default.
3. With no state page, `fps_present_cap()` in `dm/gfx/nvn/hle_nvn.c` returns `DM_GAME_FPS_TARGET` (60), and `present_itv()` then presents every vsync. The game's own present interval 2 is ignored.
4. The game still steps its time by its own interval, 1/30 s per frame. 60 presents a second means 2 s of game time per second. Audio has its own clock, so it stays at normal speed.

The game's log (below) shows the game setting present interval 2, and 60 fps throughout.

Workaround: choose 30 fps in the settings window (`DM_FPS_TARGET=30`). Then the cap matches the game's interval and the speed is right.

### What you expected

A version without the frame step stubs runs at the game's own speed (30 fps, as on the Switch), as the profile's own `DM_FPS_TARGET=0` does.

### Launch options changed from the defaults

`DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=metalfx`, `DM_LANG=zh-Hant`, `DM_METAL_HUD=1`. Frame rate left at its default (60) for the run below.

### Copy diagnostics

The game log at the end of the diagnostics was from my test of the fix (below), so I left it out here; the log of the run with the problem is in the next section.


### Game profile lines from the build log

The launcher's build log of this game is gone (the last build in the diagnostics is another game). That build was derived the same way: the script's status line for a derived profile is the `[RED] this Mac app uses v655360 (1.4.2), which game profile 0100F2C0115B6000 was not brought up on (v720896 1.4.3): …` form, as in the diagnostics' last build of 0100FF500E34A000. The derived build row and keys, from running `derive_profile` again on this game's extracted 1.4.2 files:

```text
build	v655360	1.4.2	main=5cb42b1cf25469fb0635fd046453d843	subsdk0=3308c1d216f788397d1451c8345a16cd	sdk=5cf080e800530a7f25bd528ec875c27b
fps_target	60
```

The built app's `Info.plist` has `DMChain b3ca4b7c621f`, `DMCommit df713726c682`, and `DMSettings` with `DM_FPS_TARGET` values `30`, `60`.

### The game's log

The run with the problem (Mac app, frame rate at its default), the lines that matter:

