I have been having trouble making a Mac or iOS app since I updated to 0.4.7. It always gave me [RED] Direct RomFS image builds require Python 3.12 or newer even though I had 3.15 installed (and never had this error prior to upgrading to 0.4.7). I downgraded back to 0.4.5 and it worked! Here's the Gemini-assisted explanation if that's ok (sorry I'm not at that technological level yet).

"What happened came down to a mismatch between how the GUI app was updated and how it interacts with macOS system paths.

Here is a breakdown of what went wrong and why rolling back to version 0.4.5 solved it:

1. Hardcoded Python Path in Version 0.4.7
In version 0.4.7, the developers updated the app's internal Swift code to call /usr/bin/python3 directly when executing background terminal scripts (such as build_ipa_from_nsp.py).

Why this broke: On macOS, /usr/bin/python3 points to Apple's built-in Command Line Tools Python stub (which is typically Python 3.9 or 3.10).

When the script ran, build_ipa_from_nsp.py checked its runtime environment, saw it was executing on Apple's system Python (3.9/3.10), and immediately threw the error:

[RED] Direct RomFS image builds require Python 3.12 or newer

2. Why macOS GUI Apps Ignore Terminal Settings
You had installed Python 3.12 via Homebrew and unlinked 3.15, which fixed your terminal environment. However, macOS GUI applications (.app bundles launched from Finder) do not inherit environment variables or PATH settings from your terminal shell (zsh).

Even though running python3 in your terminal opened Python 3.12, clicking the NS Port Builder GUI app launched it in a isolated environment where it could only see standard system binaries—meaning it kept calling /usr/bin/python3.

3. Why Changing the Script Didn't Help
When we modified the script or re-linked Python using Homebrew, the 0.4.7 GUI app binary continued to pass the exact literal string /usr/bin/python3 as the argument to execute the script process, bypassing any local environment configurations or symlinks.

4. Why Rolling Back to 0.4.5 Fixed It
Version 0.4.5 uses a flexible lookup mechanism. Instead of hardcoding /usr/bin/python3, version 0.4.5 scans standard paths (including Homebrew's /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 or /opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.12/bin/python3) and selects the first Python interpreter that satisfies the version check and has the required modules installed.

Once you went back to 0.4.5, it detected your clean Python 3.12.16 Homebrew setup instantly!"
title: Downgrading from 0.4.7 to 0.4.5 worked

body:
While working on the Mac launcher (#27, #28) I read `scripts/sync_upstream.py` to make sure my changes survive a sync, and found something that affects engine fixes merged here in general. Sharing it as a suggestion; it's your call how the fork should work.

### What the sync does with engine files

The sync takes the vendored paths (`dm/`, `scripts/`, `docs/`, `AGENTS.md`, `ref/`) from upstream file by file. Two kinds of files keep the fork's changes:

- the fork's own files (`OURS`: the RomFS archive layer, the BC decoder), and
- the nine patch carriers (`PATCHED`), whose patchers re-apply the fork's changes; the patcher-drift check fails when a carrier was edited without its patcher.

Any other engine file is simply replaced by upstream's version the next time upstream changes it. A fix merged here into such a file is then gone, without a warning.

### An example

#26 added `CreateWithAdjustableSystemClock` to `dm/host/hle_time.c` (and a test in `dm/host/tests/t_time.c`). Upstream doesn't have it (seedds/nxnative has no `AdjustableSystemClock`), and neither file is in `OURS` or `PATCHED`. The next time seedds touches `hle_time.c`, the sync will drop the fix, and what needed it breaks again.

My own #27 had the same problem: it changed `settings.py`, `pack_app.py`, `build_ipa_from_nsp.py` and `shader_split.py`. Carried here, the last two would have failed the drift check (or been reverted). I took those parts out of #27 and proposed them upstream instead (seedds/nxnative#352). #27 now touches no file under `dm/`, `docs/` or `scripts/`.

### Suggestion

Keep the fork's own layer to what it adds around the engine (the GUIs, the packaging and releases, the RomFS archive), and send engine fixes upstream first, so they come back with the sync. For a fix upstream doesn't take, the existing `PATCHED` mechanism is the safe place, with a patcher, so the drift check guards it.

A small CI check could make this automatic: fail a PR that edits a vendored file outside `OURS` and without a patcher entry, with a note to send the change upstream or add a patcher. That would have caught #26 and my #27.

I know upstream closes many PRs, so this isn't always easy. Happy to help, e.g. by porting #26 upstream.
title: Engine fixes in vendored files are reverted by the next sync

body:
I've added support for Phyre shader containers targeting Nintendo Switch NVN in `shader_split.py`.

### Implementation

- Detects Phyre/NVN containers using the `RYHPX` signature and NVN marker.
- Extracts and validates shader code/control pairs.
- Determines vertex and pixel stages from the SPH stage bits.
- Preserves the existing shader key calculation convention (SHA-256 over the first `0x880` bytes of the control section plus the code area).
- Integrates the new reader into both `scan_blob()` and `scan_file()`.

### Validation results

- **Targeted test:** successfully extracted 2 shaders from each of three `FlashSprite*.fx.phyre` files.
- **Integration test:** `shader_split.py` completed successfully and detected 5 unique shaders, including shaders from `pause_menu/Shaders/NVN/` and `PhyreIMGUI.fx.phyre`.
- **iOS shader compilation:** 5/5 shaders compiled successfully.
- **Full build:** completed successfully, producing `FinalFantasyXX2HdRemaster.ipa` (389.9 MB).
- `python3 -m py_compile` and `git diff --check` both passed.

The initial integration test required installing `lz4` in an isolated Python virtual environment; this was an environment dependency issue, not a shader parsing failure.

### Remaining validation

I haven't tested the IPA on a device yet, so runtime behavior and rendering still need to be verified. The build also reports that the game uses a provisional profile, meaning the game may not boot until the profile is brought up.

This implementation currently covers **Phyre shaders targeting Nintendo Switch NVN**. It does not add support for Sony-targeted Phyre shader formats.
title: Phyre/NVN shader support implemented and build successful

body:
While building **Final Fantasy X/X-2 HD Remaster** (`0100B3600AE9A000`), the build failed during the NSO rewrite stage with the following error:

```text
RuntimeError: 44 ldr x18, #0xfffffffffff40370
```

The issue appears to be that `patch_nso.py` scans an NRO file from offset `0`, which includes the NRO header. In this case, the reported instruction was actually part of the build ID/header data, not executable code.

#### Proposed fix

For files with the `NRO0` magic at offset `0x10`, start scanning at offset `0x80` instead of `0`. Apply this boundary consistently when filtering instruction scan results and building `CODE_RANGES`. Keep the existing behavior for non-NRO files.

```python
CODE_START = 0x80 if d[0x10:0x14] == b'NRO0' else 0
starts = sorted(x for x in starts if CODE_START <= x < TEXT_END)

DATA_BLOCKS = [
    (max(s, CODE_START), e)
    for s, e in nso_code.data_blocks(IMG, TEXT_END, md)
    if e > CODE_START
]

CODE_RANGES = list(zip(
    [CODE_START] + [e for _, e in DATA_BLOCKS],
    [s for s, _ in DATA_BLOCKS] + [TEXT_END]
))
```

#### Test results

- `patch_nso.py` passes Python syntax compilation.
- The NSO rewrite stage completed successfully, processing **1,434 modules**, including 1,432 NROs.
- The build then progressed to the shader-splitting stage, where it failed for a separate reason: no supported shaders were found.

This suggests that skipping the NRO header resolves the original rewrite-stage failure for this game. Further testing on other titles would help confirm that the change does not introduce regressions.



### Update: Phyre shader containers identified in Final Fantasy X/X-2 HD Remaster

Further investigation of the shader-splitting failure revealed that the game's RomFS contains Phyre shader containers that are not currently handled by `shader_split.py`.

**Files examined**

The following files were found under `pause_menu/Shaders/NVN/`:

- `FlashSprite.fx.phyre`
- `FlashSpriteMask.fx.phyre`
- `FlashSpriteMaskedNode.fx.phyre`

The containers use the `RYHPX` magic and contain recognizable NVN graphics code (`GFX_MAGIC`, `0x78563412`) and control sections (`CTL_MAGIC`, `0x98761234`).

**Verified shader pairs**

Two shader pairs were validated in `FlashSprite.fx.phyre`:

Stage | Code offset | Control offset | Code size | Declared control size
-- | -- | -- | -- | --
Pixel | 0x471D | 0x4B1D | 0x400 | 0xE68
Vertex | 0x68E5 | 0x6AE5 | 0x200 | 0xAE8



Both pairs pass the existing structural checks: the code ends exactly where the control section begins, the magic values are valid, and the control section's `+0x704` field matches the code size.

The other two files contain the same general structure. Their vertex shaders share the key `eb7e3757ad271eaf`; `FlashSprite.fx.phyre` and `FlashSpriteMaskedNode.fx.phyre` also share the pixel shader key `fbeabaf94a7fb2cf`.

These keys were calculated using the existing splitter's convention of hashing the first `0x880` bytes of the control section plus the code. Hashing the full declared control lengths produces different keys, so the correct key convention for Phyre still needs to be confirmed.

**Proposed next step**

Implement and test a Phyre/NVN reader in `dm/gfx/tools/shader_split.py` that extracts validated code/control pairs and feeds them into the existing shader pipeline. The reader should preserve the current key-generation behavior until the correct convention is established.

This investigation confirms that shader data is present and structurally recognizable; it does not yet establish that extraction, translation, or runtime rendering will succeed.

Note: these findings concern Phyre shaders compiled for Nintendo NVN. Support for Sony-targeted shader formats remains a separate, unverified question.
title: Fix: Skip the NRO header when scanning code ranges

i used gemini for the writeup and ideas about how to fix the issue for me. 

When launching a build through the NS Port Builder macOS GUI, the .NET first-run configuration crashes immediately with an ENOENT error during NuGet-Migrations.

Because macOS LaunchServices aggressively strips environment variables (specifically $HOME) from graphical applications, the background .NET subprocess does not know where the user's home directory is. It attempts to read a blank path (""), which causes a fatal lstat failure

System.IO.IOException: The system cannot open the device or file specified. : 'NuGet-Migrations'. One or more system calls failed: lstat("", ...) == -1; errno == ENOENT;
   at System.Threading.Mutex.CreateMutexCore(Boolean initiallyOwned, String name, NamedWaitHandleOptionsInternal options, Boolean& createdNew)
   ...
[20:20:26] dotnet's first-run configure failed (NuGet-Migrations); clearing the NuGet caches and retrying once (issue #3)

We tried to manually inject the missing environment variables directly into the scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py file to force the subprocess to see them

import os
os.environ["HOME"] = "/Users/username"
os.environ["DOTNET_CLI_HOME"] = "/Users/username"
os.environ["DOTNET_SKIP_FIRST_TIME_EXPERIENCE"] = "1"

This failed. The macOS app sandbox still aggressively scrubbed the variables before the .NET subprocess could execute, resulting in the exact same crash when the script attempted its cache-clearing retry workaround:

System.IO.IOException: The system cannot open the device or file specified. : 'NuGet-Migrations'. One or more system calls failed: lstat("", ...) == -1; errno == ENOENT;
[RED] dotnet exit code 1 (full output: /private/var/folders/.../0100317013770000_survey/logs/nuget_clear.log)

The only way to successfully bypass the macOS GUI sandbox restriction was to physically create the .NET sentinel files via the terminal. This tricks the framework into thinking initialization is already complete, bypassing the broken lstat check entirely.

the fix; 

mkdir -p ~/.local/share/NuGet/Migrations
touch ~/.local/share/NuGet/Migrations/1
mkdir -p ~/.dotnet
touch ~/.dotnet/10.0.403.dotnetFirstUseSentinel

after this it worked. why not make it so the .net first time user experience is skipped, is there a downside to skipping the check ?
title: macOS GUI .NET NuGet-Migrations crash (LaunchServices $HOME stripping)

# 哈迪斯2 iPhone 版「读取存档必死锁」完整分析报告（供 issue 使用）

## 标题
Hades II: loading a save freezes the render loop on iPhone (v0 & v1.0.137380); audio keeps playing

## 环境
- iPhone 14 Pro (iPhone15,2), iOS 26.7.1
- 移植方案: nxnative-romfs-archive (fork @ 2026-10-23 同步树), --prepare-xcode + xcodebuild 真机签名
- 测试版本: ① v0 = 0.0.126424（登记 build，patches 全应用）② v1.0.137380（title version v458752，main=cf8ddaab… 未登记，派生 profile）
- 文件服务两种形态都测过: 内嵌 romfs 树 / ROMFSARC 归档（bundle romfs/romfs.idx），无差异
- 语言 zh-Hans；entitlement increased-memory-limit 已确认签入

## 症状
- 标题画面正常渲染（v0 30fps / v1 60fps），新建游戏可玩，**存档写入完全正常**（log 见 `save commit #N … swapped atomically`，毫秒级）
- 标题 → 读取存档：**渲染循环在 ~1 秒内永久停摆**（帧计数停止，presents 停止），音频线程继续跑
- 前台挂死任意时长不会自愈；切后台/锁屏 10 秒内被 iOS 杀死

## 崩溃证据（0x8BADF00D scene-update watchdog）
- 主线程: `__psynch_cvwait ← _pthread_cond_wait ← dm_gfx_suspend ← -[_UISceneLifecycleMonitor didEnterBackground]`
- 游戏主线程: `__psynch_cvwait ← guest_clock_read_wait ← gate_dispatch ← dm_gate ← guest_main`
- 纹理线程: `__psynch_cvwait ← up_wait_zero ← up_begin ← pkg_upload ← tex_init_fill ← tex_by_id`
- watchdog 统计: wall 10s 超时，进程 CPU 0%（阻塞非死循环）

## 已排除
- 存档文件损坏（**新建档 → 保存 → 立刻读取同样卡死**；写入路径健康）
- 文件服务路径（树/归档等价卡死）
- 签名/内存权限（entitlement 在；挂死时 footprint 仅 ~2GB）
- 版本专属（v0 登记版与 v1 派生版同死）

## 猜测
读档路径上 guest 与纹理上传/呈现线程形成环形等待：tex_init_fill 的 up_wait_zero
等一个永远不会清的 fence，而 guest 在等纹理就绪；foreground 下 guest 的阻塞点
未能在崩溃报告里定格（clock wait 是后台化之后的次生现象）。

## 请求
- 是否已知问题？v0/v1 读档路径是否有人实测通过？
- 若需要更多日志（log.txt 全文 / 崩溃 ips 原文），可直接索取

NS Port Builder v0.3.0 detects the Homebrew .NET SDK successfully, but the build then fails to launch `nx_extract` because the child process uses a different .NET root.

### Environment and reproduction

- Apple Silicon macOS, .NET SDK 10.0.402 and Microsoft.NETCore.App runtime 10.0.13 installed through Homebrew.
- The dependency panel reports .NET SDK 10 as available at `/opt/homebrew/bin/dotnet`.
- `~/.dotnet` contains user caches/sentinels, but no runtime installation.
- Start an IPA build. Building `nx_extract` succeeds, then its launch fails at extraction with exit code 131:

```text
You must install .NET to run this application.
Architecture: arm64
App host version: 10.0.13
.NET location: Not found
Environment variable:
  DOTNET_ROOT = <home>/.dotnet
```

Meanwhile, `/opt/homebrew/bin/dotnet --list-runtimes` reports the installed runtime under `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/dotnet/10.0.402/libexec/shared/Microsoft.NETCore.App`.

### Cause in v0.3.0

[`findDotnet()`](https://github.com/LNPANDY/nxnative-romfs-archive/blob/v0.3.0/frontend/Sources/NSPortBuilder/ContentView.swift#L502) searches several installations, including `/opt/homebrew/bin/dotnet`, and the dependency panel accepts the detected SDK.

However, [`startBuild()` line 246](https://github.com/LNPANDY/nxnative-romfs-archive/blob/v0.3.0/frontend/Sources/NSPortBuilder/ContentView.swift#L246) unconditionally sets:

```swift
"DOTNET_ROOT": NSHomeDirectory() + "/.dotnet"
```

The SDK command can therefore build the extractor through PATH, while the generated apphost cannot find its runtime through the forced root.

### Expected behavior

Use the actual runtime root associated with the detected .NET installation for build subprocesses. For this Homebrew installation, `/opt/homebrew/opt/dotnet/libexec` is the working root. Account for launcher symlinks rather than assuming the directory containing `/opt/homebrew/bin/dotnet` is the runtime root. Keep any architecture-specific DOTNET_ROOT variables consistent if they are supplied.

### Verified workaround and limits

On this machine, adding only `~/.dotnet/host` and `~/.dotnet/shared` symlinks to the corresponding existing Homebrew runtime directories lets `nx_extract` start with the app's forced `DOTNET_ROOT`.

Verification ran the actual generated extractor with `DOTNET_ROOT=<home>/.dotnet` and `--help`. It reached its usage message and exited 2 because that CLI does not accept `--help`, instead of failing with runtime error 131. No game files or keys were opened by that check. A complete extraction/build after the workaround was not verified.

This is separate from the Python dependency issue #1.
title: NS Port Builder v0.3.0: detected Homebrew .NET ignored by hardcoded DOTNET_ROOT, nx_extract exits 131

In NS Port Builder v0.3.0 on Apple Silicon macOS, the dependency check detects Homebrew Python 3.15 but reports “Python + packages … is missing packages”. The Install button cannot resolve this configuration.

### Reproduction

1. Install Homebrew Python 3.15 and launch NS Port Builder v0.3.0 from Finder.
2. The app detects `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3` and reports missing packages.
3. Click Install. The dependency remains missing, without a useful pip error in the UI.

On the affected machine, `lz4`, `capstone`, and `fontTools` were indeed absent from that interpreter. Python itself was present and working.

### Findings in the v0.3.0 source

- [`findPython`, line 496](https://github.com/LNPANDY/nxnative-romfs-archive/blob/v0.3.0/frontend/Sources/NSPortBuilder/ContentView.swift#L496) unconditionally requires `import lz4, capstone, fontTools, backports.zstd`. Python 3.14+ already provides `compression.zstd`. The available `backports.zstd` releases declare Python `<3.14`, so requiring that backport also rejects an otherwise usable modern Python.
- [Line 555](https://github.com/LNPANDY/nxnative-romfs-archive/blob/v0.3.0/frontend/Sources/NSPortBuilder/ContentView.swift#L555) installs packages with `python -m pip install --user lz4 capstone fonttools backports.zstd`. Homebrew's externally managed Python rejects this with `error: externally-managed-environment` under PEP 668. This was reproduced with the same command plus `--dry-run --no-index`, without changing the installation.
- [`installDep`, lines 582–593](https://github.com/LNPANDY/nxnative-romfs-archive/blob/v0.3.0/frontend/Sources/NSPortBuilder/ContentView.swift#L582) redirects stdout/stderr to pipes without displaying them, does not report the nonzero exit status, and simply reruns detection. This hides the actionable error.

### Suggested behavior

- Manage a dedicated virtual environment and use its Python for both dependency detection and build scripts. Avoid changing or bypassing Homebrew's managed environment.
- Accept `compression.zstd` when available, falling back to `backports.zstd` on older Python versions. Only install the backport when needed.
- Surface pip failures and their stderr in the UI.

### Verified workaround

A dedicated virtual environment using an already-installed Python 3.12, with `lz4`, `capstone`, `fonttools`, and `backports.zstd`, passes all four imports. Launching the app with that environment's `bin` directory prepended to `PATH` lets `findPython` discover it. The user confirmed the dependency check then works.

This verifies dependency detection only. A complete game build through this UI was not tested, and compatibility of every dependency with Python 3.15 is not claimed.
title: NS Port Builder v0.3.0: Python 3.15 dependency check requires unsupported backports.zstd; Install fails silently on Homebrew
